title: planning-publication-reconcile: parent:GH#NNN task lines fail silently and keep publication:pending
body:
## Observed

`planning-publication-reconcile.sh reconcile` reports `failed=N` without printing any warning for tasks whose TODO line uses an issue-number parent, e.g.:

```
- [ ] tNNNN Title #tag #no-auto-dispatch parent:GH#<parent-issue> ref:GH#<issue> brief:todo/tasks/tNNNN-brief.md
```

Those issues keep `publication:pending` forever, and the post-merge full-loop summary shows `PUBLICATION_RECONCILE_SUMMARY ... failed=5` with no way to see why.

## Root cause (from `bash -x` trace)

1. `_publication_reconcile_one` → `_publication_desired_labels` → `parse_task_line` (`issue-sync-lib-parse.sh`).
2. `_task_parent_value` calls `task_identity_validate "GH#<n>"`, which only accepts `tNNN` / namespaced ids → returns 1.
3. `parse_task_line` does `return 1` on parent-validation failure, so the entire line is rejected (not just the parent field).
4. `_publication_desired_labels` returns 1 → `_publication_reconcile_one` line 202 does `|| return 1` with no `print_warning`, so the failure is silent.

This happens when the parent is a GitHub-only issue with no task ID (for example a roadmap parent created issue-first).

## Expected

- Either accept `parent:GH#NNN` as a valid parent reference (the issue-first parent case), or ignore/warn on an unparseable parent value instead of failing the whole line.
- `_publication_reconcile_one` should `print_warning "<task>/#<issue>: task line parse failed; retaining publication:pending"` on the `_publication_desired_labels` failure path, matching the other failure branches.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-lib-parse.sh` — `_task_parent_value` / `parse_task_line` (parent handling)
- `.agents/scripts/planning-publication-reconcile.sh` — `_publication_reconcile_one` (~line 202, silent return)

## Verification

- A TODO line with `parent:GH#123` parses (or parses with the parent dropped plus a warning) via `parse_task_line`.
- `planning-publication-reconcile.sh reconcile --task tNNNN` on such a line either reconciles or prints a specific warning; it never produces a silent `failed=1`.

title: feat(approval): keep locked issue approvals valid across write-authorized title/body edits
body:
## Problem

After #33089 (PR #33091), comments that write-authorized users post after the approval no longer stale a locked issue's approval. Edits to the issue **title or body** still do, even when a maintainer makes them. A common example is enriching the brief with `### Files Scope` or a reproducer after approval. That edit forces a `sudo aidevops approve` re-sign, which needs the maintainer at a terminal. A slow reply then blocks dispatch.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** approve an issue from an external author with `sudo aidevops approve issue N owner/repo`. As the maintainer, edit the issue body to add a `### Files Scope` section. Then run `approval-helper.sh verify issue N owner/repo`.

**Actual output:** `STALE_APPROVAL` (exit 4).

**Expected:** `VERIFIED` when every post-approval edit to the title or body was authored by a user with live `admin`/`maintain`/`write` permission.

## Root cause

`_approval_verify_locked_issue_continuity` (`.agents/scripts/approval-helper-continuity.sh`) rebuilds a candidate snapshot and compares its digest against the single signed `snapshot_digest`. The title and body are hashed together with everything else, so any edit changes the digest. The verifier also cannot tell who made the edit: REST exposes no editor identity for issue bodies.

## Proposed design

1. **Editor identity.** Fetch `userContentEdits` for the issue through GraphQL (`issue(number:) { userContentEdits(first:100) { nodes { editor { login } editedAt } } }`). Accept the edit history only if every edit after the approval comment's `created_at` has an editor with live `admin`/`maintain`/`write` permission, checked with `_approval_continuity_actor_authorized`. Fail closed with `API_ERROR` on a missing editor, a deleted-user (`ghost`) editor, pagination beyond one page, or any GraphQL error.
2. **Comparison without re-signing.** Current payloads contain only the whole-snapshot digest, so the verifier has two options for comparing everything except the title and body:
   - Option A: replace `.title` and `.body` in the candidate with the values from the approved snapshot. This requires the signed payload to carry the original title and body, or their hashes, so it only works for future signatures.
   - Option B: add per-component digests to new `aidevops-approval/v2` payloads (for example `issue.content_digests.{title,body,comments,linked_references}`). Keep verifying existing payloads exactly as before.

   Option B is preferred. It is additive, and old signatures keep today's behaviour.
3. **What stays unchanged.** Untrusted edits, edits made before the approval, unlock/relock, and all PR approvals keep their current binding.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/approval-helper-continuity.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/approval-snapshot-v2.sh` (payload construction for component digests)
- `.agents/scripts/approval-helper.sh` (only if payload schema plumbing needs it)
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-approval-helper-content-binding.sh` (the gh stub needs a `graphql` case)
- `.agents/reference/auto-merge.md`

## Verification

`bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-approval-helper-content-binding.sh` with new cases:

- A trusted body edit after approval on a locked issue returns `VERIFIED`.
- An untrusted editor returns `STALE_APPROVAL`.
- A `ghost` editor or missing edit history returns `API_ERROR`.
- A legacy payload without component digests plus a body edit returns `STALE_APPROVAL`.
- A trusted body edit on an unlocked issue returns `STALE_APPROVAL`.

Also run `shellcheck` on the touched scripts and the other `test-approval-*` suites.

Ref #33089.

title: t18561: fix: repos migrate-layout apply fails on OpenCode DBs with no matching rows
body:
## What

`aidevops repos migrate-layout apply` refuses with `OpenCode database verification failed: <isolated opencode.db>` after the repository move and main DB update, leaving a partial receipt.

## Why (root cause, verified)

`plan_consumers` records every isolated `opencode-interactive/*/opencode/opencode.db` as a database consumer, including ones with zero matching rows (drift guard). For those, `changes == []`. In `.agents/scripts/repo_layout_migrate.py`, `database_change_state()` returns `"before"` for an empty change set, so `update_database()` runs an empty transaction and its post-verify then requires `"after"` and raises. Any install with more than one isolated OpenCode DB hits this on the first zero-row DB.

Observed receipt: `repository:0`, `consumer:repos_json`, `consumer:tabby`, `consumer:database:0` completed; `consumer:database:1` (zero rows) started and failed.

## How

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/repo_layout_migrate.py` `update_database()` — return early (no write transaction) when `details["changes"]` is empty. Rollback already treats empty as `before` and returns.
- Verify: `python3 tests/test-repo-layout-migrate.py` (existing suite); resume the partial receipt with the same plan/confirm.

## Acceptance

- Apply completes when isolated DBs have no matching rows.
- Resuming a receipt stuck at a zero-row `consumer:database:N` completes without drift errors.

title: fix(pulse): old-bundle worker-exit refills still block setup Pulse reconciliation (regression of #32546)
body:
## What

Recover regression #33113 of #32546: old-bundle worker-exit Pulse refills can
respawn during setup reconciliation, acquire the shared instance lock, and
prevent a newly activated bundle from starting.

## Observed evidence

On 2026-09-30, setup stopped pre-reconciliation Pulse processes and launchd
accepted a restart, but no new activated-bundle process appeared. Refill-only
processes from the previous bundle kept appearing with
`--refill-source=worker-exit`; the new launchd Pulse then lost its instance lock.
This is historical evidence: verify the current owning path before changing it.

## Approach and boundaries

Follow the worker-exit refill entry through runtime pinning and the setup
reconciliation helper. Prefer fixing the entry boundary so an old worker starts
its refill from the verified active bundle before lease/instance-lock acquisition.
Preserve ordinary invocation pinning, missing/invalid active-root failures,
process identity checks, bounded replacement proofs and managed launchd ownership.
Do not accept an arbitrary refill lock as activation evidence, disable guards,
kill unrelated processes, or weaken worktree/source permissions.

### Files Scope

- EDIT if needed: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`
- EDIT if needed: `.agents/scripts/pulse-runtime-pin.sh`
- EDIT if needed: `.agents/scripts/pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh`
- Existing tests: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh`
- Existing tests: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-event-refill.sh`
- Existing tests: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-runtime-pin.sh`
- Exact fix/test placement is not yet known; establish it by tracing the entry.
- Hard boundary for concurrent mission unit #33303: do not edit
  `headless-runtime-lib.sh`, `headless-runtime-worker.sh`, manual-dispatch or
  pre-edit ownership code. Return a serialization need if that boundary is needed.

## Acceptance and verification

- Reproduce activation B while a worker pinned to A requests its exit refill;
  the request uses B before taking the lock, or current code is proven to do so.
- Setup reconciliation observes a newly started active-bundle managed process
  and returns success; old-bundle refills cannot continuously win the lock.
- Current-bundle, sourced/test invocation, invalid active root and unrelated-owner
  negative paths retain their existing behavior.
- Exercise the normal CLI/process paths in isolated existing fixtures, run both
  existing suites, syntax, ShellCheck and changed-file lint. High-risk lifecycle
  work requires runtime evidence and independent closeout review.
- Never activate or terminate unrelated production services to construct a test.

## Dispatch authority

The repository owner authorized this unattended backlog mission, with at most
two independent mission workers. This thinking-tier self-hosting unit is independent of the
manual-worker ownership repair; parent owns integration, issue disposition and
the explicitly authorized final release. If the premise is already fixed,
return exact merged-fix/runtime evidence instead of a speculative patch.

[effort:thinking] Implement and verify within this scope, then push a ready PR
and return exact-head evidence to the parent. Do not merge, release, edit shared
mission planning, or delegate again. Parent performs integration and closeout.

title: t18562: fix(worker): route unverified post-PR handoff with durable PR to checkpoint, ...
body:
## What

A headless worker that exits with a `POST_PR_HANDOFF` signal after opening a ready PR that uses a non-closing reference (`For #N` / `Part of #N`), or a ready PR still missing its `MERGE_SUMMARY`, is routed as a failure today:

- the claim is released with `worker_post_pr_handoff_unverified`;
- fast-fail is reported with crash type `overwhelmed`, which escalates the tier at threshold 1 and posts "could not produce commits" / "failed to produce a PR";
- the issue returns to `status:available` with `auto-dispatch`, so pulse redispatches while the PR is still open.

Route these exact-head durable PR states through the existing checkpoint preservation handlers instead.

## Why

Observed on a managed app repo on 2026-09-28 and 2026-09-29. Two worker runs on one issue both exited 0 with `result=post_pr_handoff` in `headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl`. Each opened a valid ready PR with a non-closing reference, because part of the scope needed maintainer credentials. Both PRs later merged.

- Each run was released as `worker_post_pr_handoff_unverified`.
- The first run posted a false "Cascade Tier Escalation: tier:standard → tier:thinking" comment.
- The issue stayed `status:available` + `auto-dispatch`, so a third worker was dispatched and self-terminated as a redundant redispatch.

### Root cause

`_hrw_finish_success_run` in `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh` has a `post_pr_handoff` gate (about line 2237). The gate calls `_worker_post_pr_handoff_confirmed`, which accepts only state `ready`.

`_pr_handoff_state_for_branch_or_issue` in `.agents/scripts/shared-claim-lifecycle.sh` never returns `ready` for these PRs:

- `For` / `Ref` PRs get `ready_missing_linkage` (`_pr_handoff_has_linked_issue` accepts only closing keywords).
- PRs without a merge summary get `ready_missing_summary`.

The gate therefore hard-fails and sets `release_needed=0`. The later `_worker_produced_output` switch never runs, although it already preserves `ready_missing_linkage`, `ready_missing_summary` and `draft_checkpoint` as `status:in-review` with `auto-dispatch` removed and the runner assigned. That is the designed exact-head continuation state.

## How

1. In `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh`, when `_hrw_finish_success_run` sees an unconfirmed `post_pr_handoff`, classify with `_worker_produced_output` first.
   - For `draft_checkpoint`, `ready_missing_summary` and `ready_missing_linkage`, call the existing `_hrw_preserve_*_handoff` helper and skip fast-fail and tier escalation.
   - Every other class keeps the existing `worker_post_pr_handoff_unverified` failure path, including fail-open `pr_exists`, `noop`, `closed_unmerged`, `unverified_open_pr` and `head_mismatch`.
   - Put this in a small extracted helper so `_hrw_finish_success_run` does not grow.
2. In `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-checkpoint-tests.sh`, add a case for an unverified `post_pr_handoff` with `ready_missing_linkage`. Model it on `test_ready_missing_summary_preserves_in_review_handoff`.
3. In `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-completion-tests.sh`, pin the existing "unverified POST_PR_HANDOFF cannot suppress failure routing" case to a non-durable class (`pr_exists`), so it does not depend on live GitHub classification.

### Reference pattern

Model on `_hrw_preserve_ready_missing_linkage_handoff` and the `ready_missing_linkage)` arm of the `_worker_produced_output` switch in the same function.

## Acceptance

- [ ] An unverified `post_pr_handoff` with `ready_missing_linkage` records `deferred|worker.deferred|checkpointed|worker_ready_missing_linkage`, returns 0 and never calls `_report_failure_to_fast_fail`.
- [ ] The existing "unverified POST_PR_HANDOFF cannot suppress failure routing" test still passes, so non-durable classes still fail.
- [ ] ShellCheck is clean on the changed files.

## Verification

The checkpoint and completion test files are sourced by `test-headless-runtime-helper.sh`.

title: fix(headless): Claude runtime sandbox skips signing/Git-auth env normalization
body:
## What

The Claude headless runtime path builds the sandbox passthrough without first normalizing the worker's process-scoped signing and Git-auth environment. The OpenCode path does this; the Claude path does not.

Found while implementing #33064 (PR #33116).

## Evidence

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-invoke.sh:239-249` (`_invoke_opencode_run_sandboxed`) calls `prepare_headless_signing_sandbox_env "$runtime_role"` and `prepare_headless_git_auth_sandbox_env "$runtime_role"`, failing with exit 87/88 if either cannot be isolated.
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh:357-359` (`_invoke_claude`) calls `build_sandbox_passthrough_csv` directly, with no provider or role arguments and neither prepare function.
- `build_sandbox_passthrough_csv` (`.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh:904-908`) forwards `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`/`GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0..2`/`GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0..2` only when `_headless_signing_sandbox_env_is_normalized` holds (`_AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS_SIGNING_GIT_CONFIG_START == 0`, `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT == 3`), and the Git-auth variables only when `_headless_git_auth_sandbox_env_is_normalized` holds.

Effect: when the launcher has any ambient `GIT_CONFIG_*` entry before the signing entries (start > 0), a Claude worker gets no dedicated signing config inside the sandbox. It then falls back to the global signing key and can fail at commit, which is the #33064 failure mode through a different route. Git-auth isolation is likely affected in the same way. This is a static trace; it has not been reproduced on a live Claude worker.

## Reproducer

Unconfirmed investigation from a static trace. To reproduce: with `commit.gpgsign=true`, a dedicated key from `aidevops signing headless-setup`, and one ambient `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1`/`GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0` exported in the launcher, dispatch a worker on the Claude runtime. Expected on current `main`: the sandbox receives no `GIT_CONFIG_*`, so the worker signs with the global (interactive) key and fails at commit. The OpenCode runtime under the same setup signs correctly.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-contract-tests.sh`

## Fix

In `_invoke_claude` (`.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh`), before `build_sandbox_passthrough_csv`, call `prepare_headless_signing_sandbox_env worker` and `prepare_headless_git_auth_sandbox_env worker` with the same fail-closed exit codes (87/88) and messages as `_invoke_opencode_run_sandboxed`. Check whether `build_sandbox_passthrough_csv` should receive the provider/role arguments the OpenCode path passes. The comment at `headless-runtime-worker.sh:333-335` says a second `_invoke_claude` copy may exist in `headless-runtime-helper.sh`; apply the fix to every live copy.

## Verification

- Extend `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-contract-tests.sh` using the pattern in `test_worker_signing_sandbox_env_excludes_ambient_git_config`: ambient `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0` plus signing entries at start=1, run the Claude path's sandbox preparation, and assert the sandbox sees `gpg.format`/`user.signingkey`/`commit.gpgsign` and not the ambient key.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-helper.sh` passes; `shellcheck` is clean.

title: Issue Sync: brief_scope rejects Next.js route paths; relationship graph fails silently on noncanonical blocked-by
body:
## Observed

While unblocking a managed project's Issue Sync (planning publication failing on every default-branch push), two framework defects surfaced in the TODO/brief parsers.

### 1. `brief_scope.py` rejects valid Next.js App Router paths

`exact()` in `.agents/scripts/brief_scope.py` accepts only `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]` path segments, so a Files Scope entry such as

```text
apps/web/src/app/[locale]/dashboard/(user)/(protected)/messages/page.tsx
```

fails with `Files Scope requires owned author-side repair`, and `issue-sync-helper.sh push` then refuses the task (`issue body composition failed`). Next.js dynamic segments (`[param]`, `[...slug]`) and route groups (`(group)`) are ordinary tracked file paths, so any brief that must edit a route file cannot be published. The only workaround is to declare an over-broad ancestor directory such as `apps/web/src/app`.

### 2. Relationship graph build fails silently on a noncanonical `blocked-by` target

`_relationship_declared_edges` in `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-relationships.sh` calls `parse_task_line`, which calls `_task_dependency_value`. A completed, canonical row carrying `blocked-by:t608.0` fails that parse because `t608.0` has a zero subtask segment. The loop returns 1 with no message, and the only output is `Cannot build a complete TODO dependency graph`. The row and the offending reference are never named, unlike the adjacent `Active dependency references historical noncanonical task ID ...` message. In the observed repo this failure was hidden behind an earlier error and only appeared once that error was fixed.

## Expected

1. Files Scope accepts repository-relative paths with `[`, `]`, `(`, `)` segment characters while still rejecting globs (`*`, `{a,b}`), `..`, `.git`, and whitespace.
2. A dependency-parse failure names the task ID and the invalid reference. For completed rows, historical noncanonical targets are skipped with an INFO line, matching how completed legacy rows are already skipped.

## Files to modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/brief_scope.py` — widen `exact()` to allow `[]()` within segments. Keep the existing `.`/`..`/`.git` part checks and keep rejecting `*`, `?`, `{`, `}`, and whitespace.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/issue-sync-relationships.sh` — in `_relationship_declared_edges`, when `parse_task_line` fails, print an error naming `task_id`. For `[x]` rows, skip dependency values that fail `task_identity_validate` instead of aborting the whole graph.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-claim-task-id-no-orphan.sh` (or the nearest existing brief-scope test) — add a Next.js route path case only if a focused case is the cheapest proof.

## Verification

- `python3 .agents/scripts/brief_scope.py check "<body with ## Files Scope listing a [locale]/(group) path>" ...` exits 0; a `*.tsx` glob entry still exits 1.
- A TODO fixture with `- [x] t9.1 ... blocked-by:t9.0` runs `issue-sync-helper.sh relationships --dry-run` without `Cannot build a complete TODO dependency graph`. An open row with the same reference emits an error naming both IDs.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/issue-sync-relationships.sh`

title: What next can hide uncommitted session work
body:
## Description

The interactive `What next` block can report both `Needed from you: None` and
`Left to capture: None` while session-owned changes remain uncommitted in a
linked worktree and the runtime requires explicit commit approval.

This creates a false ready-to-close signal. A user following it can close the
session while completed work has no durable Git checkpoint, making substantial
work easy to overlook or lose.

## Root cause

The session policy requires a general capture check but does not explicitly
require a live Git-status check across every touched repository/worktree before
writing `None` or `Ready to close`. It also does not classify uncommitted files
as uncaptured work or require missing commit approval to appear under
`Needed from you`.

## Target files

- `.agents/AGENTS.md`
- `.agents/reference/session.md`
- focused regression coverage under `tests/`

## Acceptance criteria

- Before returning control, interactive sessions inspect live Git status in
  every repository and linked worktree touched by the session.
- Session-owned modified, staged, or untracked files are reported under
  `Left to capture` until committed.
- If commit approval is required and absent, the approval appears under
  `Needed from you` and `Close` remains `Not yet`.
- Earlier status snapshots cannot satisfy the final capture check.
- A focused regression check prevents removal of these prompt invariants.

## Verification

- Run the focused session-capture policy test.
- Run ShellCheck on the new test.
- Run Markdownlint on both policy documents.
- Run `git diff --check`.

An interactive session has a verified local fix in progress; automatic worker
dispatch should remain held to avoid duplicate edits.

## Dispatch Hold

Interactive session has a verified local fix in progress; avoid duplicate worker changes

title: t18563: fix(skill-update): authenticate GitHub lookups and route non-GitHub skill sources
body:
## What

`skill-update-helper.sh check` fails for 12 of 14 imported skills, so upstream-synced skills have silently gone stale. `remotion` and `cloudflare-platform-skill` were last synced 2026-01-21, while upstream `remotion-dev/skills` had a commit on 2026-09-29 (`gh api "repos/remotion-dev/skills/commits?per_page=1"` → `a1b09e9`).

## Why

Imported skills (Remotion, Cloudflare, HeyGen, nothing-design, video-use, Cloudron and others) are only worth keeping if they stay current. The daily auto-update freshness path (`auto-update-freshness-lib.sh`) calls this helper non-interactively, so the failures are logged but nobody sees them.

## Root causes (verified 2026-09-30)

1. **Unauthenticated GitHub API.** `get_latest_commit()` in `.agents/scripts/skill-update-core-lib.sh:169-191` uses bare `curl` against `api.github.com`. After the first request it hits the 60/hour anonymous limit. Direct evidence: `curl -s https://api.github.com/repos/remotion-dev/skills/commits?per_page=1` returns `API rate limit exceeded`, while `gh api` returns the commit. The same pattern is in `.agents/scripts/skill-update-batch-lib.sh:110-117` and `:506-514`.
2. **Non-GitHub sources routed to the GitHub checker.** Sources on `clawdhub.com` and `git.cloudron.io` go to `_check_github_skill()` (`skill-update-core-lib.sh:503-521`). `parse_github_url` then yields `https:/`, which fails with `Could not fetch latest commit for caldav-calendar (https:/)`.
3. **`help` runs a full check.** `skill-update-helper.sh:148-198` treats a bare `help` as a skill name, so `skill-update-helper.sh help` runs `check`. Only `--help` and `-h` show help.

## How

- Prefer `gh api` (authenticated, already a framework dependency) for GitHub commit lookups. Fall back to curl with `GH_TOKEN` or `GITHUB_TOKEN` only when `gh` is unavailable. Make one shared function used by both libs.
- Route non-GitHub URLs to the existing content-hash path, the one `convos` uses successfully with `https://convos.org/skill.md`. For git hosts that are not GitHub, use `git ls-remote <url> HEAD` when the URL is a git repository.
- Accept `help` as a command alias.
- After the fix, run `skill-update-helper.sh check` and report which skills have updates. Do not auto-apply the updates in this PR; re-syncing content is separate follow-up work.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/skill-update-core-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/skill-update-batch-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/skill-update-helper.sh`

## Acceptance criteria

- `skill-update-helper.sh check` reports `Check failed: 0` for reachable sources on a machine with authenticated `gh`.
- Non-GitHub sources report up-to-date or update-available through the content-hash or `ls-remote` path, never `https:/`.
- `skill-update-helper.sh help` prints help and makes no network calls.
- ShellCheck is clean for all three files.

## Verification

```bash
.agents/scripts/skill-update-helper.sh check
.agents/scripts/skill-update-helper.sh help
shellcheck .agents/scripts/skill-update-core-lib.sh .agents/scripts/skill-update-batch-lib.sh .agents/scripts/skill-update-helper.sh

```

Context: found during the framework value audit (interactive session, 2026-09-30) while checking whether imported Remotion and Cloudflare skill content was current.

title: Pulse: per-class dispatch cap (max share of worker slots for a labelled issue class)
body:
## What

Let a project cap how much of a machine's worker capacity one class of issues may use, for example "award-enrichment issues may use at most 50% of this machine's simultaneous worker slots".

Proposed shape (implementer may refine):

- A label such as `dispatch-class:<name>` on issues.
- Per-repo config in `repos.json` (or `.aidevops.json`): `"dispatch_classes": { "award-enrichment": { "max_share_pct": 50 } }`, with an optional absolute `max_workers`.
- In the Pulse dispatch loop, before launching a worker for an issue with a class label, count active workers for issues of the same class (from the shared worker discovery path) and skip the issue when `active >= floor(simultaneous_target_final * max_share_pct / 100)` (minimum 1). Log the skip reason in `pulse.log` and the dashboard.

## Why

Observed on 2026-09-30 while preparing a batch of about 50 data-only award-enrichment issues (project repo, product class):

- `pulse.log` `Dispatch_capacity` reports `simultaneous_target_final=8` on this machine.
- `pulse-capacity-alloc.sh` provides product/tooling class reservations (`PRODUCT_MIN=5`, `TOOLING_MAX=3`) and a `check_repo_worker_cap` function (default `MAX_WORKERS_PER_REPO=5`), but the only caller of `check_repo_worker_cap` is the `repo-cap` CLI command in `pulse-wrapper-commands.sh:87`; the dispatch loop does not use it. There is no per-label or per-class cap.
- Result: a large batch of `auto-dispatch` issues of one kind can occupy every product slot on every maintainer machine, starving feature and bug work in the same repo. The only current workaround is manual drip-feeding of `auto-dispatch` labels.

The maintainer asked for enrichment to use "up to 50% of available concurrency".

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-capacity-alloc.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`
- `.agents/reference/worker-diagnostics.md`

(Exact dispatch-loop file may differ; locate the loop that launches workers after `Dispatch_capacity` is computed.)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With `max_share_pct: 50` and `simultaneous_target_final=8`, at most 4 workers run for issues labelled with that class; other issues in the same repo still dispatch into the remaining slots.
- [ ] Issues without a class label behave exactly as today.
- [ ] Skips are logged with class, active count and cap.
- [ ] Documented in `reference/worker-diagnostics.md` next to the minimum concurrency floor.

## Verification

- Existing pulse dispatch test harness (for example `tests/test-dispatch-min-concurrency.sh`) extended with a class-cap case.
- `shellcheck` on changed scripts.

title: Project single status:blocked for open terminal-blocker circuits and release it on trusted retry
body:
## What

When a terminal-blocker circuit opens or is already open, the release path still projects `status:available`, contradicting the circuit's "Projected state: status:blocked" text and leaving dual-status issues (reported in #33025 follow-up comments: an issue temporarily carried both `status:available` and `status:blocked`). Project exactly one `status:blocked` while a known-class circuit is open, and return the issue to `status:available` when a trusted OWNER/MEMBER `terminal-blocker-circuit:retry` directive (or a relevant revision) re-arms dispatch.

## Why

Found during #33025 and blocked by #33025: start after its PR merges, because this builds on its collaborator-runner hold evidence in `terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`. The circuit now engages for collaborator runners (#33025), but label state still says the issue is available while dispatch is held, which misleads operators and other tooling. `status:blocked` is also a hard pre-claim gate (`_dispatch_preclaim_brief_scope_verdict` in `pulse-dispatch-core.sh`), so projecting it without an automatic release on retry would break the documented retry-only recovery — both halves must ship together.

## Reproducer

Static code-path evidence on `main` at `cdcfe21` (confirmed by reading source, not yet reproduced on a live issue):

1. `terminal-blocker-circuit.sh:375` writes the circuit comment with `Projected state: status:blocked.`
2. `headless-runtime-failure.sh` `_hrff_handle_terminal_blocker_release` (`circuit` and `open` branches, ~L606-620) then calls `_hrff_release_rate_limit_circuit_cleanup` -> `clear_active_status_on_release`.
3. `shared-constants.sh` `clear_active_status_on_release` (~L1436-1455) projects `available` when no linked PR exists, so a circuit-held issue with no PR ends up labelled `status:available` while dispatch is suppressed.

## How

- `headless-runtime-failure.sh` `_hrff_handle_terminal_blocker_release`: in `circuit`/`open` modes, replace the `_hrff_release_rate_limit_circuit_cleanup` → `clear_active_status_on_release` (projects `available`) call with a single-status `set_issue_status ... blocked` projection plus assignee removal and unlock.
- Add a release path: when `terminal_blocker_circuit_active` stops being active for an issue labelled `status:blocked` whose newest blocked reason is a terminal-blocker circuit (not a brief hold, dependency, permission-helper or other hold), project `status:available` once. Candidate owner: `terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh` `_tbr_check_entry` (already detects re-arm and retires the queue entry) — verify it runs on every runner that opened a circuit.
- Keep `needs-maintainer-permissions` reserved for `worker-permission-helper.sh` requests (see `_hrff_apply_terminal_permission_hold`).

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`

## Acceptance

- Opening or hitting an open circuit leaves exactly one status label: `status:blocked`.
- A trusted OWNER/MEMBER retry directive (or relevant code/brief revision for non-permission classes) returns the issue to `status:available` without manual label edits; collaborator retries do not.
- Unknown-class blockers keep today's retryable behaviour (no durable hold).
- Brief holds, dependency blocks and permission-helper holds are never released by this path.

## Verification

`bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`, `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-release-unlock.sh` (note: its draft-checkpoint case fails identically on main as of cdcfe21), and `shellcheck -x` on modified files.

title: t18564: Framework value audit: retire obsolete scaffolding and keep the ideas worth keeping
body:
Planning-only: parent tracker for the framework value audit. Children carry the implementation.

## What

This audit, run with the maintainer in an interactive session on 2026-09-30, asked which parts of aidevops no longer earn their place given current frontier models and modern harnesses. It aims to retire those parts while keeping any idea behind them that is still worth having.

## Decision rule

Keep anything that provides:

- access: MCPs, APIs, credentials, account workflows
- deterministic mechanics: gates, hooks, worktree safety
- durable state: memory, TODO.md, issues
- post-cutoff facts or house decisions
- exact data models cannot recall, such as brand tokens

Retire generic knowledge restatement, reasoning crutches such as self-grading loops and prompt optimisers, token-squeezing wrappers, and code indexing.

## Decisions (maintainer-confirmed)

- **Keep:** TOON, `subagent-index.toon`, the design library, model availability and fallback checks, `/autoresearch`, the pageindex generator, Context7, `/cross-review`, the Drizzle-specific docs, and the Cloudflare and Remotion knowledge (after refresh).
- **Retire:**
  - osgrep and Augment leftovers, llm-tldr, context-builder/repomix, rapidfuzz
  - DSPy and DSPyGround
  - the Ralph loop
  - the contest and response-scoring chain
  - dead pattern-tracker callers
  - Beads
  - `todo-ready.sh`, `mission-skill-learner.sh`
  - textbook skills: modern-javascript, clean-ddd-hexagonal, feature-slicing
  - `claude-flow-comparison.md`
- **Replace:**
  - Beads becomes an issue/PR discussion archive on a separate branch in the same repo, written by a routine the pulse runs.
  - The Ralph loop becomes a keep-going hook for Claude Code, matching OpenCode's `session-continuation-guard.mjs`.
  - The contest chain is replaced by model-replay, model-ab and `frontier-harness-eval`, which already exist.
- **Ideas captured from retired code:**
  - Rule-violation counts from `ttsr.mjs` feed the list of rules that should become hooks.
  - Evidence-based model tier step-down belongs with model-ab data, not the archived pattern tracker.

## Children

Children are linked as sub-issues. GH#33135 (skill-update checker fix) is the prerequisite for the Remotion/Cloudflare re-sync child.

### Files Scope

- `TODO.md`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All child issues closed with merged PRs.

## Outcome

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief


## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-09-30
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Issue:** GH#33143
- **Conversation context:** Framework value audit (parent GH#33139); maintainer approved retiring redundant tooling while keeping the useful ideas.

## Why

OpenCode sessions have a continuation guard that stops models ending turns before the work is done. Claude Code has no equivalent, so behaviour differs between runtimes, especially for models that tend to stop early.

## What

Add a lightweight Claude Code `Stop` hook that pushes back when a session tries to stop with work still open. Parent: GH#33139.

This replaces the retired Ralph loop with the "light encourager" the maintainer asked for, for models that tend to stop early to seek reassurance.

OpenCode already has this behaviour in `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/session-continuation-guard.mjs`:

- `isExplicitCompletionClaim` and `activeTodos` come from `session-continuation-utils.mjs:73` and `:87`.
- It uses a repeated-failure threshold, `DEFAULT_FAILURE_THRESHOLD = 3`.
- Checkpoints are saved through `session-checkpoint-helper.sh recovery-save`.

Claude Code has no equivalent. `.agents/hooks/` only contains PreToolUse and PostToolUse guards, and `update-claude-settings.py` registers no `Stop` hook.

## Design constraints (decide and record in the PR)

- Block the stop only on clear evidence: the transcript's latest TodoWrite state still has `pending` or `in_progress` items, and the final message is not a question to the user or an explicit blocker report.
- Cap it. Use the `stop_hook_active` input field to avoid an infinite loop, allow at most N blocks per session (suggest 2), and after that allow the stop.
- The block reason should be one short sentence: continue the next open todo, or state the blocker and the remaining todos.
- Never block headless or worker sessions that the pulse supervises (they have their own watchdog), and never block when the user explicitly asked to stop.
- Keep the logic in one small Python hook alongside `git_safety_guard.py`, using only the standard library and failing open on any parse error.

## How: reference pattern

- Registration: model on the PreToolUse registration in `.agents/scripts/update-claude-settings.py:33-60`.
- Detection semantics: model on `session-continuation-guard.mjs:120-200`.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/hooks/session_continuation_stop.py`
- `.agents/scripts/update-claude-settings.py`
- `.agents/scripts/install-hooks-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-session-continuation-stop-hook.sh`
- `.agents/reference/session.md`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With open todos and no blocker or question, the hook returns a block decision with a one-sentence reason.
- [ ] With `stop_hook_active` true, or after the cap is reached, the hook allows the stop.
- [ ] With no todos, a question to the user, or a malformed transcript, the hook allows the stop (fail-open).
- [ ] `setup.sh --non-interactive` registers the hook idempotently in Claude Code settings.
- [ ] `reference/session.md` has a two-line note on the behaviour and the override.

## Verification

python3 -m py_compile .agents/hooks/session_continuation_stop.py

**Task ID:** `t18571` | **Status:** open
**Logged:** 2026-09-30
**Tags:** `auto-dispatch` `feat`

## Outcome

feat(backup): archive issue and PR discussions to a same-repo orphan branch via pulse routine

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief


## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-09-30
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Issue:** GH#33146
- **Conversation context:** Framework value audit (parent GH#33139); maintainer approved retiring redundant tooling while keeping the useful ideas.

## Why

Issue and PR discussions, reviews and outcomes live only on the forge, so losing the forge would lose decision history. `forge-portability.md` records this gap. Beads was meant to cover it but does not.

## What

Keep issue and PR knowledge inside each managed repo, so losing the forge (account suspension, outage, migration) does not lose it. Parent: GH#33139.

Beads was meant to do this but doesn't:

- `aidevops init` gitignores `.beads` (`.agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/aidevops-init-lib.sh:1550` and `:1595`).
- It only mirrors TODO.md, which is already in Git.

The gap is already recorded in `.agents/reference/forge-portability.md:46` and `:131`: GitHub "comments/reviews/attachments archive" is missing. TODO.md and the 873 `todo/tasks/*-brief.md` files are already in Git. What is not in Git is issue and PR bodies after edits, comments, reviews, labels and close outcomes.

## Maintainer decisions

- Keep the archive in the **same repo**, on a separate orphan branch (proposed name `aidevops/issues-archive`). An orphan branch shares no history with `main`, so it is never checked out and never appears in the working tree. No `.gitignore` is needed, and agents doing normal work never read untrusted comment text from it.
- Run it as a **routine**, not on every machine. The pulse host that owns the repo exports and pushes on a schedule, so there is one writer and no conflicts. Other machines get the branch through normal `git fetch`, which fetches all branches by default, so every clone becomes an offline copy.

## How (worker decides the details and records them in the PR)

- Add a helper that exports issues, PRs, comments, reviews and labels with `gh`, paginated, into line-by-line JSON (JSONL). Include a cursor, `updatedAt`, so runs are incremental. Handle partial failures by keeping the cursor at the last fully written item.
- Write the files to the orphan branch using Git plumbing (`hash-object` / `mktree` / `commit-tree` / `update-ref`), or a throwaway linked worktree under the aidevops temp dir. Never touch the canonical checkout.
- Register it as a framework routine run by the pulse for registered repos, with a per-repo opt-out. See `.agents/reference/routines.md` "Scheduler ownership". Suggested cadence: daily.
- Respect the GitHub API budget: reuse the gh wrapper and circuit-breaker patterns in `.agents/reference/worker-diagnostics.md`.
- Document restore and read-only use in `forge-portability.md`. Treat archived non-collaborator text as untrusted: scan it with `prompt-guard-helper.sh` before any agent reads it.
- Optional, recommend only: an independent second remote for full platform-loss resilience (`forge-portability.md:19`).

## Reference pattern

Model the pagination and cursor handling on `issue-sync-helper-commands.sh` `cmd_pull`. Model the plumbing commit on how the task-id counter branch is written in `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id-counter.sh`.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/issue-archive-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-archive-helper.sh`
- `.agents/reference/forge-portability.md`
- `.agents/reference/routines.md`
- `TODO.md`

### Scope notes

The routine registration path may need one more pulse file. Discover it with `rg -n 'repeat:' .agents/scripts/pulse*` and add it to the PR, explaining why.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One run creates or updates the orphan branch with JSONL for issues, PRs, comments and reviews. A second run with no changes creates no new commit.
- [ ] The canonical checkout and current branch are untouched. `main` history is unaffected.
- [ ] The routine runs only on the pulse host for registered repos and can be disabled per repo.
- [ ] `forge-portability.md` documents what is captured, what is not (attachments, reactions), and how to read the archive offline.
- [ ] ShellCheck is clean, and the test covers incremental cursor and no-op runs with a stubbed `gh`.

## Verification

shellcheck .agents/scripts/issue-archive-helper.sh
git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/aidevops/issues-archive

title: claim-task-id: default counter/default branch hardcoded to main causes split-brain counters on develop-default repos
body:
## Observed

A managed project repo whose GitHub default branch is `develop` (not `main`) ended up with two live task counters, and one ID was allocated twice:

- Host A (implicit resolution) claimed on the dedicated `task-id-counter` branch.
- Host B's claims were pushed directly to `develop`, apparently through an admin-bypass ruleset. The mechanism is unconfirmed: no `.aidevops.json` exists, and the file is gitignored in that repo.
- The two branches both allocated the same two IDs within about an hour of each other, producing duplicate `tNNNN:` issue titles.
- Afterwards `task-id-counter` looked "stale" against the TODO seed, so `resolve_implicit_counter_branch` (`claim-task-id-counter.sh:489-547`) refused it. The helper fell back to `COUNTER_BRANCH="main"` (`claim-task-id.sh:198`), whose `.task-counter` was a years-old value (213), and failed with `PROTECTED_COUNTER_BRANCH`. All allocation on this host stopped.

Manual repair: a fast-forward commit on `task-id-counter` setting `.task-counter` to develop's value. After that, implicit selection and pre-claim reconcile worked.

## Gaps

1. `DEFAULT_BRANCH` and `COUNTER_BRANCH` default to the literal `main` instead of the remote's default branch (`gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef` or `git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`). The stale check and reconcile therefore compare against the wrong branch, and a stale `main` counter can pass validation.
2. The recovery guidance says to set `.aidevops.json counter_branch`, but projects may gitignore `.aidevops.json`. Then the setting is per-checkout, and worktrees and other hosts never see it.
3. A counter push to a protected default branch through admin bypass should be refused, or at least warned about, when a dedicated counter branch exists. Otherwise hosts split across two counters.
4. When `task-id-counter` is behind the default branch, the helper could offer an explicit, audited `sync-counter-branch` action (fast-forward only, target = max(default-branch counter, TODO seed, counter branch)) instead of only refusing.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id-counter.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-claim-task-id-protected-counter-branch.sh`

## Verification

Fixture repo with default branch `develop`, a protected `develop` holding counter N, and `task-id-counter` holding counter M < N:
- The helper must not select `main`.
- The sync action fast-forwards to N.
- A claim then allocates N.

title: claim-task-id: reconcile fetch omits --depth=1 in isolated counter context and times out on large repos
body:
## What

`claim-task-id.sh` fails with `UNRECOVERABLE_COUNTER_DESYNC: cannot fetch origin/<branch> for reconciliation` on large repositories. The reconcile fetch skips the `--depth=1` that every other fetch in the isolated counter context uses, so it transfers full branch history and exceeds `CAS_HTTPS_TIMEOUT_S` (default 30s) on both HTTPS and the SSH fallback.

## Evidence

On a large private project repo (counter branch = default branch `develop`), run twice with defaults:

```text
[INFO] Using isolated Git context for canonical counter discovery and CAS
[INFO] AIDEVOPS_TASK_COUNTER_STATUS=reconciling detail=branch=origin/develop
[WARN] git timed out after 30s on HTTPS — retrying via SSH (...)
[WARN] SSH fallback also timed out after 30s — both transports unavailable
[ERROR] UNRECOVERABLE_COUNTER_DESYNC: cannot fetch origin/develop for reconciliation
```

With `CAS_HTTPS_TIMEOUT_S=180`, the same command succeeded (`recovered_contention detail=refetched`, claim in 0s). A normal `git fetch origin develop` from a linked worktree of the same repo finishes quickly, because that object store already holds the history.

## Root cause

`.agents/scripts/claim-task-id-counter.sh`:

- `_cas_fetch_counter_branch_for_reconcile()` (around line 701) runs `fetch -q "$REMOTE_NAME" "$COUNTER_BRANCH"` with no depth limit and no `--no-tags`.
- The other isolated-context fetches already use `_counter_context_is_isolated && depth_args=(--depth=1)` (around lines 506, 747 and 1139). The comment at line 503 explains why: depth is limited to the isolated bare context, so the shared object store is never made shallow.
- Also audit the other fetches without a depth limit, around lines 851 and 906 (`fetch -q "$REMOTE_NAME" "$COUNTER_BRANCH"`), for the same gap.

## How

- Apply the same `depth_args` pattern and `--no-tags` in `_cas_fetch_counter_branch_for_reconcile()`. Keep the explicit remote-tracking refspec form used at line 508 if the later reconcile code reads `refs/remotes/<remote>/<branch>`.
- Apply the same fix to the other isolated-context fetches found in the audit. Never add depth when the context is not isolated.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Every fetch in the isolated counter context uses `--depth=1 --no-tags`. Non-isolated fetches are unchanged.
- [ ] The reconcile path completes within the default 30s on a repo with deep history.
- [ ] The shared object store never gains a `shallow` file (existing invariant, line 503).

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/claim-task-id-counter.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-claim-task-id-https-ssh-fallback.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-claim-task-id-no-orphan.sh
```

If a test stubs `git fetch`, add an argument assertion that the reconcile fetch carries `--depth=1` in isolated mode.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/claim-task-id-counter.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-claim-task-id-https-ssh-fallback.sh

title: planning-publisher: pre-commit validation diffs temp index against stale worktree HEAD, so upstream files block planning commits
body:
## What

`planning-commit-helper.sh` can refuse a TODO.md-only change because of files it never touched. The planning publisher builds a temporary index from the fresh remote tip (`parent_sha`), then runs `pre-commit-hook.sh` against that index. The hook's staged-file detection (`git diff --cached`) compares the index with the worktree's `HEAD`, not with `parent_sha`. When `HEAD` lags the remote, every upstream change since `HEAD` looks staged, and the hook validates or blocks those files.

## Evidence

In a linked worktree of a private project repo, the worktree was created from `origin/develop`. Then `develop` gained a commit that changed `.github/workflows/security.yml` (adding a self-hosted runner label unknown to actionlint). The only local change was one added TODO.md line (`git status --short` → ` M TODO.md`).

```text
[plan] Planning files to commit:
  - TODO.md
[INFO] Checking staged GitHub Actions workflow files...
[INFO] Linting 1 workflow file(s) with actionlint...
[ERROR] Workflow lint FAILED: .github/workflows/security.yml
...
[plan] Planning publication validation failed; nothing pushed
```

After `git merge --ff-only origin/develop` in the worktree, so that `HEAD` equals the remote tip, the same command passed and published directly.

## Root cause

- `.agents/scripts/planning-publisher.sh`: `_planning_publish_build_index` (around line 516) runs `read-tree "$parent_sha"`. `_planning_publish_validate` (around line 596) then runs `GIT_INDEX_FILE="$index_file" HOOK_MODE=pre-commit "$hook"` without telling the hook what the base is.
- `.agents/scripts/pre-commit-hook.sh` derives staged files from plain `git diff --cached`, which diffs against `HEAD`. Examples: `check_workflow_files` (around line 1082), the shell-file list (around line 58), TODO checks (around lines 86, 541, 550, 558, 704, 719, 727), counter (136), the general list (475) and new root files (1037).

Any failing check can be triggered this way, not only actionlint. Upstream ShellCheck or root-file findings would block planning publication in the same way, whenever the worktree is behind.

## How

- Add an optional base override to the hook. For example, when `AIDEVOPS_PRE_COMMIT_BASE` is set, staged-file helpers use `git diff --cached <base>`. Route all `git diff --cached` call sites through one helper so none are missed.
- In `_planning_publish_validate`, pass `AIDEVOPS_PRE_COMMIT_BASE="$parent_sha"` alongside `GIT_INDEX_FILE`.
- Ordinary `git commit` behaviour, with no override, is unchanged.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A planning publication from a worktree whose `HEAD` lags the remote validates only the planning paths it changes.
- [ ] A planning change that itself breaks a check still fails validation.
- [ ] Normal pre-commit runs are unaffected.

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pre-commit-hook.sh .agents/scripts/planning-publisher.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-planning-publisher.sh
```

Add a regression to `test-planning-publisher.sh` in which the remote tip changes a non-planning file that fails a hook check, while the worktree `HEAD` lags.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/pre-commit-hook.sh
- .agents/scripts/planning-publisher.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-planning-publisher.sh

title: claim-task-id: reconcile seeds from stale local TODO.md, and a foreign-title tNNN prefix match is reported as recovery (ID collision)
body:
## What

`claim-task-id.sh` allocated two task IDs that were already in use, one after the other. Each time it found the other session's issue by `tNNN:` prefix, reported it as "recovered", created nothing, and burned the ID. A third run was needed to get a free ID.

## Evidence

The project repo uses the counter on its default branch `develop`, with an isolated counter context. Counter history on the remote:

```text
02:16:49 chore: claim t18413
02:40:04 chore: reconcile task counter (18414->18419)
02:40:09 chore: claim t18419
```

Between 02:16 and 02:40, another session created t18414–t18420 (issues and TODO rows) without advancing `.task-counter`. The next claims then did this:

```text
Counter at 18419, claiming t18419..t18419, new counter: 18420
Found existing OPEN issue #<A> with exact t18419 prefix, skipping duplicate creation
Recovered issue #<A>, but publication:pending could not be verified
Issue creation failed for t18419 (non-fatal — ID is secured)
--- rerun ---
Counter at 18420, claiming t18420..t18420, new counter: 18421
Found existing OPEN issue #<B> with exact t18420 prefix, skipping duplicate creation
```

Issue #<A> is titled "t18419: <another session's feature>" and my requested title was "ci: declare …". The titles are unrelated, yet the collision was treated as a recovery. The remote `develop:TODO.md` already contained t18419 and t18420 at that time.

## Root causes

1. **The reconcile floor reads a stale local file.** `_compute_counter_seed()` in `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id-counter.sh` (around line 1028) reads `${repo_path}/TODO.md` from the working tree. When `repo_path` is the canonical checkout, which is a read-only mirror that lags the remote, the seed misses recently published IDs. Reconcile around line 767 then sets the counter below IDs that are already taken. It should read `TODO.md` from the fetched remote counter branch ref (`git show <remote>/<branch>:TODO.md`) that reconcile already has.
2. **Foreign-title prefix matches count as success.** `_check_duplicate_issue()` in `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id-issue.sh` (around lines 416–431) returns any open issue whose title starts with `tNNN: `. On a new allocation, a match whose title differs from the requested title is an ID collision, not an idempotent retry. It should fail loudly, for example with `TASK_ID_COLLISION`, and ideally bump the counter past the colliding ID and retry, instead of reporting `Recovered issue`.
3. **Undetected: the allocator that skipped the counter.** Some path created t18414–t18420 without CAS-advancing `.task-counter`. The creating path is unknown from this session. Check `issue-sync-helper.sh` push/allocation and `planning-commit-helper.sh next_task_id --offline` for writes of a `tNNN` that bypass the counter.

## Acceptance

- [ ] The reconcile seed uses the remote branch's `TODO.md` and ignores the local working tree.
- [ ] A new allocation whose `tNNN:` issue already exists with a different title does not report recovery. It either retries with the next free ID or fails with an explicit collision status.
- [ ] Idempotent retries (same title) still recover the existing issue.
- [ ] Finding 3 is investigated. Either fix the bypassing path or record which path it was.

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/claim-task-id-counter.sh .agents/scripts/claim-task-id-issue.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-claim-task-id-no-orphan.sh
```

Add a regression where the remote TODO.md holds a higher ID than both the counter file and the local TODO.md. Add another where an open issue with the allocated prefix has a different title.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/claim-task-id-counter.sh
- .agents/scripts/claim-task-id-issue.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-claim-task-id-no-orphan.sh

- **Issue:** GH#33159
- **Conversation context:** Found while publishing framework value audit tasks t18572 and t18574; their claim-generated TODO lines failed planning publication.

## What

When `claim-task-id.sh` auto-detects a predecessor (GH#20834), the TODO line it writes, or prints for canonical checkouts, contains `blocked-by:GH#NNN`. The issue-sync parser rejects that form, so planning publication never reconciles the task. It stays `publication:pending` and never dispatches.

## Why

Observed on 2026-09-30 with t18572 (GH#33148) and t18574 (GH#33150):

- `claim-task-id.sh` auto-detected GH#33135 as the predecessor of t18574 and suggested a TODO line whose dependency field used the `GH#NNN` form.
- After that line merged, `full-loop-helper.sh merge` reported `t18574/#33150: task line parse failed; retaining publication:pending`. t18572 failed the same way.
- Every other task in the same PR reconciled.
- Rewriting the dependency fields to the task IDs t18563 and t18571 made `parse_task_line` succeed.

Root cause:

- `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id-issue.sh:739-741` appends `blocked-by:${_CLAIM_BLOCKED_BY_REFS}` verbatim, and that value can hold `GH#NNN` refs (`claim-task-id.sh:1573-1575`).
- `_task_dependency_value` in `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-lib-parse.sh:248-263` validates through `task_identity_parse_list`, which accepts only task IDs. Every `blocked-by:` in TODO.md uses task IDs.

## How

1. In `claim-task-id-issue.sh` `_ensure_todo_entry_written` (around `:736-741`), map each `GH#NNN` in `_CLAIM_BLOCKED_BY_REFS` to its task ID:
   - First, the TODO.md line carrying `ref:GH#NNN`.
   - Otherwise, the issue title prefix `tNNN:` using the existing gh wrappers.

   Write only task IDs into the TODO line. If a ref cannot be resolved, omit it from the TODO line and log a warning. The GitHub `blocked-by:GH#NNN` label and the native relationship stay unchanged.
2. Leave `task_identity_parse_list` strict. Widening a shared parser is out of scope.

## Reference pattern

Reuse the task-ID lookup in `.agents/scripts/task-identity-lib.sh`, if it resolves `ref:GH#` to a task ID. Otherwise follow the `ref:GH#` grep already in `claim-task-id-issue.sh`.

- `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-claim-task-id-blocked-by-todo.sh`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A description naming a predecessor `GH#NNN` whose issue title is `tMMM: ...` produces a TODO line containing `blocked-by:tMMM` and no `blocked-by:GH#`.
- [ ] `parse_task_line` accepts the generated line (rc 0, `blocked_by=tMMM`).
- [ ] The GitHub `blocked-by:GH#NNN` label and sub-issue or dependency behaviour are unchanged, with no regression for descriptions that already use `blocked-by:tNNN`.
- [ ] An unresolvable `GH#NNN` does not break the TODO line; it is omitted with a warning.

- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Issue:** GH#33166
- **Conversation context:** Found when GH#33159 was falsely labelled status:blocked from prose examples in its body.

## What

The dependency graph treats any issue-body line containing the dependency phrase as a real dependency, including prose and backtick-quoted examples. An issue that only discusses dependency syntax gets `status:blocked` and never dispatches.

## Why

Observed on 2026-09-30 with GH#33159 (t18575), a claim-task-id bug report with no real predecessor:

- Its Why section quoted two example TODO dependency fields containing t18563, t18571, GH#33135 and GH#33150, all open.
- A pulse run relabelled it from `status:available` to `status:blocked` 17 minutes after creation, with no comment. Planning publication then added `status:available` back, leaving both status labels at once.
- Rewording the two prose lines so no task ID or issue number followed the phrase removed the false dependency.

Root cause: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph.sh:89` matches the phrase anywhere, case-insensitively, and captures to end of line. `:90-91` then collect every task ID and `#NNN` on the rest of that line. There is no anchoring to a field and no skipping of code spans or fenced blocks.

This is the same failure class as GH#26391, where body text created a circular dependency; that fix only changed the meta-issue filer.

## How

1. In `pulse-dep-graph.sh`, restrict body parsing to the structured forms the framework emits:
   - A line beginning (after optional list marker) with the bare TODO field.
   - The brief-template bold field.

   Strip fenced code blocks and inline code spans before matching, but keep accepting backtick-quoted IDs inside the bold field value, which is what `brief-template.md` emits.
2. Leave label-based and native-relationship dependencies unchanged.
3. Check `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh` predecessor detection (around `:1522-1626`) for the same prose-capture pattern. Document the result in the PR; change it only if it shares the defect.

## Reference pattern

Use the fence-aware visible-text helpers already used for briefs (`_unfenced_brief_text` / `_visible_brief_text` in `.agents/scripts/brief-readiness-helper.sh`) rather than a new parser.

title: scope-guard-pre-push compares against stale local main instead of origin/main
body:
## Observed

`scope-guard-pre-push.sh` blocked a new-branch push in a linked worktree and listed
files that were already merged to `origin/main` by an earlier PR. The branch
itself changed only two in-scope files (`git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD`).

## Cause

`_compute_baseline()` (`.agents/hooks/scope-guard-pre-push.sh`, around lines
231-257) reads `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`, then strips the `refs/remotes/origin/`
prefix with `sed`, leaving the bare name `main`. `git merge-base HEAD main` then
uses the local `main` branch, which is often stale in a canonical checkout that
sessions must not update. Every file merged upstream since that stale local
`main` is counted as out of scope.

## Fix

Keep the remote-qualified ref (for example `origin/main`) for `merge-base`: strip
only `refs/remotes/`, or resolve `refs/remotes/<remote>/HEAD` directly. Check
whether `complexity-regression-pre-push.sh`, which the comment says this mirrors
(GH#20045), has the same pattern.

## Verification

Reproduce: a linked worktree whose canonical local `main` is behind
`origin/main`; branch from `origin/main`; commit one in-scope file; push a new
branch. Expected: no out-of-scope files reported.

title: Planning publication reconcile adds status:available beside status:blocked; TODO blocked-by:#N breaks task-line parse
body:
## What

Planning-publication reconciliation ignores issue-number blockers, and TODO `blocked-by:` rejects them outright. A task blocked by a GitHub issue that has no task ID therefore can't be expressed safely:

1. **TODO field breaks the task line.** `blocked-by:#NNN` in a TODO.md task line makes `parse_task_line` fail. `_task_dependency_value` (`.agents/scripts/issue-sync-lib-parse.sh`) passes the value to `task_identity_parse_list` (`.agents/scripts/task-identity-lib.sh`), which accepts task IDs only. `_publication_reconcile_one` then reports "task line parse failed" and keeps `publication:pending`, which fails the Issue Sync workflow on every push to the default branch. `pulse-dep-graph.sh` accepts the same syntax (`tests/test-pulse-dep-graph-parse.sh`: `'blocked-by:#18429,#18430'`), so the two parsers disagree.
2. **Label path is overridden at publication.** The supported alternative, an issue label `blocked-by:#NNN` plus `status:blocked` (read by `pulse-dep-graph.sh` and unblocked by `dependency-event-reconciler.sh` when the blocker closes), is not seen by `_publication_task_has_dependency` (`.agents/scripts/planning-publication-reconcile.sh`), which reads only the task line. Reconciliation computes `status:available` and adds it next to the existing `status:blocked`. The issue then carries both, and is dispatchable until a later pulse cycle normalises it (`pulse-dep-graph.sh` "available -> blocked — unresolved dependency evidence").

## Observed evidence (2026-09-30, aidevops v3.37.32, private managed repo; names withheld)

- Task A's issue was labelled `blocked-by:#<B>` and `status:blocked` before its brief was published; B is an open issue with no task ID, resolved by an open PR.
- Issue Sync run: `PUBLICATION_RECONCILE_SUMMARY reconciled=2 deferred=0 stale=0 failed=0`.
- Labels on issue A immediately after: `status:available,status:blocked,auto-dispatch,...,blocked-by:#<B>`. `status:available` had to be removed by hand.
- The first attempt put `blocked-by:#<B>` in the TODO line; `task_identity_parse_list` rejection was confirmed by reading the code before publishing, so it was reverted.

## Proposed fix

- `_publication_task_has_dependency` (or `_publication_status_label`): also treat an open-issue `blocked-by:#N` / `blocked-by:GH#N` label, or an existing `status:blocked` label, on the issue as dependency evidence. Never add `status:available` beside `status:blocked`.
- `_task_dependency_value`: accept `#N` / `GH#N` issue references alongside task IDs (matching `pulse-dep-graph.sh`), and pass them through to relationship sync as native `blockedBy` edges, or ignore them with a warning, as `_task_parent_value` does for `parent:GH#N`. Never fail the whole line.

## Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/planning-publication-reconcile.sh` — functions `_publication_task_has_dependency` and `_publication_reconcile_one`
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/issue-sync-lib-parse.sh` — function `_task_dependency_value`

Reference pattern: `_task_parent_value` in `issue-sync-lib-parse.sh` (warn-and-ignore for issue-only refs), and label parsing in `pulse-dep-graph.sh`.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/planning-publication-reconcile.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-lib-parse.sh`

## Verification

- Unit: a task line with `blocked-by:#123` parses (no failure); `blocked_by` is either the issue ref or empty with a warning.
- Unit: reconciling a pending issue that already has `status:blocked` and `blocked-by:#123` (blocker open) ends with `status:blocked`, no `status:available`, and `publication:pending` removed.
- Regression: an unblocked task still gets `status:available`; a task with `blocked-by:tNNN` behaves as today.
- `shellcheck` on changed scripts.

title: t18578: perf(ci): remove duplicate serial ShellCheck pass from required Framework Validation critical path
body:
## Problem

PR time-to-merge is dominated by one required check. Across the 40 most recent merged PRs, `Framework Validation` was the last required check to finish in 37 of them (the other 3 were `ShellCheck (macos-latest)`). Merge lag after checks finish is usually 1–12 minutes. CI is the main bottleneck.

Evidence (40 recent completed `Code Quality Analysis` runs):

| Job | avg run | max run |
|-----|---------|---------|
| Framework Validation (required) | 440s | 534s |
| ShellCheck (ubuntu-latest) | 371s | 416s |
| ShellCheck (macos-latest) (required) | 336s | 414s |
| Complexity Analysis (required) | 164s | 198s |

Step timing for `Framework Validation` in run 36669233531: the `ShellCheck Lint` step took **532s**; the next largest step took 69s.

## Root cause

`.github/workflows/code-quality.yml` runs the same full-repository `shellcheck -S error` pass three times per PR (Framework Validation, ShellCheck ubuntu, ShellCheck macOS). Each pass starts one `shellcheck` process per file, one at a time, over every tracked `*.sh` file. The copy inside Framework Validation adds about 9 minutes to the required critical path. It uses the same file list (`lint_shell_files`) and the same severity as the `cross-platform-shellcheck` matrix job, so it adds no coverage.

## Fix

1. Remove the duplicate `ShellCheck Lint` step from the `framework-validation` job. The `cross-platform-shellcheck` matrix still enforces the same rule on Linux and macOS, and `ShellCheck (macos-latest)` remains a required check.
2. Make the `cross-platform-shellcheck` pass (and its macOS `/bin/bash -n` pass) run in parallel batches (`xargs -0 -n <batch> -P <cpus>`). ShellCheck finds `.shellcheckrc` per file, so batching does not change results. `linters-local-validators.sh` `run_shellcheck` already batches.

## Files

- `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml` (jobs `cross-platform-shellcheck` and `framework-validation`)

## Verification

- `actionlint` / workflow YAML parses; existing workflow contract tests (`.agents/scripts/tests/test-reusable-workflow-*.sh`) pass.
- On the PR: `ShellCheck (ubuntu-latest)` and `ShellCheck (macos-latest)` still pass and still fail on an injected error (checked locally with the same command against a temporary bad script). `Framework Validation` runtime drops by about 8–9 minutes.
- Compare the PR's required-check completion time with the 40-PR baseline above.

title: task-id guard flags a valid task ID followed by a sentence period as malformed
body:
## What

`task_identity_has_malformed_candidate` in `.agents/scripts/task-identity-lib.sh` (around line 190) flags a valid task ID followed by a sentence-ending period as malformed. The task-ID collision guard then blocks the commit with `__malformed__ — malformed task identity`.

## Reproduction (observed 2026-09-30, v3.37.34)

Commit body: `... to the PFT overlay, and splits point 5 into t112.` (t112 is a validly claimed ID.)

Result: `[task-id-guard][BLOCK] ... __malformed__ — malformed task identity`. Rewording to `into t112 (brief added)` passes.

## Cause

`candidate_ere` is `[tT][0123456789][[:alnum:].-]*`. It includes `.` in the continuation class, so the trailing sentence period becomes part of the candidate (`t112.`), which fails `task_identity_validate`. The design comment at line ~133 intentionally treats dots as non-boundaries to catch truncated IDs such as `t7.0`, but a dot followed by whitespace or end of text is ordinary punctuation.

## Suggested fix

Before validating, strip one trailing `.` from the candidate when it is followed by whitespace or end of text. Keep rejecting inner dots (`t7.0`, `t7.x`).

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/task-identity-lib.sh` (`task_identity_has_malformed_candidate`, and `task_identity_extract_first`/`extract_all` if they share the boundary)
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-task-identity-lib.sh` (add: `"split into t112."` is not malformed; `"t7.0 marker"` stays rejected)

## What

title: release: release-run-capture-authorization exits 1 on empty JSON and strands the lane reserved for 5 minutes
body:
## What (unconfirmed investigation)

The first `aidevops release patch 33136 incremental` run for v3.37.35 exited 1 after about 42s at resolver stage `release-run-capture-authorization`, with `unexpected end of JSON input`. No version files changed, but the lane stayed `reserved` with a dead executor. The same-source retry was refused until the lane was 5 minutes old. The next retry recovered the stale lane and published v3.37.35 (exit 8, then reconcile to `published`). GitHub API rate limits were healthy at the time.

The cost was a 5-minute stall in an interactive release and a misleading hard failure (exit 1) for what behaved like a transient empty read.

## Reproducer

Not yet reproducible on demand. Observed once on 2026-09-30 (source PR #33136, release PR #33176, tag v3.37.35).

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-helper.sh`

## How

1. Find the `release-run-capture-authorization` phase: `rg -n "release-run-capture-authorization" .agents/scripts/`.
2. Identify the `jq` or JSON parse that receives empty input: most likely a `gh api`/`gh run` read returning empty stdout on transient failure.
3. Treat an empty or unparseable read as indeterminate: bounded retry, then exit 8 (pending), not a terminal exit 1 that strands the lane in `reserved`. Keep lane fencing and the reconcile-only rule unchanged. Do not add a new override.
4. If the parse input cannot be identified, say so on this issue with the evidence gathered, rather than guessing.

## Acceptance

- An empty read in that phase no longer exits 1 with a raw `jq` parse error. It either retries successfully or exits 8 with the exact resume command.

title: fix(worktree-helper): add <branch> diverges from existing unmerged remote branch instead of checking it out
body:
## Problem

`worktree-helper.sh add <branch>` does not check out an existing, unmerged remote branch (for example, an open PR head). It creates a **new local branch from `origin/main`** that diverges from the remote, and prints only a warning:

```text
Stale remote branch detected: origin/bugfix/oauth-pool-add-console-tty (NOT merged)
Headless mode: proceeding without deleting (unmerged remote preserved)
New local branch will diverge from stale remote ref
Creating worktree with new branch '...' based on 'origin/main'...
branch '...' set up to track 'origin/main'.
```

Observed while taking over an open PR, #33055. `interactive-session-helper.sh claim` correctly said "continue branch '...' instead of taking over ownership". There was no helper path to create a linked worktree on that branch. Destructive `git reset --hard` is blocked by policy (correctly), so recovery required merging the PR head into the main-based branch by hand.

## Expected

When `origin/<branch>` exists and has an open PR, or is otherwise unmerged, `add` should create the worktree **on the remote head**: `git worktree add -b <branch> <path> origin/<branch>`, with the upstream set to `origin/<branch>`. An explicit `--base REF` should still override this. The "stale" delete prompt should apply only to remote branches that are already merged.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper.sh`: the `add` command and its stale-remote detection (search `Stale remote branch detected` and `New local branch will diverge`).
- Pattern: the existing `--base REF` handling in the same command.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper-add.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper-git.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worktree-helper-unmerged-remote.sh`

## Verification

- In a test repo, push branch `x` with one commit not on main, then run `worktree-helper.sh add x`. `git -C <wt> rev-parse HEAD` must equal `origin/x`, and `git status -sb` must show `...origin/x` with no divergence.
- A merged or absent remote branch must still be based on `origin/<default>` (unchanged behaviour).
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/worktree-helper.sh` is clean.

title: perf(ci): scope-gate heavy Code Quality jobs so version/docs-only PRs stop saturating runners
body:
## Problem

GitHub-hosted runner queue time is now the second PR bottleneck. It follows GH#33182 (PR #33185), which removed the duplicate serial ShellCheck pass from `Framework Validation`.

Evidence, collected 2026-09-30:

- Hourly average job queue time (started minus created) for `Code Quality Analysis`: 02h 24s, 03h 216s (max 1045s), 04h 135s (max 705s), 05h 260s (max 1226s).
- In a 35-minute window (04:59–05:34Z), 726 jobs executed. `Code Quality Analysis` used **40,249 of about 58,000 runner-seconds (~69%)** across 141 jobs. The next largest was Issue Sync at 3,039s. Peak was 45 concurrent jobs.
- A single PR head fans out to 51 Actions check runs (33 executed, 18 skipped).
- Release-preservation PRs (e.g. #33193, which changes version files only) run the full `Code Quality Analysis`. On #33193, `ShellCheck (macos-latest)` took 10m28s. Each release lane waits for that PR, so heavy CI on version-only PRs serializes releases.

## Root cause

`Code Quality Analysis` (`.github/workflows/code-quality.yml`) runs every full-repository job on every PR and every push to `main`. It never checks what changed. PRs that touch only version or changelog files, planning files, or docs still pay for full-repo ShellCheck on Linux and macOS, `Framework Validation`, Complexity, SonarCloud, and the rest.

## Proposed fix

Add a scope job to `code-quality.yml` and gate the heavy jobs with a job-level `if:`. A job skipped by `if:` reports a passing status to required checks. A workflow-level `paths:` filter does not, and would leave required checks stuck at "expected". Do not use `paths:`.

1. Add a `detect-scope` job, following the pattern in `.github/workflows/qlty-regression.yml` (`detect-scope`, `should_scan` output, `git diff --name-only BASE HEAD`). Output `shell=true` when any `*.sh`, `.shellcheckrc`, `.github/workflows/*`, or `.agents/scripts/**` file changed. Push events and unknown scope must fail open to `shell=true`.
2. Gate `cross-platform-shellcheck` on `needs.detect-scope.outputs.shell == 'true'`. Gate the other full-repo jobs the same way where the scope is provably irrelevant. Version-only release PRs (`VERSION`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `package.json`, `.agents/VERSION`, and similar) and docs/`todo/**`-only PRs should skip them.
3. Keep the required check names (`Framework Validation`, `ShellCheck (macos-latest)`, `Complexity Analysis`) unchanged. Verify that a skipped required job still satisfies branch protection, `pulse-merge-required-checks.sh`, and `full-loop-helper.sh wait-checks`. `pulse-merge-required-checks.sh` accepts `skipped` in several paths (around lines 585 and 973), but around line 545 it prefers the latest *executed* run for a family. Confirm that an exact-head skip is not blocked by that rule. See `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-required-checks-filter.sh`.

### Files Scope

- `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml`

## Verification

- `actionlint .github/workflows/code-quality.yml` is clean.
- A shell-touching PR still runs both ShellCheck legs and `Framework Validation` steps.
- A version-only or docs-only PR shows `ShellCheck (macos-latest)` as skipped. `full-loop-helper.sh wait-checks <PR>` and branch protection treat it as passing, and the PR merges.
- Re-measure runner-seconds by workflow over a 30–60 minute window (Actions API `runs/{id}/jobs`, `completed_at - started_at`) and compare with the 69% baseline above.
