title: Dependency Security: root override still pins fast-uri 3.1.7 (GHSA-hrr3-gc8f-f4qj needs 3.1.8)
body:
## What

Raise the root `fast-uri` override from `3.1.7` to `3.1.8` so `bun audit` (the required-looking but non-required `Dependency Security / audit` job) passes on `main` again.

## Why

`GHSA-hrr3-gc8f-f4qj` (moderate) affects `fast-uri >=3.0.0 <3.1.8`. PR #33180 (GH#33124) bumped `fast-uri` to `3.1.8` only in `.agents/package-lock.json` and `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/package-lock.json`. The root `package.json` `overrides` block still pins `3.1.7`, and root `bun.lock` follows it. `.github/workflows/dependency-security.yml:76` runs `bun audit` at the repository root, so the job has failed on every `main` push since 2026-09-30T05:00Z (run on `3a6a78364b`) and on release PR #33193.

Evidence (failing log excerpt, run 36673106317):

```text
fast-uri  >=3.0.0 <3.1.8
  ajv › fast-uri
  moderate: fast-uri vulnerable to inconsistent host case normalization via percent-encoded octets - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-hrr3-gc8f-f4qj
1 vulnerabilities (1 moderate)
```

## Reproducer

```bash
git grep -n '"fast-uri"' origin/main -- package.json bun.lock
# package.json:82  "fast-uri": "3.1.7",
# bun.lock:71      "fast-uri": "3.1.7",
# bun.lock:299     "fast-uri": ["fast-uri@3.1.7", ...]
bun audit   # at repo root → 1 vulnerabilities (1 moderate), exit 1
gh run list --repo marcusquinn/aidevops --workflow dependency-security.yml --branch main --limit 3
# 2026-09-30T05:00:13Z 3a6a78364b failure (previous two runs: success)
```

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:simple`. Exact version and integrity are already verified in-repo (`.agents/package-lock.json:37-40`); three literal replacements, trivially reversible.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: package.json:82` — override `"fast-uri": "3.1.7"` → `"3.1.8"`
- `EDIT: bun.lock:71` — overrides entry `"fast-uri": "3.1.7"` → `"3.1.8"`
- `EDIT: bun.lock:299` — package entry version and integrity

### Implementation Steps

1. `package.json`:

   oldString: `    "fast-uri": "3.1.7",`
   newString: `    "fast-uri": "3.1.8",`

2. `bun.lock` line 71 (overrides): same replacement as step 1.

title: planning-commit-helper.sh exits 1 silently on detached HEAD after printing 'Committing'
body:
## Problem

Run from a linked worktree on a detached HEAD, `planning-commit-helper.sh "plan: ..."` prints `Planning files to commit:` and `Committing: ...`, then exits 1. It prints no error, publishes nothing, and leaves the planning edit uncommitted. The output looks like success, so a caller can wrongly assume the TODO change was published.

Observed 2026-09-30 while marking t18578 done in a worktree created with `git worktree add --detach ... origin/main`. After I ran `git switch -c <branch>` in the same worktree, the helper worked (`AIDEVOPS_PLANNING_COMMIT_RESULT=pr`, PR #33200).

## Root cause

`.agents/scripts/planning-commit-helper.sh`, `commit_planning_files()`:

```bash
current_branch=$(git -C "$repo_root" symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null) || return 1
```

The failure is silenced (stderr goes to `/dev/null`) and nothing is logged. Also, `current_branch` is never read after this assignment.

## Fix

Choose one:

- Preferred: publication already runs through a temporary index against the remote default branch, so it may not need a local branch. If `current_branch` is unused, remove the check and confirm that `planning_publish` / `todo_commit_push` work from a detached HEAD.
- Otherwise: keep the check and add `log_error "Planning publication requires a named branch; detached HEAD is unsupported (git switch -c <branch>)"` before `return 1`.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/planning-commit-helper.sh`

Target: `commit_planning_files()`, around line 590.

## Verification

- In a linked worktree created with `git worktree add --detach <path> origin/main`, edit one TODO.md line and run `planning-commit-helper.sh "plan: test"`.
- Expect either a successful publication or a clear error, never a silent exit 1.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/planning-commit-helper.sh` is clean.

title: pulse dispatch: claim_snapshot unbound in _dedup_layer7_claim_lock blocks every dispatch since #33103
body:
## Observed

Since #33103 (GH#32638, merged 2026-09-29 23:13 UTC), every pulse dispatch on this runner fails before launch:

```text
pulse-dispatch-dedup-layers.sh: line 630: claim_snapshot: unbound variable
pulse-dispatch-dedup-layers.sh: line 631: _claim_started_ns: unbound variable
[pulse-wrapper] Stage failed: dispatch_candidate_<N> exited with 1
[pulse-wrapper] Dispatch_max: #<N> (...) pre-launch failure stage=dispatch_with_dedup rc=1 reason=unclassified_signal
```

- `pulse.log` has 35 occurrences across runtime bundles 3.37.32, 3.37.33 and 3.37.37, in several repos.
- The last successful `Dispatched worker PID` is before the first occurrence. No worker has launched on this runner since then (about eight hours).
- The error is classified as `unclassified_signal`, not a hard failure, so nothing alerts on it.

## Root cause

`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-dedup-layers.sh`: the #33103 hunk that declares the claim snapshot landed in the wrong function.

- `_dedup_layer5_dispatch_comment` (lines 336-341 on `main`) declares `local claim_snapshot` and `local _claim_started_ns` and runs `mktemp`. It never uses either variable, and it leaks one `dispatch-claim.XXXXXX` temp file per attempt.
- `_dedup_layer7_claim_lock` (lines 630-649) is the only function that uses them. Under `set -u` it aborts at the pre-check, so dispatch never reaches the claim.

## Fix

Move the six-line block (comment, `local claim_snapshot`, `mktemp`, `local _claim_started_ns`, `_ds_now_ns`) from `_dedup_layer5_dispatch_comment` into `_dedup_layer7_claim_lock`, inside the `if [[ -x "$dedup_helper" ]] ...` block and before `_precheck_output`. The existing `rm -f "$claim_snapshot"` calls in layer 7 already cover each exit path after the claim.

## Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-dedup-layers.sh`

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-dedup-layers.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-precreation-failure-skip.sh` (references `_dedup_layer7_claim_lock`)
- After deploy (`setup.sh --non-interactive`), `pulse.log` shows no `claim_snapshot: unbound variable` and shows `Dispatched worker PID` again.

Interactive fix in progress: the runner cannot dispatch a worker for this while dispatch itself is broken.

title: Bug: terminal-blocker circuit never trips for external-trigger waits because task revision tracks default-branch HEAD
body:
## What

The terminal-blocker circuit never trips for issues that wait on an external trigger (unclassified `reason=unknown`) in a high-velocity repo, so pulses on several runners redispatch the same no-op worker dozens of times a day.

## Evidence (observed 2026-09-30 by the daily pulse sweep)

- Issue #32876 ("Adopt Claude Haiku 5.5 ... when released") has an explicit trigger: *if the Haiku 5.5 ID is not published, leave the issue open and do nothing*. `opencode models anthropic` on 2026-09-30 still lists only `claude-haiku-4-5`.
- Its label timeline shows about 40 `status:available -> queued -> in-progress -> available` cycles between 2026-09-29T06:17Z and 17:20Z across three runners, with more attempts after that (CLAIM_RELEASED comments at 18:28Z, 19:56Z, 20:07Z, 00:01Z; dispatch at 04:44Z on 2026-09-30). Each attempt is `tier:thinking`.
- Every terminal-blocker observation has the same `blocker=6986da1ae19a0543f4b73332` but a different `revision=` (076dbc85..., 261d74cd..., 57e954f2..., fdcd2647...). The circuit requires two observations at the same revision, so it never opens.
- The runner-local integration-recovery queue carries the same request (`reason: missing_context`, "third consecutive attempt with unchanged external evidence").

## Root cause

`.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`:

- `terminal_blocker_capture_output()` (about line 155) accepts only `missing_files_scope`, `files_scope_excluded`, `target_code_blocker` and `permission_required`; anything else (including `missing_context` / an unmet external trigger) becomes `unknown`.
- `terminal_blocker_task_revision()` (about lines 219-245) hashes `{task, dependencies, target_revision}` for `unknown` and `target_code_blocker`, where `target_revision` is the default-branch HEAD from `_terminal_blocker_target_revision()`. On `marcusquinn/aidevops` the default branch moves every few minutes, so every attempt produces a new revision and the two-observation threshold is never reached.

## How (proposed)

1. Add an allowlisted class for an unmet external trigger/dependency (for example `external_trigger_pending`) to both `_terminal_blocker_reason()` (line 107 list) and the capture allowlist (line 155), and document it in the worker contract that emits `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON`.
2. For that class, compute the revision like `missing_files_scope`: hash of reason + title/body (+ dependency signature), **not** the target HEAD, so unrelated merges do not re-arm it. A brief edit or a trusted `terminal-blocker-circuit:retry` still re-arms.
3. Consider the same for `unknown`: fall back to a body+dependency hash once N observations share the same blocker fingerprint within a window, so an unclassified repeat cannot storm.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`
- `.agents/reference/worker-discipline.md` (Terminal-blocker recovery section: list the new class)
- worker contract text that lists allowed `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON` values (locate with `rg -n "TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON=" .agents/scripts --glob '!tests/*'`)

## Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh
```

Add a case: two `external_trigger_pending` observations with the same body but different default-branch HEADs must open the circuit; a body edit must re-arm it.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Repeated external-trigger blockers open the circuit after two observations regardless of default-branch movement.
- [ ] Brief edits and trusted retries still re-arm; permission blockers keep their current semantics.
- [ ] After deployment, #32876 stops cycling (label timeline shows no new dispatch after the circuit opens).

title: Design discussion: opt-in lifecycle checks for existing closeout review evidence
body:
# Design discussion: opt-in lifecycle checks for existing closeout review evidence

**Discussion only; not an implementation assignment.** Please retain a
`no-auto-dispatch` hold pending a maintainer decision on fit and scope. This
requests architectural feedback, not permission to change defaults, deploy a
plugin, enroll repositories, or bypass existing authority checks.

## Problem

An operator may want selected workflows to require current, accepted closeout
review evidence before being classified as successfully complete or merged,
without manually requesting reviews and supervising each repair.

Aidevops already has the review/repair policy, evidence bundling, CI and bot
gates. This is not a claim that those mechanisms are absent or broken. The
question is whether their existing review contract should support an optional,
runtime-neutral lifecycle prerequisite, including evidence produced through
operator customization, rather than a separate review framework.

A runtime-local hook can observe reviewer Tasks and block selected tool calls,
but it cannot by itself govern Pulse's separate shell merge process, an isolated
worker that does not load the hook, or an already-queued GitHub auto-merge. A
wrapper around a whole Pulse pass also does not revalidate each PR's exact head
at its final merge decision.

## Proposed solution for discussion

Extend or expose an existing lifecycle check only where a repository explicitly
opts in. Reuse `review-evidence-helper.sh` and `aidevops.review-evidence/v1`;
do not add a competing patch format, finding schema, or review policy.

The execution owner continues to gather evidence, assess findings, make justified
in-scope repairs, and re-review changed evidence under `review-core.md`. The
lifecycle consumer would check that the required evidence is present, current,
accepted, and bound to the actual operation. It would not call models, infer
acceptance, repair code, or dispatch a competing supervisor from a merge pass.

Potential responsibilities, subject to maintainer approval:

- Bind lifecycle metadata to the exact reviewed head/base, shared evidence
  digest, policy version, execution owner, target repository/PR when applicable,
  and freshness limit. Keep private identities outside the shared patch bundle.
- Validate producer provenance and owner disposition through a defined trust
  contract. A hand-written `CLEAN` object or successful child exit is not proof.
  For independent native reviews, validate policy-required runtime properties;
  equivalent exact-head bot evidence need not pretend to be a native model run.
- For enrolled paths, reject successful completion/readiness/merge when required
  evidence is missing, stale, blocked, uncertain, or unverifiable. Return the
  reason through existing ownership and checkpoint/continuation mechanisms.
- Recheck immediately before head-matched merge transport. Decide how local-only
  evidence interacts with queued/deferred native auto-merge before enrollment.
- Report unsupported runtimes/profiles explicitly; do not weaken isolation to
  load a plugin. Leave unenrolled behavior unchanged.

Completion here means the authoritative **success classification**, not making
it impossible for a failed/cancelled process to exit. A draft checkpoint or an
authorized handoff is not a false successful completion. Existing cancellation,
timeouts, ownership transitions, and repair routing must remain valid.

## Preserve existing framework policy

The proposal should follow the current shared review core, not impose the
prototype's stricter operator preferences as framework defaults:

- Low risk: direct inspection and repository checks, no second model by default.
  Medium risk: advisory review when useful. High/critical: independent review in
  addition to required tests. One reviewer by default; panels only when explicit
  or risk-justified. Extra operator requirements require explicit policy.
- Default closeout findings remain P0 only; wider priorities require explicit
  user intent or repository/risk policy. Keep the existing finding schema.
- Reuse equivalent clean evidence for an unchanged bundle, including eligible
  exact-head bot findings. A lifecycle check should not purchase another review
  for reassurance or wording.
- Preserve the pause after two review-triggered patch cycles; continue only when
  every remaining accepted finding is an in-scope blocker. Preserve scope-growth
  reclassification and critical exceptions from `review-core.md`.
- Model judgment owns defect validity, root cause, scope and disposition.
  Deterministic checks cover identity, freshness and required evidence, not code
  quality itself. Host completion never implies owner acceptance.
- Keep review subordinate to CI, author/issue authority, branch protection and
  existing merge rules. Passing this check grants no publication permission.

## Evidence and limits

A local synthetic OpenCode experiment used a deliberately flawed owner-only
predicate: a premature todo-completion call was rejected; a tool-free reviewer
identified the bypass; the owner independently reproduced and repaired it; four
behavioral probes passed; fresh routine/critical reviews passed; todo completion
then succeeded. Persisted native records verified parentage, requested/observed
model variants, bound payloads, terminal responses and zero reviewer tools.

This establishes a narrow producer/repair experiment, **not** an integrated Pulse
completion or merge gate, a portable trusted receipt format, or a measured
production quality improvement. Two reviewers were an explicit test policy, not
a proposed new default. Synthetic checks do not prove cross-runtime coverage.

There is also an unpublished local integration sketch. It is not an implementation
being offered for acceptance and should not determine the upstream architecture.
Further framework integration is deferred pending this design discussion.

## Alternatives considered and customization boundary

- **Existing review instructions only:** preserve the current low-overhead
  approach; may be sufficient. Is there already a supported way to require its
  accepted evidence at the relevant lifecycle boundaries?
- **Operator-owned runtime plugin or custom wrapper:** appropriate for private
  models and stricter policy; survives updates when installed in supported
  operator locations. Its process scope does not establish final per-PR coverage.
- **Required GitHub checks/rules:** potentially stronger for merges by other
  actors, but require repository authority and a trustworthy publisher; they do
  not establish local worker success classification. No GitHub-wide protection
  is claimed for a local gate.
- **Editing deployed framework scripts:** not an update-safe solution and not
  requested. Nor is a mandatory global review panel or second scheduler.

No request is made to bundle, support, or test a private third-party plugin in
aidevops. Any framework-owned contract and its own tests would need maintainer
approval; external implementations remain their operators' responsibility.
Local evidence shares the operator's OS-user trust boundary, not a new security
sandbox against that same user's malicious processes.

## Candidate code context, not a write assignment

Paths were checked against upstream `main` during preparation:

- Reference patterns: `.agents/reference/review-core.md`,
  `.agents/scripts/review-evidence-helper.sh`, and
  `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/objective-receipt-tool.mjs` (explicit
  acceptance, not a substitute for code-review disposition).
- Possible lifecycle consumers: `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh`,
  `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`, `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh`,
  and `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh`.
- Worker success classification: investigate
  `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh` and its owning call chain; the
  exact insertion point and any new adapter paths are deliberately undecided.
- Extension documentation: `.agents/reference/customization.md`.

If approved, use the existing scoped evidence/worker/merge tests, starting with
`.agents/scripts/tests/test-review-evidence-helper.sh`, and changed-file lint.
Qualify a real supported owner cycle: defect -> verified finding -> in-scope
repair -> changed evidence -> accepted review -> permitted lifecycle transition.
Negative cases must cover absent/forged provenance, wrong target/head/base or
policy, expiration, review failure, cancellation/restart, concurrent head change,
unavailable verifiers, and queued auto-merge. Verify unchanged unenrolled behavior
and reuse without extra model calls. The supported runtime matrix must be agreed
before claiming coverage; no new broad test infrastructure is proposed here.

## Related work and questions for maintainers

- #28632 already unified evidence collection and review policy adapters. This
  proposal should consume that work, not recreate it.
- #32495 added explicit parent acceptance reminders (merged via #32514), without
  inferring acceptance from child completion. That is relevant provenance work,
  not by itself a per-PR code-review lifecycle gate.

Searches of open/closed issues and PRs for independent review, review gates,
review evidence, enforcement and closeout found those related efforts, but no
exact match for this opt-in lifecycle question. This is a bounded search, not a
claim that no other relevant design exists.

1. Is this a framework extension worth supporting, or should the full requirement
   remain operator customization? Is there an existing supported route we missed?
2. If in scope, should the first increment be a merge-only evidence check, with
   worker success classification considered separately?
3. Which existing policy/configuration and evidence/acceptance structures should
   own enrollment, disposition, provenance and equivalence? No new schema or
   configuration key is presumed approved.
4. Which runtimes, merge paths and queued-auto-merge behavior should be supported
   first, and what evidence would justify broader rollout?

## Environment and scope

- Current preparation diagnostics: aidevops 3.37.37, OpenCode, macOS 26.6.2.
- Synthetic runtime qualification used OpenCode 1.18.33; this does not qualify V2
  or other runtimes.
- Upstream reference point checked during preparation:
  `4fa83818ba4190aa090e7197a965f8a16c97f74a`.
- Publication is for discussion only. Implementation, release and live repository

title: gh_create_issue scope rejection prints a WARN, never says the issue was not created, and contradicts scope_hint
body:
## Problem

When `_gh_ci_validate_dispatch_scope` in `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-create.sh` rejects an auto-dispatch body at line 307, it prints only:

> [WARN] auto-dispatch implementation brief requires canonical ##/### Files Scope with EDIT/NEW paths; review legacy Files declarations before publication

and returns 1, so `gh_create_issue` (line 638) creates nothing. Observed via `gh-write-helper.sh issue create`: the output contained the warning and no issue URL. Two problems:

1. The message is a warning and never says the issue was **not created**. An agent can easily take it as advisory and assume the issue exists.
2. It points at the wrong fix. The body already had a `## Files Scope` section with `- EDIT: \`path\`` lines. What failed was trailing prose after the path on the same line (`- EDIT: \`path\` (worker-guidance line ...)`). The same function's `scope_hint` (line 293) says a different thing again: bare `- \`path\`` lines, "no prefix, nothing after it". Yet `- EDIT: \`path\`` lines with nothing after them passed in a sibling issue created minutes earlier.

## Fix

- Line 307: use `print_error`, say "auto-dispatch issue not created", and reuse `scope_hint` so both rejection paths describe one accepted line shape. Mention that text after the path is not allowed.
- Make `scope_hint` consistent with what `_brief_files_scope_has_path` actually accepts (optional `EDIT:`/`NEW:` prefix, nothing after the path).

## Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-create.sh`

## Verification

- `gh_create_issue --dry-run`-equivalent test, or the existing wrapper tests (`.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-wrapper-guard.sh`), still pass.
- A body whose Files Scope line has trailing prose prints an error containing "not created" and the accepted line shape, and exits non-zero.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-create.sh` is clean.

title: aidevops_bounded_operation rejects every cwd when the OpenCode session root is a non-repo parent directory
body:
## What

`aidevops_bounded_operation` (OpenCode plugin) cannot run any command when the OpenCode session was started in a directory that is not itself a Git repository. A common case is an organisation parent folder (the `<owner>/<repo>` layout from `reference/repo-organization.md`) that holds canonical repos. Every `start` call then fails:

```
{"schema":"aidevops.interactive-operation/v1","error":"Operation workdir: the session project root is not an existing Git worktree root."}
```

## Observed

- Session root: an organisation parent directory. It is not a Git repo; it holds canonical checkouts as `<owner>/<repo>`.
- Requested `cwd`: an existing registered linked worktree for one of those child repos, under the standard worktree base directory.
- A full-loop resumed an existing PR branch worktree that an earlier session had created. I started vitest, typecheck and `drizzle-kit check`, all three were rejected, and I had to fall back to foreground Bash with long timeouts. The `wait-checks` calls in the same session also went through Bash, and each timed out at 20–30 minutes before I reran it.

## Root cause (from reading deployed code)

- `bounded-interactive-operation.mjs` `resolveCwd` (around lines 60–62) accepts `cwd` only when it is inside `projectRoot`. Otherwise it calls `resolveSessionOwnedWorktreeRoot`.
- `gpt-image-worktree.mjs` `resolveSessionOwnedWorktreeRoot` (line 73) runs `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` on the session root. It throws `the session project root is not an existing Git worktree root` whenever the startup directory is not a repo, before it ever inspects the requested worktree.
- It then requires the same `--git-common-dir` as the startup root and `worktree-helper.sh registry verify-owner <root> <sessionID>`. So even a session started inside the canonical repo would probably reject a worktree an earlier session created, which is the resume-an-existing-PR case. I have not verified this path; please confirm it.

## Expected

Starting a session from a directory that holds several repos is a normal layout. The bounded-operation tool should accept a registered linked worktree whose canonical repo lies under the session root, or that is otherwise tied to a repo registered in `repos.json`. It must keep its current safety properties: no symlinks, a linked worktree rather than the canonical checkout, and repo identity bound to a registered repo.

## How (suggested)

1. In `resolveSessionOwnedWorktreeRoot`, when the startup root is not a Git repo, resolve the requested worktree's `--git-common-dir`. Accept it if the canonical checkout of that common dir lies within the startup root, or is registered in `repos.json`. Otherwise fail closed with a specific message that names the fix.
2. Decide the ownership policy for resuming an existing PR worktree that an earlier session created. Options: let `verify-owner` accept the interactive claim's worktree, or offer an explicit, audited adopt step in the worktree registry. Today the only path left is Bash fallback, which loses the bounded/background behaviour.
3. Make the error say what to do, for example "start the session inside the repo, or pass a worktree registered to this session".

The worktree resolver is shared with `gpt_image_generate`, so check both callers.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/gpt-image-worktree.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-interactive-operation.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs`
- `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper.sh`

## Verification

- Extend `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs` with these cases:
  - session root is a non-repo parent directory, `cwd` is a registered linked worktree of a child repo → accepted;
  - `cwd` belongs to an unrelated repo → rejected;
  - `cwd` is a canonical checkout → rejected;
  - `cwd` is a symlink → rejected.
- Manual: open OpenCode in an organisation parent directory, create a worktree for a child repo, run `aidevops_bounded_operation start` with that `cwd`, and confirm it runs.
<!-- aidevops:origin:interactive -->
<!-- aidevops:sig -->

title: feat(pulse): surface stranded interactive draft PRs (green checks, claim owner gone)
body:
## Problem

A finished fix can stall indefinitely when an interactive session opens a **draft** PR with all required checks passing and then ends without marking it ready. Every automated path skips it:

- Interactive `commit-and-pr` creates PRs as drafts by default (`workflows/full-loop.md` step 4.2), so readiness depends on the originating session.
- `pulse-merge-stuck.sh` skips drafts unconditionally (`:209-210` in the stuck classifier, `:259`, and the `.isDraft == false` filter around `:1517`). The PR never shows up as stuck.
- The linked issue keeps `status:claimed` plus the assignee, so pulse dispatch treats it as in flight. `interactive-session-helper.sh scan-stale` / `release-if-dead` fail closed for **cross-host** claims (the claim came from a different machine), so nothing releases it.

Observed: #33054 / PR #33055 sat as a clean, mergeable, fully passing draft for about 12 hours until a maintainer noticed and took it over by hand.

## Expected

Pulse finds **stranded interactive drafts** and brings them to a human. It does not auto-ready them, because readiness is the author's decision.

A stranded interactive draft is an open PR where all of the following hold:
- `isDraft == true` and the PR has `origin:interactive`;
- all required checks on the current head are terminal-success;
- the head commit and last PR activity are older than a configurable threshold (default 12h);
- the linked issue (via `closingIssuesReferences`) is open and still claimed (`status:claimed` / `status:in-review` with an assignee);
- the PR has no `hold-for-review` or `no-auto-dispatch`.

Action (idempotent, one per head SHA):
1. Post a single marker-tagged comment (for example `<!-- aidevops:stranded-draft:<head_sha> -->`) that mentions the PR author. It states that the PR is green and waiting on `gh pr ready`, or on a maintainer takeover via `/full-loop <issue URL>`.
2. List it in the existing stuck-PR / maintainer health digest that `pulse-merge-stuck.sh` produces, so it is visible without opening GitHub.

Never convert to ready, merge, unassign, or post again for an unchanged head.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-stuck.sh`: add a separate stranded-draft classifier next to the existing stuck classifier. Keep the current draft skip for the stuck/merge path. Reuse the PR field list at `:142` (`isDraft,labels,author,updatedAt,headRefOid`) and the digest section around `:1281`.
- Reference pattern for idempotent marker comments: search `rg -n "<!-- aidevops:" .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-*.sh`.
- Threshold config: follow the existing pulse env/config knob conventions in the same file.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-stuck.sh`
- `.agents/configs/pulse-merge-stuck.conf`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-stuck.sh`

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-stuck.sh` is clean.
- Existing pulse-merge tests pass (`rg --files .agents/scripts/tests | rg pulse-merge`).
- Dry run against the live repo: a draft `origin:interactive` PR with green required checks, older than the threshold, is reported exactly once. Re-running without a new head posts nothing. Non-draft, held, or failing-check PRs are not reported.
<!-- aidevops:origin:interactive -->

title: fix(release): successful preservation fallback still logs a Runtime bundle convergence ERROR
body:
## What

A successful post-release deploy logs a stray `[ERROR]` line. During the v3.37.37 release (`aidevops release reconcile 33189`, 2026-09-30), the output contained:

```text
[ERROR] Runtime bundle convergence failed: active realpath bundle ID does not identify release commit dce390236604
[SUCCESS] Post-release aidevops runtime already contains release dce390236604 through validated preservation merge e29f87a70714 (verified no-op)
```

The release finished correctly: v3.37.37 was published, postflight passed, and the deployed `VERSION` is 3.37.37. The `ERROR` line is a false alarm. Operators and agents then have to investigate it, and log-scanning diagnostics may count it as a real failure.

## Root cause

`_verify_post_deploy_runtime_convergence` in `.agents/scripts/version-manager-release.sh` (around line 951) first calls `verify_aidevops_runtime_bundle_convergence`, which is the exact-tag check. Only when that fails does it try `_verify_active_release_preservation_merge`, which accepts a validated descendant runtime. The exact-tag verifier in `.agents/scripts/runtime-bundle-verifier.sh` reports every failure through `_runtime_bundle_verify_emit_error` (around line 15). That function always calls `print_error` or writes `ERROR:` to stderr. So the expected failure of the first attempt is printed as an error, even when the fallback then accepts the runtime.

`run_post_release_agent_sync` (around line 1009) already checks the preservation path *before* deploying. The problem is only on the post-deploy path.

## How to fix

1. In `runtime-bundle-verifier.sh`, make error output suppressible. Recommended: record the message in a global such as `_AIDEVOPS_RUNTIME_VERIFY_LAST_ERROR` and print it only when a caller-scoped quiet flag is unset, for example `local _AIDEVOPS_RUNTIME_VERIFY_QUIET=1` in the caller. Default behaviour must stay unchanged for other callers, including `aidevops update` (see `.agents/scripts/tests/test-aidevops-update-transaction.sh:221`, which asserts on the message text).
2. In `_verify_post_deploy_runtime_convergence`, call the exact verifier in quiet mode. If the preservation fallback also fails (the `print_error ... did not converge` branch), print the saved exact-verifier reason first so the real failure diagnostics are kept.
3. Do not weaken any convergence checks. This change affects log output only.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/runtime-bundle-verifier.sh` (`_runtime_bundle_verify_emit_error`)
- `.agents/scripts/version-manager-release.sh` (`_verify_post_deploy_runtime_convergence`)

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/runtime-bundle-verifier.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/version-manager-release.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-version-manager-protected-publication.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-agent-auto-sync.sh`

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/runtime-bundle-verifier.sh .agents/scripts/version-manager-release.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-version-manager-protected-publication.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-aidevops-update-transaction.sh
```

Acceptance:

- When the preservation fallback succeeds, no `Runtime bundle convergence failed` line is printed.
- When both checks fail, the exact-verifier reason is still printed next to `runtime bundle provenance did not converge`.

Related history: #32971, #32656, #31533 (convergence fallbacks were added there; this is the leftover log noise).

title: release: competing authorized release should finalize a published lane whose executor is dead
body:
## What

When `aidevops release <patch|minor|major> <PR>` finds another source's lane still `active`, `_full_loop_release_guard_competing_lane()` currently refuses the new release (exit 75) and prints `aidevops release reconcile <other-PR>`. That is correct while the other release is still running, but not when that release has already **published on every channel** and its executor is **dead**. The only remaining step then is finalization (exact-tag deploy and terminal receipt). The competing start should do that finalization through the existing reconcile path, then continue its own release. It should not strand the lane until a human notices.

## Why

Observed on 2026-09-30:

- Source PR #33136 released `v3.37.35`. GitHub, npm and Homebrew all published by 05:05Z. The owning session read `RELEASE_REMOTE_STATE=published` from `status` and exited (see #33192 for its earlier transient failure). It never finalized the lane.
- The lane stayed `{"active":true,"source_pr":33136,"phase":"remote-publication","tag":"v3.37.35","terminal_receipt":null}` with `RELEASE_EXECUTOR={"state":"dead","reason":"process-absent"}` for about an hour.
- The next authorized release (`aidevops release patch 33177 incremental`) was refused with `ACTIVE_RELEASE_LANE source_pr=33136 …`. A human-directed session had to run `aidevops release reconcile 33136` by hand. That finalized the lane (`terminal_receipt=published`). Only then did `v3.37.36` proceed.
- By contrast, `v3.37.37` (source #33189) finalized itself within about 6 minutes, because its owning session ran reconcile. The gap only appears when the owner exits after publication.

`reference/release-lane-coordination.md` intentionally says "publication phases … are not automatically released", and this issue keeps that rule. The proposal does not *release* the lane. It *completes* it through the same verified reconcile path a human would run, triggered by an already-authorized competing release. No new authority is created.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `aidevops release patch 33177 incremental` (run from a linked aidevops worktree on 2026-09-30, while #33136's lane was published but unfinalized)

**Actual output:**

```text
ACTIVE_RELEASE_LANE source_pr=33136 phase=remote-publication tag=v3.37.35
RELEASE_EXECUTOR={"state": "dead", "reason": "process-absent"}
Inspect/resume publication: aidevops release reconcile 33136
```

(exit 75, no version bump). At the same moment `aidevops release status 33136` reported:

```text
RELEASE_LANE={"active":true,"source_pr":33136,"phase":"remote-publication","tag":"v3.37.35","updated_at":"2026-09-30T05:07:30Z","terminal_receipt":null}
RELEASE_EXECUTOR={"state": "dead", "reason": "process-absent"}
RELEASE_RECEIPT=missing
GITHUB_RELEASE=v3.37.35
NPM_VERSION=3.37.35
HOMEBREW_VERSION=3.37.35
RELEASE_REMOTE_STATE=published
```

**Expected:** the competing authorized release finalizes #33136's lane through the existing reconcile path (as the manual `aidevops release reconcile 33136` then did, giving `terminal_receipt=published`) and continues its own release.

Regression fixture shape: a lane JSON with a different `source_pr`, `phase` of `remote-publication` or `exact-tag-deployment`, `terminal_receipt=null`, executor observation `dead`, and remote inspection reporting published channels for its tag.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:thinking`. It changes a `#aidevops:trust-boundary` path in release publication (lane ownership and deployment side effects). The authority-binding decisions below must be preserved exactly; the worker must also decide how to handle a partially failing finalization.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/full-loop-release-helper.sh:638-663` (`_full_loop_release_guard_competing_lane`): add a finalize-then-continue branch before the `ACTIVE_RELEASE_LANE` refusal.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/release-lane-liveness.sh` (optional): a predicate `_release_lane_published_owner_dead` beside `_release_lane_abandoned_reservation` (same `#aidevops:trust-boundary` style), if that keeps the guard function small.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-helper.sh`: extend the existing competing-lane cases (around `:726`, which already overrides `_full_loop_release_guard_competing_lane`).
- `EDIT: .agents/reference/release-lane-coordination.md`: document the competing-start finalization next to the "Age alone never unlocks a lane" paragraph (~`:99-108`).

### Implementation Steps

1. **Eligibility predicate** (all must hold; any uncertainty keeps today's refusal, exit 75):
   - the lane is `active`, has a different `source_pr`, a non-null `tag`, and `terminal_receipt == null`;
   - `phase` is `remote-publication` or `exact-tag-deployment`;
   - `_release_lane_executor_observe` reports `state == "dead"`. `unknown` is not dead.
   - `_full_loop_release_inspect_remote` (in `full-loop-release-reconcile.sh`) verifies the lane's tag is published on GitHub Release, npm and Homebrew.
2. **Finalize via the existing path only.** Invoke the same code that `aidevops release reconcile <lane-source-PR>` runs (`_full_loop_release_existing_with_lane reconcile <lane_pr>`), in the same process. That path already binds to the lane's **persisted** authorization manifest (`_full_loop_release_validate_published_reconciliation_intent`), verifies tag provenance, and uses CAS lane writes. Do not add a new trust flag or skip any of its checks.
3. **Continue or refuse:** re-read the lane (`release_lane_read`).
   - If it is now inactive with a terminal receipt, print `RELEASE_LANE_FINALIZED source_pr=<N> tag=<T> receipt=<R>` and return 0 so `_full_loop_release_start_new` proceeds with the new reservation.
   - Otherwise, or if reconcile exits 8 or fails, print the existing `ACTIVE_RELEASE_LANE` and liveness report and return 75. Never bump, and never retry more than once.
4. Keep `release_lane_liveness_report`'s status wording unchanged apart from, optionally, noting that a competing authorized release will finalize a published and dead lane automatically.
5. `shellcheck` the changed scripts; run the tests listed under Verification.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** the lane owner might revive, or another session might be reconciling at the same moment. Rely on the existing CAS lane writes; a lost CAS must result in refusal (75), never a forced write.
- **Authority:** the finalized source's authorization comes from its persisted manifest; the new source's authorization is unchanged. Headless publication guards (trusted priority/scope) must apply exactly as they do today. If a headless caller cannot reconcile, it refuses.
- **Deployment ordering:** finalization deploys the older exact tag locally, then the new release deploys the newer tag. That is the same outcome as today's manual sequence.
- **Idempotency/retry:** a second run finds the lane already inactive, so it takes the normal path.
- **Partial failure:** the reconcile may publish the receipt but fail deployment (exit 76 stale-runtime deferral). Treat this as not finalized: refuse with 75 and leave the reconcile's own deferral state intact.

### Complexity Impact

- `_full_loop_release_guard_competing_lane` is currently 26 lines. Keep the new logic in a helper (for example `_full_loop_release_finalize_published_competing_lane`) so the guard stays under 40 lines.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/full-loop-release-helper.sh .agents/scripts/release-lane-liveness.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-helper.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-release-lane-liveness.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-release-lane.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-reconcile.sh
```

- **Surface mapping:** the helper test covers competing-lane branches (eligible leads to finalize-and-continue; live, unknown, unpublished, or failed reconcile each lead to 75). The liveness and lane tests cover the predicate and CAS behaviour. The reconcile test proves the reused path is unchanged.
- **Broad verification trigger:** not required. This is a scoped change to the release helper.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/release-lane-liveness.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-helper.sh`
- `.agents/reference/release-lane-coordination.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

title: gh-checks-wait-helper: warn that review-bot pass on a draft PR may mean the bot skipped
body:
## Observed

Interactive `gh-write-helper.sh pr create` defaults PRs to draft (`_gh_create_pr_should_default_draft` in `shared-gh-wrappers-create.sh`), as documented in `workflows/pr.md`. Running `gh-checks-wait-helper.sh wait <PR> --all` on that draft reported:

```
CodeRabbit: pass
...
PASS: all checks completed in 120s (pass=4)
```

CodeRabbit had in fact skipped the PR ("Draft PR not reviewed" comment). Its status check is green whether it reviewed or skipped, so the helper's PASS looks like a completed review. The review only ran after `gh pr ready`, and it raised two findings that needed code changes. `full-loop-helper.sh merge` refuses drafts, so this did not cause a bad merge. It did cost a wrong "reviewed" signal and a second check cycle.

## Proposed change

In `.agents/scripts/gh-checks-wait-helper.sh`, read `isDraft` with the initial PR state. When it is true:
- print one line: `NOTE: PR is draft; review bots (e.g. CodeRabbit) may skip drafts and still report pass. Run gh pr ready, then wait again for review evidence.`
- keep the exit code unchanged (checks did pass), so existing callers are unaffected.

Optional: in `workflows/full-loop.md`, next to the merge step description, add one sentence saying that check results on a draft are not review evidence.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/gh-checks-wait-helper.sh`: initial state read and output.
- `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md`: one sentence near the `full-loop-helper.sh merge` description (optional).

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/gh-checks-wait-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-checks-wait-helper.sh`
- `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md`

## Verification

- ShellCheck clean on the helper.
- Run `gh-checks-wait-helper.sh wait <draft PR>` against a draft PR: the NOTE line prints once and the exit code is unchanged.
- Run it against a non-draft PR: no NOTE line.

title: Stale recovery supersedes live interactive claims after 600s without GitHub activity
body:
## What

Stale-assignment recovery should not supersede a live interactive claim (`interactive-session-helper.sh claim`) just because its issue has had no GitHub activity for 600 s.

## Observed (aidevops v3.37.30 interactive session, pulse on another maintainer machine at v3.37.37)

1. An interactive session claimed a managed-repo issue at 08:41 UTC (`status:claimed`, self-assigned). It captured pages, wrote a spec and built an artifact locally, all without GitHub writes, then waited about two hours for the user to unlock GPG.
2. At 10:43 UTC the pulse posted "Stale assignment recovered: dispatch claim 7300s old, last activity 7300s old (threshold=600s)" and removed the assignee.
3. At 10:46 UTC it dispatched a headless worker on another machine for the same issue. The worker exited `blocked` at 11:06 UTC.
4. At 13:26 UTC stale recovery escalated. At 13:29 UTC it filed a consolidation task that would have closed the parent issue as "not planned", while the interactive session was about to publish.
5. The interactive session restored its claim, published, closed the parent and closed the consolidation task manually.

## Why

Interactive claims represent a human-attended session whose work is mostly local (capture, builds, dry runs) and can legitimately go hours without GitHub activity. Superseding it duplicates work, risks two writers on the same live target, and can close the issue under the active session.

## How

- In the stale-recovery path, treat an issue carrying an interactive claim marker (`aidevops-interactive-claim/v1` comment plus `status:claimed` with the claimant as sole assignee) as live for a much longer window (hours) or until the claim is explicitly released.
- Alternatively, let `interactive-session-helper.sh` post or refresh a lightweight heartbeat that stale recovery honours, and have it warn when the heartbeat is older than the threshold.
- Do not file consolidation tasks for issues whose only "stale" signal is an interactive claim without activity.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-stale.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-stale-recovery-age-floor.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-stale-recovery-escalation.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An interactively claimed issue with no GitHub activity for 2 h is not unassigned or redispatched.
- [ ] Headless worker claims keep the current 600 s behaviour.
- [ ] A released or abandoned interactive claim (explicit release, or past the extended window) is still recovered.

title: aidevops secret wrapper should exit non-zero when gopass/GPG is locked instead of hanging or running with an empty environment
body:
## What

`aidevops secret NAME... -- <command>` should fail closed when gopass/GPG cannot decrypt a requested secret, instead of hanging silently or running the command without the variables.

## Observed (aidevops v3.37.30, OpenCode, Linux, gopass with a GPG key whose passphrase cache had expired)

1. With the GPG key not cached (`gpg-connect-agent "keyinfo --list" /bye` shows no cached flag), `aidevops secret A B C -- <command>` produced no output and hung until an outer 30-60 s timeout. No prompt or error reached the non-TTY agent shell.
2. In one run, shortly after the passphrase cache expired, the wrapped command ran but all three requested variables were absent from its environment. A downstream runner then failed with its own "credentials are required" error. The wrapper exited without reporting that decryption failed.
3. After the user unlocked the key in a terminal, the same command injected all variables correctly.

## Why

Agents treat the wrapper as the only credential path. A silent hang looks like a stuck tool, and running the command with an empty environment defers the failure to the consumer, which may behave differently without credentials (for example, fall back to an unauthenticated path).

## How

- In the `aidevops secret` inject path, check each requested name after decryption. If any is empty or missing, exit non-zero before exec with `secret NAME unavailable: gopass/GPG locked or entry missing`, never printing values.
- Before decrypting in non-interactive mode, probe the agent (for example `gpg-connect-agent` keyinfo, or `gopass` with a no-prompt option) and fail fast with an unlock hint instead of waiting for pinentry.
- Optionally print a hint about `default-cache-ttl` / `max-cache-ttl` in `gpg-agent.conf` for long headless sessions.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-secret-helper.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With a locked key, the command exits non-zero within a few seconds with an unlock hint and never runs the wrapped command.
- [ ] With one requested name missing, the command exits non-zero and names the missing secret.
- [ ] With an unlocked key, behaviour is unchanged.

title: consolidation-task: merge thread on #32876 into single spec
body:
## Consolidation target: #32876

**Parent issue:** #32876 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`
**Parent title:** Adopt Claude Haiku 5.5 as the Anthropic simple-tier model when released
**Parent labels:** `enhancement,status:available,tier:thinking,origin:interactive,consolidation-in-progress`

> You do **NOT** need to read #32876. Everything required is inlined below.
> Reading the parent wastes the token budget and is explicitly disallowed for this task.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `~/.aidevops/agents/templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `### Files Scope` — the successor's write surface, one repo-relative path per line and nothing else on the line (`- EDIT: path/to/file` or `- NEW: path/to/file`). Carry over the parent's scope when present. Read-only references belong in `## How`, not here. The pulse holds `auto-dispatch` briefs whose scope fails `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check`, so prose after a path makes the successor undispatchable.
   - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #32876 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`

3. **File the new consolidated issue:**

```bash
gh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,auto-dispatch,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body "<merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Without it, the issue is born `origin:interactive` (raw `gh issue create` has no origin auto-detection), which triggers the GH#18352 dispatch-dedup block and drains the queue.

**Dispatch handoff:** `auto-dispatch` is also mandatory. The consolidated successor marker and this explicit handoff must both be present before `_has_consolidated_label` permits implementation dispatch.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close the parent #32876:**

```bash
gh issue comment 32876 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 32876 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 32876 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
```

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #32876 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @marcusquinn @vladimirdulov."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- **Do NOT read #32876** — it is inlined below. Reading it wastes the token budget.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @marcusquinn @vladimirdulov

## Parent body (verbatim)

## What

Adopt Claude Haiku 5.5 as the Anthropic `simple`-tier model when it is released, following the same pattern as the Sonnet 5.5 adoption (#32848, v3.37.21).

## Why

Anthropic's Sonnet 5.5 launch page (anthropic.com/claude-sonnet-5-5, 2026-09-28) said Haiku 5.5 would arrive in the "coming weeks". The `simple` tier still falls back to `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5`.

2. Add catalog entries alongside the old ones: `model-pricing.json` (specific key before the generic `haiku-4`; bump the pricing version if rates change), `model-limits.mjs`, CLI names in `config-hook.mjs`, aliases in `claude-proxy-context.mjs`, and `compare-models-helper.sh`.

title: fix(dispatch): let workers own Files Scope discovery instead of holding trusted unscoped briefs as status:blocked
body:
## What

Stop parking trusted-author auto-dispatch briefs as `status:blocked` (`missing_files_scope`, owner=brief-author) when the pulse cannot derive a canonical Files Scope. Dispatch them instead, and make the worker's first step scope discovery: record a canonical `### Files Scope` in the issue body through the signed write wrapper before editing, then continue.

## Why

Since GH#32531 (2026-09-27) the pre-claim gate holds any auto-dispatch brief without a canonical Files Scope until the brief author edits it. The authors are AI sessions that have already ended, so nobody comes back. On 2026-09-30, 10 of the 14 open `status:blocked` issues carried the `aidevops:brief-hold reason=missing_files_scope` marker (#33125 #33152 #33194 #33229 #33230 #33232 #33234 #33235 #33242). Creation-time gates only cover some entry points (the `gh_create_issue` PATH shim and interactive `claim-task-id.sh`). Library callers, runners on older versions and raw `gh` bypass them. Choosing files is routine analysis an AI worker can do, and `reference/worker-discipline.md` "Integration scope recovery" already lets workers persist scope corrections.

## How

- `pulse-dispatch-core.sh` `_dispatch_preclaim_brief_scope_verdict`: after the trust check and the self-heal attempt, dispatch (return 0) instead of holding. Keep the hold as an opt-out (`AIDEVOPS_BRIEF_SCOPE_WORKER_DISCOVERY=0`).
- `pulse-dispatch-brief-scope.sh` `_release_repaired_brief_hold`: also release existing trusted holds whose latest blocker is still the brief hold, so the current backlog flows without body edits.
- Worker contract (`headless-runtime-lib.sh`, `pulse-dispatch-worker-prompt.sh`) and `reference/worker-discipline.md`: a missing scope means scope discovery first. `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON=missing_files_scope` applies only when the scope cannot be persisted.
- Update `workflows/brief.md` section 6 and the creation-time messages so they no longer claim the pulse will hold the issue.

title: fix(pulse): blocked-status refresh and brief-hold release starved by cycle budget
body:
## What

Blocked-status maintenance stages (`build_dependency_graph_cache`, `refresh_blocked_status_from_graph`, `release_repaired_brief_holds`) are starved by the pulse cycle budget. They run late in `_pulse_run_deterministic_pipeline` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`), after preflight, prefetch (~340-460s) and dirty-PR sweep (~250-310s). `_pulse_stage_cycle_timeout` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-watchdog.sh`) then defers them with `Stage deferred: <stage> cycle budget exhausted`.

Evidence (local pulse log, 2026-09-29 → 2026-09-30):

- The last completed `build_dependency_graph_cache` was on 2026-09-29 07:16; `dep-graph-cache.json` mtime has not changed since.
- The three stages logged `cycle budget exhausted` in every full cycle since then (8+ consecutive cycles).
- Result: issues whose blockers closed, and `missing_files_scope` holds whose briefs were repaired (e.g. #33235, #33234, #33232, #33230, #33229, #33194, #33152, #33125), stay `status:blocked` indefinitely even though GH#32689 / GH#33243 added automatic release.

## Why

Hold release and blocker refresh are the only automatic path back to `status:available`. When they starve, blocked counts grow monotonically and look like new human-action blockers.

## How

- Add a starvation catch-up to the async post-dispatch housekeeping lane (`_pulse_run_post_dispatch_housekeeping_stages` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`, t3055). That lane runs with `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_STAGE_CYCLE_CLAMP=0` under its own lock.
- When the dep-graph cache is missing or older than `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_BLOCKER_REFRESH_MAX_AGE_S` (default 1800s), force-rebuild the graph, then run `refresh_blocked_status_from_graph` and `release_repaired_brief_holds`.
- Harden the atomic cache write in `build_dependency_graph_cache` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph.sh`): use a unique `mktemp` sibling instead of `.tmp.$$`, because the async lane and the in-cycle stage share the pulse PID.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-post-dispatch-housekeeping.sh`

## Acceptance

- Fresh cache: housekeeping does not run the catch-up stages.
- Stale or missing cache: housekeeping runs graph rebuild → blocked refresh → brief-hold release, in that order.
- `AIDEVOPS_PULSE_BLOCKER_REFRESH_MAX_AGE_S=0` disables the catch-up.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-post-dispatch-housekeeping.sh` and `test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh` pass; ShellCheck clean.
- Runtime: after deploy, the pulse log shows the catch-up stages completing and the repaired scope holds leave `status:blocked`.

title: fix(setup): retired DSPy cleanup aborts non-interactive setup on runtime-bundle installs
body:
## What

`setup.sh --non-interactive` aborts at `cleanup_retired_prompt_tooling` on runtime-bundle installs:

```text
[WARNING] Skipping retired DSPy cleanup: managed path is not an owner-controlled directory
[INFO] Finished setup stage: cleanup_retired_prompt_tooling (0.02s, exit=1)
[ERROR] ./setup.sh:1551 exit 1
```

## Reproducer

1. Install with runtime bundles, so that `~/.aidevops/agents` is a symlink to `~/.aidevops/runtime-bundles/<id>/agents`.
2. Run `./setup.sh --non-interactive` from the canonical repo.
3. Observe the exit 1 above. `~/.aidevops/logs/setup-stage-timings.log` shows `cleanup_retired_prompt_tooling ... 1` on every run since GH#33141 (#33222).

## Root cause

- `cleanup_retired_prompt_tooling` (`.agents/scripts/setup/modules/migrations.sh`) rejects every symlinked managed path (`[[ -L "$path" ]]`). That includes `$HOME/.aidevops/agents`, which is always a symlink to the active runtime bundle, so the one-time migration can never complete or write its marker.
- `_setup_run_noninteractive_migrations` (`setup.sh`) calls the cleanup without the `|| print_warning` fallback the interactive path (`setup.sh` "Retired prompt tooling cleanup incomplete") already uses. A best-effort cleanup refusal therefore aborts the whole deploy. The auto-updater retries around it, but manual `setup.sh --non-interactive` deploys fail.

## How

- `migrations.sh`: when `$agents_dir` is a symlink, resolve it with `cd -P` and accept it only when the target is an owner-controlled directory under `$HOME/.aidevops/runtime-bundles/`. Keep all other symlink and ownership refusals unchanged.
- `setup.sh`: make the non-interactive step non-fatal with the same warning the interactive path uses.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/migrations.sh`
- `setup.sh`

## Acceptance

- `./setup.sh --non-interactive` completes on a runtime-bundle install, and the migration marker `gh33141-retired-dspy-*` is written.
- Redirected symlinks outside `runtime-bundles/` are still refused (warning, no deletion), without aborting setup.
- ShellCheck clean on touched files.

title: fix(full-loop): create-pr --replace-pr ancestry guard is defeated by WIP finalization
body:
## What

`full-loop-helper.sh create-pr --replace-pr N --replacement-reason ...` can never pass its own ancestry guard once the branch has more than one commit. WIP finalization squashes the branch before the final guard checks that the replaced PR's head is an ancestor of `HEAD`.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `full-loop-helper.sh create-pr --no-rebase --issue 32993 --replace-pr 32996 --replacement-reason "..."`, run on a branch that merged PR #32996's head (`git merge FETCH_HEAD`) plus one fix commit.

**Actual output:**

```text
[INFO] Finalizing WIP history into one commit relative to origin/main at f75d8452...
[INFO] WIP history finalized as: GH#32993: fix: promote OpenCode V2 2.0.20 compatibility
...
[ERROR] Aborting duplicate PR creation: open PR #32996 remains durable work, or its head is not preserved by this replacement
```

Without the merge, the guard fails the same way, because nothing preserves the head. Without `--no-rebase`, the rebase also rewrites the preserved commit. The only working path was to close the superseded PR manually and then create the PR without replacement flags.

## Root cause

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh` calls `_finalize_wip_history` (defined in `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh`, around line 1051) before the final `issue_open_pr_guard_check ... 1` (require_ancestry) near line 270.
- `.agents/scripts/issue-open-pr-guard.sh` `issue_open_pr_guard_check` requires `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$ISSUE_OPEN_PR_HEAD_SHA" HEAD`. A squash (and a rebase) always discards that ancestry.

## How

Pick one approach and document it in the helper usage:

1. When `--replace-pr` is set, skip WIP finalization and rebase if the replaced head is an ancestor of the pre-finalization `HEAD`. Preserve the merge.
2. Or, when `--replace-pr` is set, validate ancestry against the pre-finalization `HEAD` and record the replaced head SHA in the PR body audit, then finalize.

Keep the existing refusal when the replaced head was never merged into the branch.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/issue-open-pr-guard.sh`

## Acceptance

- `create-pr --replace-pr N` succeeds on a branch that merged PR N's head plus new commits, with or without `--no-rebase`.
- It still fails when PR N's head is not contained in the branch.
- Existing full-loop tests still pass (`test-full-loop-closed-issue-bookkeeping.sh`, `test-full-loop-wip-finalization.sh`).

title: fix(stale-recovery): expired interactive claim falls back to the 600s worker threshold and unassigns a live session
body:
## Problem

Stale-assignment recovery unassigned a live interactive session. When a maintainer's interactive claim is 2 hours old and the session has posted nothing to GitHub, recovery stops treating the issue as interactive. It then applies the 600-second headless-worker threshold and recovers the issue straight away.

## Evidence (managed private repo; issue numbers withheld)

Timeline on one award-enrichment issue (labels `origin:worker`, `auto-dispatch`, because a generator script created it):

- 08:41:11 A second maintainer posted an `aidevops-interactive-claim/v1` claim (`status:claimed` plus self-assignment) and kept working locally. The session signature later reported 4h 55m of interactive time.
- 10:43:18 Stale recovery posted "dispatch claim 7300s old, last activity 7300s old (threshold=600s, interactive=false)", unassigned the maintainer and relabelled the issue `status:available`.
- 10:47 A headless worker was dispatched. It released the claim as `blocked` at 11:06.
- 13:26 The second stale-recovery tick reached the escalation threshold and set `status:blocked`. The terminal-breaker bridge then filed a consolidation task (see the sibling issue on terminal-breaker consolidation).
- 13:42 The maintainer claimed the issue again and completed it at 13:48.

The claim was 7,327 s old at recovery time, just over `INTERACTIVE_STALE_THRESHOLD_SECONDS=7200`.

## Root cause

`.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-stale.sh`:

- `_stale_assignment_has_live_interactive_claim` (around line 862) returns 1 once `claim_age >= INTERACTIVE_STALE_THRESHOLD_SECONDS`.
- `_resolve_stale_threshold` (around line 896) then sets `is_interactive=false` and falls back to `STALE_ASSIGNMENT_THRESHOLD_SECONDS` (600 s), unless the issue carries `origin:interactive`.
- Interactive sessions usually work locally without posting comments. For them, "last activity" measured from GitHub comments is not a liveness signal.

As a result, an interactive claim stays protected for 2 hours after it is posted. After that it is judged by the headless-worker threshold, which is the wrong one for a human session.

## Expected

A claimant who is still assigned and holds `status:claimed` with a matching `aidevops-interactive-claim/v1` marker should never be recovered through the 600 s worker threshold. Past the interactive window, the pulse should use an interactive-appropriate rule. Options, in order of preference:

1. Keep `is_interactive=true` whenever the claim marker's author is still assigned with `status:claimed`, and compare `last activity` against the interactive threshold.
2. Let `interactive-session-helper.sh` post or refresh a lightweight heartbeat (for example on each commit or push) that counts as activity.
3. Before unassigning an expired interactive claim, post one notice to the claimant and wait for a further interactive window.

## Files to modify

- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-stale.sh`: `_stale_assignment_has_live_interactive_claim`, `_resolve_stale_threshold`.
- Possibly `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper.sh` for a heartbeat (option 2).
- Regression coverage alongside the existing stale-recovery tests, for example `.agents/scripts/tests/test-stale-recovery-age-floor.sh` and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-dedup-stale-terminal-evidence.sh`.


### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-stale.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-stale-recovery-age-floor.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-dedup-stale-terminal-evidence.sh`

## Verification

- A fixture issue with `origin:worker`, `status:claimed`, the claimant assigned, an interactive-claim marker 7,300 s old and no later comments must not be recovered at the 600 s threshold.
- Worker-claimed issues without an interactive marker keep the 600 s behaviour.
- `shellcheck` stays clean on the changed scripts.

title: fix(pulse-triage): terminal breaker files consolidation tasks for threads with zero substantive comments
body:
## Problem

When stale recovery reaches its escalation threshold, `_route_terminal_breaker_to_consolidation` files a consolidation task even when the issue has no substantive comments. The consolidation child then has nothing to merge, and the worker slot and GitHub writes it uses are wasted. The breaker's real cause (see the sibling interactive-claim expiry issue) stays unaddressed.

## Evidence (managed private repo; issue numbers withheld)

- An award-enrichment issue was stale-recovered twice. The first recovery wrongly treated a live interactive claim as a worker claim. At 13:26 the escalation comment set `status:blocked`.
- At 13:29 the pulse posted "Issue Consolidation Dispatched" and filed a `consolidation-task` child. Its notice said "Contributors (_none detected_)".
- Before 13:29 every comment on the parent was automation: dispatch claims and leases, `CLAIM_RELEASED`, stale-recovery and tier-escalation notices. `_consolidation_filter_substantive_comments` excludes all of them, so the substantive count was 0.
- A maintainer finished the parent interactively 19 minutes later, and the child was closed without producing a spec.

## Root cause

`.agents/scripts/pulse-triage.sh`, `_route_terminal_breaker_to_consolidation` (around lines 85-105), calls `_dispatch_issue_consolidation` for every exhausted breaker. It never checks whether consolidation has any material to work with. By contrast, `_issue_needs_consolidation` gates on `_consolidation_filter_substantive_comments` and `ISSUE_CONSOLIDATION_COMMENT_THRESHOLD`.

## Expected

Terminal-breaker routing should reuse the same predicate. When the substantive count is 0, skip consolidation: leave `status:blocked` and the escalation comment as the human-review signal, and log `terminal breaker consolidation skipped: no substantive comments`. Consolidation remains the right route when the thread holds real scope discussion.

## Files to modify

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-triage.sh`: `_route_terminal_breaker_to_consolidation`.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-triage-evaluation.sh`: reuse `_consolidation_filter_substantive_comments`; no new filter.
- Regression coverage next to `.agents/scripts/tests/test-consolidation-dispatch.sh`.


### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-triage.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-triage-evaluation.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-consolidation-dispatch.sh`

## Verification

- A terminal breaker on an issue whose comments are all automation creates no consolidation child and leaves `status:blocked`.
- A terminal breaker on an issue with at least one substantive human comment still dispatches consolidation.
- `shellcheck` stays clean.

title: fix(pulse): async post-dispatch housekeeping is killed with the launchd process group before blocker refresh runs
body:
## What

Async post-dispatch housekeeping (`_pulse_start_post_dispatch_housekeeping`, `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`) is launched as `( ... ) &` plus `disown`. That leaves it in the pulse wrapper's process group. The launchd job (`com.aidevops.aidevops-supervisor-pulse`, no `AbandonProcessGroup`) kills the job's process group when `pulse-wrapper.sh` exits. Housekeeping therefore dies at whatever stage is running when the cycle ends, and every stage after that is skipped. That includes the GH#33246 blocker-refresh catch-up (dep-graph rebuild, `refresh_blocked_status_from_graph`, `release_repaired_brief_holds`) and `preflight_ownership_reconcile`.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `rg -c "Async post-dispatch housekeeping: (launched|complete|reclaiming stale lock)" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` (one pattern per run)

**Actual output (2026-09-30):**

```text
launched=50  complete=11  reclaiming stale lock=38
```

Recent cycles all stop mid-stage and are followed immediately by the next `pulse-wrapper invoked` line:

```text
93088:[pulse-wrapper] Stage start: preflight_ownership_reconcile (timeout 600s)
93118:[2026-09-30T17:31:10Z] pulse-wrapper invoked: pid=55302 ...
94025:[pulse-wrapper] Stage start: post_merge_scanner (timeout 600s)
94040:[2026-09-30T18:04:50Z] pulse-wrapper invoked: pid=14841 ...
```

Each next launch logs `reclaiming stale lock (pid=<previous housekeeping pid>)`, which means the previous process was dead, not finished. `dep-graph-cache.json` mtime is still 2026-09-29T07:16, so blocked-status refresh has not completed for more than 30 hours.

## How

- In `_pulse_start_post_dispatch_housekeeping`, turn on bash job control (`set -m`) only around the background launch, so the subshell gets its own process group. Then restore the previous monitor-mode state. The launchd process-group teardown no longer reaches it. Probe: a non-TTY `/opt/homebrew/bin/bash` script gives the child a distinct PGID, with no warnings, and flags are restored.
- The existing lock, per-stage timeouts and stale-lock reclaim still bound a hung run.
- Linux systemd services kill by cgroup, not process group. This change does not address that path; its behaviour there is unverified.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-post-dispatch-housekeeping.sh`

## Acceptance

- The async housekeeping child's PGID differs from the launcher's (regression assertion).
- After deploy, `pulse.log` shows `Async post-dispatch housekeeping: complete` for most launches, and `dep-graph-cache.json` is refreshed.
- Existing housekeeping, stage-wiring and dep-graph suites pass; ShellCheck is clean.

Related: GH#33246 (catch-up runs inside this lane).

title: Large-file gate lagging-mirror proof rejects NEW: targets, stranding dispatch
body:
## Problem

The large-file gate defers dispatch of every issue that lists a `NEW:` target whenever the canonical mirror lags behind the remote default branch. The lagging-mirror fallback proof, `_large_file_gate_targets_match_remote_default`, returns 1 as soon as a target path cannot be resolved locally. A file the issue is going to create never exists yet, and a missing file cannot exceed the size threshold, yet it blocks the whole proof.

Because `_pulse_refresh_repo` deliberately leaves the canonical checkout unchanged ("differs from origin/develop; canonical checkout unchanged"), these deferrals repeat every cycle until the mirror happens to converge. That can take hours.

## Evidence (managed private repo; issue numbers withheld)

- The pulse log shows the same `Large-file gate: deferring #N (...); <repo> is not at the verified remote default-branch commit` for more than 10 distinct issues in one repo across 29–30 Sep. At least one issue was deferred across roughly 12 cycles over a day. The aidevops repo is affected too.
- One award-data issue was deferred continuously from 19:16Z to 21:31Z. Its scope is `NEW:` data files only: one `.md` and one `.json`. Deferral stopped only when an interactive merge sync brought the canonical checkout to the remote head.
- Read-only probe against a real checkout, calling the function with `remote_sha = HEAD`:
  - `package.json` → `rc=0`
  - `todo/.../does-not-exist-yet.json` → `rc=1`
  - both together → `rc=1`

  The failure is in `_large_file_gate_resolve_full_path` at line 373, before any SHA comparison, so it applies to every lag.

## Root cause

`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-large-file-gate.sh:360-384`, `_large_file_gate_targets_match_remote_default`:

```bash
full_path=$(_large_file_gate_resolve_full_path "$target" "$repo_path") || return 1
```

Absence locally is treated as "unverifiable" rather than "cannot be large".

## Expected

For each target that does not resolve locally:

- If `git ls-tree "$remote_sha" -- <path>` (checking the same `.agents/` and dot-prefixed variants the resolver tries) is also empty, the path is verified-absent at the remote commit. Skip it: a new file has zero measured lines.
- If the path exists at `remote_sha` but not locally (added upstream after the mirror lagged), keep `return 1`, which is the current fail-closed behaviour.
- Keep the existing `cat-file -e "${remote_sha}^{commit}"` precondition, so a mirror without the remote objects still defers.

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-large-file-gate.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-large-file-gate-continuation-verify.sh`

## Verification

- Lagging mirror (local HEAD != remote SHA, remote commit object present), with a target absent both locally and at `remote_sha` → the proof returns 0 and dispatch proceeds.
- Lagging mirror, target present at `remote_sha` but absent locally → returns 1 (defers).
- Existing Test 9 ("stale pulse checkout → defer before local measurement") still passes for existing over-threshold targets.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-large-file-gate.sh` is clean.

Related: #32453 (canonical checkouts go stale). This issue is narrower: the fallback proof exists precisely for stale mirrors but cannot handle `NEW:` targets.

title: Worker BLOCKED classifier matches quoted BLOCKED in continuation summary
body:
## Problem

`output_has_blocked_signal` classifies a headless worker run as terminal `blocked` when the substring `BLOCKED` appears anywhere in the run's text parts. That includes the continuation summary, which quotes the dispatch instruction "stop only at `FULL_LOOP_COMPLETE` or `BLOCKED` with evidence".

A worker that simply stopped early, ending with a progress report and "Next steps", is therefore recorded as `cause=blocked` / `terminal_blocked`. It is released with `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked` and no blocker evidence, and it gets no continuation.

## Evidence (managed private repo; issue numbers withheld)

- Worker-failure excerpt for an award-data issue: `[WORKER_EXIT_DIAGNOSTICS] exit_code=0 ... cause=blocked classification_source=model_blocked_signal classification_pattern=terminal_blocked`.
- The worker's final assistant text was a status report: "Progress so far is research and preparation... Open problems: fee PDF not yet located; Node v26 vs expected 24... Next steps: 1. Find and capture the fee PDF...". It contains no `BLOCKED`.
- `rg -o '.{0,80}BLOCKED.{0,40}'` on the excerpt finds exactly two hits, both inside the continuation summary: "...stop only at `FULL_LOOP_COMPLETE` or `BLOCKED` with evidence" and "...report `FULL_LOOP_COMPLETE` or `BLOCKED` with evidence".
- The issue comment thread shows only `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked`, with no reason. The work was resumable (captures done, scope updated), but the run was marked terminal.

## Root cause

`.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-model.sh:810-840`, `output_has_blocked_signal`, joins every `type == "text"` part and tests `blocked_marker in model_text`. This is an unanchored substring match across the whole session, including injected summary or synthetic parts. `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-result.sh:174-185` then returns 83 with `terminal_blocked`.

## Expected

- Evaluate only the final non-synthetic assistant message, and exclude compaction or summary parts (`synthetic: true` / summary metadata).
- Require an anchored terminal marker, such as a line beginning with `BLOCKED` or `**BLOCKED**` (the shape `_PULSE_DEP_GRAPH_NON_DEP_BLOCK_MARKERS` already recognises), not a quoted mention of the word.
- A natural stop without `FULL_LOOP_COMPLETE` and without an anchored `BLOCKED` should fall through to the existing incomplete/continuation path rather than terminal blocked.

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-model.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-output-classification.sh`

## Verification

- Output whose only `BLOCKED` occurrence is inside a summary or quoted instruction, with a final "Next steps" report → not classified `terminal_blocked`.
- Output whose final assistant message starts with `BLOCKED: <evidence>` → still returns the blocked signal (rc 0 from `output_has_blocked_signal`).
- The existing provider test at `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-provider-tests.sh:191` still passes.
- `shellcheck` is clean.
<!-- aidevops:origin:interactive -->
