title: consolidated: adopt Claude Haiku 5.5 as Anthropic simple-tier model when released
body:
_Supersedes #32876 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Adopt Claude Haiku 5.5 as the Anthropic `simple`-tier model once Anthropic releases it. Follow the same pattern as the Sonnet 5.5 adoption (#32848, PR #32855, v3.37.21).

## Why

Anthropic's Sonnet 5.5 launch page (anthropic.com/claude-sonnet-5-5, 2026-09-28) said Haiku 5.5 would arrive in the "coming weeks". The `simple` tier still falls back to `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5`.

## Trigger (check before starting — external wait)

Start only after Anthropic has published the Haiku 5.5 model ID and pricing. Use only an ID taken from Anthropic's page or API; never guess it. If it is not published, make no changes and exit with `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON=external_trigger_pending`.

- Check: `opencode models anthropic --refresh`, or Anthropic's model and pricing pages.
- Status at consolidation (2026-09-30): `opencode models anthropic` still lists only `claude-haiku-4-5` / `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`. The trigger is **not met**, so this issue is filed with `status:blocked` (per @marcusquinn, see Context).
- Wake condition: once the ID and pricing are published, set `status:available` and the brief runs as written.

## How

Use the #32848 change set (PR #32855) as the reference pattern:

1. Replace the current-default Haiku IDs with the new ID in the routing table, defaults, `shared-model-tier.sh`, `headless-runtime-helper.sh` and docs. Do not change CHANGELOG, TODO.md or `todo/` history.
2. Add catalog entries alongside the old ones:
   - `model-pricing.json`: put the specific key before the generic `haiku-4` key, and bump the pricing version if rates change.
   - `model-limits.mjs`.
   - CLI names in `config-hook.mjs`.
   - Aliases in `claude-proxy-context.mjs`.
   - `compare-models-helper.sh`.
3. If models.dev lacks the ID, add it to `PENDING_ANTHROPIC_MODELS` in `anthropic-catalog-bridge.mjs`.
4. Check the reasoning variants. Haiku 4.5 has only budget variants (`high`/`max`). See the reasoning-mapping bullet in `.agents/tools/context/model-routing.md`.
5. Add a one-time user-settings migration with backups. Model it on `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/migration-sonnet-5-5.sh`: marker `gh32848-sonnet-5-5-settings`, function `migrate_sonnet_5_5_settings`. It is wired into `setup.sh` at the `source` (about line 355) and the two call sites (about lines 1561 and 1769). Add a test modelled on `.agents/scripts/tests/test-sonnet-5-5-migration.sh`.

Read-only references: `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/migration-sonnet-5-5.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-sonnet-5-5-migration.sh`, PR #32855.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The trigger is verified first: the Haiku 5.5 ID and pricing come from an Anthropic source, not a guess.
- [ ] The `simple`-tier Anthropic fallback uses Haiku 5.5, and a live headless run succeeds.
- [ ] User pins are migrated once, with backups.
- [ ] Linters and plugin tests pass.

### Verification

```bash
node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-model-limits.mjs .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-observability-pricing.mjs
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-haiku-5-5-migration.sh
opencode run -m anthropic/<haiku-5-5-id> "Reply with only the number: 17+40"
```

### Files Scope

- EDIT: .agents/configs/model-routing-table.json
- EDIT: .agents/configs/aidevops.defaults.jsonc
- EDIT: .agents/configs/model-pricing.json
- EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/model-limits.mjs
- EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/config-hook.mjs
- EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/claude-proxy-context.mjs

- EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/compare-models-helper.sh
- EDIT: .agents/tools/context/model-routing.md
- EDIT: setup.sh
- NEW: .agents/scripts/setup/modules/migration-haiku-5-5.sh
- NEW: .agents/scripts/tests/test-haiku-5-5-migration.sh

## Context & Decisions

- Original brief, trigger rule (never guess the ID), reference pattern (#32848/PR #32855) and scope: per @marcusquinn, #32876 body.
- Tier: per @vladimirdulov (the automated self-hosting detector comment), the pre-dispatch self-hosting detector set `tier:thinking` because the brief touches `headless-runtime-helper.sh`, which is on the dispatch path. Bypass: `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_SELF_HOSTING_DETECTOR=1`.
- Dispatch pause: per @marcusquinn (2026-09-30), the trigger was still unmet. About 40 `tier:thinking` dispatch cycles ran in 11 hours across three runners, and each worker correctly stopped with no changes. `status:blocked` was set to stop redispatch, and the circuit defect was filed as #33225 (now closed). Wake condition: Anthropic publishes the Haiku 5.5 ID and pricing; then set `status:available`.

title: fix(pulse): treat For/Ref #N open PRs as in-flight for consolidation
body:
## Problem

`_consolidation_resolving_pr_exists` treats only GitHub closing keywords (`close|fix|resolve`) as evidence that work on a parent issue is in flight. Briefs that keep the parent open intentionally tell workers to reference it with `For #N` (or `Ref #N`) so a merge cannot close it. While such a PR is open, the consolidation gate does not see it and files a new `consolidation-task` child for the same parent.

Follow-up to #33255 (its fix, PR #33277, covered empty terminal-breaker comments only; this gap was reported in a comment on #33255 after the fact).

## Evidence (managed private repo; issue numbers withheld)

- Parent timeline: `consolidation-in-progress` at 20:55Z, then `needs-consolidation` plus a new `consolidation-task` child at 20:57Z, while a PR referencing the parent with `For #N` was open. The PR merged and the parent closed at 21:31Z; the child was closed as redundant.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-triage-evaluation.sh:889-899` filters candidate PR bodies with `(?i)\b(close[ds]?|fix(es|ed)?|resolve[ds]?)[ \t]+#N\b`; `For`/`Ref` never match.

## Fix

- In `_consolidation_resolving_pr_exists` only (in-flight detection, not closure semantics), also accept `(?i)\b(for|ref)[ \t]+#N\b` in an open PR body.
- Keep the existing fail-open behaviour on API errors and the `#N` vs `#N1` word boundary.

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-triage-evaluation.sh` — `_consolidation_resolving_pr_exists`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-consolidation-dispatch.sh` — add `For #N` / `Ref #N` / bare `#N` cases

## Verification

- An open PR whose body has only `For #N` or `Ref #N` → `_consolidation_resolving_pr_exists N` returns 0.
- A PR mentioning bare `#N`, or `For #N1`, still returns 1.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-consolidation-dispatch.sh` passes; `shellcheck` clean.

title: fix(worker): keep ready-missing-linkage handoffs in review after claim release
body:
## Problem

When a worker hands off a ready PR that intentionally uses a non-closing reference (`For #N`, as briefs require for issues that stay open), `_hrw_preserve_ready_missing_linkage_handoff` projects the issue to `status:in-review`, assigns the runner and removes `auto-dispatch` (GH#33115 intent). The claim release that follows then undoes that projection: `_release_dispatch_claim` calls `clear_active_status_on_release`, which only counts PRs with closing keywords, finds none, and sets `status:available` and unassigns the runner.

Net effect: the durable partial-delivery PR is orphaned from its issue. The issue looks unclaimed and idle while an open PR carries the work. The same applies to `worker_ready_missing_summary` whenever the PR body lacks a closing keyword.

## Evidence (managed private repo; numbers withheld)

Issue timeline for one worker run (2026-09-30, UTC):

- 22:58:30 `auto-dispatch` removed, 22:58:40 `status:in-progress` removed, 22:58:45 `status:in-review` added (checkpoint handoff).
- 22:59:13 `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=worker_ready_missing_linkage`.
- 22:59:37 runner unassigned, 22:59:48 `status:in-review` removed, 22:59:54 `status:available` added (generic release projection).

Mechanism:

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh` `_escalate_worker_pr_checkpoint` sets and verifies `status:in-review`, then calls `_hrw_release_dispatch_claim "$session_key" "$release_reason"`.
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh` `_release_dispatch_claim` special-cases only `worker_ownership_lost` and `worker_draft_checkpoint`; every other reason falls through to `clear_active_status_on_release`.
- `.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh` `clear_active_status_on_release` filters linked PRs with `(close[ds]?|fix(es|ed)?|resolve[ds]?)[[:space:]]*#N`, so a `For #N` PR projects `available`.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-checkpoint-tests.sh` mocks `_release_dispatch_claim`, so the round trip is untested.

## Fix

- In `_release_dispatch_claim`, treat `worker_ready_missing_linkage` and `worker_ready_missing_summary` like other preserved handoffs: post the `CLAIM_RELEASED` audit comment and unlock the conversation, but skip `clear_active_status_on_release` so the verified in-review projection and runner assignment stay in place.
- Update the stale draft-checkpoint assertion in `test-headless-runtime-release-unlock.sh`: it expects a "Preserving issue ownership..." message that no longer exists, while current code projects draft checkpoints as blocked partial work. The file currently fails on `main`.

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh`: `_release_dispatch_claim`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-release-unlock.sh`: add ready-missing-linkage/summary cases; align the draft-checkpoint assertion with current behaviour

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-release-unlock.sh` passes (currently fails on `main` at the draft-checkpoint case).
- Release with `worker_ready_missing_linkage` or `worker_ready_missing_summary` posts `CLAIM_RELEASED`, does not call `clear_active_status_on_release`, and still unlocks.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-checkpoint-tests.sh` still passes; `shellcheck` is clean.

title: fix(worker): project Node selection does not reach OpenCode tool shells
body:
## What

Headless worker tool shells run the Homebrew default Node (`/opt/homebrew/bin/node`, v26) even though worker prepare selects the project Node. One example is `/opt/homebrew/opt/node@24/bin` for a repo with `.nvmrc` 24.18.0 and `engines.node` `>=24 <25`.

## Evidence

- In an awards enrichment worker on v3.37.37 (which includes GH#32815 / `4df309af08`), `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` reported `Unsupported engine: wanted {"node":">=24.0.0 <25.0.0"} (current: {"node":"v26.4.0"})`. The worker then reported "Node 26 vs expected 24" as an open problem.
- Running `_project_node_bin <repo> .` from `project-node-runtime.sh` against the same repo prints `/opt/homebrew/opt/node@24/bin`, so selection works.
- `headless-runtime-worker-prepare.sh:387-393` exports `PATH="${node_bin}:$PATH"` in the helper process. The OpenCode tool-shell PATH is not seeded from that process PATH. An OpenCode session's tool-shell PATH is: plugin-prepended framework dirs (`shell-env.mjs` `prependFrameworkPaths`), then the login-profile order (`/opt/homebrew/bin` first from `brew shellenv`). So only `shell.env` hook prepends reliably reach tool shells.

## Fix

1. `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker-prepare.sh`: when `_project_node_bin` selects a bin dir, also `export AIDEVOPS_PROJECT_NODE_BIN="$node_bin"`. It already crosses the sandbox via the `AIDEVOPS_*` passthrough in `build_sandbox_passthrough_csv`.
2. `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/shell-env.mjs`: in the `shell.env` hook, prepend `process.env.AIDEVOPS_PROJECT_NODE_BIN` after the framework dirs when it is an absolute existing directory containing an executable `node`.

## Verification

- `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-shell-env-origin.mjs` (or the closest existing shell-env test) passes.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker-prepare.sh` is clean.
- After deploy, the next awards worker's `pnpm install` emits no `Unsupported engine` warning.

title: feat(browser-qa): layout step and custom viewport widths for journeys
body:
## What

Add layout checks to the declarative browser QA journey (`browser-qa-helper.sh journey`):

1. A new `layout` step that compares the rendered boxes of two elements.
2. Custom viewport widths, in addition to the named `desktop` (1440×900) and `mobile` (375×667).

## Why

An interactive session had to confirm that a WordPress admin search field matched its button's height and top edge at 1440, 1024, 782, 600 and 375px, on two WordPress versions (core buttons are 30px on WP 6.2 desktop and 40px on WP 7 and on small screens). The current steps (`navigate`, `click`, `visible`, `count`, `text`, `attribute`, `no-horizontal-overflow`) cannot assert geometry, and only two fixed viewports exist, so the session wrote a one-off Playwright script (login, loop widths, `getBoundingClientRect()` on both elements, compare height/top, check overflow, clip screenshots). With these two additions the same check is a reusable, read-only journey config for any app.

## How

Files to modify:

- `.agents/scripts/browser-qa-journey-config.mjs`
  - `STEP_FIELDS`: add `layout: { selector: 'text', compare: 'text', match: 'layoutMatch' }` (names are a suggestion). `match` is a non-empty array of unique edges from a fixed allowlist: `top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`, `width`, `height`, `centerX`, `centerY`. Optional `tolerancePx` is an integer 0–8 (default 1). Add the matching check to `FIELD_CHECKS` and handle optional fields in step validation.
  - `validateViewports()`: also accept objects `{ "name": "tablet-782", "width": 782, "height": 900 }`, with integer bounds (e.g. width 320–3840, height 320–2160), unique names and a cap on the count (e.g. 8). Named strings `desktop`/`mobile` keep working unchanged.
- `.agents/scripts/browser-qa-journey-steps.mjs`
  - Add a `layout` handler following the existing `pollUntil` pattern: read `boundingBox()` of the first match for `selector` and `compare` (with `probeTimeout`), compare each requested edge within tolerance, and fail with a message that names the edges and measured values, e.g. `layout assertion failed: height 30 vs 40`. Never evaluate config-supplied code.
- `.agents/scripts/browser-qa-journey.mjs`
  - `runViewport()` currently uses `VIEWPORTS[viewportName]`; resolve custom viewport objects too, and report the viewport name and size in each result.
- `.agents/tools/browser/browser-qa.md`: document the `layout` step and custom viewports with an example (field and button same `top` and `height`, plus `no-horizontal-overflow`, at 1440/782/375).
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-browser-qa-journey.sh`: extend the existing validation cases (accept valid `layout` steps and custom viewports, reject unknown edges, out-of-range tolerance or sizes, duplicate names). This extends an existing suite; it does not add new test infrastructure.

Reference pattern: the existing `count`/`attribute` handlers and their `STEP_FIELDS` entries; `no-horizontal-overflow` for a page-level geometry check.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/browser-qa-journey-config.mjs`
- `.agents/scripts/browser-qa-journey-steps.mjs`
- `.agents/scripts/browser-qa-journey.mjs`
- `.agents/tools/browser/browser-qa.md`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-browser-qa-journey.sh`

## Acceptance criteria

- A journey config with a `layout` step passes when both boxes match within tolerance and fails with a redacted, specific message otherwise.
- `viewports` accepts a mix of `"desktop"` and `{ name, width, height }` objects; invalid entries fail validation before any browser launch or sign-in.
- Existing configs (named viewports only, existing step types) behave unchanged. `SCHEMA_VERSION` stays 1 if the change is purely additive.
- `test-browser-qa-journey.sh` passes; ShellCheck is clean for any touched shell.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-browser-qa-journey.sh`
- Run a journey against a local isolated page with a form field next to a button: assert `match: ["top", "height"]` at viewports 1440, 782 and 375, then change one element's CSS height and confirm the step fails with both values in the message. No external authenticated site or credentials are needed for this geometry verification.

## Recovery context

The unattended backlog mission restores the canonical Files Scope above without changing the requested implementation. The previous launch on 2026-10-01 ended with `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=worker_ownership_lost` and a terminal lease. Verify current ownership normally before continuation; do not bypass a live owner or an external-directory permission boundary.

title: Footprint gate: claimed no-auto-dispatch coordination issues reserve Files Scope indefinitely and block worker children
body:
## What

`_footprint_get_inflight` in `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh:719-784` treats any open issue labelled `status:claimed` as an in-flight file owner and reads its `### Files Scope` and its `EDIT:`/`NEW:`/`File:` paths. The only exemption is `parent-task` (lines 754-758). An interactive coordination or pilot issue (`origin:interactive`, `no-auto-dispatch`, `status:claimed`, not `parent-task`) that declares a Files Scope therefore reserves those files for as long as the maintainer keeps it claimed, which can be days. Every worker-ready child that edits the same file is deferred with `FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP`, logged as a benign block.

## Evidence (v3.37.37/38, 2026-09-30 → 10-01)

- One coordination issue in a managed private repo (pilot tracker, claimed interactively for more than 2 days, `no-auto-dispatch`, `### Files Scope` listing a single runbook doc) blocked six different auto-dispatch children over about 20 hours. Each logged repeated `[footprint-defer] event=deferred ... blocker=#<coordinator>` / `FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP (issue=#<coordinator> files=<runbook>)` cycles with `wake_reason=candidate_footprint_changed` churn.
- No worktree, PR or live session was editing that file under the coordinator during that time.
- Manual mitigation: removed the Files Scope declaration from the coordinator body. The next cycle no longer reports the coordinator as a blocker.

## Proposed fix

Make a claimed `no-auto-dispatch` issue hold a footprint only when there is evidence of active implementation. Evidence means a live interactive session stamp with a linked worktree on a branch for that issue, an open linked PR, or a dispatch ledger entry. When none of these exist, skip the issue as a coordination container, as `parent-task` is skipped today. Alternatively, apply a TTL to `status:claimed` footprints that the claim heartbeat refreshes. Either way, log a distinct reason, such as `footprint_stale_coordinator`, so repeated defers are not classified as benign.

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-footprint-overlap.sh`

## Verification

- Extend `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-footprint-overlap.sh`. A claimed `no-auto-dispatch` issue with a Files Scope and no worktree, PR or ledger evidence must not block a candidate sharing the same file. The same issue with an open linked PR must still block it.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh`

title: Terminal blocker first observation says status:blocked but releases to available; external_trigger_pending retry is always wasted
body:
## What

On the first terminal-blocker observation, the recovery text says `Projected state: status:blocked`. The same release then puts the issue back to `status:available`. The circuit opens only on the second identical observation. That second dispatch is by design, but the comment tells maintainers the issue is held when it is not.

For `external_trigger_pending`, the free retry is also predictably wasted. The task revision for that reason ignores unrelated merges, so nothing in the repository can change the outcome before the next dispatch.

## Evidence (2026-10-01, v3.37.38)

A project issue's worker exited with `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON=external_trigger_pending`. Its timeline:

- 00:48:34Z: CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked, with an observation fragment saying "Projected state: status:blocked."
- 00:48:49Z: unassigned
- 00:48:55Z: `status:blocked` removed
- 00:48:57Z: `status:available` added

A maintainer had to apply the hold by hand to avoid a second authenticated worker run that would give the same result.

## How

1. EDIT: `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`
   - `_terminal_blocker_recovery()`, around line 355: make the `Projected state:` line depend on the release mode. For the first observation, say `status:available` (one verification retry before the circuit opens). Keep `status:blocked` for the circuit and open modes.
   - Optionally, treat `external_trigger_pending` like `permission_required`: open the circuit on the first observation, because no repository revision can satisfy it.
2. EDIT: `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh`
   - `_hrff_prepare_terminal_blocker_release()`, around line 527: pass the mode to the fragment builder, or select the circuit path directly for reasons that hold immediately.
3. Reference pattern: the `permission_required` special case in `terminal_blocker_task_revision()`, around line 229.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-lifecycle-comms.sh`, which asserts the first and second observation fragments around line 509.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-approval-helper-content-binding.sh`
- ShellCheck is clean on all edited scripts.

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-lifecycle-comms.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/approval-snapshot-v2.sh` (GH#33243 integration scope recovery: `_approval_snapshot_v2_comments_json`'s `canonical_terminal_blocker_release` regex hardcodes the literal text `Projected state: status:blocked\.`; it must also accept the new first-observation `status:available` text or newly generated audit-only release comments stop being excluded from approval-signature binding, producing false drift)

Related: #33138 (single status:blocked projection for open circuits).

title: Shared local test sites are overwritten by parallel worktree syncs; add a freshness-checked sync helper and guidance
body:
## Problem

Parallel interactive sessions each work in their own linked worktree, but they often verify on **one shared local site**, such as a LocalWP site for a WordPress plugin. Each session copies its own worktree into the same `wp-content/plugins/<slug>/` folder with `rsync --delete`, so the last copy wins:

- Session A merges a PR, fast-forwards `main` and syncs `main` into the site. The user is told to look.
- Session B's worktree was cut a few minutes before A's merge. It syncs its in-progress worktree for its own test and silently removes A's merged work from the site.
- The user sees old behaviour, assumes A's change is broken, and has no idea which of many sessions to ask. They can't tell which session last deployed.

Observed 2026-10-01 on a WordPress plugin repo with about 10 active worktrees. It resolved only because session B happened to merge `origin/main` and sync again.

`tools/wordpress/wp-dev.md` ("Sync to LocalWP") documents a plain `rsync --delete` from one canonical checkout. It doesn't mention parallel worktrees, freshness against the default branch, or who last deployed.

## Proposed fix

1. **Helper** `.agents/scripts/local-site-sync-helper.sh sync --src <worktree> --dest <plugin-or-theme-dir> [--exclude-from .distignore] [--force]`:
   - Refuse, unless `--force`, when the source `HEAD` lacks the default remote branch (`git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/<default> HEAD` after a fetch). The message tells the session to merge the default branch first. This keeps a shared site from ever going backwards past merged work.
   - Before syncing, read a stamp file kept **outside** the synced folder (for example `<dest>/../.<slug>.synced-from.json`, holding worktree path, branch, `HEAD` SHA, a dirty flag, session id if known, and time). Print it, and warn when another worktree synced in the last 30 minutes, since that session may still be testing.
   - After syncing, write the new stamp.
   - `status --dest <dir>` prints the stamp, so a session can answer "which branch is on the site, and who put it there?"
2. **Docs** in `tools/wordpress/wp-dev.md` (Sync to LocalWP) and a short note in `services/hosting/local-hosting.md`:
   - A shared site is shared by every session.
   - Merge the default branch before syncing.
   - Use the helper.
   - Prefer a throwaway per-worktree site (Docker `wordpress` image on a unique port) for in-progress verification; keep the shared site for showing the user.
   - After merging, check `status` before telling the user to look.

## Files

- New: `.agents/scripts/local-site-sync-helper.sh`. Follow the existing helper conventions: source `shared-constants.sh`, `local var="$1"`, explicit returns, ShellCheck clean, Bash 3.2.
- Edit: `.agents/tools/wordpress/wp-dev.md`, `.agents/services/hosting/local-hosting.md`.

## Verification

- ShellCheck clean.
- In a temporary Git repository with two worktrees and a temporary destination folder:
  - Syncing a worktree behind `origin/main` is refused.
  - `--force` syncs and writes the stamp.
  - A second worktree's sync warns about the recent stamp.
  - `status` prints the stamp.

title: feat(wordpress): plugin release build, WordPress.org preflight and Plugin Check helper + submission guide
body:
## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-01
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** While preparing a private WordPress plugin for a GitHub release channel (Git Updater) and a later WordPress.org submission, the plugin needed build, preflight and Plugin Check scripts plus a submission checklist. aidevops has only a one-line generic release checklist (`.agents/tools/wordpress/wp-dev.md:144`) and nothing on WordPress.org submission, SVN, assets or Git Updater packaging, so every plugin project rediscovers these. The working reference scripts live in a private repository; everything a worker needs from them is inlined below.

## What

A reusable WordPress plugin release and WordPress.org preflight capability for any plugin repository:

1. `NEW: .agents/tools/wordpress/wp-plugin-release.md` — subagent doc: two release channels (GitHub releases, optionally through Git Updater; WordPress.org), building from a Git ref, per-channel exclusions, the WordPress.org preflight checklist, submission, SVN and assets, with official sources.
2. `NEW: .agents/scripts/wp-plugin-release-helper.sh` — `build`, `preflight` and `plugin-check` subcommands that work in any plugin repo. It never tags, pushes, publishes, uploads or commits.
3. `EDIT: .agents/tools/wordpress/wp-dev.md:144` — keep the release checklist line and point to the new doc and helper.
4. `EDIT: .agents/subagent-index.toon:138` — add `wp-plugin-release` to the `tools/wordpress/` list.

## Why

WordPress.org rejects or delays plugins for avoidable reasons (slug, readme, updater code, remote assets, contributors), and a GitHub release built by hand can break Git Updater users (wrong asset name, pre-release `Version:` on the default branch). The checks are deterministic, so they belong in a helper, with the judgement items in a checklist.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** New files with a decided command surface and inlined check list; the worker still designs the shell structure, main-file detection and option handling.

## How (Approach)

### Worker Quick-Start

Facts verified while building the reference implementation (2026-10-01; WordPress 7.1.2, Plugin Check 2.1.0, wp-cli image `wordpress:cli-php8.3`):

- **Build from Git, not the working tree:** `git archive --format=tar REF | tar -x`, then `rsync -a --exclude-from=<.distignore>` into `<slug>/`. `.distignore` usually lists itself and is often `export-ignore`d, so read it with `git show REF:.distignore`. Zip with one top folder `<slug>/`. For reproducible zips, `touch -t 202001010000` every file and `zip -qrX`; two builds then give the same SHA-256.
- **Per-channel exclusions:** optional `.distignore-wporg` (rsync patterns, applied on top of `.distignore`) for code WordPress.org forbids, such as updater integrations. Optional header lines to strip from the main file in the WordPress.org build (Git Updater's `GitHub Plugin URI`, `Primary Branch`, `Release Asset`, and any `*Plugin URI` lines for other updaters).
- **Git Updater packaging:** it installs the first release asset whose name starts with the plugin slug, and treats tags with letters as non-stable. So: GitHub asset `<slug>-X.Y.Z.zip`; WordPress.org zip named so it does not start with the slug (`wordpress-org-<slug>-X.Y.Z.zip`); never a pre-release `Version:` on the default branch, because Git Updater compares the default branch's `Version:` with installed copies. Publish the release in the same sitting as the version merge.
- **Plugin Check in Docker:** network + `mariadb:10.6` + a named volume, wp-cli via `docker run --rm --user 33:33 wordpress:cli-php8.3 php -d memory_limit=1G /usr/local/bin/wp ...`. The default 128 MB limit dies during `wp core download`. `chown 33:33` the volume first (run once as root). Plugin Check needs WordPress 6.3+, so use latest core. `wp plugin check <slug> --format=json` prints `FILE: <path>` lines each followed by a JSON array of findings (`type`, `code`, `line`...), or `Success: Checks complete. No errors found.` Treat output with neither as "did not run" (failure). Codes seen: `plugin_updater_detected` (an `Update URI` header), `stable_tag_mismatch`. Remove containers, volume and network in an EXIT trap; use a unique name prefix and never touch other containers.
- **PHP lint at the minimum PHP:** `docker run --rm -v <dir>:/src:ro php:<Requires PHP>-cli` with `php -l` on every file (local PHP 8.x misses 7.x incompatibilities); `node --check` every JS file.
- **WordPress.org APIs:** latest core = first `"current"` in `https://api.wordpress.org/core/version-check/1.7/` (later offers are older branches). Slug taken: `https://api.wordpress.org/plugins/info/1.2/?action=plugin_information&request[slug]=<slug>` returns `"error":"Plugin not found."` when free. Contributor exists: `https://profiles.wordpress.org/<user>/` returns 200, 404 when there is no such account. All network checks need an `--offline` switch.
- **OpenCode Bash policy:** interactive sessions cannot run commands with redirects, `$(...)`, globs or `xargs` directly; run the helper as a script.

### Files to Modify

- `NEW: .agents/scripts/wp-plugin-release-helper.sh` — model on `.agents/scripts/local-site-sync-helper.sh` (subcommand dispatch, `shared-constants.sh` sourcing, usage text, explicit `return 0`/`return 1`).
- `NEW: .agents/tools/wordpress/wp-plugin-release.md` — model the frontmatter and AI-CONTEXT block on `.agents/tools/wordpress/wp-dev.md:1-40`.
- `EDIT: .agents/tools/wordpress/wp-dev.md:144` — append: "Builds, preflight and WordPress.org submission: `tools/wordpress/wp-plugin-release.md` and `wp-plugin-release-helper.sh`."
- `EDIT: .agents/subagent-index.toon:138` — add `wp-plugin-release` to the pipe-separated list.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** new helper is called by people and agents from a plugin repo root; docs are read through `wp-dev.md` and the subagent index. No existing script calls it (`rg -n wp-plugin-release .agents` is empty today).
- **Writers/mutation paths:** the helper writes only to its `--out` folder (default `dist/` in the plugin repo) and a `mktemp -d` folder it removes; `plugin-check` creates and removes its own Docker resources.
- **Existing verification/tests:** none for WordPress release; verify by running the helper (below).
- **Schemas/config:** reads the plugin's `.distignore`, optional `.distignore-wporg`, main-file headers and `readme.txt`. No aidevops config.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** deployed to `~/.aidevops/agents/` by `setup.sh`; no generated files to edit.
- **Migrations/backfills:** none (new capability).
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert the PR; the helper leaves no state outside `--out`.

### Implementation Steps

1. Main file and slug: the slug defaults to the repo's top-level folder name (`--slug` overrides); the main file is `<slug>.php` if it exists, else the single root `*.php` with a `Plugin Name:` header (`--main-file` overrides). Fail clearly when ambiguous.
2. `build [--ref REF] [--out DIR] [--wporg-strip-headers 'A|B'] [--quiet]`: as in Quick-Start; writes `<slug>-X.Y.Z.zip`, `wordpress-org-<slug>-X.Y.Z.zip` and `SHA256SUMS`; version from the main file's `Version:` at REF.
3. `preflight [--ref REF] [--strict] [--offline] [--no-docker]`: builds into a temp folder, prints `ok`/`warn`/`ERROR`/`note` lines, exits 1 on errors (or warnings with `--strict`). Checks:
   - Errors: `Version:` not numeric `X.Y.Z`; a `define(..._VERSION, ...)` constant in the main file that differs; `readme.txt` `Stable tag` differs or is `trunk`; `Requires at least`/`Requires PHP` missing from the main file or different in `readme.txt`; `Update URI` header; `Text Domain` not the slug; license not GPL-compatible; no short description; `Tested up to` not `major.minor`; zip top level not exactly `<slug>/`; main file missing from a zip; development files in a zip (`.git`, `.github`, `.agents`, `.distignore*`, `.gitattributes`, `.gitignore`, CI files, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `node_modules`, `tests`, `phpunit.xml*`, `scripts`, `dist`, `.DS_Store`, `__MACOSX`, `*.log`, `*.bak`); PHP or JS syntax errors; WordPress.org zip still containing `.distignore-wporg` files or stripped headers; asset names (GitHub zip must start with the slug, the WordPress.org zip must not).
   - Warnings: `readme.txt` over 10 KB; short description over 150 characters; more than 5 tags; `Tested up to` below the latest WordPress; no changelog entry for the version, or an `Unreleased` section left; readme title differs from `Plugin Name`; slug made from `Plugin Name` (lowercase, non-alphanumerics to `-`) differs from the slug; name starting with `WordPress`, `WP`, `Woo`, `WooCommerce` or `Gutenberg`; `Plugin URI` equal to `Author URI`; contributors without a WordPress.org profile; WordPress.org build PHP/JS mentioning `Plugin_Upgrader`, `Theme_Upgrader`, `site_transient_update_plugins`, `auto_update_plugin`/`auto_update_theme` or `api.github.com/repos`; `wp_enqueue_*`/`wp_register_*`/`<script`/`<link` with a remote URL; tag `vX.Y.Z` existing on another commit.
   - Notes: zip sizes and file counts; slug already listed on WordPress.org; hosts found in PHP/JS that `readme.txt` does not name (excluding `w3.org`, `gnu.org`, `wordpress.org`, `w.org`, `wp.org`, `example.com`); REF not on `origin/<default branch>`.
4. `plugin-check [--ref REF | --zip FILE ...] [--keep-output DIR]`: as in Quick-Start; prints one line per finding (type, code, file:line) and counts; exits 1 when any zip has errors.
5. Write `wp-plugin-release.md` with: the two channels and their naming rules; the GitHub release steps (version PR → preflight + plugin-check → merge → tag from the default branch → build from the tag → `gh release create vX.Y.Z dist/<slug>-X.Y.Z.zip`; never attach the WordPress.org zip); the WordPress.org checklist below; that release and submission need the owner's explicit say; and the helper's usage.
6. `shellcheck` the helper and run the verification below.

WordPress.org checklist content (sources: developer.wordpress.org Plugin Handbook pages "Detailed Plugin Guidelines", "Planning, Submitting, and Maintaining Plugins", "Plugin Readmes", "How Your Plugin Assets Work", "Using Subversion"):

- Slug comes from `Plugin Name` and can change only once, before approval; ask for the wanted slug in the submission notes so it matches the text domain.
- Submit a complete, working plugin (guideline 16); no trademark at the start of the name (17); GPL-compatible code and assets (1); no trialware or locked features (5); services documented with terms and privacy links, no tracking without consent (6, 7); no code installed or updated from outside WordPress.org, and JS/CSS shipped locally unless part of a service (8); affiliate links disclosed and not cloaked (12); no admin hijacking: notices contextual and dismissible, no dashboard ads (11).
- readme: Contributors are case-sensitive WordPress.org usernames; short description ≤150 characters, no markup; 1–5 tags, no competitor names; `Tested up to` major version only; `Stable tag` is a version (never `trunk` for new plugins) and must also be right in `tags/X.Y.Z/readme.txt`; under 10 KB, older changelog in `changelog.txt`; `Requires at least`/`Requires PHP` are read from the main file since WordPress 5.8; check with the official readme validator.
- Assets in SVN `/assets/` (not in the zip): `banner-772x250` and `banner-1544x500` (png/jpg, ≤4 MB), `icon-128x128` and `icon-256x256` (png/jpg/gif, ≤1 MB) plus optional `icon.svg`, `screenshot-N` (png/jpg, ≤10 MB) captioned in `== Screenshots ==`. Suggest keeping sources in `.wordpress-org/`, excluded from the build.
- Review takes about 1–10 business days; reply from the same account; fix in the source repo.
- SVN after approval: `https://plugins.svn.wordpress.org/<slug>/` with `trunk/`, `tags/X.Y.Z/`, `assets/`; SVN password is separate from the account password; no zips in SVN; SVN is for releases, not development; release = commit trunk, `svn cp trunk tags/X.Y.Z`, `Stable tag: X.Y.Z`. Mention release confirmation emails (Handbook page of that name). An SVN deploy subcommand is out of scope here (see Scope Boundaries).

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** `plugin-check` uses `<prefix>-$$` names and removes only its own resources; other running WordPress containers on the host must be left alone.
- **Migration/rollback:** new files only; rollback is reverting the PR.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** Bash 3.2 compatible (macOS); BSD and GNU `sed`/`stat` differences (no `sed -i`, no `\I` flag); `shasum -a 256` or `sha256sum`.
- **Idempotency/retry:** builds overwrite their own zips; re-running is safe.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** EXIT traps remove temp folders and Docker resources; a failed build leaves no partial zip in `--out` (zip to temp, then move).

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/wp-plugin-release-helper.sh
# Scratch plugin: a temp git repo with wp scaffold plugin output (or a minimal main file + readme.txt + .distignore), committed.
.agents/scripts/wp-plugin-release-helper.sh build --out <tmp>/dist      # two zips, one <slug>/ folder each
.agents/scripts/wp-plugin-release-helper.sh preflight --offline          # exit 0 or warnings only
# Negative: add "Update URI:" and "Version: 1.0.0-beta1" without committing, then test the stash commit:
.agents/scripts/wp-plugin-release-helper.sh preflight --ref "$(git stash create)" --offline   # ERRORs, exit 1
.agents/scripts/wp-plugin-release-helper.sh plugin-check                 # Plugin Check runs; Docker resources gone afterwards
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Surface mapping:** `build` proves layout/exclusions/naming; `preflight` positive and negative runs prove the error/warning gates; `plugin-check` proves Docker lifecycle and parsing; linters cover shell style and docs.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required (new helper and docs; no shared contracts).

### Scope Boundaries

**Hard boundaries:** the helper never creates tags, pushes, publishes GitHub releases, uploads to WordPress.org or commits to SVN. No changes to WordPress update behaviour in any plugin. An `svn-deploy` subcommand is a separate follow-up once tested against a real or local SVN repository.

**AI brief owner:** marcusquinn (interactive session that filed this issue).

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/wp-plugin-release-helper.sh`
- `.agents/tools/wordpress/wp-plugin-release.md`
- `.agents/tools/wordpress/wp-dev.md`
- `.agents/subagent-index.toon`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `build` produces `<slug>-X.Y.Z.zip` and `wordpress-org-<slug>-X.Y.Z.zip`, each with exactly one `<slug>/` top folder, files from the Git ref only, `.distignore` (and for WordPress.org `.distignore-wporg`) applied; two builds give identical `SHA256SUMS`.
- [ ] `preflight` exits 1 on a pre-release `Version:` or an `Update URI` header, and 0 on a clean scratch plugin.
- [ ] `plugin-check` runs Plugin Check on both zips, exits 1 when Plugin Check reports an error or does not run, and leaves no containers, volumes or networks.
- [ ] Nothing in the helper runs `git tag`, `git push`, `gh release`, `svn` or uploads.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "git tag |git push|gh release|svn (ci|commit)"
    path: ".agents/scripts/wp-plugin-release-helper.sh"
    expect: absent
  ```

- [ ] `wp-dev.md` points to the new doc; the doc cites the Plugin Handbook pages it relies on.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "wp-plugin-release"
    path: ".agents/tools/wordpress/wp-dev.md"
  ```

- [ ] `shellcheck` and `linters-local.sh --changed` are clean.

## Context & Decisions

- Two builds rather than one: WordPress.org forbids updater code (guideline 8), but a GitHub channel through Git Updater needs it; per-channel exclusion keeps one source tree.
- The WordPress.org zip name must not start with the slug, so Git Updater cannot install it by mistake.
- Static checks belong in the helper; guideline judgement (services, notices, defaults, files written outside the plugin folder) stays a checklist.
- Not in scope: SVN deploy, asset generation, a CI workflow.

<!-- aidevops:sig -->

title: Pre-edit check refuses a manual-cli worker's own worktree (regression of #28426)
body:
## What

Regression of #28426: a headless worker launched with `dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh` (session key `manual-cli-<issue>-<epoch>`) is refused by `aidevops_pre_edit_check` on its own dispatcher-created worktree, because the tool treats the worker's own wrapper as "another active session/process".

## Reproducer

Launch a worker with `dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh` (manual path), and let its model call `aidevops_pre_edit_check` on the pre-created worktree. Observed once (v3.37.38, OpenCode 1.18.33, 2026-10-01); evidence below.

Worker failure excerpt `~/.aidevops/logs/worker-failure-excerpts/manual-cli-<issue>-1790835194-20261001T063400Z-71841.log` (the file suffix 71841 is this worker's wrapper PID), line 25, tool `aidevops_pre_edit_check` with `targetPaths` for two in-scope files:

```text
Pre-edit check exit 2: Create a worktree before proceeding with edits.
BLOCKED: linked worktree is owned by another active session/process
WORKTREE_OWNERSHIP_CONFLICT=true
ACTION_REQUIRED=create_worktree
WORKTREE_OWNER_PID=71841
WORKTREE_OWNER_SESSION=manual-cli-<issue>-1790835194
WORKTREE_OWNER_SINCE=2026-10-01T06:14:15Z
```

The reported owner PID and session are the worker's own. The worker then stopped without editing (`[WORKER_EXIT_DIAGNOSTICS] cause=premature_exit`), asked a human whether PID 71841 was stale, and released its claim with `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=worker_ownership_lost`. About 20 minutes of research work was left uncommitted in the worktree.

Pulse-dispatched workers (`issue-<N>` session keys) running at the same time did not hit this; I have only this one `manual-cli-*` occurrence today.

## Hypothesis (unverified)

The #28426 fix recognises the exact wrapper owner for pulse-dispatch session keys or environment, but the `manual-cli-*` launch path either does not export the same owner proof to the OpenCode child, or the proof check does not match that session-key form. Note: the manual launch's sandbox passthrough list does include `AIDEVOPS_WORKTREE_OWNER_PID`, `AIDEVOPS_WORKTREE_OWNER_SESSION` and `AIDEVOPS_ALLOW_WORKER_WORKTREE_OWNER_TRANSFER`.

## How

- Compare the owner-proof path from #28426 across the two launch paths:
  - `.agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh` (manual launch, session key `manual-cli-*`)

title: Bug: required ShellCheck (macos-latest) context never reports on non-shell PRs after #33218 scope gate
body:
## Observed

Branch protection on `main` requires the status context `ShellCheck (macos-latest)`. Since #33218 (merged 2026-09-30T10:39Z, closes #33197) added a job-level `if: needs.detect-scope.outputs.shell == 'true'` to the `cross-platform-shellcheck` matrix job in `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml`, PRs that change no shell files get a single skipped check run named literally `ShellCheck (${{ matrix.os }})`. The matrix never expands, so the required `ShellCheck (macos-latest)` context never reports and the PR stays `mergeStateStatus: BLOCKED`.

Evidence (2026-10-01):

- PR #33279 head `593b02d7085e`: check run `ShellCheck (${{ matrix.os }})` conclusion `skipped`; every other check green; `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED`.
- Pulse merge log: `_check_required_checks_passing: 1 required context(s) not passing for PR #33279 ... (1 never reported, 0 check(s) in flight)`. PR #33224 (Issue Sync, docs-only) has the same line.
- `gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/branches/main/protection/required_status_checks` lists `ShellCheck (macos-latest)`.
- The last 15 merged PRs (#33272–#33300) all touched `.sh` files. No docs- or deps-only PR has merged since the scope gate landed.

Impact: every non-shell PR (dependency bumps, docs, TODO sync, workflow-only) is blocked. This adds to the open-PR backlog and keeps the PR backlog guardrails suppressing dispatch.

## Fix

Keep the scope optimisation but make the required context always report. Use **one** of these, whichever fits the existing workflow best:

1. Move the scope condition from job level to step level. Keep `runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}` and the matrix, and add `if: needs.detect-scope.outputs.shell == 'true'` to each heavy step (install ShellCheck, ShellCheck, Bash 3.2 syntax, platform smoke, model replay macOS). Matrix legs then expand and report `ShellCheck (ubuntu-latest)` / `ShellCheck (macos-latest)` as success with only checkout run. Checkout can also be gated.
2. Or add a small always-running job named exactly `ShellCheck (macos-latest)` that succeeds when `detect-scope.outputs.shell != 'true'`. Mutually exclusive `if` conditions prevent duplicate contexts.

Prefer option 1: no duplicate-name risk and no branch-protection change.

### Files Scope

- `.github/workflows/code-quality.yml`

Do not change branch protection. Do not remove the scope gate added by #33218.

## Verification

- `actionlint .github/workflows/code-quality.yml` (if available) and repo workflow lint via existing pre-commit hooks.
- After the PR's own CI runs (the PR touches no `.sh`, so it exercises the skip path): `gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/commits/<head>/check-runs --jq '.check_runs[]|select(.name|startswith("ShellCheck"))|{name,conclusion}'` must show `ShellCheck (macos-latest)` with conclusion `success`, and the PR must not be BLOCKED on that context.
- Regression: a PR that changes a `.sh` file must still run full ShellCheck on both OSes. Confirm from the job log of the next shell-touching PR.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Non-shell PRs report `ShellCheck (macos-latest)` = success without running the full lint.
- [ ] Shell-touching PRs still run full ShellCheck plus Bash 3.2 validation on macOS.
- [ ] #33279 and #33224 become mergeable after a rebase/re-run once this lands.

title: Bug: consolidation pre-flight Gate 3 ignores reopen-after-merge, permanently deferring reopened file-size-debt issues
body:
## Observed

A file-size-debt issue reopened by the Large File Simplification Gate can never be dispatched. That also permanently holds every bug the gate parks behind it.

Live case (2026-10-01):

1. Bug #33303 was deferred: `Large-file gate: #33303 ... targets .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh (2291 lines)`. The gate reopened the canonical file-size-debt issue #28838.
2. Dispatching #28838 logs:
   - `Consolidation pre-flight: #28838 in marcusquinn/aidevops — merged closing PR #28842 → skip (t3050)`
   - `Dispatch deferred for #28838 in marcusquinn/aidevops: issue needs comment consolidation`
3. PR #28842 merged on 2026-07-29T02:50:56Z. #28838 was reopened on 2026-10-01T07:41:47Z, after several earlier close/reopen cycles, so the merge belongs to an earlier lifecycle.

Result: `_issue_needs_consolidation` is true (the close/reopen churn left many comments), and `_dispatch_issue_consolidation` aborts at Gate 3 of `_consolidation_skip_if_resolved`. `_dispatch_dedup_scope_gates` still returns 1 ("deferred"). Each cycle the issue is neither consolidated nor dispatched, and #33303 stays held.

## Root cause

GH#33071 taught `dispatch-dedup-pr.sh` (`_ddpr_first_merge_after_reopen`, about line 715) that a merged closing PR older than the issue's latest reopen belongs to an earlier lifecycle (`REOPENED_AFTER_MERGE`). The sibling Gate 3 in `_consolidation_skip_if_resolved` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-triage-dispatch.sh`, about lines 840–852) still treats any structurally linked merged PR as "resolved", with no reopen-time comparison.

There is a second defect in `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh` `_dispatch_dedup_scope_gates` (about lines 488–493): it defers dispatch even when `_dispatch_issue_consolidation` declined to create a consolidation child. A skipped consolidation must not become a permanent defer.

## Fix

- In `_consolidation_skip_if_resolved` Gate 3, apply the same reopen-aware rule: skip only when the linked PR's `merged_at` is after the issue's latest `reopened` event. Reuse `_ddpr_first_merge_after_reopen` or its timeline lookup rather than duplicating it. Fail open on lookup errors, as Gate 3 already does.
- In `_dispatch_dedup_scope_gates`, defer only when a consolidation child was actually dispatched or is in flight. If the pre-flight skipped consolidation, continue to the remaining gates.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-triage-dispatch.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-triage.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-consolidation-skip-resolved.sh`, extending the existing Gate 3 case with a merged-before-reopen variant that must proceed.

Integration scope recovery (worker, GH#33306): `.agents/scripts/pulse-triage.sh` added because `_dispatch_issue_consolidation` owns the pre-flight skip branch (`_consolidation_dispatch_preflight_skips` returns 0 there with rc 0, indistinguishable from "child created/in flight"). It must expose a one-variable outcome so `_dispatch_dedup_scope_gates` can stop deferring on a skip. No other caller behaviour changes.

## Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-consolidation-skip-resolved.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-triage-dispatch.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-triage.sh
```

Live check after deploy: `pulse-wrapper.sh --command dispatch 28838 marcusquinn/aidevops ...` no longer logs `merged closing PR #28842 → skip` followed by `Dispatch deferred ... needs comment consolidation`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Merged closing PR after the latest reopen: Gate 3 still skips (existing regression case keeps passing).
- [ ] Merged closing PR before the latest reopen: Gate 3 proceeds.
- [ ] A consolidation pre-flight skip no longer defers implementation dispatch indefinitely.

title: Pulse batch dispatch starved: merge pass consumes cycle budget, dispatch_max processes 0 candidates for 45+ min
body:
## What

The pulse's batch dispatch path dispatched no implementation workers for about 45 minutes. Each dispatch pass began after the cycle wall-clock budget was already used up, mostly by the deterministic merge pass. Eligible `auto-dispatch` issues sat at `status:available` while the class cap had free slots: 0 class-capped workers were active and the cap was 4.

## Reproducer

There is no synthetic reproducer. The evidence comes from `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` (v3.37.38) for the long-lived pulse process started at `2026-10-01T06:45:09Z` (pid 7139).

**Symptom command:** `rg -n -e "deterministic_merge_pass timing" -e "per-candidate floor" -e "implementation_dispatched=" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`

**Actual output**, from one cycle's merge pass:

```text
deterministic_merge_pass timing: repo=<managed-private-repo> total_s=356 list_s=3 list_state=complete mergeability_s=19 ruleset_s=6 branch_protection_s=9 stuck_detector_s=0 merged=1 closed=0 failed=0 prs=12
deterministic_merge_pass timing: total_s=528 merged=1 closed_conflicting=0 failed=0 eligible_unmerged=0
```

For that repo, the named sub-timings add up to about 37 s of the 356 s total, so about 319 s is unattributed.

Every later dispatch pass then reported (abridged):

```text
Dispatch_max stopping early: cycle wall-clock budget below per-candidate floor (remaining=-201s floor=600s)
Dispatch path=max complete: implementation_dispatched=0 ... processed=0/25 simultaneous_worker_slots_targeted=7
... remaining=-458s ... implementation_dispatched=0 ... processed=0/23
... remaining=-695s ... implementation_dispatched=0 ... processed=0/25
... remaining=-883s ... implementation_dispatched=0 ... processed=0/25
```

Over the same period, the worker-exit event refill path still dispatched 2 workers (`[dispatch_with_dedup] Dispatched worker PID ... for #...`). Batch dispatch was the only path starved. Earlier in the same process, a pass dispatched with `remaining=588s floor=600s` stopping early after 3 candidates.

## Impact

A 12-award batch queue in that repo idled with 0 class-capped workers until the maintainer session launched workers manually (07:53Z).

## How (investigation first)

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` and the merge-pass module that emits `deterministic_merge_pass timing`. Find the unattributed time: per-PR review-bot gate, hygiene sync, or closing-comment work. Add it to the timing line.
- Find where `Dispatch_max` computes `remaining`. Then decide (maintainer trade-off; the 600 s floor itself must not be lowered without authorization):
  - (a) Cap the merge pass's share of the cycle budget, deferring the remaining PRs to the next cycle.
  - (b) Reserve at least one per-candidate floor for dispatch before the merge pass starts.
  - (c) Let the dispatch pass take at least N candidates whenever class-cap slots are free and nothing is active.
- Keep the existing early-stop safety for genuinely overrun cycles.

## Acceptance

- With free class-cap slots and eligible issues, a long merge pass no longer causes repeated `implementation_dispatched=0` cycles.
- The merge-pass timing line accounts for most of its `total_s`.

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh
rg -n "per-candidate floor|implementation_dispatched=" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log
```

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-pass.sh` (deterministic merge-pass module; per-repo timing row)
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-timing.sh` (emits the `deterministic_merge_pass timing` line)
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh` (adjacent integration, GH#33307 worker scope recovery: the per-repo PR loop where backlog enrichment and per-PR processing time is spent; required to attribute the unattributed `total_s`)

title: pulse: cycle index records dispatched:0 for a cycle that launched a worker
body:
## What

`pulse-cycle-index.jsonl` can record `"dispatched":0` for a pulse cycle in which a worker was launched successfully. Operators read this file to answer "did pulse do anything", so the miscount leads to wrong conclusions about idle versus working cycles.

## Evidence (project repo names omitted)

- `dispatch-stages.tsv` has a completed `dedup.worker_launch_total` row for one issue at 12:06:27Z, with run id `20261001T120145Z-61051`.
- The cycle with that run id finished at 12:23:07Z. Its `pulse-cycle-index.jsonl` record reads: `{"ts":"2026-10-01T12:23:07Z","duration_s":1239,"workers":"0/2","dispatched":0,"merged":0,"closed":0,"killed":0,"prefetch_errors":0}`.
- So a successful launch inside the cycle was recorded as `dispatched:0`.

## Not yet established

- Whether the counter intentionally counts only a different launch path (for example the LLM supervisor path versus the deterministic `dispatch_with_dedup` path), or whether the early-dispatch / refill stages are not counted. The implementer should confirm which stages feed the counter.
- Whether `workers:0/2` is sampled at cycle end, which would hide workers that finished or were launched earlier.

## Files to modify

- The writer of `pulse-cycle-index.jsonl` in the pulse wrapper (locate with `rg -n 'pulse-cycle-index' .agents/scripts`).
- The counters it reads for `dispatched` (locate where `dispatch_with_dedup` successes are accumulated).

Reference pattern: the `dedup.worker_launch_total` stage record already written for each launch is a reliable source.

## Verification

- Add or extend a test that runs one simulated cycle with a successful deterministic launch and asserts `dispatched >= 1` in the index record.
- Cross-check against `dispatch-stages.tsv`: the number of completed `dedup.worker_launch_total` rows within a cycle's run id equals `dispatched`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A cycle that launches N workers through any dispatch path records `dispatched: N`.
- [ ] The field's definition (what counts, when `workers` is sampled) is documented next to the writer.
- [ ] Existing cycle-index tests still pass.

title: pulse: publication:pending issues without tNNN title are blocked forever and starve the repair window
body:
## What

Issues that carry `publication:pending` but have no `tNNN` title prefix and no TODO.md task line can never be reconciled. They stay dispatch-blocked indefinitely, and pulse reports nothing actionable. In one observed run, 8 worker-ready issues sat blocked for about 5 hours while pulse ran 8 cycles at 0/3 worker capacity.

## Why

The publication fence is intended to hold dispatch only until the planning commit reaches the default branch. For issues outside the `tNNN` scheme, the reconciler cannot ever confirm publication, so the fence has no exit path other than manual label removal.

## Evidence (project repo names omitted)

- A roadmap batch of issues titled like `PF-D03: Benchmark ...` (no `tNNN` prefix) was created with `publication:pending`. A search of the project's TODO.md finds no task lines for them.
- Issue event timeline for one of them: `publication:pending` labeled 07:28Z, planning commit landed on the default branch 08:35Z, label removed 12:42Z (manual removal, same actor as the owner token). Total block: about 5h14m.
- `pulse.log` contains 144 lines `Dispatch blocked for #N in <repo>: publication:pending label present` over the window. `dispatch-stages.tsv` shows every candidate attempt ending at stage `dedup.publication_pending` with no worker spawn.
- Seven consecutive `PUBLICATION_RECONCILE_SUMMARY reconciled=0 deferred=0 stale=0 failed=10` lines from about 08:05Z, one per pulse pass, with no changes in between. `failed=10` equals the pulse repair window.
- `pulse-cycle-index.jsonl` showed `dispatched:0`, `workers:0/3` for all these cycles. Nothing in pulse output named the real cause.

## Root cause (verified by reading the code)

1. `cmd_reconcile` in `planning-publication-reconcile.sh` (loop over pending issues, around lines 325-351) extracts the task id with `grep -oE '^t[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)*'` on the title. A title without that prefix hits `failed=$((failed + 1)); continue`, silently and every pass. There is no stale/escalation path for this branch (the stale path only applies to rc=3 mapping misses).
2. `_repair_pending_planning_publications` in `pulse-issue-reconcile.sh` (around lines 1295-1313) calls the reconciler with `AIDEVOPS_PUBLICATION_RECONCILE_LIMIT=10`. `gh issue list` returns newest first, so ten permanently unpublishable issues fill the window every cycle. Newer, valid `tNNN` issues beyond the window can starve. (This starvation was not observed; it follows from the code and the observed `failed=10`.)
3. The dispatch gate in `pulse-dispatch-core.sh` (around line 367) blocks on the label alone and logs per attempt. It has no age-based escalation or one-time warning.

## Files to modify

- `.agents/scripts/planning-publication-reconcile.sh` (`cmd_reconcile` title parsing and failure accounting)
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh` (`_repair_pending_planning_publications` window and logging)
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh` (gate message; optional age-based diagnostic)
- Related tests: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-planning-publication-reconcile.sh`, `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-core-publication-pending.sh`

Reference pattern: the existing rc=3 / `PUBLICATION_STALE_HOURS` handling in `cmd_reconcile` (deferred vs stale accounting).

## Suggested approach (implementer decides)

- Treat a pending issue with no `tNNN` title prefix as a distinct, explicitly reported class (for example `unmapped=N`) rather than a generic failure. Do not let it consume the repair window.
- Apply the same age-based escalation as the stale path: after `PUBLICATION_STALE_HOURS`, emit one visible diagnostic (log plus a single idempotent issue comment) naming the cause and the fix, instead of silently retaining the label.
- Order or paginate the repair window so unpublishable issues cannot starve valid ones.
- Decide separately whether issue-creation paths should refuse to apply `publication:pending` to issues that have no TODO.md mapping. The creating path in this run is unknown.

## Verification

- Add a test where the pending set includes N titles without a `tNNN` prefix plus one valid `tNNN` issue; assert the valid one is reconciled and the summary reports the unmapped class distinctly.
- Assert that an unmapped issue older than the stale threshold produces exactly one diagnostic, not one per pass.
- Run `shellcheck` on the modified scripts and the existing publication tests.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Unmapped pending issues are reported explicitly and do not consume the repair window.
- [ ] A valid `tNNN` pending issue behind 10+ unmapped ones is still reconciled in the same pass.
- [ ] Stale unmapped issues surface one non-repeating diagnostic that names the cause.
- [ ] No existing publication test regresses; `publication:pending` is still never removed without published-state verification.

title: consolidated: reopen-aware consolidation gates and skipped-child dispatch handoff
body:
_Supersedes #33306 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Fix consolidation pre-flight and dispatch handoff so reopened file-size-debt issues are not permanently deferred by a merged PR from an earlier lifecycle, and implementation dispatch continues when consolidation pre-flight skips without creating or finding an in-flight consolidation child.

## Why

Observed on 2026-10-01: bug #33303 was deferred by the Large File Simplification Gate because `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh` had 2291 lines. The gate reopened canonical file-size-debt issue #28838. Dispatching that issue logged:

```text
Consolidation pre-flight: #28838 in marcusquinn/aidevops — merged closing PR #28842 → skip (t3050)
Dispatch deferred for #28838 in marcusquinn/aidevops: issue needs comment consolidation
```

PR #28842 merged at 2026-07-29T02:50:56Z; issue #28838 was reopened at 2026-10-01T07:41:47Z after earlier close/reopen cycles. The merge belongs to an earlier lifecycle. Comment churn makes `_issue_needs_consolidation` true, Gate 3 aborts consolidation, and `_dispatch_dedup_scope_gates` still returns 1. Neither consolidation nor implementation proceeds, so #33303 remains held.

Per @marcusquinn, a second live instance affects Gate 5: open bug #33057 (`status:available`, `tier:thinking`) logs `Consolidation pre-flight: #33057 ... 1/1 child PRs merged → skip (t3050)` followed by `Dispatch deferred for #33057 ... issue needs comment consolidation`. Its only body reference is #17671, a framework trust-boundary reference rather than a child issue. Gate 5 counts it as a merged child. The issue has been permanently deferred since at least 2026-09-30T08:41Z (`consolidation-skipped` marker). Correcting the skipped-consolidation handoff resolves this deferral too; changing Gate 5 reference classification is not required for this fix.

## Reproducer

The parent report provides two observed reproductions, not a new live dispatch performed by this consolidation task:

1. With issue #28838 reopened after PR #28842 merged and substantive comment churn triggering consolidation, attempt its normal pulse dispatch. Actual result: Gate 3 emits `merged closing PR #28842 → skip`, then dispatch emits `issue needs comment consolidation` and defers. Expected result: the historical merge does not resolve the reopened lifecycle; consolidation or implementation can proceed through the remaining gates.
2. With issue #33057's contextual #17671 reference counted by Gate 5 as 1/1 merged children, attempt its normal pulse dispatch. Actual result: consolidation skips, then implementation is deferred anyway. Expected result: a pre-flight skip with no consolidation child does not indefinitely defer implementation.

The scoped test command in Verification is the safe local reproduction surface for both regression cases; live dispatch must use the documented wrapper invocation and normal ownership protections.

## How

### Recover existing work first

PR #33312 is CLOSED and its head commit `aff9986398e4a9d1d4ea065eedf5c8e60c41f737` remains pushed on `feature/auto-20261001-085656-gh33306` (verified 2026-10-01 during consolidation). Recover these commits and continue them rather than restarting. Rebase the recovered work onto current `origin/main`, inspect the diff, and repair the code without weakening CI.

The previous PR had a terminal **Complexity Analysis** failure:

- https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/actions/runs/36837335618/job/110288073213
- Feedback identity: `ci:PR33312:SHAaff9986398e4a9d1d4ea065eedf5c8e60c41f737`.
- The bounded in-place repair exhausted its retry budget: attempts 1 and 2 both reported stage `head_fetch`, result `launch_failed`, failure reason `pr_head_fetch_failed`, next action `verify_remote_branch_access_and_retry`.
- Original fallback: restore access to the branch and rerun deterministic merge pass; keep PR #33312 open until retry is impossible. This preservation instruction is now superseded by the verified CLOSED PR state, but its commits remain salvageable.

Read the terminal failed check evidence before repairing, preserve accumulated CI/review feedback, and address every terminal failing check caused by the replacement changes, including advisory checks. Report unrelated or pre-existing failures with evidence instead of expanding this task.

### Implementation

Current references verified against default-branch commit `1158a6ee0`:

1. `.agents/scripts/pulse-triage-dispatch.sh:808–874`, `_consolidation_skip_if_resolved`, Gate 3 at lines 840–852: skip only when a structurally linked PR actually merged in the current issue lifecycle, not before the latest `reopened` event. Preserve the no-reopen merged-PR skip case. Reuse `_ddpr_first_merge_after_reopen` or its timeline lookup from read-only reference `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-pr.sh:93–137`; the existing reopen-aware caller is around lines 715–729 (GH#33071). Avoid duplicating timeline logic. Fail open on lookup errors, as Gate 3 already does.
2. `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh:474–494`, `_dispatch_dedup_scope_gates`: defer for consolidation only when a child was actually dispatched or is in flight; if pre-flight skipped consolidation, continue to the remaining gates. Preserve existing manual-hold and active-ownership safety deferrals; a skip must not bypass them.
3. `.agents/scripts/pulse-triage.sh:227–269`, `_dispatch_issue_consolidation`: the pre-flight skip at lines 243–246 returns 0, currently indistinguishable from child-created/in-flight. Expose a one-variable outcome for the caller to distinguish this skip. This adjacent integration scope was explicitly authorized in the parent worker brief; do not change other callers' behavior.
4. `.agents/scripts/tests/test-consolidation-skip-resolved.sh`: extend the existing structurally linked merged-PR Gate 3 regression with a merge-before-latest-reopen variant that proceeds. Include a dispatch regression in which Gate 5 skips consolidation and implementation proceeds. Preserve the merge-after-reopen skip and actual-child deferral cases.

### Verification

Existing Bash scripts and scoped test file are present; ShellCheck 0.9.0 is available. Run:

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-consolidation-skip-resolved.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-triage-dispatch.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-triage.sh
```

Repair the recovered PR's Complexity Analysis failure using existing repository tooling and verify the replacement exact head. These checks were validated as existing paths/commands during consolidation, not run as implementation verification in the operational task.

Live check after authorized deploy: `pulse-wrapper.sh --command dispatch 28838 marcusquinn/aidevops ...` must no longer log `merged closing PR #28842 → skip` followed by `Dispatch deferred ... needs comment consolidation`. The ellipsis denotes existing required wrapper arguments, not a runnable literal command; use the documented wrapper invocation. This is a post-deploy validation, not independent deployment authority.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A linked closing PR merged after the latest reopen still makes Gate 3 skip; existing regression coverage keeps passing.
- [ ] A linked closing PR merged before the latest reopen makes Gate 3 proceed.
- [ ] A genuinely merged closing PR with no reopen still makes Gate 3 skip.
- [ ] Gate 3 lookup errors fail open without inventing resolution evidence.
- [ ] A consolidation pre-flight skip no longer indefinitely defers implementation dispatch; remaining gates still run.
- [ ] The Gate 5 skip case described for #33057 proceeds to implementation dispatch.
- [ ] A child actually dispatched or already in flight still defers implementation, and manual-hold/active-ownership protections and other caller behavior remain intact.
- [ ] Salvageable PR #33312 commits are recovered, its terminal Complexity Analysis failure is repaired without weakening CI, and all scoped verification plus terminal failures caused by the replacement changes are addressed.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-triage-dispatch.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-triage.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-consolidation-skip-resolved.sh

## Context & Decisions

- Original problem statement and reopen-aware approach: @marcusquinn. GH#33071 already established the lifecycle rule in the dedup helper; consolidation Gate 3 must reuse it rather than treating any historical merge as resolution.
- Per @marcusquinn's 2026-10-01T07:55:20Z comment, the self-hosting detector applied `tier:thinking` because `pulse-dispatch-` appears in the issue body. Workers fixing dispatch execute through the code being fixed. Retain the thinking tier to avoid lower-tier retry churn; runtime routing still owns the exact model/reasoning level. The recorded detector bypass is `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_SELF_HOSTING_DETECTOR=1`, not an instruction to use it. The one-time comment marker is `<!-- self-hosting-tier-override -->` (t2819).
- Per @marcusquinn's 2026-10-01T08:02:38Z comment, the defect is broader than reopened issues: Gate 5 can skip on a contextual non-child reference such as #17671. Acceptance must include this skip-and-proceed case.
- Parent integration-scope recovery authorized `.agents/scripts/pulse-triage.sh` because it owns the ambiguous successful pre-flight skip return. The one-variable outcome changes that handoff only; other caller behavior remains unchanged.
- Deterministic merge-pass CI feedback from PR #33312 is cumulative repair evidence, not a reason to discard prior work. The two fetch failures and current reachable branch are recorded above.
- Consolidation is operational task #33316. It does not implement this fix, alter repository code, or require a consolidation PR. This successor is explicitly handed off for implementation through `consolidated` plus `auto-dispatch`; it must not retain `needs-consolidation`, `consolidation-task`, or `consolidation-in-progress` labels.

title: full-loop: manual-release repos cannot record release:published; init/sync-workflows offer no release-verify caller
body:
## What happened

On a maintained, non-aidevops repository (private WordPress plugin, in `repos.json` with `init_scope: standard`, `pulse: false`), a feature PR was merged with `full-loop-helper.sh merge` and then released as `vX.Y.Z` in the same session. The release followed the repository's own documented manual process: a version-bump PR, an annotated tag on that PR's merge commit, and `gh release create` with one zip asset.

`full-loop-helper.sh record-published-release <feature-PR> vX.Y.Z <owner/repo>` then failed with:

```
Cannot record release:published: release, tag, and successful release workflow evidence do not match PR #N
```

The release, tag and asset were all correct, so the feature PR's lifecycle receipt is stuck as unreleased.

## Root causes (from `_full_loop_verify_published_release` in `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-state-lifecycle.sh`)

1. **The only accepted evidence is a successful GitHub Actions run** at the tag commit (`event=release`, or push/dispatch with `--workflow`). A repository that publishes by hand and has no workflows (this one has zero, and no `.github/`) can never meet it.
2. **The tag is on the version-bump PR's merge, not the feature PR's.** The check requires `tag_commit == merge_commit`, and deliberately refuses a generic ancestry check (`#aidevops:trust-boundary`). For non-aidevops repos, nothing records a feature PR as *included in* a later release. `release:superseded` exists only through the aidevops signed-tag aggregation trailers.
3. **`aidevops init` installs no workflows.** Callers come only from the opt-in `aidevops sync-workflows`, and `templates/workflows/` has no release caller. So "in repos.json, with a forge and runners" never produces release evidence today.

## Proposed fix

1. **Release-verify caller template:** add `templates/workflows/release-verify-caller.yml`, triggered on `release: published`. It is read-only (`contents: read`). It checks out the tag, confirms the release has the expected asset(s), and runs the repository's own preflight if one is configured. It never builds, tags or uploads anything, so it gives `event=release` evidence without changing who publishes. Repos where releases need the owner's say keep that.
2. **Offer it from init and sync-workflows:** `sync-workflows-helper.sh` (opt-in, PR per repo, as today) installs it for repos with a GitHub remote and Actions available. `aidevops init` offers it when the repo is registered with a forge remote. For Gitea/Forgejo, use the equivalent Actions path, or say clearly that it is unsupported.
3. **Inclusion receipt for feature PRs (trust boundary):** add a verified path that records a feature PR as `release:superseded` (or "included in") a release whose **source PR** already has a `release:published` receipt. It must link that receipt and verify the feature merge SHA is in the source PR's tag. Keep the existing ban on substituting ancestry for the release PR itself, and mark the new check `#aidevops:trust-boundary`.
4. **Manual-release documentation:** document this path for manual-release repos in `workflows/full-loop.md` (section 4.6 area) and `workflows/release.md` → Manual Release. Today the docs cover only the aidevops release and Cloudron catalog cases.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-state-lifecycle.sh` (`_full_loop_verify_published_release`, `cmd_record_published_release`)
- `.agents/scripts/sync-workflows-helper.sh`, `.agents/scripts/check-workflows-helper.sh`
- `.agents/templates/workflows/` (new caller)
- init flow (exact path not confirmed, likely `aidevops.sh` / the init helper)
- `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md`, `.agents/workflows/release.md`
- Tests: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-completion-evidence.sh`

## Verification

- A manual-release repo with the caller installed: create a release on a version-bump PR's merge, the workflow succeeds, `record-published-release <bump-PR>` records `release:published`, and the new inclusion command records the feature PR.
- Negative cases: a feature SHA that is not in the tag, a draft release, a failed workflow, and a source PR with no published receipt all fail closed and leave receipts unchanged.
- Repos without the caller keep today's behaviour.

<!-- aidevops:sig -->
