## Consolidation target: #28838

**Parent issue:** #28838 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`
**Parent title:** file-size-debt: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh exceeds 2000 lines
**Parent labels:** `status:available,auto-dispatch,tier:thinking,origin:worker,needs-consolidation,consolidation-in-progress,file-size-debt`

> You do **NOT** need to read #28838. Everything required is inlined below.
> Reading the parent wastes the token budget and is explicitly disallowed for this task.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `~/.aidevops/agents/templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `### Files Scope` — the successor's write surface, one repo-relative path per line and nothing else on the line (`- EDIT: path/to/file` or `- NEW: path/to/file`). Carry over the parent's scope when present. Read-only references belong in `## How`, not here. The pulse holds `auto-dispatch` briefs whose scope fails `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check`, so prose after a path makes the successor undispatchable.
   - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #28838 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`

3. **File the new consolidated issue:**

```bash
gh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,auto-dispatch,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body "<merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Without it, the issue is born `origin:interactive` (raw `gh issue create` has no origin auto-detection), which triggers the GH#18352 dispatch-dedup block and drains the queue.

**Dispatch handoff:** `auto-dispatch` is also mandatory. The consolidated successor marker and this explicit handoff must both be present before `_has_consolidated_label` permits implementation dispatch.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close the parent #28838:**

```bash
gh issue comment 28838 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 28838 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 28838 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
```

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #28838 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn @vladimirdulov."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

## Constraints

- **Do NOT read #28838** — it is inlined below. Reading it wastes the token budget.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.
- **Contributors to @-mention** on the new issue: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn @vladimirdulov

title: planning-publisher privacy scan blocks a private repo's own slug in its planning files
body:
## What

`planning-publisher.sh` `_planning_publish_validate` rejects a planning publication whose files mention the target repository's own slug, even when that target repository is private. The normal pre-push privacy guard skips private remotes; the planning publisher does not.

## Observed

- Interactive `/new-task` flow in a private managed project repo (placeholder: `<private-owner>/<private-repo>`).
- `claim-task-id.sh` created the issue; `brief-readiness-helper.sh stub <task> <issue> <slug>` captured the issue body into `todo/tasks/<task>-brief.md`. The capture provenance JSON includes `"url": "https://github.com/<private-owner>/<private-repo>/issues/N"` and `"repository": "<private-owner>/<private-repo>"`.
- `planning-commit-helper.sh "plan: ..."` then printed only `Planning publication validation failed; nothing pushed`.
- Re-running the same checks by hand found that `pre-commit-hook.sh` passed. `privacy_scan_diff` flagged the brief's own repo slug, its basename, and the production domain that contains the basename.
- Removing the provenance block and the domain allowed direct publication to succeed.

So the helper's own capture output cannot be published into the repo it describes, and the failure message does not give the reason.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/planning-publisher.sh` `_planning_publish_validate` (around lines 584-613): skip `privacy_scan_diff` (the private-slug scan, not the secret-material scan) when the publication remote is private. Reuse the visibility probe and cache in `.agents/scripts/privacy-guard-helper.sh` (around lines 100-160) that the pre-push guard already uses. Keep the scan fail-closed for public or unknown remotes.
- Print the privacy hits, or at least their file:line locations, when validation fails, so the reason is visible.
- Model the change on how the pre-push privacy guard decides to skip private targets.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/planning-publisher.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-planning-publisher.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- Publishing a planning file that contains the private target repo's own slug succeeds when the remote is private.
- The same content still fails when the remote is public, and the failure output names the offending file:line.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-planning-publisher.sh` and `shellcheck .agents/scripts/planning-publisher.sh` pass.
<!-- aidevops:origin:interactive -->

title: Pulse: stale permission requests from terminated sessions block redispatch and need manual sudo approval
body:
## Summary

Stale permission requests from terminated worker sessions block redispatch indefinitely and can only be cleared by a human running `sudo aidevops approve permissions ...`. Pulse knows the session is dead (CLAIM_RELEASED + terminal lease) but still waits for a human, and does not surface this in a way that distinguishes it from a stuck issue.

## Observed (v3.37.38, 3 pulse-enabled repos, single runner)

- Two `status:available` + `auto-dispatch` issues in one repo have not been dispatched for ~13 days. Pulse logs only `Reused existing verified conversation lock for #N` every cycle, with no skip reason.
- The only explanation is a Pulse-authored comment (posted by v3.37.37, still unresolved at v3.37.38): "Redispatch blocked — stale permission request ... session terminated (CLAIM_RELEASED + terminal lease). The unsigned request blocks automatic redispatch. Action required: aidevops approve permissions issue N <slug> --request perm-<id>".
- `aidevops approve verify-permissions issue N <slug>` returns `NO_APPROVAL`; granting requires `sudo`, so it cannot be done by an agent.
- `worker-activity-helper.sh summary --since 7d` reports 17 retained supervisor permission blockers; 12 are `permission_required` from `session_key=supervisor-pulse` itself (`source=opencode-permission-broker`), the oldest from Sept 18. `pulse-check-helper.sh` flags this as `retained-supervisor-permission-blockers` (medium) and recommends a manual `worker-blocker-cli.mjs resolve-stale-supervisor-session` run.
- The parent issue of the two blocked children is CLOSED, so nothing else will ever unblock them.

## Expected

1. A permission request whose owning session has a terminal lease should expire automatically (audited, non-blocking terminal event), and the issue should be redispatched with a fresh session, not require a human sudo approval for a dead session.
2. If a human decision is genuinely needed, apply a visible label (for example `needs-maintainer-review` or a dedicated `blocked:permission` label) and log the skip reason in `pulse.log` and `pulse-diagnose-helper.sh`.
3. Investigate why the `supervisor-pulse` session raises `permission_required` 12 times in 7 days. A headless supervisor should not need interactive bash permission, or the specific commands should be allowlisted.
4. Auto-resolve retained supervisor blockers whose session is stale, using the existing `resolve-stale-supervisor-session` command, instead of recommending it as a manual step.

## Files to investigate

Paths are unverified; start with `rg -n "Redispatch blocked" ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts` and `rg -n "resolve-stale-supervisor-session|permission_request_captured" ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts`, plus `worker-blocker-cli.mjs` and the dispatch-dedup path that emits `Reused existing verified conversation lock`.

## Verification

- Create a worker session, let it hit a permission gate, terminate it, and confirm the next pulse cycle either redispatches or applies a visible blocker label with a logged reason within one cycle.
- `worker-activity-helper.sh summary --since 7d` shows 0 retained supervisor blockers older than a defined TTL.
<!-- aidevops:origin:interactive -->
<!-- aidevops:sig -->

title: Pulse: recurring worker premature_exit (model_stopped_before_completion) with no visible resume outcome or model down-weighting
body:
## Summary

Headless workers repeatedly end with `premature_exit` / `launch_failure_cause=model_stopped_before_completion` (exit code 77). The failure family is classed `recovery_outcome=recurring` with `next_action=resume_session_with_completion_contract`, but I see no evidence in the 7-day summary that the resume path runs or succeeds.

## Observed (v3.37.38, 7-day window)

- 64 terminal session outcomes: 34 success, 15 blocked, 12 `premature_exit`, 2 `post_pr_handoff`, 1 `permission_required`. Runtime handoff rate is 65% against a productivity target flagged as missed by `pulse-check-helper.sh` (`worker-runtime-handoff-rate-regression`, medium).
- All 12 premature exits share one fingerprint: `ff-v1:launch-failure`, `kill_reason=natural`, `exit_code=77`, 12 distinct sessions, first about 2026-09-28, last 2026-10-01.
- In the five examples returned by the summary, every one used the same model (`openai/gpt-6.1-sol`). I did not verify whether all 12 did, so please check the provider/model split with `worker-activity-helper.sh providers --since 7d`.
- Sessions run 2 to 22 minutes before exiting, so each failure consumes real model spend and a worker slot.

## Expected

1. Confirm whether the `resume_session_with_completion_contract` next action is actually executed, and record the outcome (resumed, succeeded, abandoned) on the failure family.
2. If one model dominates the failures, down-weight or exclude it for the affected tier after N consecutive premature exits instead of continuing to route to it.
3. Report the per-model premature-exit rate in `pulse-check-helper.sh` so the dominant cause is visible without manual clustering.

## Files to investigate

Paths are unverified; start with `rg -n "model_stopped_before_completion|resume_session_with_completion_contract" ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts` and the model-routing/escalation code used by `headless-runtime-helper.sh`.

## Verification

- After the fix, the 7-day summary shows each `premature_exit` family with a resume outcome, and the handoff rate recovers above target.
- `worker-activity-helper.sh summary --since 7d --json` lists a per-model breakdown for failure families.

title: Pulse: worker blocked on missing human input recorded as reason=unknown and re-evaluated for dispatch every cycle
body:
## Summary

When a worker reports it is blocked on missing human input (for example an unavailable deployment target), the terminal blocker is recorded as `reason=unknown` and the issue returns to `status:available`. Pulse then re-evaluates and attempts to dispatch it every cycle, hitting `dedup_active_claim` each time. It burns API calls and cycle time, and the issue never shows as waiting on a human.

## Observed (v3.37.38)

- Worker comment: "BLOCKED: ... supplies no already-authorized staging HTTPS origin or independently verified deployment SHA ... No endpoint was guessed". It left a partial PR open.
- Pulse then posted: `Terminal blocker: reason=unknown owner=worker-triage ... Projected state: status:available. Next action: Interpret the protected dossier and record a known blocker class or repair the brief.`
- In the last hour `pulse-diagnose-helper.sh cycle-health` shows `dispatch_candidate_<N>` ran 6 times for that issue (p50 18s, p95 117s). `pulse.log` shows `non-dep block detected (comment-marker)` followed by `dispatch_with_dedup returned rc=1 ... blocked:dedup_active_claim benign dispatch block` on repeated cycles.
- The issue stays labelled `status:available` + `auto-dispatch`, so the queue count overstates dispatchable work: `pulse-check-helper.sh` reports "5 available (5 label-eligible; launch admission not verified)".

## Expected

1. Map "no authorised target / missing human input" worker blocks to a known blocker class (for example `needs-human-input`), apply a visible blocked label, and exclude the issue from candidate evaluation until a human comments.
2. Resolve the `reason=unknown` triage within one cycle, or time-box it, rather than leaving the issue dispatch-eligible in the meantime.
3. Make `pulse-check-helper.sh` report launch-admissible queue size separately from label-eligible size.

## Files to investigate

Paths are unverified; start with `rg -n "terminal-blocker-observation|worker-triage|non-dep block detected" ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts` and `rg -n "blocked:dedup_active_claim" ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts`.

## Verification

- A worker that reports blocked-on-human-input results in the issue leaving the dispatch candidate list until a human reply, with at most one dispatch attempt logged.
- `pulse-diagnose-helper.sh cycle-health` shows no repeated `dispatch_candidate_<N>` runs for it.
<!-- aidevops:origin:interactive -->

title: Consolidated successor issues are created without status:available and never dispatch
body:
## What

Consolidated successor issues are created without any `status:*` label. The pulse fill-floor enumerator skips them silently, so they never dispatch. Fix the consolidation-task brief so successors are created with `status:available`. Preferably also route creation through the signed wrapper, not raw `gh issue create`.

## Evidence (managed project repo, 2026-10-01)

- Three consolidation successors were filed on the same day by consolidation-task workers. Each carried `consolidated,origin:worker,auto-dispatch,tier:standard` plus parent labels, and none had a `status:*` label. The issue timeline shows that label set applied at creation and nothing added afterwards.
- `backfill-status-available.sh --dry-run --repo <slug>` listed exactly those three as candidates. `--apply` healed them (`found=3 applied=3 failed=0`).
- `pulse.log` shows only a conversation-lock reuse line for one successor and no dispatch-candidate lines, which is consistent with the enumerator skipping it.
- One successor also listed `- NEW:` for a brief and a spec that already existed on the default branch, merged by an earlier recovery PR. The template's Files Scope guidance doesn't tell the worker to check the default branch for existing paths, so a `NEW` scope can contradict the repo state.

## Root cause

`.agents/scripts/pulse-triage-dispatch.sh` (deployed copy, lines 91-98): step 3 of the consolidation-task brief template instructs:

```
gh issue create --repo "${repo_slug}" \
  --title "consolidated: ..." \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,auto-dispatch,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>"
```

The required label list has no `status:available`. Workers reasonably drop the parent's `status:*` label because the parent is being closed.

## How (suggested)

1. In the template in `.agents/scripts/pulse-triage-dispatch.sh`, add `status:available` to the mandatory label list. Exclude parent `status:*` labels explicitly so there is exactly one status.
2. Optional: in the Files Scope guidance (line 85), tell the worker to mark a path `EDIT:` when it already exists on the default branch (`git ls-files` / `gh api .../contents`).
3. Optional hardening: in the consolidation-task completion path, or a reconcile pass, add `status:available` to any open `consolidated` + `auto-dispatch` issue that has no `status:*` label, so the routine heals without a manual backfill.

## Verification

- `tests/test-consolidation-dispatch.sh` and `tests/test-pulse-consolidation-phase2.sh` pass.
- Grep the generated brief text for `status:available` in the step-3 label list.
- Optional: a fixture for the reconcile heal, if step 3 is implemented.
<!-- aidevops:origin:interactive -->
<!-- aidevops:sig -->

title: bug(cleanup): ownerless async lock directory wedges cleanup forever (disk-full deadlock)
body:
## Bug

The mkdir-based async cleanup locks never recover from an **ownerless** lock directory (directory exists, `pid` file missing or empty). `_lock_acquire` only reclaims a lock when a `pid` file exists, is non-empty, and the PID is dead. Otherwise it returns 1 and the caller logs `Lock held by live instance — skipping this invocation` forever.

An ownerless lock is created whenever a run dies between `mkdir "$LOCK_DIR"` and the PID write (SIGKILL, OOM, reboot, or a disk-full PID write). Three of the four helpers write the PID with `|| true`, so a full disk guarantees an ownerless lock.

This is a self-reinforcing failure: a full disk wedges cleanup, and wedged cleanup keeps the disk full.

## Evidence (observed on a Linux host)

- `cleanup_worktrees.lock` was an empty directory from 2026-09-24T21:31Z; last successful cycle 2026-09-24T21:11Z (`cleanup_worktrees.last-run`).
- Every later invocation logged `Lock held by live instance` while no cleanup process existed.
- Recovery maintenance runs after each successful cleanup cycle, so recovery-archive reclamation (22 GB store) also did not run for 7 days.
- The wedge was cleared only by manually running `rmdir` on the empty directory.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/cleanup-worktrees-lock.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/cleanup-stashes-async-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/cleanup-remote-branches-async-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive-async-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-cleanup-worktrees-async.sh`

## Fix

Treat a lock as stale when it has no valid owner AND is older than a grace period:

1. No `pid` file, empty `pid` file, or non-numeric content, and the lock directory mtime is older than `AIDEVOPS_LOCK_OWNERLESS_GRACE_SECONDS` (default 300).
2. Reclaim with the same `rm -rf` + `mkdir` re-acquire sequence the dead-PID branch already uses, and log the age: `Reclaiming ownerless lock (age Ns)`.
3. A young ownerless lock (inside the grace period) must still be treated as held, because a live acquirer may be between `mkdir` and the PID write.
4. Replace the misleading `Lock held by live instance` message with one that distinguishes live holder vs ownerless-young.

Use a portable mtime read (Linux `stat -c %Y`, macOS `stat -f %m`); see the stat portability rules in `reference/shell-style-guide.md`. Keep Bash 3.2 compatibility and explicit `return` in every function.

## Reference pattern

The dead-PID reclaim branch already in each `_lock_acquire` (`Reclaiming stale lock (PID ... no longer alive)`).

## Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-cleanup-worktrees-async.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/cleanup-worktrees-lock.sh .agents/scripts/cleanup-stashes-async-helper.sh .agents/scripts/cleanup-remote-branches-async-helper.sh .agents/scripts/opencode-db-archive-async-helper.sh
```

Add cases to the existing test: (a) ownerless lock older than grace is reclaimed and cleanup runs; (b) ownerless lock younger than grace is NOT reclaimed; (c) empty `pid` file older than grace is reclaimed.

## Out of scope

Separate problem: recovery archive deletion stays blocked by `cwd-visibility-degraded` until the opt-in CWD inspector is installed (see `reference/worktree-cwd-visibility.md`). Do not add process-name exemptions (GH#31882).
<!-- aidevops:origin:interactive -->
<!-- aidevops:sig -->

title: aidevops update fails on apt hosts: tap-qualified brew formulas resolved via unrelated apt package
body:
## Problem

On Linux hosts with `apt-get` but no Homebrew, `aidevops update` can fail on every run:

```
sudo apt-get install --only-upgrade -y steveyegge/beads/bd
E: Unable to locate package steveyegge/beads
Tool maintenance failed: 1 action(s) did not complete or verify.
```

## Root cause

`_tool_latest_version` in `.agents/scripts/tool-version-check.sh` resolves `brew`-category entries without brew via `get_apt_candidate "${pkg##*/}"`. Stripping the tap prefix turns `steveyegge/beads/bd` into apt package `bd`, an unrelated Ubuntu tool (`bd 1.03-3`). The installed Beads `0.61.0` then looks outdated, the entry is queued, and the update command passes the full tap name to `apt-get`, which cannot resolve it.

title: Dispatch classes need runner capability requirements so runners without required secrets defer instead of claiming
body:
## What

Let an issue, or its `dispatch-class:*`, declare runner requirements: named secrets that must resolve via `aidevops secret`, and optionally a local-data probe. A pulse runner that doesn't meet them should then defer the candidate, logging a `runner_capability_unmet` reason, instead of claiming it. Runners that do meet them dispatch as normal.

## Why (evidence, managed project repo, 2026-10-01)

A data-publication class needs maintainer-held staging credentials and a current local database. Two of its issues were claimed by peer maintainers' runners that had neither:

- **Issue A:** the peer runner's dry run failed with "No award exactly matches worker artifact target" because its local DB was stale. The worker stopped. The work had to be salvaged and later consolidated into a successor issue, costing several hours of wall-clock time.
- **Issue B:** the peer runner had its GPG/gopass store locked and no admin credentials. The worker built correct specs and opened a non-closing PR, then released with `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked` and an `unknown` terminal-blocker class. The issue returned to `status:available` and needs a second dispatch on a capable runner to publish.

In both cases, nothing published, and the second runner had to redo verification. The brief can only tell a worker to block after it starts; the dispatcher has no way to send the work elsewhere before it claims.

## How (suggested)

1. Add an optional requirement declaration per dispatch class. For example, in repo `.aidevops.json`:
   - `dispatch_class_requirements: { "<class>": { "secrets": [...], "probe": "<repo-relative command>" } }`
   - or a `requires-secrets:` line in the brief.
2. In the pulse candidate filter, before the dispatch claim, check that each named secret resolves, by name only, without reading values. Optionally run the probe with a short timeout. If unmet, defer with a distinct reason and post no claim.
3. Add a terminal-blocker class `runner_capability_unmet`, so a worker that finds missing credentials after claiming releases with a known class rather than `unknown`.

Target files: `pulse-dispatch-core.sh` (candidate gate); `dispatch-dedup-assignment.sh` or the candidate filters; `reference/dispatch-blockers.md` (document the reason); the terminal-blocker classification. Exact insertion points need confirming against the current candidate pipeline.

## Verification

- Unit fixture: a candidate with a class requiring an unresolvable secret is deferred with `runner_capability_unmet`, and with a resolvable one it proceeds.
- `shellcheck` is clean on the changed scripts.

title: Large-file gate path extractor matches .json/.jsonl as .js and gates data-only briefs
body:
## What

`_large_file_gate_extract_paths` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-large-file-gate.sh` (deployed copy, lines 201-205) matches code targets with:

```
grep -oE '`[^`]*\.(sh|py|js|ts)[^`]*`'
```

The extension group has no end anchor, so `.json` and `.jsonl` match through the `.js` prefix. (`.tsx`, `.tsv` and `.shtml` match the same way.) Data-only briefs whose Files Scope lists only `.md`, `.json` and `.jsonl` paths are therefore treated as code-edit targets and enter the large-file gate.

## Why it matters (evidence, managed project repo, 2026-10-01)

- Data-only enrichment issues list `- NEW: <dir>/specs/<slug>*.json` and `- NEW: <dir>/log/*/*/<slug>-*.jsonl`. Piping one issue body through the extractor's two greps returns both globs.
- Whenever the canonical mirror lags the remote default branch, which happens after every merge because nothing fast-forwards it (see aidevops#32453), the gate then logs `Large-file gate: deferring #N ... is not at the verified remote default-branch commit` for every such issue. It returns rc=1, and `blocked:policy_gate benign dispatch block` follows. One pulse cycle deferred all 4 eligible candidates this way while the class cap had free slots. Two separate stalls on the same day needed a manual audited fast-forward to clear.
- These briefs edit no code file, so the gate should never apply to them.

## How

1. Anchor the extension in the backtick pattern so the match must end at the closing backtick or a `:line` qualifier. Include the code extensions that currently match only by accident, such as `.tsx`. For example: `` '`[^`]*\.(sh|py|js|jsx|mjs|cjs|ts|tsx)(:[0-9]+(-[0-9]+)?)?`' ``. Keep the t2024 line-qualifier forms working (`file.sh:10-20`).
2. Review the first `agents/scripts/` pattern on line 175 for the same prefix issue: `[^`"[:space:],]+` accepts any extension, which is probably intended there.
3. Optional: skip glob targets (`*`), which can't be measured by `wc -l` anyway.

## Verification

- Extend `tests/test-large-file-gate-*.sh` (or the nearest extractor test) with cases:
  - `- NEW: \`a/b*.json\`` and `- NEW: \`x/*.jsonl\`` extract nothing.
  - `- EDIT: \`x.sh:10-20\``, `- EDIT: \`y.ts\`` and `- EDIT: \`c.tsx\`` still extract.
- `shellcheck` is clean on the changed script.
### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-large-file-gate.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-large-file-gate-extract-edit-only.sh`

title: Security posture misses nested tracked .env.* files and lacks encrypted-secret remediation guidance
body:
## Goal

Make the security-posture tracked-secret check catch committed env files in subdirectories. When it flags a file, give safe remediation that moves secrets out of plaintext files and into encrypted `aidevops secret` storage.

Follow-up to #33339 / PR #33350.

## Evidence

`_check_tracked_secret_files` in `.agents/scripts/security-posture-helper-repo.sh` lists candidates with:

```bash
git -C "$repo_path" ls-files '*.env' '*.pem' '*.key' 'credentials.json' '.env.*'
```

Git pathspec `'.env.*'` only matches at the repository root. Probe with a scratch repo tracking `.env`, `.env.local`, `app/.env`, `app/.env.local`, `app/.env.production`, `services/api/.env.example` and `app/x.env`:

- Current pathspecs match: `.env`, `.env.local`, `app/.env`, `app/x.env`.
- **Missed**: `app/.env.local`, `app/.env.production`, `services/api/.env.example`.
- Adding `'*/.env.*'` matches all seven.

Monorepos therefore get a PASS while committing real per-service env files, which is the opposite of the #33339 false positive.

The current critical message has no remediation guidance. Users are not told how to get the secret out of git safely or where to keep it instead.

## Scope

1. **Detection**: add `'*/.env.*'` to the `ls-files` pathspec in `_check_tracked_secret_files`. Nested templates (`services/api/.env.example`) then go through the existing content classifier from #33350, because `_posture_is_env_template_path` already matches on basename. Nested real env files (`app/.env.local`) become critical by filename, which is the intended behaviour change.
2. **Remediation output** (printed after the critical line, using the same `print_info` style as other posture fixes). The guidance must never echo values:
   - Rotate any credential that was committed. Removing the file does not remove it from git history.
   - Store each value encrypted with `aidevops secret set <NAME>` (gopass/GPG-backed; the value is entered at a hidden terminal prompt, never in chat or in files). Run `aidevops secret init` first if the store is not initialised.
   - Use secrets at runtime through `aidevops secret run <cmd>` or `aidevops secret <NAME> -- <cmd>` instead of a plaintext `.env`.
   - Stop tracking the file with `git rm --cached <path>` and add it to `.gitignore`. Keep a template copy (`.env.example`) that contains names or placeholders only.
   - Point to `reference/secret-handling.md` for the full policy. The `credentials.sh` plaintext fallback (chmod 600) is mentioned only as a fallback, never as the primary recommendation.
3. Keep the existing redaction contract: the output names the path, reason class and line only.

Out of scope: history-rewriting tools (filter-repo/BFG) as automatic actions. They may be mentioned as a manual option after rotation, never run.

### Files Scope

title: Worker git push still fails closed at network-policy helper timeout under load after #32955 retry
body:
## What

Headless workers still fail `git push` closed at the shared network-policy helper's 10-second timeout under host load, after the single retry added in #32955. The worker preserves a local commit but can't publish it, and the issue releases with an `unknown` terminal blocker. An interactive session on the same host then pushes the same branch immediately.

## Evidence (managed project repo, 2026-10-01)

- **First case:** a data-enrichment worker reported that its push "failed closed twice at the shared network-policy helper's 10-second timeout, including a standalone retry after the compound command was split". It then released with `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked` and `Terminal blocker: reason=unknown`. The commit existed only in the local worktree.
  - Minutes later an interactive session on the same machine ran a plain `git push -u origin <branch>` from that worktree, and it succeeded first time.
  - Host load at that moment: 2 to 4 concurrent headless workers plus the pulse.
- **Second case, earlier the same day:** a worker on the same repo stalled on `git push` (network-policy timeout) and was watchdog-killed. Orphan recovery salvaged its branch only because an earlier push had succeeded.

## Why it matters

The worker's whole output (a research checkpoint, 33 minutes and 130k tokens here) becomes invisible to other runners and to orphan recovery. Recovery then depends on a human or interactive session noticing the local-only commit.

## How (suggested)

1. **Timeout:** for `git push` and `git fetch` specifically, raise the helper timeout or make it scale with load average, or exempt them from the policy-helper round trip when the remote matches the repo's own `origin`.
2. **Classification:** when the policy helper times out on a push, classify the release as a known transient blocker such as `push_policy_timeout`, not `unknown`, and record the local branch and HEAD in the release marker. The pulse or orphan recovery on the same runner can then push it later.
3. **Optional sweep:** on the same runner, have the pulse push released workers' unpushed branches (same trust boundary as orphan recovery, GH#20819).

Target files: the OpenCode plugin's network-policy helper invocation (the #32955 path); the worker release and terminal-blocker classification; the orphan-recovery path. Exact paths need confirming.

## Verification

- A fixture where the policy helper exceeds its timeout twice for a push yields release reason `push_policy_timeout`, with the branch and HEAD recorded.
- If the sweep is implemented, the next pulse pass on the same runner pushes that branch.
### Files Scope

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks-policy-runner.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/quality-hooks-git-safety.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-git-safety-gate.mjs`
- `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-result.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`

Implementation: keep policy evaluation fail-closed; use larger bounded default budgets for Git push/fetch; preserve a retryable push_policy_timeout class and local branch/HEAD release metadata. No optional pulse sweep. Verify with node --test tests/test-git-safety-gate.mjs, bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh, and scoped ShellCheck.

title: fix(release): tagless snapshot retry requires manual --expected-sources (empty set defaults to requested PR)
body:
## What

A tagless pre-publication retry of a **snapshot** release fails closed unless the operator passes the full `--expected-sources` manifest by hand. This contradicts `workflows/release.md`, which says "Omitting the option discovers all merged PRs through the snapshot automatically."

## Reproducer

Observed 2026-10-01 for the v3.37.39 release:

1. `aidevops release patch 33359 incremental` failed in the version-manager secretlint preflight (fixture false positive, fixed by #33365). The lane moved to `reconcile-required`, with no tag.
2. Retry: `aidevops release patch 33359 incremental`, with no `--expected-sources`. It failed with `release-provenance: observed release source manifest does not exactly match the trusted expected source set`, then `Failed pre-publication release recovery refused: reviewed retry source is neither a valid direct source nor aggregate`.
3. Retry with `--expected-sources <all 47 PRs in v3.37.38..origin/main>` succeeded. The tag was published as v3.37.39.

## Root cause (evidence)

In `.agents/scripts/release-provenance-helper.sh:145` (`_release_provenance_expected_sources`), the code runs `[[ -n "$raw_sources" ]] || raw_sources="$requested_pr"`. With an empty expected set on the retry path (`_full_loop_recovery_prepare_reserved_retry_source` → `_full_loop_recovery_prepare_prepublication_source`), the expected set is `{requested_pr}`. The observed set is the multi-PR snapshot, so `_release_provenance_assert_expected_sources` always mismatches. The first-run path discovers the snapshot correctly.

Minor: during the same run, `aidevops release status 33359` printed a `reconcile 33365` hint in one line and `33359` in another.

## How

In snapshot mode with no explicit `--expected-sources`, the retry path should use the discovered snapshot manifest (or the persisted authorization expanded through the existing `reserved-authorization-refresh` transaction) rather than defaulting to `{requested_pr}`. Keep explicit `--expected-sources` as an exact assertion. Do not weaken any fail-closed check for direct or aggregate modes.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/release-provenance-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-aggregate-recovery.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-aggregate-recovery.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-release-provenance-helper.sh`

### Integration scope recovery

The current retry caller `_full_loop_release_resolve_persisted_intent` in `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-helper.sh` replaces an omitted assertion with persisted sources before calling reserved recovery. The snapshot resolver already discovers omitted sources. Its existing release-helper regression currently asserts the substituted persisted set; update that adjacent regression alongside the caller. Preserve the original CLI intent at this caller so the existing verified reserved-authorization-refresh transaction can expand the snapshot. The assigned worker verified the OWNER-authored open issue, current assignment, and no open collision PRs via prework discovery. Verify with both acceptance suites and ShellCheck, plus the existing release-helper suite. No publication or guard weakening is authorized.

## Acceptance

- A fixture with a snapshot lane in `reconcile-required` (no tag) succeeds on retry without `--expected-sources`, where main has advanced with additional merged PRs.
- A mismatching explicit `--expected-sources` still fails closed.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-aggregate-recovery.sh` and `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-release-provenance-helper.sh` pass; ShellCheck is clean.

title: Worker For-only PR closes issue; worker_complete release labels an open blocked issue status:done
body:
## What

A worker PR whose body uses only a non-closing reference (`For #N`) still closed issue #N on merge. Later, after the worker reopened the issue and set `status:blocked`, its own claim release (`CLAIM_RELEASED reason=worker_complete`) replaced `status:blocked` with `status:done` while the issue stayed **open**. The issue is now open with `status:done`, so the pulse will never dispatch it again. The blocked outcome is hidden.

## Why (evidence, managed project repo, 2026-10-01, all times UTC)

Issue event timeline for the affected issue:

```text
19:36:51 labeled   status:in-progress   (peer runner)
20:14:51 closed                          (merge of the worker's data PR, by the same runner)
20:17:41 reopened                        (worker: "the merge helper closed it despite For #N")
20:17:44 unlabeled status:in-progress
20:17:45 labeled   status:blocked
20:29:47 comment   CLAIM_RELEASED reason=worker_complete
20:29:58 unlabeled status:blocked
20:30:00 labeled   status:done          <- issue still OPEN
```

- The PR body's only issue reference is `For #N`. The squash commit message has no closing keyword. Yet `gh pr view <PR> --json closingIssuesReferences` returns `[N]`, so something linked the issue as closing (a sidebar or development link, or a helper).
- The worker's final comment explicitly says it is blocked (missing credentials, no publication). The runtime still classified the exit as `worker_complete` because a merged PR existed, and the release path projected `status:done`.

Related: aidevops#33284 (For/Ref in-flight handling) fixed dispatch-side treatment of `For`, not the closing link or the release projection.

## How (suggested)

1. Find what adds the closing link for `For #N` PRs. Candidates: the merge helper used by headless workers (the worker called it "gate-enforced merge helper"), or PR creation adding a development link. A `For`/`Ref`-only PR must never be closing-linked. Use the PR body keywords as the source of truth, not `closingIssuesReferences` alone.
2. In the claim-release / worker-outcome path (`headless-runtime-failure.sh` exit trap → `_release_dispatch_claim`, and the status projection that applies `status:done`), never apply `status:done` to an **open** issue. If the issue is open and carries `status:blocked`, preserve it. A merged non-closing PR is a checkpoint, not completion; classify it as `worker_draft_checkpoint` or blocked.
3. Add a reconciler invariant: an open issue must not carry `status:done`. Heal it to the last non-terminal state (blocked if a blocker comment is newest, otherwise available) and log the heal.

## Verification

- Fixture: a merged PR with body `For #N` and open issue N labelled `status:blocked`. The release leaves the issue `status:blocked`, open.
- Fixture: a merged PR with body `Resolves #N`. Existing `status:done` behaviour is unchanged.
- The invariant check reports, and heals, an open + `status:done` issue.
- `shellcheck` is clean on the changed scripts; the existing claim-release label tests pass (`tests/test-claim-release-label-mutation.sh`, `tests/test-clear-active-status-on-release-preserves-merged-pr.sh`).


### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-actions.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-clear-active-status-on-release-preserves-merged-pr.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-claim-release-label-mutation.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-open-done-nonclosing-regression.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-clear-active-status-on-release-no-pr.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-clear-active-status-on-release-preserves-pr.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-issue-reconcile.sh`

Verification integration: the existing recurrent-debt stage-2 tests still expect stale done to close open issues. Update them to assert the authorized open/done healing invariant, retain stage-1 debt closure coverage, and stub the new read-only issue/comments lookups separately from mutations.

Integration evidence: `_ensure_worker_pr_linkage` appends Resolves to any nonempty body lacking a closing reference, including a deliberate For/Ref checkpoint. Preserve that explicit intent before the linkage-repair write; verify using the focused regression suite and the existing worker PR linkage suite.

Integration scope recovery: the two sibling claim-release fixtures also stub the same live issue API and must provide state/labels for the new fail-closed projection guard. No concurrent related PR was found; verify all four existing release suites.

Verification: ShellCheck on changed scripts; existing claim-release tests and focused open-done/non-closing regressions. Live issue state bounds terminal projection; PR body closing intent bounds native closing metadata.

title: fix(release): stale .deployed-sha after bundle activation blocks exact-tag reconcile; setup lane guard needs canonical fetch
body:
## What

After v3.37.39 published (lane phase `exact-tag-deployment`, source PR #33359), the post-release deploy gate failed with:

`Runtime bundle convergence failed: deployed SHA 6e3d711843d6… does not match release commit 08c6db90b53e…`
`Post-release deployment gate could not verify the active runtime before deployment`

The local state was inconsistent:
- `~/.aidevops/agents` → `runtime-bundles/3.37.39-08c6db90b53e-1790886887-…/agents`. This is a validated bundle at 08c6db9, a descendant of the release tag, activated around 19:54:47Z.
- `~/.aidevops/.deployed-sha` = `6e3d711843d6498c66268f1fa02b2b554972dc2a`, which is stale.

Some path (most likely auto-update's setup run around the lane transition from `remote-publication` to `exact-tag-deployment` at 19:55:42Z) activated the new bundle without writing `.deployed-sha`. `_verify_active_release_preservation_merge` (`version-manager-release.sh`) then rejects the active bundle, so `aidevops release reconcile` can never reach the verified preservation no-op.

Secondary: `aidevops update` run from inside an agent session cannot clear this. Its generic setup calls `release_lane_setup_guard` (`release-lane-helper.sh:1401`), and that runs `git -C <canonical> fetch … refs/tags/<tag>` in `_release_lane_source_contains_tag` (line 1393). The session's canonical Git guard shim blocks that fetch, so the guard fails closed with exit 75 (`Active exact-tag release deployment blocks generic setup`), even though canonical HEAD contains the tag. `git merge-base --is-ancestor v3.37.39 HEAD` returns 0.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `aidevops release reconcile 33359` (after a bundle activation that left `.deployed-sha` stale)
**Actual output:** `Runtime bundle convergence failed: deployed SHA 6e3d711… does not match release commit 08c6db9…`, then `PARTIAL RELEASE SUCCESS`, with exit 1.

## How

1. Find every path that switches the `~/.aidevops/agents` activation symlink. Make stamp writing atomic with activation (same transaction), or have the convergence verifier accept the bundle manifest `git_sha` when it is validated and its CLI and sentinel hashes match.
2. In `_release_lane_source_contains_tag`, check a locally present tag that is verified against `git ls-remote origin refs/tags/<tag>` before requiring a canonical-mutating fetch. Alternatively, fetch into a temporary ref namespace that the canonical guard allows. Keep the trust boundary that the tag commit must match the remote.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/agent-deploy.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/auto-update-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/release-lane-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/version-manager-release.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-release-lane.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-aidevops-update-transaction.sh`

## Acceptance

- A bundle activation always leaves `.deployed-sha` equal to the active manifest `git_sha`.
- With a remote-verified `exact-tag-deployment` lane and a canonical HEAD containing the tag, generic setup proceeds without mutating canonical refs.
- `test-release-lane.sh` and `test-aidevops-update-transaction.sh` pass; ShellCheck is clean.

title: Prevent overlapping issue scopes from dispatching concurrently
body:
## Problem

Automatic dispatch can launch two independently valid issues that target the same files and declarations before their dependency or conflict is recognized.

Observed on 2026-10-01 in a maintained project: two open issues both targeted the same typography declarations in `src/styles/global.css`, but requested incompatible letter-spacing outcomes. Both entered worker processing. The interactive session had to stop the conflicting lane, complete the prerequisite first, and narrow the second issue before it was safe to resume.

The framework already requires an interactive prework collision check through `prework-discovery-helper.sh`, but equivalent target-overlap evidence is not enforced before automatic issue dispatch.

## Goal

Prevent concurrent auto-dispatch when worker-ready issue scopes overlap materially, while allowing unrelated files and explicitly ordered work to continue in parallel.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/prework-discovery-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-prework-discovery-helper.sh`
- `.agents/reference/worker-discipline.md`

Additional dispatch tests may be required; their exact canonical path is unknown because this report was produced from the deployed framework rather than a framework checkout. Use the nearest existing Pulse dispatch test file.

## Expected behavior

1. Parse canonical `### Files Scope` entries from available and active issues.
2. Before launch, compare the candidate scope with currently claimed, queued, in-progress, and in-review work in the same repository.
3. Treat exact file overlap as a collision requiring one of:
   - explicit dependency ordering,
   - verified non-overlapping line or component scope,
   - or deferral until the active issue reaches a terminal state.
4. Emit a concise diagnostic identifying both issue numbers and overlapping paths.
5. Do not permanently block dispatch: reevaluate after the conflicting issue changes state.
6. Preserve parallel dispatch for disjoint scopes.
7. Fail open only when an issue explicitly declares that its paths cannot yet be known; require that worker to discover and publish scope before editing.

## Acceptance criteria

- Two available issues with the same scoped file are not launched concurrently without dependency or non-overlap evidence.
- Disjoint issues remain concurrently dispatchable.
- A completed or cancelled conflicting issue no longer blocks the candidate.
- Diagnostics identify the collision rather than presenting a generic no-work result.
- Existing prework and Pulse dispatch tests pass with focused collision coverage added.

## Verification

- Run the existing `prework-discovery-helper.sh` test suite.
- Run the nearest existing Pulse dispatch tests.
- Add fixtures for exact overlap, disjoint paths, ordered dependency, terminal predecessor, and unknown scope.

## Evidence

The project incident involved two typography issues touching the same CSS rules. It caused unnecessary worker startup and manual recovery but no production regression because the conflict was intercepted before the second change merged.

title: Recover full-loop PR creation from stale branches and shared worktrees
body:
## Problem

The interactive full-loop path did not recover cleanly when a worker branch already existed remotely and the repository used a bare/shared linked-worktree layout.

Observed sequence on 2026-10-01:

1. A previously killed worker left a remote branch with the intended name.
2. The next push was rejected because the remote branch had diverged.
3. A replacement branch push succeeded, but automatic PR creation still failed until an explicit head branch was supplied manually.
4. Canonical synchronization then refused the repository layout even though the linked worktree itself was valid.

The task was recovered without force-pushing or data loss, but the normal full-loop consumed repeated manual discovery and GitHub operations.

## Goal

Make the full-loop recovery path deterministic when a stale remote branch or shared-worktree repository layout is encountered.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers-create.sh`
- `.agents/workflows/git-workflow.md`
- `.agents/reference/dirty-worktree-preservation.md`

The exact existing test files are unknown from the deployed framework. Extend the nearest full-loop and GitHub wrapper suites rather than creating a new harness.

## Expected behavior

1. Before push, detect whether the intended remote branch already exists and whether it is the same lineage as the local branch.
2. If it diverges, preserve both histories and propose or automatically choose a collision-free replacement branch; never force-push.
3. Carry the final pushed branch name into PR creation explicitly as `--head` rather than relying on ambient branch inference.
4. If push succeeded but PR creation failed, print a single deterministic recovery command and preserve lifecycle state for retry.
5. Recognize valid linked worktrees whose common Git directory is a bare/shared repository; do not require an editable canonical checkout for PR completion.
6. Keep canonical synchronization lossless and refuse only when actual unpreserved state is at risk.

## Acceptance criteria

- A stale divergent remote branch results in a new collision-free branch and a PR without manual force operations.
- PR creation uses the exact successfully pushed head branch.
- A valid bare/shared linked-worktree repository can complete PR creation and postflight without a false canonical-layout failure.
- Genuine dirty or unpreserved canonical state remains protected.
- Existing full-loop, Git wrapper, and worktree-preservation tests pass with focused regressions added.

## Verification

- Reproduce with a fixture remote containing a divergent branch of the requested name.
- Verify both remote histories remain reachable and the PR head is the replacement branch.
- Reproduce from a linked worktree backed by a bare common Git directory.
- Run existing full-loop and wrapper test suites.

## Evidence

The observed project ultimately merged successfully after explicit branch replacement and manual `--head` selection. The failure therefore concerns recovery ergonomics and state propagation rather than GitHub availability.

title: Stale recovery supersedes a live worker that pushes branch commits but has no PR yet
body:
## What

Cross-runner stale recovery (`_is_stale_assignment` in `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-stale.sh`) superseded a **live, productive** headless worker. Its liveness signals are only issue comments, issue `updatedAt` and open-PR activity (`_stale_assignment_has_recent_open_pr_activity`). A worker that is pushing commits to its issue branch, but has not opened a PR yet, looks dead.

## Why (evidence, managed project repo, 2026-10-01, UTC)

- 18:44: runner A dispatched a worker for issue N (data-enrichment class; the brief tells workers to "commit and push specs as they are written so a stopped worker loses nothing", and to open the PR only at the end).
- 18:44–21:06: the worker pushed two commits to `feature/auto-…-ghN` (about 34k lines of source-backed specs). It wrote a third spec file at 21:06. It posted no issue comments and had no PR.
- 20:51:45: runner B's pulse posted `Stale assignment recovered … dispatch claim 7623s old, last activity 7577s old (threshold=600s)` with `WORKER_SUPERSEDED runners=A`. It unassigned A and relabelled `status:available`.
- 20:54: runner C dispatched a new worker. It found the source site down (HTTP 522), opened a separate draft PR containing only a brief, and released as blocked. The new worker never saw runner A's branch.
- 21:07: runner A's worker exited with `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=worker_ownership_lost`, leaving one spec uncommitted. A maintainer salvaged it by hand.

Result: about 2h of productive work was nearly lost, and the issue gained a duplicate draft PR.

## How (suggested)

1. In `_is_stale_assignment`, before recovering, check for recent pushes to issue-linked branches: the pattern `*-gh<N>` / `*gh<N>*`, or the branch named in the dispatch comment. Use `gh api repos/{o}/{r}/branches/<branch>` (commit date) or a `git ls-remote` plus commit-date lookup. Only check once comments and PRs are quiet, as the open-PR check does now, to save API budget.
2. Treat a branch commit newer than the threshold as liveness (`return 1`), like recent open-PR activity.
3. On recovery, record the superseded runner's last pushed branch in the recovery comment, so the next worker resumes from it instead of starting over.

Insertion point: next to `_stale_assignment_has_recent_open_pr_activity` (around line 1211 of `dispatch-dedup-stale.sh`).

## Verification

- Fixture: an issue with a quiet thread, no PR, and a branch `feature/auto-x-ghN` with a commit 120s old → not stale. With the commit 2h old → stale, and the recovery comment names the branch.
- Existing stale tests pass: `tests/test-dispatch-dedup-stale-terminal-evidence.sh`, `tests/test-dispatch-dedup-stale-no-worker.sh`.
- `shellcheck` is clean on `dispatch-dedup-stale.sh`.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-stale.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-dedup-stale-no-worker.sh`

title: Bug: profile scratch recovery rejects unchanged untracked canonical files
body:
### Description

Profile publication permits pre-existing untracked files in the canonical checkout, but its archive-first scratch-worktree recovery requires the canonical checkout's full status to be empty. Consequently, successful publication can be followed by a cleanup failure even when those unrelated files were present before the run and were not touched.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Use an otherwise clean canonical profile repository with an unrelated untracked file or directory.
2. Run a profile update in its detached publication worktree.
3. Exercise the archive-first fallback after normal guarded scratch removal refuses the candidate (the existing boundary fixture supplies a refusing helper safely).
4. `_profile_publication_worktree_recovery_is_safe` rejects the unchanged canonical untracked content, leaving the scratch worktree behind.

### Expected Behavior

Recovery should preserve the canonical HEAD and its captured pre-publication status, rather than requiring unrelated pre-existing files to be deleted. Existing ownership, provenance, durable-archive and active-process guards should remain intact.

### Error Output

```text
Warning: profile publication worktree cleanup failed: <publication-worktree>
Error: profile publication worktree remains for guarded recovery: <publication-worktree>
```

### aidevops Version

Observed on 3.34.13; the contradictory check remains in upstream main at `2d3d39143`.

### Operating System

Ubuntu / Debian

### AI Assistant

OpenCode

### Third-party Tool Involvement

None required to reproduce the profile recovery defect. Protected Linux CWD observation is a separate issue already addressed upstream; this report does not request duplicate inspector tooling.

### Additional Context

Implementation scope:
- `.agents/scripts/profile-readme-helper.sh`: retain/reset the already captured canonical status alongside HEAD; compare it in `_profile_publication_worktree_recovery_is_safe`.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-profile-readme-boundary.sh`: extend the existing dirty-scratch recovery fixture with a pre-existing untracked canonical file, verify archive/removal succeeds, and verify the file's content and canonical status survive.
- Reference pattern: `_profile_run_in_worktree` already captures canonical status and verifies it after publication; `_profile_assert_canonical_clean` deliberately excludes untracked files.
- Verification: `shellcheck` on both files, `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-profile-readme-boundary.sh`, and `git diff --check`.

The narrow fix and regression fixture pass all 27 boundary tests. No process-observation bypass, root cleanup, dependency, or configuration change is needed.

### Pre-submission Checklist

- [x] Searched existing issues; no matching open profile-canonical-status issue was found.
- [x] Noted the installed version and checked the current upstream implementation.

title: t18582: Extend macOS indexing/backup audit with dev churn paths and exclusion coverage
body:
## What

Extend the macOS indexing/backup optimisation helper so its dry-run audit covers the high-churn developer paths found in a live incident and reports actual Time Machine and Backblaze exclusion coverage.

## Why

Live diagnosis on a 128 GB Mac: `fseventsd` reached 82 GB, swap was exhausted (79 GB used) and `bztransmit -completesync` used 9.4 GB. The `/optimise-macos-indexing-backups` audit recommended only caches. It missed the largest churn sources that were still backed up:

- OrbStack VM data: `~/Library/Group Containers/HUAQ24HBR6.dev.orbstack` (125 GB, continuously rewritten sparse disk image)
- LM Studio models: `~/.lmstudio` (91 GB, re-downloadable)
- OpenCode generated session data: `~/.local/share/opencode/snapshot` and `storage` (16 GB)
- Toolchains: `~/.bun` (13 GB; only `install/cache` was listed) and `~/.rustup` (3.7 GB)

The audit also could not tell the user whether these were already excluded. Backblaze's `use_time_machine_excludes` setting ("Also exclude Apple-specified exclusions" in the GUI) was `false`, so `node_modules` paths already excluded from Time Machine were still uploaded. Enabling it was verified in the Backblaze GUI.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/optimise-indexing-backups-helper.sh`
  - Add the paths above to `_candidate_paths macos`; add the portable equivalents (`~/.lmstudio`, opencode `snapshot`/`storage`, `~/.bun`, `~/.rustup`) to linux.
  - Add a read-only macOS coverage report for existing candidate paths: Time Machine status from `tmutil isexcluded`, and Backblaze status from `bzdirfilter whichfiles="none"` prefix matches in `bzinfo.xml`. Backblaze matching is case-insensitive.
  - Report the Backblaze `use_time_machine_excludes` value and recommend enabling it when false.
  - Allow a `AIDEVOPS_BACKBLAZE_BZINFO` override. Never print identity or login fields.
  - Include the coverage data in `--json` output.
- `.agents/tools/terminal/optimise-macos-indexing-backups.md`: document the new paths, the coverage report and the Apple-exclusions toggle.

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/optimise-indexing-backups-helper.sh`
- `.agents/tools/terminal/optimise-macos-indexing-backups.md`

## Acceptance

- `optimise-indexing-backups-helper.sh macos scan` lists the new paths and shows per-path Time Machine and Backblaze status, plus the Backblaze Apple-exclusions setting.
- `--json` includes `coverage` and `backblaze` objects.
- Scan stays read-only, with no sudo and no backup-config edits.
- `shellcheck` is clean and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-optimise-indexing-backups-helper.sh` passes.

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/optimise-indexing-backups-helper.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-optimise-indexing-backups-helper.sh
.agents/scripts/optimise-indexing-backups-helper.sh macos scan
```

title: Runner capability check: peer runner claims issue despite requires-secrets it cannot satisfy
body:
## Observed

A peer runner on aidevops v3.37.41 claimed an issue whose body had a line-start `requires-secrets:` declaration naming five secrets, two of which that runner does not hold. The worker started, confirmed the two names were absent from its name-only inventory, and released the claim as blocked about a minute later (`CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked`).

Timeline (UTC, 2026-10-02), on one private managed repo:

- 00:43Z: first claim on that runner; the worker posted a blocked dossier naming the absent secrets. The body did not yet declare them.
- 00:48:38Z: issue body edited to add `requires-secrets: <5 uppercase names>` on its own line (GraphQL `userContentEdits` confirms the time).
- 00:53:48Z: the same runner wrote `DISPATCH_LEASE phase=ready` and dispatched again. 00:55:00Z: `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked`, then `DISPATCH_LEASE phase=terminal`.

On the maintainer runner (v3.37.40), `runner_capability_check` behaves correctly. `aidevops secret check MISSING_NAME` returns 1, a present name returns 0, and `pulse.log` shows `deferred: runner_capability_unmet` for other repos' issues.

## Suspected causes (unverified; peer runner not inspectable)

1. `issue_meta_json` reached `runner_capability_check` from a pre-edit prefetch or cache, so the body lacked the line (the t2996 single-bundle metadata path in `pulse-dispatch-core.sh` around `_dispatch_load_and_validate_metadata`).
2. A v3.37.41 change bypasses or reorders the GH#33341 check (for example a lease, continuation or consolidation path that dispatches without `dispatch_with_dedup`).
3. `aidevops secret check` returns 0 for an absent name on that runner's secret backend.

## Impact

Each wasted claim burns a worker slot and the class cap, adds `status:blocked` churn, and feeds terminal-blocker backoff and circuits. One issue reached `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_BACKOFF failures=2` from these claims.

## Suggested fix and verification

- Make the capability check read the body fresh (or the metadata bundle fetched in the same dispatch attempt) immediately before claim, and log `runner_capability_check source=<fresh|cache> requirements=<count>` (names only).
- Audit v3.37.41 dispatch paths that write `DISPATCH_LEASE phase=ready` without passing through `runner_capability_check`.
- Add a regression case to `tests/test-runner-capability.sh` that covers a body edited after prefetch, if the cache path is confirmed.
- Verify: on a runner missing one declared name, `pulse.log` shows `runner_capability_unmet` and no `DISPATCH_LEASE` comment appears on the issue.

Related: GH#33341 (closed; introduced the check).

title: pre-edit check blocks a manually dispatched worker on its own worktree (owner = its own wrapper PID)
body:
## Observed

A worker launched by `dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh dispatch` (session `manual-cli-<N>-<ts>`, OpenCode 1.18.34, aidevops 3.37.41) ran `aidevops_pre_edit_check` in its own pre-created worktree and got:

```
Pre-edit check exit 2: BLOCKED: linked worktree is owned by another active session/process
WORKTREE_OWNERSHIP_CONFLICT=true
WORKTREE_OWNER_PID=<the worker's own detached launch wrapper PID, as printed by "Dispatched PID:">
WORKTREE_OWNER_SESSION=<the worker's own session key>
```

`ps -p <pid>` showed the owner as `bash` with PPID 1 — the detached wrapper that runs this worker. The worker treated this as a terminal blocker (`TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON=permission_required`), so the dispatch ended with no work done. Other workers dispatched the same way in the same minute proceeded, so it depends on whether the worker calls the pre-edit check.

## Expected

The pre-edit check recognises the owner as the same worker when the recorded owner session equals the caller's session (or the owner PID is an ancestor of the caller), and passes; or the worker prompt makes clear the dispatcher pre-created the worktree so the check is skipped.

## Files likely involved

- `.agents/scripts/pre-edit-check.sh` (worktree ownership check)
- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh` / `headless-runtime-helper.sh` (`--detach`: which PID/session is recorded as owner, and whether the worker's environment carries that session key)

## Verification

Dispatch one worker with `dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh dispatch <N> <repo>` and confirm `aidevops_pre_edit_check` inside the worker passes in its worktree; a second, unrelated session still gets the ownership conflict.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`

### Worker Guidance

The current default branch already exports exact wrapper ownership proof and checks ancestry in `pre-edit-check.sh` (GH#28426). Its proof requires `AIDEVOPS_SESSION_ORIGIN=worker` and a true headless marker. Manual launch currently inherits both values from its caller; `headless-runtime-helper.sh` preserves nonempty inherited values. Normalize those two markers in `_dsi_launch_worker` without weakening ownership proof or unrelated-session rejection. Extend the existing detached-envelope regression with an interactive/non-headless caller and assertions on the launched worker environment.

Verification: `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`, `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pre-edit-check.sh`, and `shellcheck .agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`. The existing pre-edit suite exercises wrapper ancestry, mismatched metadata, and unrelated live owners without dispatching another implementation worker.

title: Worker network-policy guard still fails closed on HTTPS tool requests after timeout (sibling of GH#33361 push fix)
body:
## Observed

On aidevops v3.37.41 (OpenCode 1.18.34), a headless worker on a private managed repo stopped as blocked at 2026-10-02 03:16Z. Its own summary: "the active worker network-policy guard fails closed while evaluating the exact beta health request, timing out after 10 seconds. A standalone policy diagnostic allowed the domain, but the subsequent guarded request still failed at the active runtime guard." The worker held every required credential; nothing was captured or published. Exact diagnostics are in that worker's protected telemetry on the maintainer runner.

The pulse classified the exit as `Terminal blocker: reason=unknown` (projected `status:available`), and the issue's live label then read `status:blocked`.

Another worker on the same host published to the same HTTPS origin successfully about an hour earlier, so the origin and allowlist are fine; the 10s guard evaluation timed out under host load.

## Relationship to prior fixes

- GH#32955: retry the policy helper once on ETIMEDOUT; label a second timeout as transient.
- GH#33361 / PR #33379: fixed recovery from the same timeout for worker `git push` only.
- This is the sibling path: an ordinary outbound HTTPS request (curl or a Node fetch inside a tool command) evaluated by the runtime network-policy guard. It still fails closed after the timeout, and the worker treats the failure as terminal.

## Suggested fix

- Apply the #33379 recovery pattern (bounded retry with backoff; a transient classification distinct from a policy deny) to the HTTPS/tool-command evaluation path in the OpenCode plugin's network-policy guard.
- Map a guard timeout to a known transient blocker class (for example `network_policy_timeout`) so the pulse requeues with a short backoff instead of `reason=unknown`.

## Verification

- Simulate a slow policy helper (delay over 10s) for an allowed HTTPS URL inside a worker tool command: expect a retry, then success or a transient classification, never a policy denial.
- Confirm the terminal-blocker comment records the transient class and that the issue returns to `status:available`.

title: Issue-sync PR hygiene fails post-merge when worker PR title uses issue-derived t<ISSUE> without a TODO task
body:
## Observed

In a managed private repo (placeholder: `<private-repo>`), the post-merge job `sync / Sync Issue Hygiene on PR Merge` failed for 5 of the last 12 merged worker PRs (2026-10-02). Every failure has the same shape:

- PR title `t<ISSUE>: ...`, where the headless worker used the **issue number** as the task ID (for example `t11374:` for issue #11374), and
- PR body `Resolves #<ISSUE>`, where the issue was filed by a wrapper without a TODO.md line.

Log excerpt:

```text
PR #<N>: task_id=t<ISSUE> linked_issues=<ISSUE>  for_ref_issues= range_syntax=
ERROR: closing issue #<ISSUE> has no exact ref:GH#<ISSUE> TODO mapping
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

The issue itself was closed with `status:done` by the normal lifecycle, so the effect is a red post-merge check that looks like a failure, plus any hygiene steps after the resolver being skipped. Merged PRs whose bodies used only `For #`/`Ref #`, or that had no closing keyword, passed.

## Root cause

`.github/workflows/issue-sync-reusable.yml` "Extract task ID" (around line 872) treats any `^t[0-9]+` title prefix as a task ID. `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-pr-task-resolver.sh` `resolve_pr_task_ids` (around lines 186-191) then sets `RESOLVED_TASK_BACKED=true` whenever a title task ID is present, and `map_issue_tasks` requires exactly one `ref:GH#<ISSUE>` TODO line for each closing issue. Issue-only work has no such line, so it hard-fails.

The issue-derived title (`t<ISSUE>`) does not exist as a TODO task. That conflicts with the "never invent task IDs" rule and is what triggers the strict path.

## Fix options (pick one, smallest first)

1. Resolver: treat a title task ID as TODO-backed only if that task ID exists in TODO.md. If it is absent and no closing issue has a `ref:GH#` mapping, exit 0 with `task_backed=false` and leave issue-only hygiene unchanged.
2. Worker PR title generation: when the issue has no TODO task, use `GH#<ISSUE>:` (or no task prefix) instead of synthesizing `t<ISSUE>`. Find the title builder with `rg -n 't\$\{?issue' .agents/scripts` (exact location not verified).

Option 1 is the safer fix because it also covers PR titles that already exist. Keep the hard failure when a title task **does** exist in TODO.md but conflicts with or lacks the closing-issue mapping, because that check guards against stale-mapping merges (#28641, #32215).

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/issue-sync-pr-task-resolver.sh`
- Run the resolver on a TODO.md fixture without `ref:GH#123`: `bash issue-sync-pr-task-resolver.sh TODO.md "123" "t123" ""` exits 0 with `task_backed=false`.
- Run it with a real task line `- [ ] t5 ... ref:GH#123` and title `t5`: it still resolves `123:t5`. With title `t6`, it still fails with a conflict.
### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-pr-task-resolver.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-issue-sync-pr-task-resolver.sh`

title: Cost circuit breaker trips on productive multi-checkpoint issues: merged For #N PRs should reset the per-issue spend sum
body:
## Observed

In a managed private repo (placeholder `<private-repo>`), the t2007 cost circuit breaker fired on two long-running "consolidated" enrichment issues within 25 minutes (2026-10-02). In both cases every counted attempt was **productive**: it ended in a merged `For #<issue>` checkpoint PR with confirmed data publications.

- Issue A: 1,775K tokens over 3 attempts (`tier:standard` budget 800K). One attempt published a class and merged its checkpoint PR. One diagnosed a real tooling defect, which was then fixed in a separate issue/PR. The third was capture work.
- Issue B: 1,032K tokens over 2 attempts. Both attempts merged checkpoint PRs, with two and four confirmed publications.

Each trip also auto-filed a `circuit-breaker-meta` `tier:thinking` diagnosis issue. That issue is auto-dispatchable, so a premium worker would have been spent diagnosing a non-failure. A maintainer had to post a `<!-- cost-circuit-breaker:reset` comment and close the meta issue by hand. An earlier trip the same day (environmental runner capability, aidevops#33399) needed the same manual reset.

## Root cause

`.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-cost.sh` `_sum_issue_token_spend` (lines ~86-162) adds up every worker signature-footer `spent N tokens` across the issue's whole comment history. The only reset boundaries are `<!-- aidevops-signed-approval -->` and `<!-- cost-circuit-breaker:reset`. A merged checkpoint PR that references the issue (`For #N` / `Ref #N`) does not reset the count. On any issue designed to deliver through several checkpoint PRs, the per-issue budget is therefore a lifetime budget, and the breaker is guaranteed to trip.

## Proposed fix (smallest first)

1. Treat the merge time of the latest **merged** PR that references the issue (`For #N`, `Ref #N` or `Resolves #N`, via the issue timeline `cross-referenced`/`connected` events or `closedByPullRequestsReferences`) as an additional reset boundary in `_sum_issue_token_spend`. Spend before a delivered checkpoint is then not counted against later attempts. A real loop with no merged output still trips at the same budget.
2. Optionally, only file the `circuit-breaker-meta` issue when at least one counted attempt has a failure-class outcome. That requires reading the outcome from the worker-lifecycle comments, which is more work, so treat it as a follow-up.

Keep the existing approval/reset markers and the fail-open posture.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-cost.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-cost-circuit-breaker.sh`

The edit goes in `_sum_issue_token_spend` and needs one extra `gh api` timeline/PR query, cached per cycle if the pulse already fetches the timeline. The test gains a case where a merged `For #N` PR between footers resets the sum.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-cost.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-cost-circuit-breaker.sh`. Existing cases must pass. New case: footers of 600K, then a merged checkpoint PR, then 300K gives a sum of 300K, under budget. Without the PR, the sum is 900K and over budget.

title: Signed permission grant cannot resume a manually dispatched worker (pulse off, session key mismatch)
body:
## Observed

A worker started with `dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh dispatch <N> <slug>` (session key `manual-cli-<N>-<epoch>`) asked for an `external_directory` read permission, wrote the pending marker `<git-dir>/aidevops-permission-pending` (`{"request_id":..., "issue":N, "session":"manual-cli-N-<epoch>"}`), posted the permission-request comment and released its claim. The maintainer then ran `sudo aidevops approve permissions issue <N> <slug> --request <id>`: the signed grant was posted, `needs-maintainer-permissions` was removed and `pulse-diagnose-helper.sh issue` shows `Signed decision: grant`.

Nothing can resume the worker after that:

1. `dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh dispatch <N> <slug>` refuses: "has a signed grant bound to its original worker session and worktree; a new manual worker cannot consume it. Resume through the original pulse/worker path" (`dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh` around line 340).
2. The pulse cannot resume it either. The repository has `pulse: false` in `repos.json`, which is why manual dispatch was used. And even with the pulse on, `pulse-dispatch-core.sh` launches with `session_key="issue-<N>"` (around line 1022), while `_hrw_prepare_permission_grant_path` / the pending-marker check in `headless-runtime-worker-prepare.sh` (lines 290-318) only export the request ID when `WORKER_SESSION_KEY` matches the marker's `manual-cli-...` session. So a pulse worker would not load the grant.
3. The issue keeps `status:blocked` after the grant.

Result: a granted request for a manually dispatched worker is a dead end. The only routes are a hand-built `headless-runtime-helper.sh run` with the original session key (bypassing the dispatcher's ledger, claim and git auth setup) or `--withdraw`, which throws away the approval.

## Expected

After a signed grant, the issue can be resumed with the bound session and worktree, for example:

- `dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh resume <N> <slug>`: reads the pending marker in the preserved worktree, reuses its session key and worktree, and runs the normal claim, ledger and git-auth path; or
- the approval kick (`_kick_pulse_after_permission_approval` in `approval-helper-permissions.sh`) resumes manual-dispatch sessions directly when the repository's pulse is off.

Also clear `status:blocked` (or set `status:available`) when the grant clears the permission hold.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh` (grant check around line 330-346, `_dsi_launch_worker`)
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker-prepare.sh` (pending marker, lines 290-318)
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh` (session key default, line ~1022)
- `.agents/scripts/approval-helper-permissions.sh` (`_kick_pulse_after_permission_approval`, label clearing)

## Verification

Manually dispatch a worker on a test issue in a repository with `pulse: false`, make it request an `external_directory` read, approve it, then resume: the resumed worker runs in the original worktree with the original session key, `AIDEVOPS_PERMISSION_REQUEST_ID` and `AIDEVOPS_PERMISSION_GRANT_FILE` are set, and the granted read succeeds without a new request.
### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/approval-helper-permissions.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-permission-grant-verification.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-approval-permissions-module.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-permission-approval-content-binding.sh`

Implementation: add explicit manual resume with verified original request/session/branch/worktree binding through the existing dispatch safety path; clear the permission-owned blocked status after approval. Existing runtime permission checks remain unchanged. Integration recovery: the existing content-binding test asserts that a permission-owned blocked status is retained; update those two assertions to the authorized status recovery and run this existing test too. Verification: ShellCheck and the three scoped existing test scripts, including signed binding rejection and resume lifecycle coverage.
