title: docs(wordpress): fleet rollout of self-hosted plugin releases; HTTP request limiters block WP-CLI update checks
body:
## What

Add guidance for rolling a self-hosted (GitHub-updater) WordPress plugin release out to a fleet of sites with WP-CLI, so agents do not misread a blocked update check as a missing token or a private-repository problem.

## Observed evidence (2026-10-03)

- After publishing a plugin release, `wp plugin update <slug>` on shared-hosting sites returned "Plugin already updated", and the updater's release cache recorded: `User has blocked requests through HTTP. (HTTP Requests Manager plugin: total_time_limit 3s < 3.7s)`.
- The agent first concluded the token/private repo was the cause. In fact every site already had the correct token in `wp-config.php` (verified by comparing a sha256 fingerprint of the secret with the site constant, never printing either).
- Cause: HTTP Requests Manager ("smart" blocking mode) blocks every outbound request once the PHP request has run for 3 s or made 3 requests, **except** in cron and on `update-core.php`. A WP-CLI run on a heavy site passes 3 s while booting, so every update check from the CLI is blocked. Running the same check with `define('DOING_CRON', true)` before `wp_update_plugins()` succeeded and found the new release.
- Fallback that worked on 18 sites: copy the release zip to the host once (checksum-verified), then per site `wp plugin install ~/<slug>-X.Y.Z.zip --force`, check `wp plugin get <slug> --field=version` and the home page status, and delete the zip afterwards.

## Change

Add a short "Fleet rollout of a self-hosted plugin release" section to `.agents/tools/wordpress/wp-cli-reference.md` (or `.agents/tools/wordpress/wp-plugin-release.md` if that fits better; pick one and link from the other):

1. Before a fleet update, check one site's update check in cron context: `wp eval 'define("DOING_CRON", true); wp_update_plugins(); ...'`. Request-limiting plugins (HTTP Requests Manager smart mode, similar firewalls) block CLI-context requests but allow cron and `update-core.php`.
2. When the updater reports a failure, read the error it recorded before blaming credentials; verify tokens by fingerprint comparison only.
3. Fallback rollout: scp the built release asset once, then `wp plugin install <zip> --force` per site, verify version + front-end status, remove the zip.
4. Note expected non-200 front ends (admin-only sites redirecting, password-protected staging) belong in the local site inventory, not in shared docs.

## Verification

- `markdownlint` (or the repo's markdown checks) passes on the edited file.
- The section names the cron-context check, the fingerprint-only token check and the zip fallback.

Paths are known; no other files need changing.
### Files Scope

- `.agents/tools/wordpress/wp-cli-reference.md`
- `.agents/tools/wordpress/wp-plugin-release.md`

title: Restore bare slash commands (/full-loop etc.) removed by prefix-only deploy + legacy prune
body:
## Goal

Restore bare slash commands (`/full-loop`, `/pr-loop`, `/recall`, `/save-todo`, etc.) for every `.agents/scripts/commands/*.md` source in OpenCode and Claude Code, keeping the `aidevops-<name>` namespaced copies.

## Evidence

- `~/.config/opencode/command/full-loop.md` is missing after `setup.sh`. Only `aidevops-full-loop.md` is deployed. The same applies to `pr-loop`, `postflight-loop`, `recall`, `remember`, `save-todo` and `list-todo`.
- Since #18096, `_generate_commands_for_runtime` in `.agents/scripts/generate-runtime-config-commands.sh` deploys `scripts/commands/<name>.md` only as `aidevops-<name>`. Bare names survived only as stale copies from older generators, so fresh installs never had `/full-loop`.
- #33384 (GH#33355) added `_prune_legacy_commands`. It treats an unchanged copy of a *current* source at a bare name as legacy and deletes it, which removed the last working `/full-loop` on long-running installs.
- Docs, `.agents/AGENTS.md` and worker dispatch still invoke bare names. Examples: `pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:497` (`/full-loop Implement issue #N`), `remote-dispatch-helper.sh:594`, `deferred-job-helper.sh:274`. Process matching (`*"/full-loop"*`) also relies on the bare token. Headless workers therefore receive an unexpanded prompt rather than the command template.
- Claude Code installs keep an April-era `full-loop.md` body that no longer matches the source.

## How

1. In `_generate_commands_for_runtime`, also deploy each `scripts/commands` source at bare `<name>`:
   - Absent, or already matching the current output: write it.
   - Matching a legacy fingerprint: replace it.
   - Unrecognised regular file: back it up under `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/backups/commands/<runtime>/` and then replace it.
   - Symlinks and non-regular entries: never follow or replace them; warn instead.
2. `_prune_legacy_commands`: skip names that have a live `scripts/commands` source, because they are now generator-owned.
3. `_opencode_command_output_matches_source` in `generate-runtime-config.sh`: verify the bare names too, so the cache self-heals.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/generate-runtime-config-commands.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/generate-runtime-config.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-runtime-command-reconciliation.sh`

## Verification

- ShellCheck is clean on the changed scripts.
- After `setup.sh --non-interactive`, `~/.config/opencode/command/full-loop.md` exists and its body matches `aidevops-full-loop.md`.

title: Bounded merge cleanup fallback breaks OpenCode worktree ownership
body:
## Problem

An authorized bounded post-merge operation is rejected after the merge helper records deferred cleanup ownership with the fallback session identity. The implementation and merge succeed, but remaining same-session verification requires a separate owned continuation worktree.

## Observed evidence

- A bounded `full-loop-helper.sh merge` completed with verified merge, safe canonical synchronization, issue reconciliation and a durable deferred cleanup receipt.
- The worktree ownership row then had `owner_session=full-loop-lifecycle`, `task_id=post-merge-cleanup` and `owner_comm=opencode`.
- Starting an existing shared-preview script from that worktree through `aidevops_bounded_operation` failed with: `Operation workdir is not owned by the current OpenCode session`.
- A normal Bash operation in the current session had a valid `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID`. The live owner was not adopted or overridden. A fresh, normally registered linked continuation worktree allowed the same bounded preview command to succeed.
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh:_merge_record_deferred_cleanup_owner` resolves the session from environment variables and then calls `claim_worktree_ownership` with task `post-merge-cleanup`.
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh` defines the `full-loop-lifecycle` fallback. The reason the real session was absent or replaced in the bounded merge environment is not yet proven; investigate propagation rather than assuming a cause.

## Scope and reference pattern

Investigate the session-identity handoff between the bounded-operation environment, `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`, `.agents/scripts/full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh` and the existing trusted worktree-owner resolver/registry. The exact bounded-operation implementation and existing regression-test paths are not known yet; discover them before editing.

Preserve the current security contract: exact repository/PR/head identity, trusted session identity, live PID and process-generation checks, lease ownership and deferred cleanup after owner exit. Do not weaken the operation guard, force-adopt a live owner's worktree, directly rewrite registry rows or bypass canonical-worktree protection.

title: t18584: fix(pulse): never-terminal 'qlty usage' pending status wedges pulse auto-merge
body:
## What

The pulse pre-merge snapshot treats every pending check as active CI. Qlty publishes a non-required commit status `qlty usage` ("You have used 90%+ of your analysis minutes this period.") in `pending` state and never completes it. Every PR on a repository that has hit that quota is then reported `not ready (active=1, blocking_failures=0, advisory_failures=0)` forever and never auto-merges.

Observed: wpallstars/wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding PRs #269 and #270 (worker PRs for #262/#263) had all checks green and the review-bot gate passing, but pulse logged `pre-merge snapshot: ... not ready (active=1 ...)` on every pass for 2+ hours. The only non-terminal status on the head was `qlty usage` = pending.

## Change

In `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-required-checks.sh` `_pmrc_snapshot_checks_acceptable()`: ignore a pending check only when it is (a) a single commit-status context, (b) not a required context, and (c) named in a fixed list of known never-terminal informational statuses (`PMRC_INFORMATIONAL_PENDING_STATUS_CONTEXTS_JSON`, currently `qlty usage`). Log each ignore. Required contexts, check runs and terminal failures are unchanged.

The flag is computed in jq and placed next to the name: `IFS=$'\t' read` collapses empty fields, so a pending row (empty conclusion) shifts every later column.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-required-checks.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-preflight-snapshot.sh`

## Verification

- `shellcheck -x` on both files: clean.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-preflight-snapshot.sh`: 110 run, 0 failed. New cases: a non-required pending `qlty usage` status passes; the same context listed as required still blocks.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-required-checks-filter.sh` passes.

title: fix(full-loop): worker merges lost to the 120s tool timeout and to an unretried permission lookup
body:
## What

Two worker merge attempts on 2026-10-03 failed for reasons unrelated to the PRs. Both PRs were left for pulse, which then could not merge them either (separate cause, fixed by #33495).

1. **Merge killed by the runtime's default tool timeout.** The worker for wpallstars/wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding #262 ran `full-loop-helper.sh merge 269 <repo>` with the default 120 s Bash timeout. Output stopped at `Merging PR #269 ... (--squash --subject <validated>)...` with `exit: null`. An interactive rerun of the same command took 116.6 s; #270 took 75.7 s. Normal merges are close to 120 s, so a worker can lose a merge mid-flight.
2. **Author permission lookup failed once with no retry.** The worker for #263 ran `full-loop-helper.sh merge 270 <repo>` and got `Merge blocked: unable to verify live repository permission for PR author marcusquinn`. Pulse logged `permission check failed for author marcusquinn (HTTP unknown, reason api-failure)` for the same PR at the same time. A direct `gh api .../collaborators/marcusquinn/permission` straight afterwards returned `admin`. `_gh_collaborator_permission_lookup` in `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-collaborator-permission.sh` retries only when a GitHub App is configured (`_gh_collaborator_permission_retry_with_gh` returns 3 otherwise), so a single transient REST failure is final when no App is configured.

## Do

- `full-loop.md` step 4.5 (both copies) tells callers to run `full-loop-helper.sh merge` with a timeout of at least 600 s, or through the bounded-operation path, and never to read a timed-out run as "not merged" without checking `gh pr view --json state`.
- When no App route is configured and the permission lookup fails with `api-failure`/`unexpected-http` (never on 404 or a parsed verdict), retry once on the same route after a short backoff. Keep the result fail-closed after the retry.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md`
- `.agents/scripts/commands/full-loop.md`
- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-collaborator-permission.sh`

## Verification

- `shellcheck -x .agents/scripts/shared-gh-collaborator-permission.sh` is clean.
- Existing permission tests pass: `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-authority-guard.sh` and `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-wrapper-rest-fallback.sh`.
- A stub that fails the first request and returns 200 `admin` on the second resolves to `admin`. Two failures still return 2.

title: Add safe offline Anthropic OAuth pool rotation diagnostic
body:
# Add a safe, reusable Anthropic OAuth rotation diagnostic

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `oauth rotation diagnostic symlink module hooks isolated probe` returned no matches; the originating session supplies the observed probe and recovery evidence below.
- [x] Discovery pass: prework discovery found 2 recent commits on the target files, 0 related merged PRs, and 0 related open PRs. An all-state issue search for `rotation diagnostic` in titles found no matches. The recent commits concern Anthropic prompt-cache stability, not an offline rotation diagnostic.
- [x] File refs verified: all existing files listed below are tracked at briefing HEAD; the new module's parent is the existing scripts directory.
- [x] Tier: standard. This is a bounded diagnostic using an existing authentication pattern inside a decided isolation boundary, not a redesign of authentication or worker dispatch. No self-hosting dispatch-path file is in the write surface. Implementation is not a verbatim transform, so simple is not appropriate.
- [x] Seeded draft PR: skipped. This request captures follow-up work; no implementation or ready-to-merge change is being claimed.

## Origin

- Created: 2026-10-04
- Created by: ai-interactive, with user acceptance of a reusable-capability brief
- Conversation context: after adding a second Anthropic account, the user requested verification of automatic fallback when one account hits limits. Live token health, deployed hook registration, and an isolated simulated 429 probe were checked. The user accepted capturing the reusable diagnostic in aidevops and explicitly wants existing running sessions left alone.

## What

Expose `aidevops model-accounts-pool probe-rotation anthropic` as an explicitly offline, bounded diagnostic of the deployed Anthropic provider's rotation logic. It must execute the real provider-auth hook and account-selection/recovery code with dummy accounts and simulated responses, report per-scenario PASS/FAIL and a truthful overall exit status, and leave running sessions, real credentials, and real pool metadata untouched.

The diagnostic must be separate from existing `diagnose` and `check`, which can contact live token/API endpoints. Do not silently turn existing commands into inference or limit-exhaustion tests. The new command's output must explicitly say simulated/offline, not live end-to-end failover.

## Why

Token health and plugin registration do not establish that a 429 will retry on another account. A reusable isolated diagnostic avoids repeated ad hoc probes, protects concurrent sessions, and provides repeatable evidence without consuming subscriptions or forcing real rate limits.

## Observed evidence

- A live pool check found two valid Anthropic accounts; status showed two available and no auth errors.
- The deployed plugin's `index.mjs` connects `auth.loader` to `createProviderAuthHook` for the built-in `anthropic` provider.
- A corrected in-memory probe passed rotation in both directions, Retry-After cooldown recording, identical-body retry, continued affinity to the replacement account, bounded exhaustion when both accounts return 429, and exclusion of an alternate already cooling down.
- Existing `test-provider-auth-getauth-recovery.mjs` and `test-oauth-refresh-backoff.mjs` passed all 3 tests. This is supporting evidence, not existing Anthropic 429 coverage.
- Important failure lesson: the first probe matched unresolved absolute module URLs in a Node load hook. The installed plugin path resolved through a deployment symlink into a runtime bundle, so its real pool module bypassed the intended stub. The probe briefly changed real cooldown/lastUsed metadata before stopping. The induced cooldown was cleared, and status returned to two available accounts. Do not repeat this approach.
- The corrected probe intercepts dependency specifiers during resolution, before symlink canonicalisation can defeat matching. It substitutes in-memory pool functions, mocks all fetch calls and SDK auth writes, and rejects filesystem mutations before importing the deployed hook. Only the retry/selection logic was exercised: request transformations and pool persistence were substituted and must not be presented as live provider admission proof.
- Session environment observed: Node v26.4.0 and OpenCode v1.18.34. Do not assume Node-only APIs available in this environment are available across the framework's supported Node versions.

## Tier

Selected tier: `tier:standard`.

The isolation boundary, public command, required scenarios, and non-goals are decided. The worker still needs to compose a compatible implementation and select minimal internal organisation using existing patterns. No authentication policy change is authorised.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `.agents/scripts/oauth-pool-helper.sh`: add `probe-rotation` command dispatch; existing `main` forwards `diagnose` to its sub-library.
- `.agents/scripts/oauth-pool-diagnose.sh`: add the shell invocation helper and document the offline command in `cmd_help`; keep normal diagnostics unchanged.
- `.agents/scripts/oauth-pool-rotation-probe.mjs` (new): isolated scenario runner importing the deployed sibling plugin's real provider hook. Verify the new path is absent before creating it.
- `.agents/tools/opencode/opencode-anthropic-auth.md`: document command, isolation, and limits of evidence; no instruction to restart existing sessions.
- `aidevops.sh`: CLI help only, if needed for discoverability. The existing `model-accounts-pool | map` branch already forwards arguments to `oauth-pool-helper.sh`; do not redesign routing.

### Complete Write Surface

The five files above are the planned implementation surface. Reuse the existing Node assertion/test machinery and shell tooling; no new runner, dependency, CI gate, production test-only API, always-loaded prompt, or authentication behaviour change. Any necessary focused regression coverage should stay in the existing plugin tests directory and be limited to this requested diagnostic's isolation and scenario contract; the exact additional filename is not yet known.

### Implementation Steps

1. Build a short-lived isolated subprocess that installs guards before importing any provider/pool code. Use only dummy credentials and in-memory state; mock all network and SDK auth writes. Intercept dependencies independently of unresolved absolute module paths. Never expose a fallback that imports real pool storage if interception fails.
2. Resolve the deployed sibling plugin from the script installation, with correct support for linked worktrees and symlinked runtime bundles. Exercise its real `createProviderAuthHook`, `provider-auth-pool.mjs`, and recovery logic rather than duplicating the 429 algorithm. Existing reference: `test-provider-auth-getauth-recovery.mjs` constructs the public hook, supplies a mock SDK client/getAuth, and invokes the returned `fetch`.
3. Run deterministic two-account scenarios: first account limited, second account limited, both limited, and alternate cooling. Assert the account sequence, original body reuse, SDK auth update, Retry-After-derived cooldown, replacement-account affinity on the next request, and bounded call count on exhaustion.
4. For each successful rotation scenario, expect `[limited, alternate]` for the initial request and only `alternate` for the next request. For both limited, expect exactly two attempts and a returned 429. For a cooling alternate, expect exactly one attempt, no SDK auth update, and a returned 429.
5. Add clear timeout/failure handling and truthful exit codes. Unsupported Node isolation APIs or unresolved deployed modules must fail/skip explicitly without trying real credentials, network, or production mutations. Document any supported-version limitation rather than falsely reporting success.
6. Connect the new offline command to the existing CLI and document the distinction between simulated logic checks, live token checks, and real request admission. Do not ask users to close or restart running sessions.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- Never read or mutate real OAuth pool/auth files, cooldowns, lastUsed, permissions, or active accounts. Do not perform real auth refreshes, curl requests, inference calls, or credential-bearing subprocess calls.
- Filesystem isolation must fail closed before imports. A missing/mismatched stub must abort, not degrade to a production module. Any controlled scratch artifacts must stay under the framework temp location and contain only dummy data.
- Cover deployment symlinks explicitly: the observed failure was caused by unresolved absolute URL matching. File-copying a production module graph is not necessary and risks stale logic.
- A request-transport substitute is acceptable for isolating retry logic, but the output must disclose the substitution. Do not claim it establishes real Anthropic admission, quota, subscription entitlement, token refresh, or persistence correctness.
- Both-account exhaustion is expected and must be bounded, not an error in the diagnostic. Distinguish a simulated returned 429 from failure to meet the expected scenario.
- Preserve running sessions. No setup/deploy/restart or live account rotation is needed to execute this offline diagnostic. This issue does not authorise publication/release.

### Verification Before Dispatch

- Briefing references verified at HEAD; prework collision search and issue dedup performed.
- Run the production command after implementation and verify all requested scenarios pass with truthful offline labels and a zero exit code.
- Verify malformed/unsupported provider input and induced isolation failures exit nonzero without contacting network or opening production credential stores.
- Verify the command succeeds through a symlinked installed module path, and that dependency-resolution mismatch fails closed.
- Check sentinel real-pool/auth contents and metadata are unchanged in a controlled regression fixture; no real user credentials are needed for this evidence.
- Run ShellCheck on changed shell files and Node syntax checks on the new module.
- Run existing focused checks: `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-provider-auth-getauth-recovery.mjs .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-oauth-refresh-backoff.mjs`, with credential-location overrides cleared/isolated. No full-repository gate is requested just to prove this capture.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Offline CLI diagnostic is discoverable and requires no real accounts, tokens, live API calls, or restarts.
- [ ] Real deployed retry/selection logic is exercised with dummy state and fail-closed isolation.
- [ ] Bidirectional 429 fallback, cooldown, same-request retry, replacement affinity, exhaustion, and cooling-alternate exclusion are asserted and reported individually.
- [ ] Symlinked deployment and isolation-failure paths are verified without touching production credentials/state.
- [ ] Exit status and output distinguish expected simulated provider errors from diagnostic failure, and never claim live end-to-end admission.
- [ ] Existing running sessions and normal auth/rotation semantics remain untouched.
- [ ] Focused existing checks and scoped lint pass; rollback is removal of the new command/module/docs changes, with no credential migration.

## Non-goals

Changing rate-limit semantics, fixing unrelated diagnostics warnings, restarting sessions, automatically resetting cooldowns, testing paid extra usage, adding OpenAI/Google/Cursor coverage, or publishing a release.

title: gh-transport: hung orphan governor holds the revalidation probe and blocks all GitHub reads
body:
## Observed

All GitHub reads through the transport governor on one machine were deferred for 13+ minutes with `error_kind=github-api-read-deferred ... reason="waiting for serialized quota revalidation"`, every retry ending at `retry_at=now+1`. The real quota was fine (`gh api rate_limit`: core 5000 left, graphql 4992).

`admission.sqlite3` (read-only) showed the `core` revalidation row owned by reservation `18e89e…`, `uncertain=0`, started 13 minutes earlier, pid 6943. That pid was a live `gh-transport-governor.py` for a single `gh api /repos/<managed-repo>/pulls/<n> --jq …` call:

- PPID 1 (orphaned: its parent session had exited), no child process.
- `sample 6943`: the main thread is blocked in `lock_PyThread_acquire_lock` → `_pthread_cond_wait`; no other Python thread.

`revalidation_wait()` defers while the probe reservation is active, and `mark_dead_reservations()` only reclaims reservations whose pid is dead or reused. So a live-but-hung governor blocks admission for that scope indefinitely, machine-wide (pulse and every interactive session). Sending SIGTERM to 6943 released it at once, and the next merge went through.

## Likely root cause (not reproduced)

`.agents/scripts/gh-transport-governor.py`:

- `__main__` installs `interrupted()` for SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP, which raises `SystemExit`.
- `execute()` calls `child.wait(timeout=90)`; its `finally` calls `child.terminate()`, `child.wait(timeout=2)`, then `child.kill(); child.wait()` without a timeout.

When the parent dies, the orphan gets SIGHUP. If `SystemExit` is raised while `Popen.wait` holds its internal `_waitpid_lock` (a plain, non-reentrant lock), the `finally` block's blocking `child.wait()` waits on that same lock forever. The matching stack is a main thread blocked on a lock with no other thread.

## Proposed fix

1. `gh-transport-governor.py`: make the signal path deadlock-free. The handler should set a flag or terminate the child rather than raising inside `wait`, or the `finally` should use bounded waits only (`os.waitpid(child.pid, os.WNOHANG)` in a short loop, then give up).
2. `gh_transport_recovery.py`: defence in depth. Treat a reservation as uncertain once it is older than the governor's own maximum lifetime (90s child timeout plus margin, for example 180s), even if the pid is alive, so one hung process cannot block admission for long.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/gh-transport-governor.py` (`execute()`, `__main__` signal handler)
- `.agents/scripts/gh_transport_recovery.py` (`mark_dead_reservations`, `revalidation_wait`)
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-transport-budget.py` (existing revalidation tests; add a stale-live-reservation case only if cheap)

## Verification

- Existing: `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-transport-budget.py` passes.
- Manual: start a governor for a slow `gh api` call, send SIGHUP during the child wait, and confirm it exits within a few seconds. A reservation older than the bound no longer defers admission.

title: Prospective merge guard fails with a missing required blob on Apple Git 2.50.1
body:
## What

Repair the prospective merge guard's scoped blob materialization so a clean, exact-head PR is not blocked by a missing changed-file blob after the guard's bounded prefetch. Do not bypass merge verification or turn this into a full-repository object download.

## Observed evidence

- The pre-merge gate verified the exact remote head, found no configured required checks, returned `PASS_ADVISORY`, and found no external authority gaps.
- `full-loop-helper.sh merge <PR> <owner/repo> --squash` then failed in the isolated prospective TODO check before merging:

```text
Merge blocked: prospective merge-tree evidence is indeterminate
warning: lazy fetching disabled; some objects may not be available
fatal: could not fetch <changed-file-blob-oid> from promisor remote
```

- Native Git was `2.50.1 (Apple Git-155)` on Darwin. A newer installed Git can be selected through the helper's existing `AIDEVOPS_REAL_GIT_BIN` option; this is not permission to disable guards.
- The affected product worktree remains clean, its deployment verified, and its PR open. Project identities, local paths, review data, and credentials are intentionally omitted from this public report.
- Related closed issue #32641 and merged PR #32659 introduced bounded prospective object transfers; this report concerns a missing required blob after that path, not a request to restore unbounded fetching.

## Files and reference pattern

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`: `_merge_fetch_pinned_commit_objects`, `_merge_prefetch_prospective_blobs`, `_merge_fetch_partial_objects`, and `_merge_guard_prospective_todo`.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge.sh`: extend the existing prospective-merge/partial-object-store checks. No new test runner is needed.
- The deployed implementation explicitly fetches candidate old/new blob OIDs using `fetch --filter=blob:none --stdin`, then runs `merge-tree --write-tree` with `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`. title: Bounded operation cancellation leaves an attributable helper Git fetch running
body:
## What

Ensure cancellation/deadline enforcement actually terminates helper-spawned Git fetch descendants before recording a terminal bounded-operation receipt. Preserve attribution: never kill processes by name or sweep unrelated process groups.

## Observed evidence

- `aidevops_bounded_operation.start` ran `env AIDEVOPS_REAL_GIT_BIN=<installed-native-git> full-loop-helper.sh merge <PR> <owner/repo> --squash` with budget 180s and progress interval 20s.
- Beyond the deadline, status stayed `timing_out`, `process_signal: SIGTERM`, `process_exit: null`, and `containment: owned_process_group`. A session-owned cancel request did not immediately terminate the remaining fetch.
- At elapsed 391s, three remaining Git processes formed one group whose root was reparented to PID 1. They were attributable by the exact target command, operation start-time range, parent chain, and working directory in the helper's newly created isolated prospective repository. Project names, local paths, process IDs, and credentials are omitted.
- The fetch was the guard's initial `git fetch --filter=blob:none ... refs/heads/main`, not a repository mutation or merge.
- After explicit TERM to that verified task-owned group, an exact-PID check returned no remaining processes and the tool reached terminal `timed_out` with exit 1 at elapsed 502s. Its captured output reported that the helper's internal 300s prospective transfer deadline had been exceeded. The PR remained open; no merge occurred.
- Native Git on this retry was 2.53.0. This is separate from the missing-blob failure tracked in #33513; do not conflate their causes.

## Investigation and write surface

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`: `_merge_run_bounded_isolated_git` calls `timeout_sec`; inspect its process ownership and signal propagation along this path.
- Locate the implementation and existing tests for the OpenCode `aidevops_bounded_operation` tool and for `timeout_sec` before editing. Their exact source paths have not been established by this report; do not patch deployed copies or invent paths.
- Determine where the helper-spawned group stops being covered by the outer operation's containment model. Either support this nesting with retained attribution, or refuse incompatible child lifecycle behavior before execution.

## Constraints and verification

- Keep cancellation session-owned and remote-target/state validation intact.
- Do not broaden cleanup to executable-name matches, user-owned processes, or unverifiable groups.
- Reuse existing lifecycle tests to cover a helper that spawns an attributable child fetch/group and receives deadline/cancel signals.
- Positive: all attributable children stop within the bounded cancellation/restoration budget, and the receipt records evidence.
- Negative: unrelated process groups remain alive; unknown attribution fails closed; no potentially mutating command continues after a purported cancellation.
- Record explicit restoration/terminal evidence, not only a `SIGTERM` field while a descendant remains running.

## Done when

- [ ] Deadline/cancel stops the observed helper child lifecycle within the supported budget.
- [ ] Terminal receipts accurately reflect process and restoration evidence.
- [ ] Existing ownership isolation and non-destructive verification remain enforced.

title: Hostinger: deactivate default Hostinger AI and Easy Onboarding plugins on new WordPress sites, offer removal
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `hostinger ssh sites plugins` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: 0 commits / 0 merged PRs / 0 open PRs touch `.agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md` in last 48h (last change f5e3d2af9e, #31446)
- [x] File refs verified: 1 ref checked (`.agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md`, 166 lines, `## Configuration` at line 34, `### WordPress multisite cron and update readiness` at line 52), present at HEAD
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — doc-only change with decided behaviour; wording and placement left to the worker
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — a single short doc section, nothing worth seeding

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-04
- **Created by:** ai-interactive (owner request)
- **Conversation context:** Hostinger installs and activates **Hostinger AI** (`hostinger-ai-assistant`) and **Hostinger Easy Onboarding** (`hostinger-easy-onboarding`) on every new WordPress site. The owner had them removed from every existing site on the shared account. They want new Hostinger sites set up by aidevops to have them deactivated by default, and the agent to offer to delete them.

## What

When an agent creates or first sets up a WordPress site on Hostinger (hPanel, Hostinger API website creation, or an addon website), the Hostinger guide tells it to:

1. Check for the Hostinger default plugins: `hostinger-ai-assistant` (Hostinger AI) and `hostinger-easy-onboarding` (Hostinger Easy Onboarding). Also list any other `hostinger*` plugin folders it finds, without acting on them.
2. Deactivate both by default, with no prompt. They are not needed to run the site; deactivating is reversible.
3. Offer to delete them (one question, default yes unless the owner says they use Hostinger's AI writer or onboarding checklist). On yes, uninstall them, which runs their uninstall routine, then delete them, after a tar backup of the plugin folders under `~/backups/` on the account.
4. Leave the `hostinger-auto-updates.php` must-use plugin and Hostinger Tools (`hostinger`) alone. Hostinger Tools covers maintenance mode, redirects and similar, so it is out of scope.
5. Record the outcome in the private site inventory notes (`~/.config/aidevops/site-inventory.json`), never in public content.

## Why

These plugins add admin screens, prompts and calls to Hostinger services on every new site, and most owners never use them. Removing them later takes a separate pass over every site. On 2026-10-04 that pass found them on 7 sites. Doing it at creation keeps new sites clean.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** documentation of a decided procedure in one file, with exact commands supplied. The worker only chooses wording and where the section goes.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md` — add a short `### New WordPress sites: Hostinger default plugins` subsection under `## Configuration`, after the multisite cron subsection (line ~52-59). Keep it within about 25 lines: the doc has a size-tightening history (simplification issues on this file).

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** agents load `services/hosting/hostinger.md` through domain routing for Hostinger work. No scripts parse it (`rg -n "hostinger.md" .agents/scripts` returns nothing relevant).
- **Writers/mutation paths:** doc only. The procedure runs on sites through `ssh <alias>` + WP-CLI, done by the agent at run time.
- **Existing verification/tests:** markdownlint via `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed`.
- **Schemas/config:** N/A. `configs/hostinger-config.json.txt` holds connection metadata only and is not changed.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** deployed copy `~/.aidevops/agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md` updates through `setup.sh`. No manual edit.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A. Existing sites were already cleaned on 2026-10-04.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert the doc commit.

### Implementation Steps

1. Add the subsection with the procedure from **What**, using these proven commands. They were verified on the shared Hostinger account on 2026-10-04.

   ```bash
   # Find them (per site docroot)
   ls -d ~/domains/<domain>/public_html/wp-content/plugins/hostinger-*
   # Deactivate (default, no prompt)
   wp --path=~/domains/<domain>/public_html plugin deactivate hostinger-ai-assistant hostinger-easy-onboarding
   # Before deleting: back up
   tar -czf ~/backups/hostinger-plugins-<domain>-before-removal-<date>.tar.gz -C <plugins-dir> hostinger-ai-assistant hostinger-easy-onboarding
   ```

2. Document the gotchas found while doing this on 2026-10-04:
   - `wp plugin uninstall` fails on Hostinger shared hosting ("Cannot do 'launch': proc_open() … disabled"). Use `wp eval-file` with a small PHP file instead, uploaded with `scp` and deleted afterwards: `deactivate_plugins($files, true)`, then `uninstall_plugin($file)` for each `is_uninstallable_plugin()`, then `delete_plugins($files)`. Need `wp-admin/includes/plugin.php` and `file.php`.
   - If Freesoul Deactivate Plugins is active, it can revert `active_plugins` writes made from WP-CLI. Re-read `active_plugins` after deactivating, and do not delete while a plugin is still listed.
   - On multisite, check network activation (`is_plugin_active_for_network`) and deactivate network-wide.
3. Optional, one line at most: some site plugins also flag these two on the Plugins screen. Do not name private projects; the procedure must not depend on any plugin.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** one site at a time over the shared SSH login. Hostinger limits concurrent connections.
- **Migration/rollback:** deactivation is reversible. Deletion is reversible from the tar backup.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** plugin slugs verified on current versions: Hostinger AI 3.0.38–3.1.2, Easy Onboarding 2.1.17–3.0.2.
- **Idempotency/retry:** the procedure skips plugins that are not installed. Running it twice is harmless.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** if a plugin is still active after deactivating, stop before deletion and report it.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
rg -n "hostinger-easy-onboarding" .agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md
```

- **Surface mapping:** lint proves the doc renders and passes markdownlint. `rg` proves the section exists.
- **Broad verification trigger:** not required (single doc file).

### Scope Boundaries

**Hard boundaries:** do not change `.agents/scripts/hostinger-helper.sh` or add new scripts in this task. Do not include real domains, account usernames or private paths in the doc (use `<domain>`).

**AI brief owner:** marcusquinn (interactive session)

### Files Scope

- `.agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `hostinger.md` has a new-site subsection that says to deactivate `hostinger-ai-assistant` and `hostinger-easy-onboarding` by default and to offer deletion after a backup.

  ```yaml

- [ ] Negative: no real hostnames or `u<digits>` account usernames are added to the doc.

    path: ".agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md"
    expect: absent
  ```

- [ ] Changed-file lint is clean (`.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed`).

## Context & Decisions

- The owner chose "deactivate by default, offer removal", not silent deletion: deactivation is safe and reversible, and deletion stays the owner's call.
- Hostinger Tools (`hostinger`) and the `hostinger-auto-updates.php` mu-plugin are out of scope.

title: docs(hostinger): wp plugin delete fails (proc_open disabled); document wp eval + WP_Filesystem alternative
body:
## What

`services/hosting/hostinger.md` should tell agents that on Hostinger shared hosting `wp plugin delete` (and other WP-CLI commands that shell out) fails, and give the working alternative.

## Observed (2026-10-04, Hostinger shared hosting, WP-CLI 2.12.0, PHP 8.x)

Removing a deactivated plugin across several sites on one Hostinger account:

```
$ wp --path=domains/<site>/public_html plugin delete <slug>
Error: Cannot do 'launch': The PHP functions `proc_open()` and/or `proc_close()` are disabled. Please check your PHP ini directive `disable_functions` or suhosin settings.
```

`wp plugin deactivate` and `wp plugin install <zip> --force` worked. `wp plugin delete` removes the folder via `WP_CLI::launch('rm -rf ...')`, which needs `proc_open`, disabled in Hostinger's PHP CLI.

Working alternative, using WordPress's own filesystem API (no subprocess):

```bash
wp --path="$WP" eval 'require_once ABSPATH . "wp-admin/includes/file.php";
if (is_plugin_active("SLUG/SLUG.php")) { echo "active, skipped"; return; }
WP_Filesystem(); global $wp_filesystem;
echo $wp_filesystem->delete(WP_PLUGIN_DIR . "/SLUG", true) ? "deleted" : "FAILED";'
```

This removes the files without running the plugin's uninstall routine, which keeps its saved data; when an uninstall is wanted, use `delete_plugins(array("SLUG/SLUG.php"))` inside `wp eval` instead (what the Plugins screen's Delete does). Plain `rm -rf` over SSH also works but bypasses WordPress and is less guarded.

## Files to modify

- `.agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md`: add a short "WP-CLI limits on shared hosting" subsection under Troubleshooting (or Configuration) with the error text, cause, the `wp eval` + `WP_Filesystem` alternative, and the uninstall vs keep-data choice. Keep it brief; AI-CONTEXT block only if it fits the size ratchet.
- Optionally `.agents/tools/wordpress/wp-admin.md` (already mentions Hostinger): one line pointing to the Hostinger note for plugin removal.
- Path unknown: whether `wp-helper.sh` has a plugin-delete wrapper that should fall back automatically; check `.agents/scripts/wp-helper.sh` and add a fallback only if a delete path exists there.

## Also useful in the same note (observed in the same session)

- Account layout: sites at `~/domains/<domain>/public_html`; one SSH login per hosting account covers every site on it (the doc already says this).
- PHP error log per site: `domains/<domain>/public_html/error_log`.
- Updating a plugin from a release zip: `scp` the zip once to the account, then `wp plugin install ~/plugin.zip --force` per site; remove the zip afterwards.
- WP-CLI's own phar autoloader can print `include(...vendor/composer/../psr/container/...): Failed to open stream` warnings for plugins that ship prefixed vendor folders (seen with Kadence Pro 1.2.5); this is WP-CLI noise, not a broken plugin install. Check the plugin's `vendor/vendor-prefixed/` path and the site error_log before "repairing" it.

## Verification

- `markdownlint` (or the repo's markdown lint) passes on the changed files.
- The note names the exact error string, so `rg "proc_open" .agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md` finds it.
- AGENTS/prompt size ratchet unaffected (change is in a subagent doc).

body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

# Reusable, resumable WordPress plugin fleet rollout

## What

Implement `wp-fleet-helper.sh` with `plan`, `backup`, `deploy`, `verify`, and `report` phases for one explicitly selected, already-published GitHub-channel plugin release. Replace per-release operational scripts with a private, versioned run manifest and resumable per-installation evidence. Default to read-only planning; deployment requires explicit operator approval of the exact plan fingerprint.

Follow-up to #33481 / PR #33483: those changes shipped a manual fleet-rollout guide, not this executable capability. Keep the release builder's no-publication contract intact.

## Why / observed evidence

An operator-authorized rollout on 2026-10-04 initially covered 17 installations / 30 logical sites. A symlink alias represented the same physical installation and required deduplication. Two staging installations disappeared during backups; the scope guard stopped before deployment. After the operator explained the retirement context and the inventory stabilized, 15 installations / 27 logical sites were updated successfully.

The completed path verified a signed tag and successful CI at its exact commit, matched published/local/server ZIP checksums, retained private DB/config/plugin backups, compared every installed release file, preserved activation states, and checked every logical site's HTTP response and read-only plugin audit. Native updates had already installed an earlier release, so identical-file checks avoided duplicate force reinstalls. These are observed outcomes, not permission for a worker to contact or change the original sites.

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `reusable WordPress fleet rollout helper backup checksums inventory resume` returned no relevant memories.
- [x] Discovery pass: one commit in the last 48h touched selected existing targets, `083a497584` / PR #33483; reassessed as complementary documentation. No open WordPress PRs or matching executable fleet-rollout issues found. Existing release-builder PR #33315 and shared-auth issue #30261 are reference patterns, not duplicate rollout implementations.
- [x] File refs verified at framework HEAD `5230b09cd88902f4016da351029ea6443a66bd1b`; existing targets and reference paths below are present. New script/test parent directories exist; proposed new files are absent.
- [x] Tier: standard; behavior, approval boundary and recovery constraints are specified, but implementation is not a verbatim patch.
- [x] Seeded draft PR: skipped; issue-only scope, no code written or live-site verification authorized.

## Origin / Tier

- Created: 2026-10-04, interactive OpenCode session, at the operator's request to brief the reusable capability.
- Selected tier: `tier:standard`. This is implementation inside an explicit operator-controlled boundary, not permission to invent production authority or change credential storage.

## How

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/wp-helper.sh` — small read-only `--export-sites` command exposing an allowlisted JSON inventory through existing tenant/server-ref/SSH-alias resolution. Never export secret values or dump arbitrary config fields.
- `NEW: .agents/scripts/wp-fleet-helper.sh` — phase CLI, private run-directory management, artifact/approval checks and transport coordination.
- `NEW: .agents/scripts/wp-fleet-runner.py` — bounded server-side filesystem/WP-CLI operations and atomic per-installation checkpoints; detect Python before staging, support the observed Python 3.6 baseline or fail clearly without changing a site.
- `NEW: .agents/scripts/tests/test-wp-fleet-helper.sh` — focused coverage using the existing shell-test/stub pattern, not a new runner or CI infrastructure.
- `EDIT: .agents/tools/wordpress/wp-cli-reference.md` — document the new commands alongside the existing fleet-rollout section, retaining updater-diagnostic guidance.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** current `wp-helper.sh` CLI at lines 592-638 and 727-797; new fleet wrapper reads its allowlisted export. Tenant/config resolution at lines 25-77 and `resolve_server_ref` remain authoritative. Existing callers retain their behavior.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `.agents/scripts/wp-fleet-helper.sh` stages the verified artifact once per selected SSH target; `.agents/scripts/wp-fleet-runner.py` writes only approved private run/backup locations and the explicitly selected plugin directory during approved deployment. Baseline manifests, checkpoints and reports are private JSON, not repository state.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-wp-helper-shared-auth-env.sh:45-105` demonstrates isolated HOME/PATH and SSH stubs. Extend that pattern for fleet guards; do not require live credentials.
- **Schemas/config:** consume existing tenant-aware `wordpress-sites.json` fields/server refs without a new credential store. Version the new run-manifest schema; include release identity, selected roots/URLs, original activation/version, baseline health, backup identity, approval fingerprint and phase outcomes. Store names/references, never secret values in control manifests.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** source belongs under `.agents/`; installed agent-script copies are deployment outputs, not editing targets. Operational manifests/artifacts stay private and out of Git/public issue bodies.
- **Migrations/backfills:** `.agents/scripts/wp-fleet-runner.py` versions its new checkpoint schema and rejects unsupported manifests rather than silently reinterpreting approvals. No WordPress data migration or bulk configuration backfill is part of this task; inventory export reads the existing registry without rewriting it.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** `.agents/scripts/wp-fleet-runner.py` owns only its staged ZIP, locks, incomplete outputs and files it actually changed. Keep backups and reports. Never recreate a retired installation, restore someone else's changes, delete historical analytics, or automatically import a DB dump.

### Implementation Steps

1. Add the allowlisted inventory export without copying tenant/auth resolution into another credential system. Preserve shared-account credentials and SSH aliases; keep connection values and secret references out of public reports. Existing release builder `.agents/scripts/wp-plugin-release-helper.sh:10-20` remains build/check-only and is not modified.
2. `plan` takes explicit plugin slug, repository, published tag/asset and selected sites/category, with an explicit tenant where needed. If registry configuration is absent, offer **explicit read-only discovery** via an operator-selected SSH alias and bounded scan parent; never silently scan an account. Canonicalize roots, reject resolved paths outside approved scan parents, deduplicate aliases, and enumerate all multisite URLs with WP-CLI.
3. Resolve and pin the release once: tag commit, signature verification result, trusted asset digest and expected plugin/version/archive root. Require a matching trusted checksum; if the tag is unsigned/unverifiable, stop and request an explicitly recorded operator trust decision rather than silently accepting it. Use argv arrays, reject archive traversal/unsafe members and mismatched plugin identity. Do not create tags, publish releases, alter distribution assets, install dependencies, or infer credentials from failed updater checks.
4. Seal the plan fingerprint over release identity, canonical installation set, logical URLs and explicit expected health states. Baseline responses such as authentication-required staging must be per-site expectations, never globally accepted. Planning must not invoke plugin updates, change options, or persistently bypass request limiters. The existing cron-context updater diagnostic remains an explicit diagnostic, not a default read-only plan step.
5. `backup` creates verified DB dumps plus plugin/config copies outside web roots, directories 0700/files 0600. Keep DB credentials inside trusted processes/private temporary client configuration, remove that temporary credential file on every exit, and report sanitized failure metadata. Completed backups are reusable only when manifest identities still match; incomplete backups do not qualify.
6. `deploy` requires `--apply` plus the exact approved plan fingerprint. Revalidate the whole selected installation/URL set and each site's version/activation immediately before writes. Drift must stop the run; never lower expected counts automatically. Stage/check the ZIP once per host; skip installation only when target version and every release file already match. Otherwise use WordPress's normal upgrader path without activation flags; validate bytes/version/activation afterward. No content edits, plugin retirement, feature opt-ins, or analytics changes are permitted by this helper.
7. `verify` checks every logical URL against its approved health baseline, fatal markers, activation/version/file identity and optional **operator-supplied read-only** WP-CLI verification argv with bounded timeouts. Never execute instructions/commands from release notes or arbitrary shell strings. Retain private structured evidence; public output is a sanitized summary, not raw config, SQL, responses or logs.
8. Resume from atomic per-installation checkpoints only after revalidating release, scope and installed bytes. Use host/canonical-root mutation locks across different run IDs, with ownership-aware cleanup and no unsafe stale-lock takeover. A failed read-only check must not roll back an installation this run never changed. Default to stop/checkpoint on failure; file rollback requires an explicitly approved migration-compatible rollback policy, verified backup, current-version/ownership checks, and no concurrent newer release. Database rollback requires separate authority and is never automatic.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** account/site retirement, alias changes, native auto-updates and other rollout sessions can race. Use atomic manifests/checkpoints and canonical-root locks; reject changed scope and never overwrite a newer release. Do not claim locks prevent unrelated hosting operations.
- **Migration/rollback:** a plugin may migrate its DB when booted. The helper cannot assume old files remain schema-compatible; fail closed on rollback unless the approved plan establishes compatibility. Keep new user data and DB backups intact.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** preserve old `wp-helper.sh` commands and tenant precedence; reject unknown manifest schemas. Shell follows Bash 3.2-compatible framework conventions, shared constants and explicit function returns.
- **Idempotency/retry:** target-version equality alone is insufficient; compare all release files and preserve activation. Resumption rechecks evidence rather than trusting stale completion flags.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** stop on first unexpected result, preserve completed-site evidence and a recovery checkpoint, and leave remaining sites untouched. Missing/retired sites require operator-reviewed scope replacement, not restoration.

### Complexity Impact

Keep `wp-helper.sh` changes as small export/parser helpers plus a dispatch arm. Its `main` currently spans lines 727-797; do not grow it into the fleet orchestrator or exceed shell complexity gates. New workflow logic lives in the dedicated wrapper/runner.

### Verification Before Dispatch

Discovery and the historical rollout evidence above are verified. **New command behavior remains UNVERIFIED until implementation.** Run these focused commands on the implementation worktree:

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-wp-helper-shared-auth-env.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-wp-fleet-helper.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/wp-helper.sh .agents/scripts/wp-fleet-helper.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-wp-fleet-helper.sh
python3 -m py_compile .agents/scripts/wp-fleet-runner.py
bash .agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Surface mapping:** the shared-auth test covers existing tenant/transport compatibility; the fleet test covers wrapper/runner approval, inventory, backups, archive/newer-version refusal, exact-byte resume, unchanged activation/options/content, expected non-200 health, interrupted checkpoints, lock contention and read-only failure without rollback. ShellCheck and Python compilation cover the changed/new code; changed-file lint covers documentation and framework conventions. Use existing shell stubs and bounded temporary directories, no new test framework or production credentials.
- **Broad verification trigger:** not required; no root CI, shared dependency or credential schema change is planned. No full-repository gate is justified merely by adding this helper.

### Recoverability Checkpoint / Safety-Stop Recovery

After focused CLI/guard checks pass, create a WIP commit before broader checks. A timeout, missing root, checksum mismatch or changed scope pauses deployment, not the objective: persist completed/remaining sites, reason, approved identity and next safe action. Resume only after immutable evidence still matches or the operator explicitly approves a new scope/rollback decision. Never rerun force installs or shrink counts to get past a stop.

### Scope Boundaries

Tool implementation and offline verification only. No live-site access/deployment, retirement, DB imports, credential migrations, hosting API integration, MainWP integration, plugin-source changes, release publication, or editing deployed framework mirrors. A disposable runtime smoke check may use an existing operator-approved environment; otherwise document it as unverified rather than provisioning one.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/wp-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/wp-fleet-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/wp-fleet-runner.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-wp-fleet-helper.sh`

title: fix: footprint overlap serialises dispatch on changelog.txt/readme.txt/README.md (WordPress repos)
body:
## What

Dispatch footprint overlap treats shared docs/changelog files as implementation ownership, so almost every issue in a WordPress-plugin repo serialises behind one in-flight worker.

## Evidence (one private WordPress plugin repo, ~24h of `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`)

- 100+ `FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP` deferrals; 32 against a single blocker issue, which itself never launched (per-candidate timeout).
- Overlapping files were always `README.md`, `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt`.
- The repo's AGENTS.md requires every feature to add a README Features/Credits row and a changelog line, so every brief lists those files under "Files to Modify".
- Global capacity was idle the whole time (`pulse-health.json written: workers=1/20`).

## Root cause

`.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh:67` — `_FOOTPRINT_LOW_INFO_BASENAMES` defaults to `VERSION VERSION.txt version.txt .version CHANGELOG CHANGELOG.md CHANGES.md HISTORY.md`. Matching in `_footprint_is_low_information_path()` (line 543) is exact and case-sensitive, so the WordPress conventions `changelog.txt` and `readme.txt` (and lowercase `changelog.md`) block. `README.md` append-only tables also block.

## Proposed fix

1. EDIT: `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh:67` — add `changelog.txt readme.txt` (WordPress.org plugin readme/changelog) to the default list.
2. EDIT: `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh:543-551` — compare basenames case-insensitively (Bash 3.2 safe: `tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]'`).
3. Consider a per-repo override in `repos.json` (e.g. `footprint_low_info_paths: ["README.md"]`) so repos with append-only README tables can opt in, instead of only the global `AIDEVOPS_FOOTPRINT_LOW_INFO_BASENAMES` env var.

Merge conflicts in these append-only files are already resolved by the conflict-feedback path, so serialising on them costs far more throughput than it saves.

## Verification

- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-footprint-overlap.sh` passes; extend it with a `changelog.txt` / `Changelog.md` case.
- On a repo whose briefs share only `README.md`/`changelog.txt`, two candidates dispatch in the same cycle with no `FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP` line.
<!-- aidevops:origin:interactive -->
<!-- aidevops:sig -->

title: feat: let workers verify against registered local dev sites instead of ending permission_required
body:
## What

Headless workers cannot reach local development sites, so WordPress (and other web) workers finish the code, open a draft PR, then end `status:blocked` / `permission_required` because runtime verification is denied.

## Evidence (one private WordPress plugin repo, 2026-10-03)

- Two workers ended with `[WORKER_BLOCKER_EVIDENCE] BLOCKED: Worker network policy denied the local HTTP verification origin ...`; both left draft PRs with committed implementations.
- The issues were projected `status:blocked` with "Terminal blocker: reason=permission_required owner=permission-maintainer", which needs a human, though the only missing step was hitting the local test site.
- Excerpts: `~/.aidevops/logs/worker-failure-excerpts/issue-<N>-*.log`.

## Root cause

`.agents/scripts/network-tier-helper.sh` denies loopback and raw IPs (`loopback_action: DENY_ACTION`, lines ~290/381; `_is_raw_ip` ~403/460). Called from `.agents/scripts/command_policy_evaluation.py:191-219` (`_evaluate_worker_network`). There is no allowance for local dev hosts registered via local hosting (`services/hosting/local-hosting.md`).

## Proposed fix

1. Allow worker HTTP to loopback / local dev hostnames **only** when the host:port is a registered local site for the worker's repo (local-hosting registry), keeping raw public IPs and exfiltration tiers denied.
2. If that cannot be expressed safely, classify "local verification denied" as a non-terminal outcome: keep the draft PR, mark it ready-for-verification, and leave the issue dispatchable/in-review instead of `status:blocked` + permission-maintainer.
3. EDIT: `.agents/configs/network-tiers.conf` — document the local-dev allowance.

## Verification

- `network-tier-helper.sh check-argv '["curl","-sI","https://<registered-site>.local/"]' --cwd <worktree> --worker-id test` allows; `curl http://127.0.0.1:9999/` for an unregistered port still denies.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-sandbox-command-policy.sh` passes.

title: fix: dispatch_with_dedup 'unable to load issue metadata' discards gh error and never retries
body:
## What

`dispatch_with_dedup` frequently fails with `unable to load issue metadata` and does not retry, so eligible issues lose whole pulse cycles.

## Evidence (one private repo, ~24h of `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`)

- 14 × `[dispatch_with_dedup] Dispatch blocked for #N in <repo>: unable to load issue metadata`, across 8 different open issues; same issues load fine with `gh issue view` interactively.
- Each is reported as `pre-launch failure stage=dispatch_with_dedup rc=1 reason=unclassified_signal`.
- In the same window a candidate hit `Dispatch_max: per-candidate timeout (600s)` → `rc=124 reason=launch_error`, and other candidates were footprint-deferred behind it for that cycle.
- `~/.aidevops/logs/gh-api-calls.log` is ~93 MB, suggesting heavy API pressure at the time.

## Root cause

`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh:844-850` (`_dispatch_load_and_validate_metadata`): `gh_issue_view ... 2>/dev/null || issue_meta_json=""` — stderr is discarded, there is no retry, and the failure returns the same rc=1 as a hard dedup block.

## Proposed fix

1. EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh:844-850` — capture stderr (first line, secrets-safe) into the log; retry once with a short backoff for transient gh/GraphQL/rate errors.
2. Return a distinct "retry later" code (like the existing rc=2 launch no-op) for transient metadata failures so `pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh` classifies it as transient rather than `unclassified_signal`.
3. Check whether the per-candidate timeout (`pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh:547-619`) correlates with the same API pressure and log the slowest stage (`dispatch-stage-instrument.sh`) when it fires.

## Verification

- `rg "unable to load issue metadata" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` lines now include a gh error reason.
- A simulated transient `gh_issue_view` failure (stub) retries and, on second failure, is classified as transient, not `unclassified_signal`.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-candidate-failure-reasons.sh` passes.

title: feat: audited repair for canonical default branch tracking a non-origin upstream
body:
## What

When a canonical checkout's default branch tracks a non-origin remote (e.g. a legacy mirror `othermirror/main`), the pulse skips refresh every cycle and there is no audited way to repair it: the canonical guard blocks `git branch --set-upstream-to=origin/main main`, and `canonical-recovery-helper.sh` has no subcommand for it.

## Evidence

- `pulse.log`: `_pulse_refresh_repo: refresh skipped: noncanonical or missing upstream for <path> — upstream <legacy>/main is not origin/main`, every cycle, silently.
- Interactive repair attempt: `BLOCKED by canonical Git guard: canonical worktree mutation via 'git branch'`.
- `canonical-recovery-helper.sh help` lists restore-default, clear-*-rebase, fast-forward-current, sync-mirror, verify-bootstrap-registration — none set upstream.

## Proposed fix

1. NEW subcommand in `.agents/scripts/canonical-recovery-helper.sh`: `repair-upstream --repo PATH --confirm REPAIR_CANONICAL_UPSTREAM` — only when the current branch is the default branch, `origin/<default>` exists, and the working tree is clean; sets upstream to `origin/<default>` and writes to `canonical-recovery-audit.jsonl`.
2. Or let `sync-mirror` repair upstream as part of convergence.
3. EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh:121-135` — surface persistent "noncanonical upstream" in the supervisor health issue with the repair command, not only in the log.

## Verification

- After repair, the next pulse cycle refreshes the repo with no "refresh skipped" line.

title: claim-task-id.sh bootstraps .task-counter on a project's default branch, then fails issue creation after allocation
body:
## Observed

In a project repo with no `.task-counter`, no `task-id-counter` branch and no TODO.md task IDs, an interactive session ran `claim-task-id.sh --title ... --brief-file ... --labels "auto-dispatch,tier:simple" --repo-path <worktree>` to file a small follow-up issue. The helper:

1. auto-bootstrapped `.task-counter` and pushed two commits straight to the project's default branch (`chore: bootstrap .task-counter (seed=1)`, `chore: claim t1 ...`);
2. then failed issue creation ("Files Scope requires owned author-side repair", status 12) even though the brief had a `### Files Scope` section, leaving `ref=none`.

The project's release build did not exclude `.task-counter`, so the file shipped in the next release zip of a WordPress plugin. It had to be removed with a follow-up PR.

## Expected

- In a repo that has never used task IDs, `claim-task-id.sh` should not push to the default branch without an explicit opt-in (or should use a dedicated counter branch), and should say so before mutating the remote.
- If issue creation will fail on the brief, validation should happen before the counter is advanced (as label validation already does, t2800).

## Steps to add to `tools/wordpress/wp-plugin-new.md` (and `wp-plugin-new-helper.sh` where scriptable)

1. **Codacy**: add the repo with Codacy API v3 (`CODACY_API_TOKEN`), read `data.badges.grade` from `GET /organizations/gh/<owner>/repositories/<repo>`, and put the Codacy badge line back into the README block.
2. **SonarCloud**: automatic analysis needs the project imported (SonarCloud org admin). Script it when a `SONAR_TOKEN` is available; otherwise give the user one link and one sentence as the only human step. Until then the quality-gate badge shows "not found".
3. **CodeFactor, CodeRabbit, Qlty, Socket**: org-level GitHub apps. Check each sees the repo (a check run or status on the first PR) and report any that do not.
4. **Repository metrics**: run `repo-metrics-helper.sh generate` once in the first PR so the metrics badges are right from the start (rename leaves the starter's numbers until the workflow runs).
5. **repos.json**: register with `features: ["code-quality"]` so the daily quality sweep covers it.
6. **First full review**: once the plugin is "made its own", open the Code Audit Routines issue and request `@coderabbitai` full codebase review.
7. **Step 6 wording** ("replace README.md"): keep the badges block and its markers when rewriting the README.
8. Private repos: SonarCloud/Codacy/CodeFactor free tiers only cover public repos. Say which services work while the repo is private and run the steps above when it goes public (the "making it public" step in `wp-plugin-release.md`).

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/wp-plugin-new-helper.sh` (Codacy add + badge, metrics, repos.json features)
- `.agents/tools/wordpress/wp-plugin-release.md` (go-public quality onboarding)

title: feat: README badges - quality services, SPDX license, releases, wordpress-plugin profile, SHA-pinned metrics workflow
body:
## What

README badges: the template and the metrics workflow need some changes before they can serve a repository like the aidevops README itself, or a WordPress plugin.

## Observed (v3.38.4, `readme-badges-helper.sh render` on a public GPL WordPress plugin with releases, SonarCloud, Codacy and CodeFactor)

1. **Quality services missing**: the aidevops README shows SonarCloud and Codacy badges, but `templates/readme/badges.md.tmpl` has no line for them, so other repos never get them. Detect them and add: SonarCloud quality gate (`project_badges/measure?project=<owner>_<repo>`), Codacy grade (`data.badges.grade` from Codacy API v3 `GET /organizations/gh/<owner>/repositories/<repo>`), CodeFactor (`codefactor.io/repository/github/<owner>/<repo>/badge`), each only when the service knows the repo.
2. **License**: always `license-see file`. Read the SPDX ID from `composer.json` `license`, `package.json` `license`, a WordPress plugin header `License:`, or the `LICENSE` text, and show it (for example GPL-2.0-or-later).
3. **Releases**: `detect_has_releases` sets `HAS_RELEASES`, but the template has no line that uses it. Add a latest-release badge.
4. **Dependencies badge** counts `require-dev` (composer) and dev dependencies. A WordPress plugin with zero runtime dependencies shows "6", which suggests runtime risk. Split runtime and dev, or label the badge.
5. **Profiles**: a `wordpress-plugin` profile (detected from a `Plugin Name:` header): Requires at least / Tested up to / Requires PHP from the header and `readme.txt`, and a WordPress.org version badge when the plugin is listed there.
6. **Repo-owned blocks**: a repo that rebuilds its block itself (for example a starter's rename script) needs `check`/`inject` to honour a repo template, for example `.github/readme-badges.md.tmpl` passed as `--template` automatically, instead of reporting drift or overwriting it.

## Metrics workflow (`.github/workflows/loc-badge-reusable.yml`, `templates/workflows/loc-badge-caller.yml`)

7. Callers that pin `uses: …@<sha>` must also set `aidevops_ref: <sha>` by hand, and Dependabot only updates the first, so the reusable YAML and the helper scripts drift apart. Default `aidevops_ref` to the caller's pinned commit (`github.job_workflow_sha`) and drop the need for the input.
8. `legacy_badge_dir` defaults to `.github/badges`. Repos that sync `.github/` to other repos (a plugin starter's core files) then copy one repo's badges into another's. Default it to the badge dir, or make it empty unless asked for.
9. The caller template uses `@main` while the repos' own actions are pinned by SHA. Give a pinned example with the tag comment.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/readme-badges-helper.sh`, `.agents/templates/readme/badges.md.tmpl`
- `.agents/scripts/repo_metrics_dependencies.py` (runtime/dev split)
- `.github/workflows/loc-badge-reusable.yml`, `.agents/templates/workflows/loc-badge-caller.yml`
- `.agents/aidevops/badges.md` (document profiles and the repo template)

- `render` for a public repo with SonarCloud, Codacy, CodeFactor, releases and a GPL license prints all of those badges, each returning `200 image/svg+xml`.

## What

`code-audit-helper.sh audit` gives silently incomplete results. Found while auditing a public WordPress plugin repository on v3.38.4.

## Defects

1. **`--services` list format**: the help says "Comma-separated services", but `--services "codacy,sonarcloud"` logs `Unknown service: codacy,sonarcloud — skipping` and finishes "complete: 0 total findings". Only the space-separated form from the examples works. Accept both, and fail (non-zero exit) when no service is recognised.
2. **SonarCloud returns 0 without `SONAR_TOKEN`**: `sonarcloud: 0 finding(s) collected` for a public project that has 340 open issues through the unauthenticated `api/issues/search`. Use the public API when there is no token, or log `skipped: SONAR_TOKEN not set` instead of reporting 0 findings.

title: Pulse dispatch head-of-line starvation: single admitted wave re-spent on deterministically blocked candidates every cycle (0 dispatches in 7h)
body:
## Summary

Pulse dispatch made **zero** launches for ~7 hours with 19 free slots and 73 candidates. Each cycle had budget for only one parallel wave of `dispatch_max`. That wave went to the same deterministically blocked candidates every cycle, so dispatchable issues behind them were never attempted.

This is a follow-up to GH#33307 (merge pass consuming the cycle budget). The reserve from GH#33307 now guarantees one per-candidate floor. With `max_parallel=6`, that buys exactly one wave. Then `Dispatch_max stopping early: cycle wall-clock budget below per-candidate floor (remaining=594s floor=600s)`.

## Observed (v3.38.4/3.38.5, single runner, 2026-10-04)

- `pulse-health.json` `cycle_state.progress`: `last_at=2026-10-03T21:53:25Z kinds=[worker-dispatched] consecutive_no_progress_cycles=14`; `issues_dispatched=0`, `workers_active=1/20`.
- The first wave of the latest cycle (`pulse.log`) went to:
  - Two issues in a private managed repo (`#A`, `#B`): `DISPATCH_BLOCK_REASON reason=permission_grant_unverified signal=STALE_APPROVAL`. Their signed grants expired after 4h the previous day, and this outcome cannot change until a maintainer signs a grant or withdrawal.
  - `#C`: already `status:blocked` by the cost circuit breaker. It was still attempted and returned `reason=cost_budget_exceeded` after **157s**.
  - `#D`: `issue needs comment consolidation` (83s). `#E`: rc=2 after **356s**. `#F`: `GH#31404: metadata fetch failed ... (transient)` after **214s**.
- Earlier cycles: `remaining=-788s`, `-994s`, `-136s` before the candidate loop. Merge pass `total_s=557`.
- Seven more `status:available` + `auto-dispatch` `priority:high` issues in the same repo were never reached. Three of them, plus `#F`, dispatched on the first attempt through `dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh dispatch <N> <slug>` ("Dedup: clear"), so they were dispatchable all along.
- The benign-block skip (`_dispatch_skip_for_benign_block`, "from current pulse cycle") is cleared on cycle exit (`_dispatch_cleanup_benign_blocks_cycle` trap in `pulse-wrapper.sh:1603`). Deterministic blocks are therefore rediscovered at full cost each cycle.

## Expected

1. Deterministic, maintainer-gated blocks should be skipped cheaply before a wave slot is spent. These include `permission_grant_unverified` (`STALE_APPROVAL`/`NO_APPROVAL`), `cost_budget_exceeded`/`status:blocked`, `needs_maintainer_permissions` and consolidation-needed. Persist the block across cycles, keyed by issue plus `updatedAt`/comment fingerprint, and re-check only when the issue changes or after a bounded TTL.
2. `status:blocked` issues should not enter the `dispatch_max` candidate list. Alternatively, they should be ordered after every `status:available` candidate.
3. When the budget only admits one wave, fill it with the highest-scoring candidates that are not known to be blocked. Head-of-line blocking should not starve the queue.
4. Report `pulse_dispatch_head_of_line_blocked` (or similar) in `pulse-current-state-helper.sh`/`pulse-check-helper.sh` when N consecutive cycles fill their only wave with repeat blocked candidates.

## Files to investigate

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh`: `_dispatch_should_skip_candidate`, `_dispatch_skip_for_benign_block`, and the cycle-budget early stop around lines 700–712.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh`: `_dispatch_benign_blocked_candidate_reason` (around line 670) and the benign reason lists (around lines 227 and 343).
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh`: the `permission_grant_unverified` block (around line 868) and the cost-budget dedup path.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`: `_pulse_cycle_budget_admits_dispatch` and `_pulse_dispatch_reserved_finalise_seconds` (GH#33307 reserve, lines 1129–1165).

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`

## Verification

- Unit: extend the existing pulse dispatch tests (`tests/test-dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`/candidate-loop tests) with a fixture where the first 6 candidates return `permission_grant_unverified` and the 7th is dispatchable. With one admitted wave, the 7th must be attempted.
- Runtime: after deploy, `pulse.log` should show blocked candidates skipped with a cached reason (no `DISPATCH_CANDIDATE_ATTEMPT`). `cycle_state.progress.kinds` should include `worker-dispatched` whenever dispatchable candidates exist.

Related: GH#33307, GH#33036, GH#29058, GH#33330.

title: bug: reject negated issue-closing keywords in managed PR bodies
body:
## Observed defect

A maintained application's partial documentation PR intentionally used a non-closing parent reference and stated that two parent criteria remained incomplete. Its body also contained a natural-language negated instruction with an adjacent GitHub closing keyword and numeric issue reference. GitHub's `closingIssuesReferences` included the parent anyway; merging closed it, applied completion metadata and removed its claim. The primary verified the incorrect completed state, reopened the parent and restored ownership.

Source inspection showed `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh` correctly reconciles GitHub-confirmed closing references; it is not evidence that ordinary `Ref`/`For` references were treated as closure authority. The defect to prevent is unsafe managed PR-body wording before the merge, not suppressing legitimate confirmed-closure reconciliation.

Explain that a partial parent should use `For`/`Ref` and prose such as “the parent remains open,” never an adjacent closing keyword and numeric issue reference even under negation. Preserve valid explicit leaf closure and normal closing-reference reconciliation.

Synthetic reproduction strings for the existing validator harness: `Do not close #123 from this PR`, `Do not resolve #123`, and `Never fixes #123`. These are fixture-only example numbers, not assigned tasks. Safe partial wording is `Ref #123. The parent issue remains open.`; legitimate completed-leaf wording is `Resolves #123`.
