title: full-loop-helper-merge: _merge_prefetch_prospective_blobs uses --filter=blob:none when fetching blob OIDs, blocking all merges
body:
## Bug

`full-loop-helper-merge.sh`: `_merge_prefetch_prospective_blobs` calls `_merge_fetch_partial_objects` with `--filter=blob:none` when fetching specific blob OIDs. Since `--filter=blob:none` instructs the server not to send blobs, the blobs are never materialized, causing `_merge_verify_prospective_blobs` to fail with "N of N required prospective blobs were not materialized by the bounded fetch." All merges via `full-loop-helper.sh merge` fail regardless of CI/review status.

## Reproducer

On any repo with a MERGEABLE/CLEAN PR (checks pass, no conflicts):

```bash
full-loop-helper.sh merge <PR> <REPO> --squash
```

Error observed (v3.38.10, runtime bundle 3.38.10-32e2778c9815):
```
[SUCCESS] Remote PR evidence verified at head <sha>; required checks are terminal-success
[SUCCESS] Review bot gate: PASS_ADVISORY — safe to merge PR #<N>
[SUCCESS] External/fork authority preflight: no external authority targets for PR #<N>
[ERROR] Merge blocked: 4 of 4 required prospective blobs were not materialized by the bounded fetch
[ERROR] Merge blocked: unable to materialize pinned PR commits for prospective TODO validation
```

Confirmed on EdgeBrand/metal-kards-proofing PR #247 (docs-only, MERGEABLE/CLEAN, checks PASS, admin author).

## Root Cause

In `_merge_prefetch_prospective_blobs` (line ~856 of 2552), after computing blob OIDs to verify, the code calls:

```bash
_merge_fetch_partial_objects "$real_git" "$object_repo" "$wanted" \
    --no-write-fetch-head --stdin -- "$_MERGE_PROSPECTIVE_REMOTE" || return 1
```

`_merge_fetch_partial_objects` unconditionally applies `--filter=blob:none` to every fetch. When called to fetch specific blob OIDs (the second use), this filter prevents those blobs from being transferred even though they are explicitly wanted by OID.

The first use (fetching commits+trees) is correct with `--filter=blob:none`. The second use (fetching specific blob OIDs) should use no blob filter or `--no-filter`.

## Fix

The second call to `_merge_fetch_partial_objects` in `_merge_prefetch_prospective_blobs` needs a mechanism to disable the blob filter. Options:
1. Add an optional `--fetch-blobs` parameter to `_merge_fetch_partial_objects` that replaces `--filter=blob:none` with no filter
2. Create a separate `_merge_fetch_blob_objects` function without the filter
3. Inline a direct fetch call in `_merge_prefetch_prospective_blobs` when stdin is a blob OID list

### Files Scope
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`

## Impact

## What

Prevent worker activity and provider/account reports from silently returning all-zero results when retained objective evidence exceeds the operating system's command-line argument limit.

## Why / observed evidence

An interactive pulse health check on 2026-10-04/05 found a contradiction: `worker-activity-helper.sh summary --since 24h` returned zero records, although its canonical runtime ledger contained 27 worker attempt records. Provider diagnostics also incorrectly omitted the account pool.

The helper serializes retained `attempt_outcome` records and passes them to jq using one `--argjson objective_outcomes` argument. The observed bounded payload contained 1,091 records and serialized to 689,348 bytes. On the inspected Linux host, this exceeds the per-argument limit. Existing stderr suppression and fail-open handling convert the failed invocation into plausible-looking zeros.

With objective evidence temporarily excluded from a read-only diagnostic invocation, the same ledger reported 27 attempts, 23 terminal sessions and 15 raw runtime handoffs. The prepared repair reads all retained evidence normally and reconciles validated outcomes rather than discarding them.

On the affected installation, run `worker-activity-helper.sh summary --since 24h --json --no-pr-check` and `worker-activity-helper.sh providers --since 24h --json` with the retained evidence unchanged: both produce empty historical projections despite nonempty in-window worker records. Compare with the read-only invocation `env AIDEVOPS_OBJECTIVE_EVIDENCE_LIMIT=1 worker-activity-helper.sh summary --since 24h --json --no-pr-check`: counts reappear. This limit override is diagnostic only, not the repair.

## What

Treat a confirmed absent root `TODO.md` in a successfully created pulse TODO-sync workspace as an explicit non-applicable skip when planning is not enabled, rather than running four failing sync stages on every cycle. ## Why / observed evidence

During a 2026-10-04/05 interactive pulse check, one pulse-enabled repository's remote default-branch tree contained no root `TODO.md`. Every cycle still invoked pull, close, reopen and relationship synchronization. Each emitted `Project root does not contain TODO.md` and `status=retryable_failure`; the aggregate sync consequently reported failure.

Pulse enablement is not proof that a repository has adopted TODO-based planning. Do not create a synthetic planning file or disable all pulse activity to suppress the symptom.

## Priority and verified planning contract

Low priority: this is truthful skip/error handling and repeated-work cleanup, not a proven worker-launch blocker or a measured major performance regression. Prioritize the confirmed reporting defect (#33621) and dispatch diagnosis (#33623).

The initialization source starts `enable_planning=false` and enables it only when the parsed feature set includes planning (`.agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/aidevops-init-lib.sh`, `_init_run_workflow`). `_init_planning_files` creates root `TODO.md` only when that feature is enabled. The affected repository's registration advertised code-quality only, not planning. Its missing file is therefore consistent with feature-specific initialization, not evidence of an incomplete all-features setup.

This source file is a read-only contract reference, not an additional implementation target. Resolve planning intent from the existing trusted project/registration metadata; do not infer it solely from pulse enablement or the existence of a file. Unknown or contradictory metadata must remain visible rather than being declared healthy. A present legacy TODO must retain current synchronization behavior even when feature metadata is absent.

title: Double-sourcing shared-model-tier.sh breaks custom routing table in ai-research-helper.sh
body:
## Description

Double-sourcing of `shared-model-tier.sh` via `shared-constants.sh` breaks custom routing table resolution in `ai-research-helper.sh`, causing it to fall back to hardcoded `gpt-5.4-mini` (which doesn't work with ChatGPT OAuth) instead of using the custom routing table's `gpt-5.6-luna`.

## Expected Behavior

`ai-research-helper.sh --model simple` should resolve to `openai/gpt-5.6-luna` (from custom routing table) and work with ChatGPT OAuth.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```bash
ai-research-helper.sh --model simple --prompt "test" --max-tokens 10
```

**Actual output**:

```
[AI-RESEARCH] OpenCode AI research call failed
```

**Expected output**:

Successful response from OpenCode using `gpt-5.6-luna` model.

**Causal status**: confirmed

**Owning-path proof**:

- **Production entry point**: `pulse-wrapper.sh` → `_pulse_run_fix_the_fixer_detector_if_stale` → `pulse-fix-the-fixer-detector.sh` → `ai-research-helper.sh` (via `_classify_via_llm`)
- **Call chain**: `ai-research-helper.sh` sources `shared-constants.sh` → `shared-constants.sh` sources `shared-model-tier.sh` → `ai-research-helper.sh` ALSO sources `shared-model-tier.sh` directly → double sourcing breaks `model_routing_table_path` resolution
- **Integrated verification**: Running `ai-research-helper.sh` in isolation works; running via pulse wrapper fails

**Causal code**:

```bash
# ai-research-helper.sh
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/shared-model-tier.sh"

# shared-constants.sh
_source_shared_module_with_retry "${_SC_SELF%/*}/shared-model-tier.sh"
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have custom routing table at `~/.aidevops/agents/custom/configs/model-routing-table.json` with `simple` tier → `openai/gpt-5.6-luna`
2. Have ChatGPT OAuth configured in OpenCode (no API key)
3. Run `ai-research-helper.sh --model simple --prompt "test" --max-tokens 10`
4. Observe failure with `gpt-5.4-mini` fallback (hardcoded in `ai-research-helper.sh`)
5. Compare with isolated sourcing: `source ai-research-helper.sh; resolve_opencode_model_id simple` → returns `openai/gpt-5.6-luna`

## Workarounds Applied

1. **Export `AIDEVOPS_AI_RESEARCH_PROVIDER=anthropic`** — bypasses OpenCode path entirely, uses Anthropic OAuth which works
2. **Isolated sourcing test** — confirmed custom routing table works when `shared-constants.sh` is not sourced first

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.38.10
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **Custom routing table**: `~/.aidevops/agents/custom/configs/model-routing-table.json` with dual-provider failover
- **OpenCode auth**: ChatGPT OAuth (Codex) + Anthropic OAuth

## Additional Context

**Models tested with ChatGPT OAuth:**
- `gpt-5.6-luna` ✅ WORKS
- `gpt-5.6-terra` ✅ WORKS  
- `gpt-5.6-sol` ✅ WORKS
- `gpt-4o` ❌ "Unexpected server error"
- `gpt-5.4-mini` ❌ "not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account"
- `gpt-5.4` ❌ "not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account"

**Root cause**: `shared-constants.sh` sources `shared-model-tier.sh` via `_source_shared_module_with_retry`, but `ai-research-helper.sh` also sources it directly. The second sourcing resets/breaks the custom table resolution, causing `model_tier_candidate_for_provider simple openai` to fail and fall back to hardcoded `gpt-5.4-mini`.

**Affected components**: `fix-the-fixer-detector` (t3077), any code using `ai-research-helper.sh` via the full sourcing chain.

**Proposed fixes**:

title: bug(update): legacy TODO metadata aborts the planning-template check
body:
## Goal

Keep `aidevops update` running when a planning-enabled repository has a legacy TODO file without `TOON:meta`, or only an outdated PLANS file. Make the optional planning upgrade prompt safe when stdin is unavailable or noninteractive.

## Observed failure

Reproduced on macOS with aidevops v3.38.10. Framework synchronization succeeds, then the command prints:

```text
Checking Planning Templates

[WARN] 4 project(s) have outdated planning templates:
```

The process exits with status 1 before listing any projects, displaying the latest template, or reaching later tool maintenance. An isolated invocation of `_update_check_planning` in a separate `bash -euo pipefail` process reproduces the same output and exit status, without running the rest of the updater.

## Root cause

`.agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/aidevops-repos-lib.sh` correctly classifies an existing planning file without `TOON:meta` as needing an upgrade. However, `.agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/aidevops-update-lib.sh`, inside `_update_check_planning`, then executes:

```bash
todo_ver=$(grep -A1 "TOON:meta" "$repo/TODO.md" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 | cut -d',' -f1)
```

When the marker is absent, `grep` exits 1. With `pipefail` the assignment fails, and `errexit` terminates the command before the existing `${todo_ver:-none}` fallback can be used. A plans-only repository has the same display failure because TODO.md is absent. After guarding the version read, the unguarded `read -r -p` also fails on EOF and can consume automation input.

## Files scope and implementation

- `.agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/aidevops-update-lib.sh`: guard both advisory version-extraction pipelines with `|| true`; display `vnone` when metadata is unavailable. Declare the response locally. Only read confirmation with terminal stdin outside `NON_INTERACTIVE=true` and auto-update mode, and place `read` in the conditional so EOF defaults to no upgrade rather than aborting.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-aidevops-update-planning.sh` (new focused regression script): source the existing update and repos libraries in separate strict Bash processes and use temporary planning fixtures.
- Reference patterns: the missing-marker handling in `check_planning_file_version`, the terminal/noninteractive check in `aidevops.sh` `_update_finish`, and existing `test-aidevops-update-help.sh` / `test-aidevops-update-tool-reporting.sh` shell regression scripts.

Do not normalize task IDs, rewrite user TODO files, or edit registered projects as part of this repair. Those advisory migrations are separate from the updater crash.

## Verification and acceptance

- Legacy TODO without `TOON:meta`: print `vnone`, report the latest template, provide manual upgrade advice, and exit successfully.
- Versioned outdated TODO: preserve the displayed version and continue.
- Missing TODO with outdated PLANS: print `vnone` and continue.
- Current TODO: remain a successful no-op.
- Template lacking metadata: report `vnone` without aborting.
- Closed stdin and piped `y`: continue without automatically upgrading projects; non-TTY input must not serve as approval.
- Preserve interactive confirmation for a normal terminal; declining or EOF must remain nonfatal.
- Test with both installed Bash and macOS `/bin/bash`, and run ShellCheck, Bash syntax checks, and `git diff --check`.

A local patch has been verified: the planning check against the original registered projects lists all four legacy projects and reaches a continuation sentinel with exit 0, without modifying them. Existing update-help checks (7) and tool-reporting checks (22) pass. The patch is prepared locally and is not yet submitted as a PR or deployed.
<!-- aidevops:origin:interactive -->
<!-- aidevops:sig -->

title: Worker egress: no explicit exact-host authorization path for owner-approved SSH aliases
body:
## What
Provide an explicit, owner-approved exact SSH-alias-to-endpoint authorization path for headless operational workers, preserving fail-closed classification. Do not auto-read SSH credential/config directories, silently resolve arbitrary aliases, or bypass worker egress checks.

## Why / observed evidence
A managed operational worker launched successfully, verified GitHub state, then terminated permission_required before contacting its owner-authorized CI host. Shared command policy rejected the existing single-label SSH alias as an unclassified destination. Interactive preflight had previously succeeded, but this must not be used to bypass the worker boundary. The framework currently provides no actionable host-specific recovery in the denial message.

## Reproducer (offline, no network or credentials)
```
python3 .agents/scripts/command-policy-helper.py network-destinations --argv-json '["ssh","-o","BatchMode=yes","ci-host-alias","id"]' --cwd <authorized-worktree>
```
Actual output:
```
{"destinations":[],"endpoints":[],"local_site_hosts":[],"recognized":true,"requires_destination":true,"unclassified":["ssh-target:ci-host-alias"]}
```
Worker policy rejects this at network-tier-helper.sh lines ~737-740 before domain tier lookup. Merely adding a tier entry for the alias therefore cannot safely solve it. A network requirement is absent from dispatch's preflight capability report, so launch succeeds only to fail immediately in the worker.

## How / source
- .agents/scripts/command_policy_transport.py ~13-26 passes SSH target to _add_destination; ~47-83 parses options.
- .agents/scripts/command_policy_network.py owns host normalization/destination classification; inspect before editing.
- .agents/scripts/network-tier-helper.sh ~727-745 rejects unclassified destinations before classification.
- Inspect existing explicit SSH site/infrastructure inventory and signed owner approval contracts for reusable exact endpoint bindings. Exact implementation/config location is unknown until discovery; no ad-hoc allow-all or automatic .ssh/config read.
- Add a supported host-specific owner-approved binding with endpoint/account/port scope as appropriate and clear failure/recovery instructions; require exact match, authenticated approval and fail-closed handling of unknown mappings, proxies/forwarding, expired approval and command mismatch.
- Include this requirement in operational dispatch preflight so unsupported/unauthorized SSH is held before claiming/launching a worker. Do not relabel it generic credential failure or create comment consolidation.

### Files Scope
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/command_policy_transport.py
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/command_policy_network.py
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/network-tier-helper.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-command-policy-helper.sh

- EDIT: .agents/scripts/command_policy_dispatch.py
- ADD: .agents/scripts/ssh_binding_helper.py
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/runner-capability-helper.sh
- ADD: .agents/reference/ssh-bindings.md

Integration evidence: analyze_network_argv must pass repository context into SSH authorization; runner_capability_check owns the fresh preclaim gate and currently supports only secrets/probes. Reuse the fixed approval-keys/approval.pub owner trust anchor with a distinct SSH-signature namespace, never SSH config or private-key discovery. The verifier and grant-preparation CLI share exact command validation; issue requirements are data, never executed commands. Config-disabled SSH commands bind alias, endpoint, account, port, repository and expiry; endpoint tier denials remain authoritative. Verification: bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-command-policy-helper.sh; bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-runner-capability.sh; bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-network-egress.sh; bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-sandbox-command-policy.sh; scoped ShellCheck and Python compile. Offline grant and preflight fixtures live in the existing command-policy suite.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Unknown SSH aliases still fail closed without network access or SSH config/private-key reads.
- An explicitly owner-approved exact binding works through the normal worker policy; no blanket filesystem, subnet, wildcard host or network allow grants.
- Proxy/forwarding ambiguity remains denied unless separately and explicitly authorized.
- Preflight surfaces missing host authorization and gives a supported exact-grant recovery path before launch.
- Existing parser/security regression suites and scoped lint pass; tests remain offline with non-secret fixtures.

## Safety and ownership
Private repository names, SSH aliases, endpoints, local paths and credentials deliberately omitted. User explicitly requests narrow access only and forbids root-directory permission requests or denial bypass. No temporary files/log directories or runtime permissions were broadened. File as thinking-tier security/dispatch work; owner requested framework defect capture alongside operational setup. This defect is separate from repository-origin drift in #33629.

title: full-loop merge: fail closed with an actionable message when native Git predates 2.44 (GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH)
body:
## Goal

Make the prospective TODO merge guard fail closed with a clear, actionable message when the selected native Git is older than 2.44. Today such hosts get the vague error "Merge blocked: unable to verify prospective blob presence".

## Why

The guard relies on `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` (set in `_merge_unset_repository_git_env`) so that its partial object store never contacts the remote implicitly. `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH` was introduced in Git 2.44. Older Git ignores it, so `cat-file --batch-check` in `_merge_verify_prospective_blobs` tries an implicit lazy fetch for missing objects and exits non-zero. The guard still fails closed, but the message names neither the cause nor the remedy.

Evidence: #33618 reported exactly this on Apple Git 2.39.5. The root cause of the blob-materialization failure itself (stdin loss in the `timeout_sec` fallback) was fixed separately in #33635; this issue only covers the diagnostic. Ref #33619.

## Files to modify

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`
  - `_merge_guard_prospective_todo` (around the `[[ -x "$real_git" ]]` check, roughly line 1000): before creating the object context, read `"$real_git" --version`, parse major/minor, and if the version is below 2.44, `print_error` something like: `Merge blocked: native Git <version> at <path> predates GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH (Git 2.44+ required for prospective TODO validation); set AIDEVOPS_REAL_GIT_BIN to a newer Git (for example Homebrew git)`, then `return 1`.
  - If the version cannot be parsed, fail closed with a similar message. Never fall through to a lazy-fetch-capable path.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge.sh`: extend the existing prospective-guard tests. `run_prospective_todo_guard` already accepts a custom Git binary as its 8th argument (see `create_prospective_git_probe` for the wrapper pattern). Add a wrapper that answers `--version` with `git version 2.39.5` and delegates everything else; assert the guard fails with the new message before any fetch.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge.sh`

## Reference pattern

- Existing fail-closed messages in `_merge_guard_prospective_todo` (`print_error "Merge blocked: ..."; return 1`).
- Version-banner variants to parse: `git version 2.50.1 (Apple Git-155)`, `git version 2.53.0`, `git version 2.39.5 (Apple Git-154)`.

## Constraints

- Do not relax lazy-fetch protection, change fetch flags, or add a bypass. This is a diagnostic only.
- Do not change the default `AIDEVOPS_REAL_GIT_BIN` (`/usr/bin/git`); current Apple Git (2.50.x) already qualifies.
- Bash 3.2 compatible; ShellCheck clean; `local var="$1"` style; explicit returns.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge.sh` must report 0 failures, with the new check passing.
- Existing prospective tests (live fetch, criss-cross, no-timeout PATH) still pass with Git 2.44 or newer.

title: t18589: Surface OpenCode provider errors in ai-research-helper.sh failures
body:
## Task


When the OpenCode provider path in `ai-research-helper.sh` fails, either from a non-zero `opencode run` exit or from output containing no response text, the helper logs one bounded, credential-scrubbed line to stderr. The line names the resolved model and gives the provider's error message. Example: `OpenCode AI research call failed (model=openai/gpt-5.4-mini): The 'gpt-5.4-mini' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account.`

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->


## Pre-flight (auto-populated by briefing workflow)

- [x] Memory recall: `ai-research-helper opencode error output` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: 1 commit (c842b638) / 0 related merged PRs in 48h / 0 open PRs touch `.agents/scripts/ai-research-helper.sh`

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-05
- **Session:** opencode:interactive maintainer review of GH#33630
- **Created by:** ai-interactive
- **Conversation context:** Reviewing GH#33630 falsified its double-sourcing root cause. The real diagnostic gap is that `call_opencode` discards OpenCode's own error output, so the reporter could only see `OpenCode AI research call failed` and guessed at the cause.

## What

When the OpenCode provider path in `ai-research-helper.sh` fails, either from a non-zero `opencode run` exit or from output containing no response text, the helper logs one bounded, credential-scrubbed line to stderr. The line names the resolved model and gives the provider's error message. Example: `OpenCode AI research call failed (model=openai/gpt-5.4-mini): The 'gpt-5.4-mini' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account.`

## Why

`call_opencode` (`.agents/scripts/ai-research-helper.sh:352-366`) captures `opencode run --format json ... 2>&1` into `raw` but never reports it on failure. Callers such as `pulse-fix-the-fixer-detector.sh:300-322` record the first 200 bytes of stderr as the failure rationale, so operators see no model and no cause. GH#33630 was filed with a wrong root cause because of this. The Anthropic path already surfaces `.error.message` (`ai-research-helper.sh:308-313`), so the OpenCode path is inconsistent with it.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** A small, local diagnostic change with a known reference pattern (`extract_opencode_text`, `scrub_credentials`). The worker still chooses the exact extraction precedence, so this is not `tier:simple`.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/ai-research-helper.sh:236-266` — add `extract_opencode_error` next to `extract_opencode_text`, using the same strip_ansi + python line-scan pattern
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/ai-research-helper.sh:351-366` — on both failure branches of `call_opencode`, log the model and the extracted, scrubbed, bounded error

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `pulse-fix-the-fixer-detector.sh:300-322` reads `head -c 200` of stderr into `RATIONALE`/cooldown reasons (log-only; the comment path at `:536` runs only on a successful YES verdict). Other callers just propagate stderr.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** N/A. Stderr diagnostics only; exit codes stay 1/2 as today.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-ai-research-helper-oauth-pool.sh` (Anthropic path; must still pass). Production path: `ai-research-helper.sh --provider opencode --model <bad-model> --prompt test`.
- **Schemas/config:** N/A. No config or schema change.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** Deployed copy under `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/`, updated by `setup.sh`/release.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** Trivial revert.

### Implementation Steps

1. `extract_opencode_error "$raw"`: strip ANSI, then prefer the last JSON event with `type == "error"` and print `error.data.message`, falling back to `error.message` and then `error.name`. Otherwise print the last non-empty, non-JSON line. Collapse whitespace.
2. In `call_opencode`, pass the result through `scrub_credentials` (`shared-constants.sh:669`) and truncate it to 160 characters, so the whole stderr line stays inside the detector's 200-byte capture. Log `<existing message> (model=<model_id>): <detail>`, or the existing message with only the model when no detail exists.
3. Run ShellCheck, then exercise the production path with a nonexistent model. Observed OpenCode error event shape: `{"type":"error",...,"error":{"name":"UnknownError","data":{"message":"Unexpected server error. ...","ref":"err_..."}}}`.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** N/A. Pure stderr formatting in one process.
- **Migration/rollback:** Revert restores the generic message.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** The existing message text remains the prefix, so log greps still match. Exit codes are unchanged.
- **Idempotency/retry:** No state.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** Extraction failure falls back to the existing generic message (`|| detail=""`).
- **Secret exposure:** The provider output can echo request data. Always pass it through `scrub_credentials` and bound its length. Never log the prompt.

### Complexity Impact

title: runner-capability: log which secret failed and why; surface locked GPG store as runner health
body:
## What

When the runner-capability gate defers an issue, log which requirement failed and why, and surface a locked-GPG condition as a runner health signal instead of a silent per-issue deferral.

## Why

On a shared Linux runner (v3.38.10), every `requires-secrets:` issue was deferred for hours with only:

```text
runner_capability_check source=fresh requirements=5
[dispatch_with_dedup] #11655 deferred: runner_capability_unmet
```

All five secrets were present in the runner's gopass store. The actual cause was that the user's GPG key is passphrase-protected and the gpg-agent cache had expired (`max-cache-ttl 7200`). Unattended decryption then fails with `gpg: public key decryption failed: No pinentry`, so every `aidevops secret check` returned rc=1 in ~0.8s. That took a manual investigation to find: the log does not distinguish "secret missing" from "store locked" from "check timed out", and does not name the secret. Secret *names* are not sensitive (they already appear in issue bodies).

Related: `get_secret_value` (`.agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh:101`) does not fall back to `credentials.sh` when gopass owns the name but decryption fails, so a user cannot fix this by adding a plaintext fallback without also removing the gopass entry. That may be intended (gopass is authoritative), but it should be stated in the deferral reason.

## How

1. In `.agents/scripts/runner-capability-helper.sh` (`run_check`, inside the embedded Python), return a reason instead of exiting on the first failure: `secret_missing name=X`, `secret_unreadable name=X` (gopass owns the name but decrypt failed), `check_timeout name=X`, `probe_failed path=...`. Print it on the existing stderr line so `_runner_capability_check_fresh_logged` logs e.g. `deferred: runner_capability_unmet reason=secret_unreadable name=BETA_QA_ADMIN_EMAIL`.
2. To tell missing from locked without decrypting twice, add a status-only mode to `.agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh` `cmd_check` (e.g. distinct exit codes: 1 missing, 3 present-but-unreadable), using `gopass_owns_secret` for presence. Never print values.
3. When the reason is `secret_unreadable` for a gopass entry, short-circuit the remaining capability checks for that cycle (the store is locked for all of them) and emit one pulse health line, e.g. `runner_health: gpg store locked — N secret-gated candidates deferred; unlock with 'gpg-connect-agent' or see reference/secret-handling.md`, so the supervisor/health dashboard shows it.
4. Document in `.agents/reference/secret-handling.md` that headless runners need a non-expiring unlock (long `max-cache-ttl` plus one unlock per agent restart) or a `credentials.sh` entry with the gopass entry removed.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/runner-capability-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/secret-handling.md`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-runner-capability.sh`

Integration evidence: the existing fixture asserts stderr is empty and names are absent from logs, which conflicts with the requested reason diagnostics. Update these existing assertions and cover cycle-scoped short-circuit/reset and status-only exit codes using synthetic fixtures; no new test infrastructure. Verify with the existing test command and ShellCheck.

## Verification

- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-runner-capability.sh` passes; extend its existing fixture cases for the new reason strings only if the test already asserts log text.
- Manual: with a gopass entry and a locked agent, the pulse log shows `reason=secret_unreadable name=<NAME>`; with the name absent, `reason=secret_missing`.
- ShellCheck clean on edited scripts.

title: full-loop merge exits on ~1s local pacing deferral while server quota is full
body:
## Observed

`full-loop-helper.sh merge <PR> <REPO>` (interactive session, private project repo) failed 7 times over about 15 minutes with:

```
[INFO] PR #<n> verification deferred ([gh-transport] error_kind=github-api-read-deferred attempted=false deferred_by=local_admission retry_at=<now+~1-3s> reason="local primary pacing from observed demand and reset"); no CI failure, repair or duplicate implementation is established
[ERROR] Merge deferred by GitHub read admission; retry_at=<now+~1-3s>.
```

- `retry_at` was 1-3 seconds after the call each time, and every retry produced a new `retry_at` a few seconds after the new call.
- At the same time `gh api rate_limit` reported `core remaining=5000/5000 reset_in=3599s`, so the server quota was not the constraint.
- Retrying after `sleep 100` (past the 60 s `admission_history` window) gave the same result, so it was not caused by earlier interactive polling alone.
- All PR checks were terminal (CodeRabbit pass, Socket pass; qlty `fail` = its own 15-minute timeout, an inconclusive status).

## Suspected cause (unverified)

`gh_transport_capacity.py` `primary_wait()` returns a pacing deferral when `retry_at > now`, even for a wait of about 1 s, and the merge path (`full-loop-helper-readiness.sh` `_full_loop_record_check_read_failure` → `full-loop-helper-merge.sh:2442`) turns that into a hard exit instead of sleeping until `retry_at`. Possibly also a stale `pacing`/budget row (old `reset`/`remaining`) that a fresh quota window does not clear, or demand from other local consumers (pulse) in the same budget scope.

## Expected

When `retry_at - now` is small (for example ≤ 30 s), the merge helper waits and retries within a bounded budget. A full server quota should not cause a deferral loop.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/gh_transport_capacity.py` (`primary_wait`, `capacity_wait`)
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-readiness.sh:306-322`
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh:~2440`
- Tests: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge.sh` (existing deferral cases near lines 839 and 1925)

## Verification

Reproduce with a populated `admission_history` for the scope and a full server quota: the merge helper should complete, or wait a bounded time when `retry_at` is close, rather than exiting with "Merge deferred".
### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge.sh`

Implementation evidence: transport already waits within its read deadline; merge recovery will retry only short local admission failures under a 30-second total budget, without changing quota or server cooldown policy. Verification: ShellCheck on these files, existing merge suite, existing transport budget suite.

<!-- aidevops:origin:interactive -->

title: fix(pulse): treat non-required Qlty 'out of minutes' status as advisory in merge snapshot
body:
## What

The pulse pre-merge snapshot gate treats a non-required `qlty check` commit status as a blocking, unclassified failure when Qlty did not analyse the code because the account is out of minutes. That wedges merges and can route a CI-repair worker at code that has nothing wrong with it.

Qlty should stay useful whenever it has minutes, and be optional while it does not.

## Evidence

- Observed on a managed WordPress plugin repo (PR merged 2026-10-05): `qlty check` commit status `state=error`, description `Qlty did not run because you are out of minutes.`
- That repository's ruleset required only its own lint, build and smoke-test contexts; `qlty check` was not required.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-required-checks.sh` `_pmrc_snapshot_checks_acceptable()` only accepts a non-required `qlty check` failure when the `Qlty Regression Gate` companion passed (`_pmrc_is_explicit_advisory_failure`), which repositories without that workflow never have, so it falls through to "unclassified non-required check ... merge blocked" and is exported in `_PULSE_MERGE_PREFLIGHT_BLOCKING_CHECKS_JSON` for CI repair.
- Precedent: t18584 already ignores the never-terminal non-required `qlty usage` status (`PMRC_INFORMATIONAL_PENDING_STATUS_CONTEXTS_JSON`).

## How

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-required-checks.sh`
  - Keep commit-status `description` in `_pmrc_normalize_snapshot_checks_json()`.
  - Add `PMRC_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED_STATUS_CONTEXTS_JSON='["qlty check"]'`, `PMRC_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED_DESCRIPTION_RE` and `_pmrc_is_quota_exhausted_status_failure()`.
  - In the non-required branch of `_pmrc_snapshot_checks_acceptable()`, count a single commit-status member of an allow-listed context whose description reports spent minutes as advisory.
- Required contexts, check runs, and any other failure of the same context keep blocking.

## Acceptance

- Non-required `qlty check` error with "out of minutes" description: snapshot gate passes, advisory audited in the log.
- Required `qlty check` with the same description: still blocks.
- Non-required `qlty check` failure without that description and without a passing `Qlty Regression Gate`: still blocks.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-preflight-snapshot.sh` (add `qlty_quota_exhausted` and `qlty_quota_exhausted_required` modes).
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-ci-repair-routing.sh`, `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-required-checks-filter.sh`.
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-required-checks.sh`.

title: fix(full-loop): merge helper should wait for local GitHub read admission retry_at instead of failing
body:
## What

`full-loop-helper.sh merge` gives up on the first local GitHub read-admission deferral and reports it as a merge failure, even when GitHub quota is healthy.

## Evidence

- Interactive merge failed three times with `error_kind=github-api-read-deferred ... deferred_by=local_admission`; rerun with `AIDEVOPS_GH_LOCAL_ADMISSION_RETRY_DELAY_SECONDS=5` merged.
- `.agents/scripts/gh-transport-controls.sh` retries a local deferral once with a short delay; `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh` maps `github-api-read-deferred` straight to an error.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`: on `deferred_by=local_admission`, wait until `retry_at` (or bounded backoff) and retry the pre-merge gate within a bounded budget (60 s, at most 3 retries); fail closed otherwise and on real GitHub rate-limit/HTTP errors.
- Do not change pulse/worker admission policy.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-cases.sh`

Integration scope recovery: PR #33659 moved the existing admission regression cases into test-full-loop-merge-cases.sh, sourced by test-full-loop-merge.sh. Updating those existing cases is necessary to verify the authorized 60-second, three-retry behavior. Collision discovery found no open related PR; verification remains bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge.sh and ShellCheck on changed scripts.

## Acceptance

- A local-admission deferral whose window opens within the budget merges without operator action.
- A deferral beyond the budget still exits non-zero with the `retry_at` detail.
- Genuine GitHub quota exhaustion is not retried in a tight loop.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge.sh`
- `shellcheck` on changed scripts.

title: gh-transport local pacer defers reads indefinitely with full GitHub quota, blocking interactive merge and claim
body:
## What

The gh-transport local admission pacer keeps deferring GitHub reads in an interactive session while GitHub reports almost the full quota, so `full-loop-helper.sh merge` cannot merge a ready PR.

## Evidence (2026-10-05, interactive OpenCode session)

- `gh api rate_limit`: core 5000/5000 remaining, graphql 4974/5000.
- `full-loop-helper.sh merge <PR> <owner/repo>`, run 7 times over about 15 minutes, with waits of 40 s, 60 s, 150 s and 180 s between attempts: every run returned `error_kind=github-api-read-deferred attempted=false deferred_by=local_admission reason="local primary pacing from observed demand and reset"` (once `reason="waiting for serialized quota revalidation"`). Each new `retry_at` was 20 to 100 seconds after the attempt, so waiting past `retry_at` never cleared it.
- In one run between deferrals, the verify and review-bot gates passed, then `Merge blocked: unable to verify live repository permission for PR author` (the collaborator permission read was deferred). The block was treated as a permission failure instead of a deferral.
- The same deferral made `interactive-session-helper.sh claim` report the repository owner as "not a maintainer-equivalent collaborator" and skip the claim.
- `gh pr checks` and `gh pr view` through plain `gh` in the same session were not deferred.

## Expected

- The pacer admits reads when the observed GitHub quota is high, or `retry_at` stays fixed rather than moving later on each attempt.
- A deferred permission read in the merge and claim gates reports "deferred", not "not a collaborator" or "unable to verify permission".

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/gh_transport_capacity.py`
- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-collaborator-permission.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper-commands.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-transport-budget.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-authority-guard.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-interactive-session-claim.sh`

### Integration evidence

The transport capacity module implements primary pacing; the shared collaborator helper owns the deferred REST result. Full-loop merge and interactive claim delegate to sourced merge/commands libraries, so these exact paths are necessary to preserve deferrals without granting permission. Existing regression suites cover these paths. Collision discovery found no related open PR or issue branch. Verify with Python transport budget tests, the existing merge-authority and claim shell suites, and scoped ShellCheck.

## Verification

With quota above 50%, run `full-loop-helper.sh merge` on a ready PR in an interactive session: the reads are admitted. With reads forced to defer, the claim and merge permission checks print a deferral, not a permission failure.

title: pulse: dispatch_max starved when REST pacing stretches preflight_early_dispatch past the cycle budget
body:
## Problem

Pulse dispatch is starved again after GH#33560 and GH#33569. On 2026-10-05, every cycle for several hours ended `Cycle outcome: typed=blocked legacy=idle` with `dispatched=0`. Workers sat at 1/20 while a managed repo had 6–14 `status:available` issues that passed their dependency checks.

Evidence from `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`:

- `Substage: preflight_early_dispatch` took 849s, 308s and **2476s** in consecutive cycles. `substage:capacity/calculate_priority_allocations` took 215–223s.
- `Dispatch_max skipped before candidate enumeration: ... remaining=531s floor=600s enumeration=793s`, then `remaining=-14s`, then `Dispatch_max skipped after candidate enumeration: ... remaining=239s floor=600s`.
- `Post-label dispatch_max skipped: insufficient wall-clock budget (remaining=0s, required=600s)` in every cycle.
- In the same window: 324 `gh-transport ... deferred_by=local_admission reason="local primary pacing from observed demand and reset"` lines. The transport's `quota` row for core showed `remaining=540/5000` about 50 minutes before reset, so reads were paced to roughly one every 5s.

Likely cause: about 40 pulse-managed repos spend the hourly REST core budget in preflight (normalize, reassign, dependency reconciler, merge pass, prefetch). Once pacing starts, preflight stretches until no wall-clock budget remains for `dispatch_max`. Dispatch is the most valuable step but runs last and gets nothing.

## Proposal

- Reserve dispatch first: run `dispatch_max` (or a bounded early dispatch wave using cached candidates) before budget-expensive housekeeping, or give it a guaranteed wall-clock and REST slice.
- When local admission pacing is active, skip or defer non-essential preflight substages (stale dependency sweeps, normalize/reassign over idle repos, merge-pass checks on drafts) instead of letting them consume the cycle.
- Log the per-substage REST points spent, so budget hogs are visible.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-cycle-gates.sh` and the pulse cycle orchestration that runs `preflight_early_dispatch` and `dispatch_max`. Exact substage ordering file to be confirmed.
- `.agents/scripts/gh_transport_capacity.py` (pacing source; behaviour looks correct, but it is the trigger)
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh` / `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` (candidate enumeration cost)

## Verification

- With core REST below about 15% and pacing active, a cycle still dispatches at least one wave when available candidates exist and worker capacity is free.
- `pulse-health.json` shows `dispatched>0` in that state, and `Dispatch_max skipped ... below dispatch reserve` no longer appears in every cycle.
### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-preflight-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh`

### Implementation and scoped verification

The current first fill waits for cleanup and cross-repository priority allocations, enumerates all repositories, and runs ancillary prepasses before implementation. Keep local host capacity calculation before the first fill; move cleanup/full priority allocation after it, bound the skip-normalization first-wave scan at the first repository with candidates (mark product discovery incomplete), and defer ancillary prepasses to the normal refill. Existing trust, claim, ledger, quota and per-candidate timeout gates remain unchanged. Integration recovery: the existing enumeration EWMA in pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh is shared by broad scans and would retain the old slow census estimate, rejecting the new first wave before enumeration; isolate the first-wave timing estimate and persisted EWMA from full scans, with the same cold-cache reserve and budget checks. title: issue consolidation drops requires-secrets prerequisite and narrows generated Files Scope paths
body:
## Problem

Issue consolidation (`_dispatch_issue_consolidation()` in `pulse-triage.sh`, worker-written successor issues) loses two dispatch-critical parts of the original body. Observed in a managed repo on 2026-10-04/05:

1. **`requires-secrets:` runner prerequisite dropped.** The originals carried `requires-secrets: <names>`, which pulse enforces so that only runners holding those secrets claim the issue. Two consolidated successors had no such line. A runner without the ordinary test credentials then claimed one and stopped with `input_required` after a full session.
2. **Generated-path Files Scope narrowed to an impossible concrete path.** A successor replaced the generated work-log pattern `NEW: todo/<area>/log/*/*/<slug>-*.jsonl` with one fixed filename, `log/consolidated/2026-10-05/<slug>-history-completion.jsonl`. The project's append helper always emits `log/<machine>/<date>/<slug>-<HHMMSS>.jsonl`. The worker correctly stopped with `files_scope_excluded`.

## Proposal

- Consolidation must copy verbatim any line matching `^requires-secrets:` and the runner-prerequisite paragraph from every superseded issue, using the union of names. Validate before filing the successor: if any superseded issue had `requires-secrets:`, the successor must too.
- Consolidation must preserve wildcard Files Scope entries for tool-generated paths. It must not narrow them to invented concrete filenames, and must not turn existing files from `EDIT` into `NEW`.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-triage.sh` (`_dispatch_issue_consolidation`) and the consolidation worker brief/template it emits; exact template path to confirm.
- Possibly `.agents/scripts/pre-dispatch-validators` / `reference/pre-dispatch-validators.md`, to add a successor-body check.

## Verification

- Consolidate a test issue that has `requires-secrets: A B` and a `log/*/*/x-*.jsonl` scope entry. Confirm the successor keeps both unchanged.
- A runner without secret `A` does not claim the successor.

title: t18590: Transport governor keeps stale low core quota across a new rate-limit window, pacing REST reads ~7.5s
body:
## Task


The REST transport governor keeps a stale, low `core` balance for the full remainder of an old reset window, even when every fresh response from the same credential reports a new window with full quota. The result is about 7.5 s of admission pacing per REST read. That pushes `_gh_with_timeout read` (15 s default) calls over their budget, so framework helpers fail with spurious read errors.

## Done when

- [ ] After one valid response for a bound credential with a later reset epoch and higher remaining, the stored `core` row reflects the new window and admission pacing returns to near zero.
- [ ] Same-window late responses and shared/unresolved-owner scopes keep the existing conservative `min()` behaviour.
- [ ] `_gh_with_timeout read` REST reads complete within the default 15 s budget after window rollover.
- [ ] Existing governor/budget tests pass; ShellCheck/ruff clean on changed files.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/gh_transport_budget.py:248-307` (`Budget.finish`): when a valid response for a bound/attributed credential reports a reset epoch strictly later than the stored reset, treat it as a newer window and accept its remaining value instead of `min()`/`max()`. Keep the conservative merge for same-window late replies and for shared/unresolved owners. Decide whether to do this directly or through `probe_recovers`; reuse its credential-binding checks.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/gh_transport_recovery.py:91` (`probe_recovers`), only if the newer-window rule belongs with the existing credential-bound recovery logic.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-transport-budget.py`: add a newer-window recovery case next to the existing `finish()` cases.

### Implementation Steps

1. Reproduce with a temp `AIDEVOPS_GH_TRANSPORT_STATE_DIR`: seed a `core` row with low remaining and a future reset, then call `finish()` with headers for the same credential reporting a later reset and high remaining. Confirm the row stays low today.
2. Change the merge so the newer-window evidence wins for bound credentials, and keep the existing conservative rules for ambiguous owners. `capacity_wait` (`.agents/scripts/gh_transport_capacity.py:14`) should need no change once the stored row is correct.
3. Verify that pacing drops to ~0 on a real read (`AIDEVOPS_GH_SHIM_TIMING=1 gh api rate_limit` does not count; use a cheap REST GET) after one response.

### Hazards

- Do not let `/rate_limit` act as a grant (existing invariant in the comment at `:268`).
- Shared owners with several credentials must keep conservative accounting; the newer-window rule applies only to a bound credential.
- Self-heals at the stale reset, so impact is bounded to under one hour per occurrence, but it recurs whenever a window rolls over while the row is low.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/gh_transport_budget.py`
- `.agents/scripts/gh_transport_recovery.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-transport-budget.py`

</details>

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

The REST transport governor keeps a stale, low `core` balance for the full remainder of an old reset window, even when every fresh response from the same credential reports a new window with full quota. The result is about 7.5 s of admission pacing per REST read. That pushes `_gh_with_timeout read` (15 s default) calls over their budget, so framework helpers fail with spurious read errors.

## Why

Observed in an interactive session on 2026-10-05 (aidevops v3.38.10):

- Governor state (`~/.aidevops/state/gh-transport/admission.sqlite3`, single scope): `core remaining=540 limit=5000 reset=1791221743`, `observed` refreshed every few seconds, `remaining` frozen at 540 across 16 admissions in 5 minutes.
- Live `gh api rate_limit` for the same session credential: `core remaining=5000 used=0`, with a reset that slides forward (`1791223154` → `1791223298`), the GitHub signature of an unused window.
- `AIDEVOPS_GH_SHIM_TIMING=1 gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq ...`: `sqlite_admission elapsed_ms=15.3 pacing_ms=7543.3`, `native_gh elapsed_ms=380.7`.
- Downstream failures in the same session: `approval-helper.sh verify` → `API_ERROR`; `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` failed in turn at origin-label readback (`_verify_pr_origin_label`, rc=124 from `_gh_with_timeout read`), open-PR linkage evidence, and recovered-PR body verification, although the PR, labels, and body were correct on GitHub. `claim-task-id.sh` also exceeded a 180 s caller timeout.

Mechanism: `Budget.finish` (`.agents/scripts/gh_transport_budget.py:270-274`). When the stored row's reset is still in the future and `probe_recovers(...)` is false, it sets `available = min(header_remaining, row_remaining)` and `reset_at = max(header_reset, row_reset)`. A response from a newer window (header reset later than the stored reset, higher remaining) therefore can never raise the balance until the stale reset passes. `capacity_wait` then paces against the stale 540.

## Context

- Workaround used in the reporting session: `AIDEVOPS_GH_READ_TIMEOUT=30` (governor admission deadline becomes `min(10, 30-5)` = 10 s, which fits the 7.5 s pacing).
- Related: `full-loop-helper-commit.sh:1399-1447` (`_verify_pr_origin_label`), `shared-gh-wrappers.sh:472` (`_gh_with_timeout`), `gh-transport-governor.py:206-219` (`_acquire`).

</details>

title: dispatch-dedup: bare #N mention in another PR's body blocks issue N (sibling/draft matching)
body:
## What

A passing `#N` mention in another issue's draft PR body blocks dispatch of issue N indefinitely. Restrict sibling-PR matching in PR bodies to keyword references; keep bare `#N` matching for titles only.

## Why

Observed on v3.38.10 in a managed private repo: draft PR A (worker-owned, `For #A_issue`) contained the sentence "the results phase (#B) stays open." The pulse then logged, every cycle for ~12 hours:

```text
Dedup: WORKER_DRAFT_CHECKPOINT: draft PR #A is a durable checkpoint for issue #B; ordinary redispatch is blocked
DISPATCH_BLOCK_REASON reason=dedup_active_claim ... issue=#B
```

Issue B had no PR of its own. Within 13 minutes of PR A leaving draft, issue B was dispatched normally. The cause is `issue_ref_pattern` in `_has_open_pr_check_healthy_sibling` (`.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-pr.sh`, `rg -n 'issue_ref_pattern=' .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-pr.sh`): its alternatives include a bare `#${issue_number}`, applied to both `.title` and `.body`. The same pattern also lets a bare body mention make an unrelated approved/mergeable PR count as a "healthy sibling".

The bare match dates from #23230 / #23247 / #23269 (tests in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-dedup-helper-has-open-pr.sh`). Those fixtures need to keep passing.

## How

1. In `_has_open_pr_check_healthy_sibling`, split matching: title may match bare `#N` / `GH#N` / `tN:` prefixes as today; body must match a keyword reference (`close[sd]?|fix(e[sd])?|resolve[sd]?|for|refs?` + optional `owner/repo` + `#N`) or `GH#N`. Apply to both the draft-checkpoint and the healthy-sibling `jq` selections.
2. Check the stale-recovery equivalent in `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-stale.sh` (`rg -n 'issue_pattern' .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-stale.sh`) for the same bare-body match and apply the same rule if present.
3. Add one fixture to the existing has-open-pr test: a draft whose body only mentions `(#N)` in prose must not block issue N; a draft with `For #N` still must.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-pr.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-stale.sh` (only if the same pattern exists)
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-dedup-helper-has-open-pr.sh`

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-dedup-helper-has-open-pr.sh` passes, including the new prose-mention case.
- ShellCheck clean.

title: pulse: stall-killed worker draft PR holds its issue indefinitely (no continuation, no attention)
body:
## What

A worker draft PR left by a stall-killed worker (`CLAIM_RELEASED reason=hard_kill_stall`) holds its issue indefinitely with no continuation and no attention record. Route these drafts to the existing exact-head continuation path.

## Why

Observed on v3.38.10 in a managed private repo: a worker committed its complete change to a draft PR at 04:28Z, was killed by the activity watchdog, and released at 04:46Z (`CLAIM_RELEASED reason=hard_kill_stall`). The release unassigned the issue and set `status:available`. For the next ~12 hours each pulse cycle logged `WORKER_DRAFT_CHECKPOINT ... ordinary redispatch is blocked` and dispatched nothing for it. A maintainer then marked the draft ready by hand and merged it at 17:01Z without changes: the work had been finished all along.

Existing paths do not cover this case:

- `_stale_recovery_preserve_draft_checkpoint` (`.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-stale.sh`) emits `STALE_PR_CONTINUATION`, but only from stale-*assignment* recovery. The stall release already unassigned the issue, so that path never runs.
- `_dispatch_blocked_checkpoint_attention` → `pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh blocked-attention` (GH#33132) handles only releases whose reason is `blocked`; for `hard_kill_stall` it prints `BLOCKED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION_SKIPPED` and nothing surfaces.
- `_dispatch_interactive_worker_checkpoint_continuation` requires `origin:interactive` + `status:in-review`.

## How

1. In `_dedup_layer_open_pr` handling of `WORKER_DRAFT_CHECKPOINT` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-dedup-layers.sh`, `rg -n 'WORKER_DRAFT_CHECKPOINT' .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-dedup-layers.sh`): when the draft is worker-owned, unprotected, has no live worker, and the latest release for its runner is a non-`blocked` failure release (`hard_kill_stall`, `no_activity`, timeout families from `.agents/scripts/worker-activity-failure-families.jq`), emit the same `STALE_PR_CONTINUATION` signal used by stale recovery so the existing bounded exact-head continuation launches.
2. Keep `blocked` releases on the GH#33132 attention path, unchanged.
3. Bound retries: if the same PR head has already had one stall-continuation that also stalled, post one attention record (reuse the blocked-attention comment format with the release reason) instead of looping.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-dedup-layers.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-pr-continuation.sh` (one fixture for a stall-released, unassigned issue with a worker draft)

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-pr-continuation.sh` and `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` pass.
- On a runner: an unassigned issue with a stall-released worker draft logs `STALE_PR_CONTINUATION` and launches one continuation worker within one cycle.

title: feat(seo): public SERP collection policy, SerpApi provider, CAPTCHA threshold probe
body:
## What

Users report questionable SERP data from DataForSEO and SerpApi-style providers. Add first-party ways to check that data:

1. **Policy update**: permit low-volume, paced, human-like collection of public, logged-out search result pages from an operator's own machine (headed or headless browser, optional authorized residential egress). Keep these rules: no automated CAPTCHA solving against search-engine protections by default, stop or hand off to a human on CAPTCHA, no account/auth bypass.
2. **SerpApi provider**: add SerpApi (`https://serpapi.com/search.json`, `SERPAPI_API_KEY`) as a keyword-research/SERP provider option alongside DataForSEO and Serper.
3. **CAPTCHA threshold probe**: a headed-browser helper that runs a keyword list with human-like pacing and stops at the first CAPTCHA / "unusual traffic" interstitial, reporting how many searches succeeded and over what time window.

## Why

- Vendor SERP data quality is disputed. Known upstream causes: Google disabled `num=100` (Sept 2025) and requires JS (SearchGuard, Jan 2025).
- Legal context, as of 2026-10-05: in *Google LLC v. SerpApi, LLC* (N.D. Cal. 4:25-cv-10826-YGR), the court dismissed Google's DMCA §1201 claims on 2026-07-20. Claims over results with no copyrighted content were dismissed without leave to amend. The case is still pending: an amended complaint was filed and a second motion to dismiss is set for hearing on 2026-10-13. Collecting public pages is defensible. Automated circumvention of access controls remains contested, so the policy draws its line there.

## How

- `.agents/aidevops/reach-capture.md`: add a "Public search-result collection" policy section and rework the CAPTCHA, rotation and safety-boundary lines.
- `.agents/tools/browser/proxy-integration.md`, `.agents/tools/browser/anti-detect-browser.md`, `.agents/tools/ai-assistants/capsolver.md`: align the wording with that section.
- `.agents/scripts/keyword-research-helper-providers.sh`: add `serpapi_request`, `serpapi_search`, `serpapi_autocomplete` (model: `serper_*`).
- `.agents/scripts/keyword-research-helper.sh`, `.agents/scripts/keyword-research-helper-analysis.sh`: `--provider serpapi`.
- `.agents/seo/serpapi.md` (new, model: `.agents/seo/serper.md`), `.agents/seo.md`, `.agents/seo/keyword-research.md`, onboarding listings, `.agents/configs/allowed-urls.txt`.
- New `.agents/scripts/serp-captcha-probe.mjs` + `serp-probe-helper.sh` wrapper (model: `browser-readiness-probe.mjs`, `playwright-runtime.mjs` `loadPlaywright`/`resolvePlaywrightBrowserExecutable`).

## Acceptance

- ShellCheck clean on touched shell files; `node --check` on the new `.mjs`.
- `keyword-research-helper.sh help` lists `serpapi`.
- The probe's `--dry-run` path validates arguments without contacting a target. A real run stops at the first CAPTCHA and never solves it.

title: t18591: Bounded operations lose the SIGTERM signal when a timed-out supervisor exits cleanly
body:
## Task


`bounded-interactive-operation.mjs` can report `process_signal: null` for an operation that the supervisor timed out or cancelled with SIGTERM. This intermittently fails the plugin test `failure, timeout, and scoped cancellation cannot appear as success` (`.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs:337`, `assert.notEqual(timedResult.process_signal, null)`).

## Done when

- [ ] A timed-out or cancelled operation reports `process_signal: "SIGTERM"` whether the supervisor died by signal or exited after handling it.
- [ ] Successful and failed operations that were never terminated still report `process_signal: null`.
- [ ] `test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs` passes on 10 consecutive local runs and in CI `import-check`.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-interactive-operation.mjs:200-211` (`mainClosed`): preserve the termination signal requested by `requestTermination` when the child closes without a signal, e.g. `operation.processSignal = scalar(signal) || operation.processSignal;`. Normal (non-terminated) operations start with `processSignal: ""` (`:138`), so they still report `null` through `bounded-operation-runtime.mjs:101`.

### Implementation Steps

1. Apply the one-line change in `mainClosed`.
2. Run `node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs` several times (e.g. 10 runs) to confirm the test is stable.
3. Check that the plugin's other tests still pass, using the same command CI's `import-check` runs (see `.github/workflows/` Plugin Import Check).

### Hazards

- Do not invent a signal for operations that exited normally. Only a previously requested termination signal may survive.
- Keep `process_exit` unchanged; a supervisor that handled SIGTERM legitimately reports its exit code.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-interactive-operation.mjs`

</details>

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

`bounded-interactive-operation.mjs` can report `process_signal: null` for an operation that the supervisor timed out or cancelled with SIGTERM. This intermittently fails the plugin test `failure, timeout, and scoped cancellation cannot appear as success` (`.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs:337`, `assert.notEqual(timedResult.process_signal, null)`).

## Why

- Observed on 2026-10-05 in the `import-check` job (Plugin Import Check, run 37348173944, job 111891983676) for release PR #33657. Failure: `not ok 7 - failure, timeout, and scoped cancellation cannot appear as success`, `Expected "actual" to be strictly unequal to: null`, at `test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs:337:12`. 1 of 1076 plugin tests failed.
- None of the release commits touched the plugin. The same test passes locally (`node --test --test-name-pattern "cannot appear as success" .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-bounded-interactive-operation.mjs`). The previous 11 `Plugin Import Check` runs passed. This is a timing race, not a regression.
- Mechanism: `requestTermination` (`.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-interactive-operation.mjs:190-198`) records `operation.processSignal = "SIGTERM"`. `mainClosed` (`:200-211`) then unconditionally overwrites it with `scalar(signal)` from the child `close` event (`:205`). The main child is a supervisor. If SIGTERM arrives before its handler is installed, it dies by signal and `signal` is `"SIGTERM"`. If the handler is installed, it contains the process group and exits with a code, so `signal` is `null` and the recorded termination signal is lost. The test's 30 ms budget makes either ordering possible.
- Impact beyond CI: receipts for genuinely timed-out or cancelled operations can lose the evidence of which signal the supervisor sent.

</details>

<summary>Brief workflow contract</summary>

## Brief Workflow

# Fail-fast terminal outcomes for bounded browser validation

## What and why

Add a concise, reusable completion-check recipe to aidevops browser guidance so agent-written browser validation distinguishes **success, blocked, failed, and timed-out** outcomes. A success-only wait in an interactive session exhausted its 120-second budget even though a terminal login-required dialog was available. This is an observed check-design mistake, **not a demonstrated Playwright, Stagehand, Google, or bounded-operation supervisor defect**.

The operator approved filing this narrow workflow-hardening issue. Keep it separate from Stagehand adoption: #32376 already delivered the opt-in v4 route and #32446 tracks a cost-capped model-backed probe. No browser-default migration, SDK install, paid model call, or new global prompt rule is requested.

## Observed evidence and reproducer pattern

An ad hoc Node/Playwright script submitted an external URL-validation job and waited for a changed result URL plus the expected structured-data result section:

```javascript
await page.waitForFunction(
  () => location.pathname.includes('/result') &&
    new URL(location.href).searchParams.get('id') !== 'prior-test-id' &&
    document.body.innerText.includes('Detected structured data'),
  {},
  { timeout: 120000 },
);
```

This excerpt is sanitized; it illustrates the actual success-only condition, not a framework-owned function or a live-site reproducer.

Recorded observation:

```text
page.waitForFunction: Timeout 120000ms exceeded.
- alertdialog "Something went wrong":
  - heading "Something went wrong" [level=2]
  - text: Log in and try again
  - button "Dismiss"
```

The script caught the timeout, printed the page state, closed its browser in `finally`, and exited zero. The supervisor correctly reported process success, but process completion is not application-validation success. The parent ultimately reported authentication blocking honestly; no successful external validation was claimed from that script.

**Workaround applied:** a second observation waited for either the expected result or terminal error/login text and returned the blocking page state without exhausting that condition's full timeout. Do not copy its broad `body.innerText` substring test as a universal detector: visible target-specific error states are stronger evidence than arbitrary page text.

**Causal status:** confirmed success-only wait in the ad hoc caller; no causal regression identified in framework executable code. This is a documentation/recipe enhancement, not a platform bug report.

## Scope and reference pattern

Verified current upstream tracked paths:

- `EDIT: .agents/tools/browser/browser-automation.md` — put the common completion/evidence contract beside existing browser debugging/verification guidance; keep the routing decision tree unchanged.
- `EDIT: .agents/tools/browser/playwright.md` — add or link a small bounded example compatible with the existing failure handoff: last URL/page state, actions already taken, and parent side-effect checks. Do not duplicate a large policy block.
- `REFERENCE ONLY: .agents/scripts/playwright-runtime.mjs` — reuse package/browser resolution for any disposable verification of the documented recipe; no runtime change is required by this issue.

Current browser guidance already says to return the last state on failure and not retry state-changing actions automatically. The missing concrete recipe is checking terminal states while a success condition is pending and reporting the semantic outcome separately from the process exit.

Discovery checked all-state issues/PRs and current target-file history. #32375 covers authenticated read-only QA journeys and has broader failure/cleanup boundaries; it is not a license to recreate that runner. The two guidance files' latest observed relevant commit is `19865e0439dc007ee64cd5c677668172cea57a93` (2026-09-27). Recheck HEAD before implementation and reuse an equivalent existing recipe if one has landed.

## Implementation approach

1. Inspect current browser docs and existing QA patterns before writing. Add the smallest shared recipe, not another browser runner or polling framework.
2. Show a finite, target-specific completion check that detects an expected success state OR visible terminal error/authentication state. Return an explicit semantic outcome with bounded, redacted evidence.
3. On terminal authentication, permission, service-error, or challenge states, stop the unsafe route immediately. Do not retry submissions, acquire credentials, bypass CAPTCHA/MFA, or switch to a user's profile automatically. A recoverable progress/loading state is not a terminal failure.
4. Explain that exit zero proves the observation command finished, not that the target accepted the operation. Actual verification checks must fail closed or clearly return `blocked`/`failed`/`timed-out` rather than masquerading as a pass. Preserve the distinction between process and application outcomes.
5. Keep browser/context cleanup in `finally` and preserve the last safe URL/state and actions taken for the parent. Redact tokens, cookies, query credentials and private content.
6. Keep examples engine-neutral where possible: this outcome contract also applies when Stagehand performs adaptive actions. Do not claim Stagehand resolves authentication or change deterministic Playwright routing.

## Acceptance criteria

- A bounded example recognizes a visible terminal error before the full success-wait budget expires.
- Success requires its actual expected result state; login/error/progress pages cannot count as successful validation.
- Outcomes distinguish success, externally blocked, failed, and timed out, without mislabeling transport/process completion.
- Failure handoff includes bounded evidence and actions already taken, with owned browser cleanup and no automatic side-effect retries.
- Existing Playwright-default and opt-in Stagehand policy, consent, profile isolation and cost boundaries remain unchanged.
- No new application test infrastructure, browser SDK, paid inference or global AGENTS.md expansion is introduced.

## Verification

- Run the existing changed-file Markdown/lint checks for the two documentation files.
- Syntax-check any extracted example using the existing Node tooling.
- Where the existing browser QA fixtures can express it, demonstrate one expected-success page, one immediate terminal-error page and one non-terminal loading page that times out. Use disposable/local fixtures and existing test machinery; do not add a new test runner or contact the original external service.
- Confirm terminal errors end the check before its configured deadline and both success and failure close owned contexts. Treat timing as bounded acceptance, not a general performance claim.

## Tier and environment

- `tier:standard`: narrow documentation/recipe work with decided safety boundaries; no unresolved architecture or billing decision.
- aidevops 3.38.11; OpenCode; macOS 26.6.2; Bash 5.3.20; GitHub CLI 2.102.0.
- Setup/security-advisory suppression: not applicable.
- Draft implementation PR: not seeded; the requested deliverable is this worker-ready documentation enhancement.

title: sandbox-exec-helper: orphaned helper keeps polling a dead PID after watchdog hard-kill
body:
## Summary

After the activity watchdog hard-kills a headless worker, its `sandbox-exec-helper.sh run` parent can survive as an orphan (PPID 1) and keep polling a PID that no longer exists. The task is already closed and its claim already released, but the leaked helper holds on for the remaining sandbox timeout (10800s).

## Observed (v3.38.10, Linux)

- Worker for a managed-repo issue was hard-killed by the watchdog (`CLAIM_RELEASED reason=watchdog_kill:hard_kill: total elapsed 2293s >= hard-kill threshold 1500s`, 17:24 UTC). The issue was already closed by a merged PR at 17:13 UTC.
- At 17:37 UTC the helper `sandbox-exec-helper.sh run --timeout 10800 ... --worker-id worker:issue-<N>:...` was still alive: PPID 1, elapsed 51 min, no `opencode run` descendant.
- `pstree -ap <pid>` showed only nested `bash` children repeatedly running `ps -o lstart= -p <dead-pid> | tr -s ' '`. The target PID did not exist (`ps -p` returned nothing).
- `ps -o lstart=` is the non-Linux fallback branch of `_sandbox_get_proc_starttime`, which is taken on Linux when `/proc/<pid>/stat` is missing, so the helper is calling it for an already-dead PID in a loop that does not exit.
- A manual `kill -TERM <pid>` ended it immediately, so no worker state was lost.

## Expected

When the watched child PID is gone, the helper's watchdog/poll loop terminates and the helper exits. A dead target must never keep the helper looping until the sandbox timeout. The hard-kill path must also leave no orphaned helper.

## Files to investigate

Paths unverified beyond the first; confirm with `rg`.

- `.agents/scripts/sandbox-exec-helper.sh`: `_sandbox_get_proc_starttime` (around line 728), the PID-recycling watchdog that calls it (around lines 780-880), and the polling loops using `kill -0` (around lines 440, 601).
- `.agents/scripts/worker-activity-watchdog.sh`: the hard-kill path that reports `CLAIM_RELEASED`; check whether it signals the helper, not just the worker.

Reference pattern: the existing `kill -0 "$wd_pid"` early-exit check in the secondary watchdog (around line 825). Apply the same dead-target exit to whichever loop is still spinning.

## Verification

1. Reproduce: start a sandboxed child, SIGKILL only the child, and confirm the helper exits within one poll interval instead of surviving. Also confirm the empty start-token case (dead PID) ends the loop.
2. `shellcheck` on `sandbox-exec-helper.sh` with zero violations.
3. Run the existing sandbox/watchdog tests under `.agents/scripts/tests/` that cover `sandbox-exec-helper.sh`. Add a test only if no existing one fits.
### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/sandbox-exec-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-sandbox-nested-process-group-cleanup.sh`

Implementation scope: make Linux dead-target identity lookup fail closed and terminate primary/secondary polling on missing, zombie, or recycled targets. Extend the existing lifecycle suite for child SIGKILL and empty-token/dead-target exit. The activity watchdog kill path has been inspected; sandbox helpers must exit independently when their target dies, without broadening signals to unrelated ancestors.

title: worker classification: clean blocked, already-delivered and consolidation exits are tagged premature_exit and resumed
body:
## Summary

Workers that exit cleanly (exit 0, `kill_reason=natural`, no provider or runtime error) after correctly reporting "already delivered", "blocked by an open prerequisite" or "partial, remainder needs a new run" are classified as `premature_exit` / `model_stopped_before_completion` and routed to `resume_session_with_completion_contract`. These are valid outcomes, so the failure family, continuation retries and the handoff-rate metric are inflated by false positives.

Related, already closed: GH#33331 (recurring `premature_exit`, no visible resume outcome) and GH#32529 (false `premature_exit` loops). This is a narrower remaining gap, not a duplicate of the model-routing questions in those.

## Observed (v3.38.10, 24h window, `worker-activity-helper.sh summary`)

- 39 terminal outcomes; 4 `premature_exit`, all `exit_code=77`, `provider_error_type=none`, all one model, in a single managed project repo.
- Inspecting the failure excerpts under `~/.aidevops/logs/worker-failure-excerpts/`:
  - Worker found the work already merged by an earlier PR and said so (no new commits, nothing to push). Outcome is valid, tagged `premature_exit`.
  - Worker ended with `BLOCKED` and a blocker dossier because a prerequisite issue was still open. Valid, tagged `premature_exit`.
  - Worker finished an issue-consolidation task (closed the parent, opened the merged spec) with no code PR. Valid, tagged `premature_exit`.
  - Worker made partial progress and stopped; the remainder was later delivered by a normal merged PR.
- One of these sessions exhausted 10 continuation retries (`continuation_outcome: exhausted`) even though the underlying state was a legitimate block, so each retry spent a worker slot and model budget without any possible progress.

## Expected

1. Before classifying a clean exit as `premature_exit`, check for explicit terminal markers in the final worker message or issue state: `BLOCKED`, `FULL_LOOP_COMPLETE`, a no-op "already satisfied by merged PR" verdict, or a closed/consolidated issue. Classify these as `blocked` / `no_work` / `success`, not `launch-failure`.
2. Do not run `resume_session_with_completion_contract` for those classes.
3. Keep `premature_exit` for genuine silent stops (no terminal marker, open issue, no PR).

## Files to investigate

Paths unverified; confirm with `rg -n "model_stopped_before_completion|premature_exit" .agents/scripts/`.

- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh` and `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-result.sh`: where the `premature_exit` cause is assigned.
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-worker.sh`: continuation/resume decision.
- `.agents/scripts/worker-activity-helper.sh`: failure-family fingerprint (`ff-v1:launch-failure`) and `continuation_outcome`.
- Existing tests to extend rather than new infrastructure: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-no-work-reclassification.sh`, `test-worker-outcome-routing.sh`, `test-headless-runtime-completion-tests.sh`.

Reference pattern: the existing no-work reclassification path (`test-no-work-reclassification.sh`). Reuse its marker detection instead of adding a second classifier.

## Verification

1. Feed the saved excerpt shapes above (blocked dossier, already-delivered no-op, consolidation with no PR) through the classifier; each must yield a non-`premature_exit` class and no resume dispatch.
2. A genuinely silent stop (no marker, open issue, no PR) must still classify as `premature_exit`.
3. `shellcheck` zero violations on changed scripts; run the three existing tests listed above.
