title: gh-transport: local primary pacing defers reads and blocks merges with full quota remaining
body:
## What

Local GitHub REST read pacing (`gh_transport_capacity.py`, reason "local primary pacing from observed demand and reset") repeatedly deferred `full-loop-helper.sh merge` in an interactive session that had almost all of its primary quota left. The deferrals blocked merges for about 20 minutes, and twice the merge gate failed hard on reads it could not make:

- `Merge blocked: unable to pin fresh PR base/head evidence for prospective TODO validation`
- `Merge blocked: unable to verify live repository permission for PR author <owner>`
- `PR #N required-check evidence is indeterminate (exact check read exit 2)`

## Evidence (one session, one repo)

- `gh api rate_limit` during the deferrals: core `remaining` 5000 of 5000 (reset more than 50 minutes away), GraphQL 4961–4977.
- 15+ consecutive deferrals across three merge attempts, each with a `retry_at` 20–40 s ahead that moved forward again on the next try. A plain `gh api repos/.../pulls/N/comments` read was deferred three times in a row the same way.
- The merge succeeded on a manual retry once the window passed. Each hard failure above came after verification had already passed in the same call, so a later read inside the merge step was refused.

## Likely cause

`primary_wait()` in `.agents/scripts/gh_transport_capacity.py` paces when `demand * seconds_left > available`, but `available` comes from `row[0] - reserved`. If the stored row (`row[0]` remaining, `row[1]` reset) is stale, or for another resource/scope than the one `gh api rate_limit` reports, the pacing applies to a nearly exhausted budget that does not exist. The `pacing` table also persists `retry_at` while `saved[0] == row[1]`, so one stale row keeps deferring until its reset.

Not verified: which resource and scope the deferred reads used, and what `row` held. Paths under `~/.aidevops/` cannot be inspected safely from the project session.

## Proposed fix

1. Refresh the remaining/reset row from response headers (or `rate_limit`, which costs no quota) before pacing, and ignore a row whose remaining is far below the live value.
2. In `full-loop-helper.sh merge`, treat a read deferred by local admission after verification as a retry (wait for `retry_at` within a bounded budget), not a hard "blocked" failure.

## Verification

- Unit-style: seed the `pacing`/budget tables with a stale low `remaining`, simulate a live `remaining=5000`, and assert `capacity_wait()` returns no wait.
- Re-run `full-loop-helper.sh merge <PR> <repo>` in a session with high quota and recent burst reads: no `github-api-read-deferred` failures, and no hard "unable to verify/pin" failures from admission deferrals.

title: full-loop start: linked-issue gate fails to fetch a readable open issue (gh shim returns empty inside helper)
body:
## What

`full-loop-helper.sh start` (and `interactive-start-helper.sh`, which calls it) fails closed with
`Maintainer gate pre-check: could not fetch linked issue #N — refusing start` for an open,
readable issue, so an interactive full-loop has no lifecycle state.

## Evidence

- `bash -x full-loop-helper.sh start "GH#372 ..."` in a linked worktree of a public managed repo:
  `_check_linked_issue_gate` (`.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-state-lifecycle.sh:736`) runs
  `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/372 2>/dev/null`, which returns empty with a non-zero exit.
  The repo slug resolved correctly from `git remote get-url origin`.
- In the same session and worktree, the same call succeeds outside the helper, both with the
  user's `gh` and with the aidevops `gh` shim invoked directly or first on `PATH`
  (`env PATH=~/.aidevops/agents/scripts:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/bin:/bin gh api ... --jq .state` → `open`).
- Repeated three times over several minutes, so not a transient API failure. The helper prepends
  the shim dir to `PATH` and sources `shared-constants.sh` / `shared-gh-wrappers*.sh` /
  `shared-gh-secondary-cooldown.sh` / `shared-gh-request-state.sh` first, so the likely cause is
  state or exported environment from those libraries (cooldown/request-state coordination, read
  timeout) that makes the shim fail; stderr is discarded, so the reason is hidden.
- `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` worked in the same worktree afterwards.

## How

1. Reproduce: in any managed repo worktree, `full-loop-helper.sh start "GH#<open issue> test"`.
2. Capture the shim's stderr in `_check_linked_issue_gate` (keep the fail-closed behaviour, but
   print the `gh` error in the refusal message) to find which wrapper path fails.
3. Fix the root cause in the shim or the sourced libraries; add the error text to the message.

## Verification

- `full-loop-helper.sh start "GH#<open issue> test"` passes the gate for a readable open issue.
- `tests/test-full-loop-gate-pulse-parity.sh` and `tests/test-full-loop-external-issue-author-gate.sh` pass.

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-state-lifecycle.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-worktree-gh-shim.sh`

Scope discovery: the live start succeeds on the current Linux worker. The entrypoint only prepends its sibling shim when its directory is absent anywhere on PATH, permitting an inherited stale shim to win when the sibling directory is already later on PATH. Verify both PATH shapes with the existing worktree shim regression, retain fail-closed issue lookup, and expose lookup stderr. Existing gate parity and external-author tests are under `.agents/scripts/tests/`.

title: docs: PHP server admin agent (PHP-FPM/LSAPI/mod_php, workers, memory_limit, OPcache), Hostinger PHP facts, directory-listing check
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

# PHP server admin agent: how PHP runs, worker and memory sizing, OPcache; Hostinger PHP facts; directory-listing check

## Pre-flight (auto-populated by briefing workflow)

- [x] Memory recall: `hostinger ssh php-fpm hosting` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons before this session
- [x] Discovery pass: 4 commits touch target files (latest 9afeb871a8 GH#33518, hostinger.md); 0 merged / 0 open related PRs in last 48h
- [x] File refs verified: 10 refs checked, all present at HEAD
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — new documentation agent following a verified precedent (GH#26936 / PR #26941); wording and section choices need judgment
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — documentation work with a clear precedent; issue-only is enough

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-05
- **Created by:** ai-interactive (owner session)
- **Conversation context:** The owner asked whether three old Cloudron forum threads hold useful hosting knowledge for any PHP app: PHP-FPM for speed, PHP `memory_limit` vs the container's memory, and empty `index.php` files against directory listing. aidevops has a Node runtime agent (`tools/runtime/node-server-admin.md`) but no PHP equivalent. The only PHP pool settings documented anywhere are LocalWP's (`tools/wordpress/localwp.md`). SSH checks of a Hostinger account gave the facts below.

## What

1. **NEW `.agents/tools/runtime/php-server-admin.md`**, a read-only assessment subagent shaped like `tools/runtime/node-server-admin.md` (frontmatter, Quick Reference in AI-CONTEXT block, Scope and Handoffs table, baseline, conditional checks, safety invariants, output contract). Content:
   - **How PHP runs** and what it means: `fpm-fcgi` (PHP-FPM pool: `pm` static/dynamic/ondemand, `pm.max_children`, `pm.max_requests`), `litespeed` (LSAPI: `LSAPI_CHILDREN`, `LSPHP_ProcessGroup=on` shares one OPcache across a user's workers, `LSAPI_MAX_IDLE`), `apache2handler` (mod_php in prefork: PHP in every Apache process, including those serving static files), `cgi`/`cgi-fcgi` (plain CGI loses OPcache on every request). Recommendation: PHP-FPM or LSAPI; never switch a working LSAPI host to FPM.
   - **Read-only baseline commands**: the SAPI of a *web* request (CLI reports `cli`; use the app's own status page, e.g. WordPress Site Health → Info → Server, or a phpinfo the owner adds and removes), `php -i` for CLI ini, worker processes and RSS (`ps -o pid,rss,etime,args -u "$(id -u)"`), LSAPI env names (`tr '\0' '\n' < /proc/<pid>/environ | grep -E '^LSAPI|^LSPHP'` on the user's own lsphp), CloudLinux LVE membership (`/proc/self/cgroup` contains `lve`), and `nproc`/`free -m`.
   - **Sizing**: workers ≈ (RAM − OPcache − database − OS reserve) ÷ average worker RSS (measured, not `memory_limit`), and the concurrency needed: busiest-hour requests that reach PHP ÷ 3600 × burst factor × p95 seconds per request.
   - **`memory_limit` vs container/plan memory**: the container limit is shared by every worker. `memory_limit` caps one request, and many runtimes default it to 128M/256M even when the container has GBs. Cron, imports and image work need the highest limit; raise it only as far as the measured peak plus a margin, never to the container size.
   - **OPcache**: `opcache.memory_consumption`, `interned_strings_buffer`, `max_accelerated_files` sized from measured use (full = restarts); `validate_timestamps`/`revalidate_freq` trade-offs; preload is unsuitable for self-updating apps (WordPress) because preloaded code changes only on a PHP restart; JIT gives little for typical CMS work.
   - **Where each host sets these**: LocalWP (`conf/php/*.hbs`, see `tools/wordpress/localwp.md`), Docker (`/usr/local/etc/php/conf.d/*.ini`, FPM pool in `php-fpm.d/www.conf`), Cloudron (the app's `php.ini` in `/app/data` where the package supports it; check the app's docs), Hostinger (hPanel → PHP Configuration; `.htaccess` `php_value` inside `<IfModule lsapi_module>`; worker counts and OPcache size are set by the host), generic cPanel/CloudLinux (MultiPHP INI Editor, LVE entry-process limit).
   - **Directory listing** check: a dated subfolder (e.g. `wp-content/uploads/<year>/`) must return 403/404, not an `Index of` page. The fix is at server level: `Options -Indexes` (Apache/LiteSpeed) only where `AllowOverride` permits it, otherwise HTTP 500, or `autoindex off;` (nginx). Empty `index.php` files protect only their own folder.
   - **Safety**: never restart PHP, edit pools/ini, or write `.htaccess`/`.user.ini` without explicit authorization; back up any file before changing it; check the site's status code and error log afterwards.
2. **Registration**, as in PR #26941:
   - `.agents/build-plus.md`: add `- php-server-admin` to the `subagents:` list after `node-server-admin` (line 63), and one Domain Expertise row after line 160: `| PHP runtime: PHP-FPM/LSAPI/mod_php, PHP workers, memory_limit, OPcache sizing, php.ini per host | tools/runtime/php-server-admin.md |`.
   - `.agents/reference/domain-index.md`: one row after line 58 with trigger terms (PHP-FPM, LSAPI, lsphp, mod_php, pm.max_children, PHP workers, entry processes, memory_limit, OPcache, php.ini, directory listing).
   - `.agents/subagent-index.toon`: regenerate with `.agents/scripts/subagent-index-helper.sh generate` (do not hand-edit).
   - `.agents/scripts/verify-agent-discoverability.sh`: add check lines for the new agent mirroring lines 263-268.
3. **`.agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md`**: a short "PHP runtime" section under Configuration, with the observed facts below, what can and can't be changed, and a pointer to the new agent.
4. **`.agents/tools/wordpress/wp-admin.md`**: one line in the Security Checklist (line 143) for the directory-listing check, pointing to the new agent.

## Why

PHP apps (WordPress, Laravel, Nextcloud, Matomo, etc.) are a large share of the sites aidevops manages. Agents currently have no guidance for telling a well-run PHP setup (FPM/LSAPI, sized OPcache) from a slow one (mod_php, plain CGI, 128M `memory_limit` in a multi-GB container, full OPcache). Without it they guess, or suggest changes that hosts like Hostinger don't allow.

Observed on a Hostinger account (2026-10-05, read-only): LiteSpeed Enterprise; `lsphp` with `LSPHP_ProcessGroup=on`, `LSAPI_CHILDREN=180`, `LSAPI_MAX_IDLE_CHILDREN=90`, `LSAPI_MAX_IDLE=600`, `LSAPI_MAX_PROCESS_TIME=300`; workers alive for over a day; CloudLinux LVE cgroup; OPcache 1024M / 130,987 files / 64M strings, JIT off, no preload; PHP 8.5 CLI with `memory_limit` 12288M (CLI only; web limits come from hPanel); directory listing returns 403 in dated uploads folders; Really Simple Security writes `auto_prepend_file` into `.htaccess` (lsapi block) and `.user.ini`. A migrated site kept a stale `.user.ini` path from its previous account.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** a known pattern (Node agent PR #26941) inside a decided boundary (read-only assessment doc plus registration); section wording and trigger terms need judgment.

## How (Approach)

### Progressive Context Plan

- **Read first:** `.agents/tools/runtime/node-server-admin.md` (117 lines): the shape to copy.
- **Load only if:** `git show 2cad39667f --stat` / the PR #26941 diff, when unsure which registration files to touch; `.agents/tools/wordpress/localwp.md` for the existing LocalWP PHP settings to link, not repeat.
- **Why:** consistent agent structure and discoverability checks.
- **Stop when:** the new file passes the discoverability checks and markdown lint.

### Files to Modify

- `NEW: .agents/tools/runtime/php-server-admin.md` — model on `.agents/tools/runtime/node-server-admin.md`
- `EDIT: .agents/build-plus.md:63` — subagents allowlist entry

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/verify-agent-discoverability.sh:263-268` — check lines for the new agent
- `EDIT: .agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md` — PHP runtime section
- `EDIT: .agents/tools/wordpress/wp-admin.md:143` — directory-listing checklist line

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** Build+ routing (`.agents/build-plus.md`), `reference/domain-index.md`, the OpenCode plugin reading `.agents/subagent-index.toon`, `verify-agent-discoverability.sh` (CI).
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `subagent-index-helper.sh generate` writes the index; everything else is hand-edited markdown.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `.agents/scripts/verify-agent-discoverability.sh` (node checks at lines 263-268); `.agents/scripts/tests/test-node-server-admin-discoverability.sh` is the node-specific precedent (adding a PHP twin is optional, not required).
- **Schemas/config:** subagent frontmatter as in `node-server-admin.md:1-14`.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `.agents/subagent-index.toon` (regenerate); the deployed agents copy updates via `setup.sh` after merge, so do not edit it.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because this is documentation-only plus a regenerated index; no stored data changes.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert the PR, then regenerate `.agents/subagent-index.toon` with `.agents/scripts/subagent-index-helper.sh generate`.

### Implementation Steps

1. Create `php-server-admin.md` from the Node agent's structure with the content in What §1. Keep the AI-CONTEXT Quick Reference under about 10 bullets; put details below it.
2. Register it (What §2), then run `subagent-index-helper.sh generate`.
3. Add the Hostinger PHP runtime section and the wp-admin checklist line.
4. Run the verification below, then `wip:` commit before any broader gate.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** the generated index may conflict with other PRs; regenerate after rebasing instead of hand-merging.
- **Migration/rollback:** none: docs only; a revert restores the previous routing.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** older installs without the file simply lack the route; nothing references it before deploy.
- **Idempotency/retry:** regenerating the index is idempotent.

title: fix(pulse): merged-PR reconciliation re-closes issues reopened for unfinished follow-up
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->
## What

Make merged-PR issue reconciliation respect the issue's latest reopen lifecycle. A closing PR merged before a later issue reopen cannot justify closing that issue again. Retain the worker ownership safety fence: fix stale closure authority, not the worker's refusal to continue on a closed target.

## Why / observed evidence

Observed 2026-10-05 in a maintained consumer repository; repository identity, private paths and task IDs are intentionally omitted from this public report.

1. A baseline source PR merged at **19:27:42Z**. The issue was closed at 19:27:44Z, then reopened at **19:31:00Z** because required follow-up acceptance remained incomplete.
2. At **19:42:07Z**, issue reconciliation closed it again. Its trusted audit comment was: `Closing: linked PR <BASE_PR> was already merged. Detected by reconcile pass.` There was no newer merged PR covering the reopened work.
3. The active worker later released its claim with `worker_ownership_lost`; metrics recorded `premature_exit`. Two follow-up commits plus additional uncommitted source/docs/tests were preserved, without a follow-up PR. Issue closure also made the next native dependent appear available despite the unmet acceptance requirement.
4. The deployed `_action_oimp_single` accepts the historical merged-PR lookup, checks recurrent file-size debt and optional issue-file overlap, then closes/labels/unlocks the issue. It does not consult the latest reopen event. The current upstream action is identical: deployed and raw upstream script SHA-256 both **a1129dfb78f01a7018cf6085e8eec3ed9df818b024cd60550ed424a5c28ac28f**. Deployed file modification time predates the incident; this is not a source-only or stale-install hypothesis.
5. A network-free isolated invocation of the deployed action with positive existing file-verification/debt predicates and historical lookup reproduced **close_called=1, unlock_called=1, reopen_lookup_called=0**. All GitHub/label/unlock effects were stubbed; no real issue or owner was changed by the reproduction. This isolates the missing lifecycle check, not a full production replay.

Separately, hosted Actions checks in the affected delivery failed to acquire runners (`The job was not acquired by Runner of type hosted even after multiple attempts`), and the GitHub Status helper reported an Actions incident. That infrastructure incident is **not** attributed to this closure bug. Do not weaken CI or build retry storms to address it.

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall for pulse/merged reconciliation/ownership returned no relevant lessons.
- [x] Discovery: checked current deployed action, upstream action, five latest target-file commits and open reconcile PRs; no open matching repair found. Related completed fixes are differentiated below.
- [x] File refs verified in deployed source and/or current upstream contents, including the two existing test harnesses.
- [x] Tier: thinking because this changes authoritative lifecycle/dispatch state in a self-hosting path; preserve ownership and unknown-evidence boundaries.
- [x] Seeded draft PR skipped: reporting a confirmed narrow mechanism, not delivering a source patch from this consumer session.

## Origin and related work

User asked whether their stalled batch was an aidevops issue requiring report/repair. This is a new reconciliation-path gap, not a request to relax closed-target worker safety.

- **#33071 (completed):** `_ddpr_latest_reopen_at` and `_ddpr_first_merge_after_reopen` already make merged-keyword dispatch dedup lifecycle-aware. Reuse/factor that validated bounded-read pattern; it does not guard `_action_oimp_single` today.
- **#33026 (completed):** unchanged live-owned worktree dispatch retries. Maintainer narrowed that repair to owner-refusal classification/cache, not historical-merge reclosure.
- **#32745 / #32933 (completed):** orphan recovery PR closing-keyword misuse. This incident used an ordinary baseline PR and a later explicit reopen, not an orphan-recovery PR.
- **#32640 (completed):** recurrent file-size debt close protection. The affected reopened issue is not a file-size-debt issue; the existing debt-specific gate is insufficient.
- Current dispatch-starvation/transport reports #33647 and #33651 concern admission/cycle time, not this deterministic close/unlock action. Do not merge these causes into one diagnosis.

## Tier

`tier:thinking`. Worker-ready implementation with normal automatic dispatch subject to upstream maintainer/trust approval. No request for private source access or live customer operations.

## Files to Modify / Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-actions.sh`: `_action_oimp_single` and a shared close-lifecycle predicate if needed. Audit adjacent stage 1/2 close actions for an actual bypass of this same contract; change only demonstrated paths.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile-close.sh`: propagate required authoritative merge timing only if the existing lookup/caller cannot supply it.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-issue-reconcile.sh`: existing isolated reconciliation harness; add temporal and unknown-evidence regression cases.
- Reference (change only if needed to share the existing predicate safely): `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-pr.sh:99-135` and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-dedup-helper-has-open-pr.sh`.

## Implementation contract

1. On the matched historical-merge path, compare authoritative PR merge time with the latest complete issue reopen evidence before any close, solved-label, fast-fail reset or unlock mutation. Ignore a merge preceding the latest reopen. Maintain the current positive behavior for genuinely completed current-lifecycle issues.
2. Use bounded existing GitHub reads and complete/paginated lifecycle evidence. Missing/malformed times, failed API reads, partial histories or unavailable current evidence must defer mutation, never imply an empty reopen history or authority to close.
3. Revalidate or fence changed lifecycle evidence immediately before mutation so a reopen between cached discovery and the close decision is not silently lost. Use the narrow existing lifecycle/revision patterns; do not invent model-based acceptance scoring or a new global controller.
4. Consolidated/superseded-source coverage must not bypass the target issue's lifecycle fence. Preserve file-size-debt, touched-file, parent-task, trust and current coverage checks.
5. Do not weaken `verify-worker-ownership`, allow workers to run on revoked/closed targets, remove unrelated holds, reset dirty worktrees, release live owners or synthesize task completion. Keep deferred state content-free and observable without issue-comment storms.

## Verification and acceptance

Extend the existing reconciliation tests, not new infrastructure:

- Old merged closing PR + newer issue reopen + remaining follow-up: no close/solved-label/unlock/reset; issue stays open.
- No reopen, or a qualifying merge after the latest reopen: original permitted closure remains functional when existing gates pass.
- API failure, partial lifecycle pagination, invalid/missing timestamps and reopen racing cached discovery: defer every mutation.
- Superseded-source/consolidated matching and all applicable adjacent close actions obey the same target lifecycle contract.
- Same-task continuation and unrelated dispatch remain safe; the worker's closed-target ownership guard still rejects revoked authority.

Run `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-issue-reconcile.sh`, `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-dedup-helper-has-open-pr.sh` if shared logic changes, and ShellCheck on changed shell files. Use synthetic fixture histories and stubbed transports; no production issue closure/worker termination/customer data is needed. Rollback is source revert while keeping preserved worktrees and history. Deliver a verified PR; report source/merge/deployed/affected-runtime confirmation separately, not as one success claim.

title: scope-guard pre-push blocks claim-task-id counter push from a task worktree
body:
## Observed

Running `claim-task-id.sh` from a linked task worktree (branch `feature/tNN-...` with a brief declaring `### Files Scope`) fails to allocate an ID:

- The CAS counter push (`.task-counter` commit pushed to the counter branch, here the default branch) runs the repo's pre-push hooks.
- `hooks/scope-guard-pre-push.sh` derives the task ID from the **current branch name** (`_extract_task_id`, `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`), not from the ref being pushed, so it applies the worktree task's Files Scope to the counter commit and blocks it: `[scope-guard][BLOCK] ... outside the declared scope for tNN: .task-counter`.
- Both CAS attempts are blocked the same way and the claim ends with `UNRECOVERABLE_COUNTER_DESYNC` (no ID allocated, counter not advanced).

Workaround used: create a separate linked worktree on a branch without a task ID and run the claim there (guard fails open).

## Expected

Allocating a follow-up task ID from inside an active task worktree works without a bypass.

## Suggested fix (one of)

- In `scope-guard-pre-push.sh`, skip pushes whose `remote_ref` is not the current branch's upstream (the counter push targets the counter branch), or skip when the pushed commit only changes `.task-counter`.
- Or have the CAS push in `claim-task-id-counter.sh` run the pre-push validation with `SCOPE_GUARD_DISABLE=1` scoped to the counter commit (the counter push already runs its pre-push hook separately before `git push --no-verify`, per GH#29417).

## Verification

`tests/test-scope-guard-pre-push.sh`: add a case where HEAD is `feature/t123-x` with a brief scope and the pushed ref is `refs/heads/main` containing only `.task-counter` — expect allow. Then `claim-task-id.sh --dry-run` / a real claim from a task worktree succeeds.

title: fix(serp-probe): fresh-profile Bing runs parse 0 organic results
body:
## What

`serp-probe-helper.sh run --engine bing --fresh-profile` can finish without a challenge but record 0 parsed organic results, while the same run with the persistent profile parses normally. The probe should either parse results on the first-visit Bing page or report clearly why it couldn't (consent page, interstitial, or a different layout), so a 0 isn't mistaken for "no results".

## Evidence (2026-10-05, macOS, Brave via Playwright, direct egress)

- `serp-probe-helper.sh run --engine bing --keyword "crm software" --keyword "project management tools" --min-delay 10 --max-delay 15 --hidden --fresh-profile --no-evidence` returned `stop_reason: completed`, `blocks: []`, `succeeded: 0`, and logged `no organic results parsed` for both queries. No HTML was kept (`--no-evidence`), so the page variant is unknown.
- Straight afterwards, `serp-probe-helper.sh run --engine bing --keyword "crm software" --min-delay 10 --max-delay 15 --hidden` (persistent profile, evidence kept) returned `6 organic results`.
- The parser was unchanged between the two runs. It was moved verbatim into `serp-probe/engines.mjs` in PR #33681, and the persistent-profile run used the moved code.

## How

1. Reproduce with evidence kept: `serp-probe-helper.sh run --engine bing --keyword "crm software" --fresh-profile --min-delay 10 --max-delay 15 --max 1` (add `--headless` if no display; note whether headless changes the outcome). Inspect `q001.html` in the reported `run_dir`.
2. Depending on the cause:
   - **Cookie or consent interstitial**: extend `detectConsent` in `.agents/scripts/serp-probe/engines.mjs` to recognise it, so `--consent reject|manual` handles it (see `handleConsent` in `.agents/scripts/serp-captcha-probe.mjs`).
   - **Different results markup**: widen the Bing `organic` selector in `.agents/scripts/serp-probe/engines.mjs` (currently `#b_results li.b_algo h2 a`) and keep the `/ck/a?...&u=a1<base64url>` decoding.
   - **Results not yet rendered**: adjust the wait in `searchOnce` (`.agents/scripts/serp-captcha-probe.mjs`) for `engine.results`.
3. Optionally record a reason on zero-result entries (for example `entry.note = 'no_results_container'` when `#b_results` is absent) so reports distinguish an empty page from a layout the parser doesn't know. Don't count this as a block.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/serp-probe/engines.mjs`
- `.agents/scripts/serp-captcha-probe.mjs`

Reference pattern: the Google parser in the same file falls back to the displayed `<cite>` for opaque links. Policy constraints in `.agents/aidevops/reach-capture.md` "Public Search-result Collection" still apply: paced queries only, stop at any challenge, never solve CAPTCHAs.

## Acceptance

- A `--fresh-profile` Bing run either parses organic results or records an explicit reason on each zero-result query.
- Persistent-profile Bing and Google parsing still work (re-run one query each).
- Qlty stays clean on the probe files: `~/.qlty/bin/qlty smells --no-snippets .agents/scripts/serp-captcha-probe.mjs .agents/scripts/serp-probe/*.mjs` reports nothing (the Qlty gates are required).

## Verification

- `node --check` on changed `.mjs` files.
- One live paced Bing query each with `--fresh-profile` and with the persistent profile; include parsed counts in the PR.
- `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed --base-ref origin/main`.

Live verification needs Playwright (`node ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/playwright-runtime.mjs check`) and outbound access to bing.com. If those aren't available, say so in the PR and verify the selector offline against the saved HTML instead.

title: browser-qa-helper times out on networkidle for sites with persistent connections
body:
## What

`browser-qa-helper.sh screenshot` (and smoke/a11y) navigate with `waitUntil: 'networkidle'`. Production sites with chat widgets, analytics beacons or long-polling never reach network idle, so every capture times out and no screenshot is produced.

Call sites:
- `.agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper.sh:273`
- `.agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper-core.sh:393`
- `.agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper-tests.sh:222`
- `.agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper-a11y.sh:211`

## Observed

`browser-qa-helper.sh screenshot --url <production WordPress site> --pages "/<award page>/" --viewports desktop,mobile` failed at both viewports with `page.goto: Timeout 30000ms exceeded … waiting until "networkidle"`. A one-off script on the same Playwright runtime using `waitUntil: 'load'` plus a fixed settle captured correct screenshots. A `domcontentloaded` + 2.5 s wait gave blank images because the page had not painted yet.

## Fix

Navigate with `waitUntil: 'load'`, then wait for `networkidle` up to a short cap (eg `page.waitForLoadState('networkidle', { timeout: 5000 }).catch(() => {})`) before capturing. Optionally add a `--wait-until` option. Keep the existing timeout semantics for genuinely failing pages.

## Verification

- `browser-qa-helper.sh screenshot` produces non-blank PNGs for a page with a persistent chat widget.
- Existing browser-qa tests still pass for local static pages.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper-core.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper-tests.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/browser-qa-helper-a11y.sh`

title: full-loop merge rejects plan(tNNN) planning PR titles that the publication contract prescribes
body:
## What

The planning-PR contract and the full-loop merge gate disagree about planning PR titles.

- `.agents/reference/planning-pr-publication-contract.md` says: "A single-task publication uses `plan(tNNN): ...`".
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh` (squash-subject validation, around lines 1370–1397) accepts only `conventional_ere` (`feat|fix|docs|refactor|perf|test|chore|style|build|ci|security`) or `task_ere` (`tNNN: …` / `GH#NNN: …`). A `plan(t18447): …` title fails with "PR #N title is not a valid squash subject; refusing merge".

## Observed

A managed private repo's planning PR titled `plan(t18447): award sync import-date defect` was refused by `full-loop-helper.sh merge` after CI and the review gate passed. Retitling it to `t18447: chore(plan): …` merged it, and publication reconciled.

## Fix

Pick one convention. Either add `plan` (with the `(tNNN[, tNNN])` scope) to the accepted squash-subject types in `full-loop-helper-merge.sh`, or change the contract (and any helper that generates planning PR titles) to `tNNN: chore(plan): …`. `pulse-merge-conflict.sh` comments already show `plan(t2059, t2060): …` subjects in history, so accepting `plan(...)` keeps history consistent.

## Verification

- A PR titled `plan(t123): …` passes squash-subject validation (or the contract and generators no longer produce that form).
- Existing tests touching `_merge_*` subject validation still pass.

title: full-loop validators fail closed on scriptless grouping workspace after root checks pass (lockfile change)
body:
## Observed

`full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` fails closed on a pnpm monorepo PR that changes
`pnpm-lock.yaml`, even after repository-root `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm run typecheck`
and `pnpm run test` (turbo across every workspace) have all passed:

```
[validators] scope=repository root reason=root-or-shared-change command=pnpm run test
[validators] scope=apps/web reason=affected-workspace command=pnpm run lint
...
[ERROR] [validators] NO SCOPED CHECKS AVAILABLE for packages/analytics
[ERROR] [validators] configure lint, typecheck, or a check-only format script in packages/analytics/package.json
```

`packages/analytics/package.json` is a scriptless placeholder (`{"name":"analytics","private":true}`);
its real packages are nested (`packages/analytics/web`, `/mobile`, `/extension`).

## Root cause

`.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit-validators.sh`:

- `_validator_all_workspace_scopes` adds every `package.json` matching the workspace
  patterns when a root/shared file (lockfile) changes, without filtering by
  `_validator_package_has_check`.
- `_run_scoped_node_checks` then returns 1 for any such scope with `check_count == 0`.
- Additionally, once the root package has checks, re-running each workspace's
  scripts duplicates the root turbo run (≈2x validator time on large monorepos).

## Suggested fix

In `_validator_all_workspace_scopes`, when the root package has a check script,
return only `.` (root already fans out); otherwise include only scopes where
`_validator_package_has_check` is true, and fail only if none qualify.
Add a regression case to the validators test fixture with a scriptless grouping
package and a lockfile-only change.

## Verification

Test fixture: pnpm workspace with root `lint`/`test`, a nested scriptless package
dir, and a lockfile change → validators pass once (root scope only).
<!-- aidevops:origin:interactive -->

**Task ID:** `t18592` | **Status:** open
**Tags:** `auto-dispatch` `bug`

## Outcome

GH transport: stale low core quota persists for multi-credential unresolved scope, pacing all REST reads

## Done when

- [ ] Two bound credentials of one owner: stored `540` with a future reset, then an incoming newer-reset `4999`, results in `4999` being accepted and pacing cleared.
- [ ] Two different owners stay isolated: neither inherits nor clears the other's balance.
- [ ] A stale stored reset is never extended by `max()` while the old `remaining` is kept.
- [ ] `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-transport-budget.py` passes.
- [ ] Runtime: with more than one bound credential and healthy live quota, `full-loop-helper.sh pre-merge-gate <PR> <repo>` does not return `github-api-read-deferred`.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/gh_transport_recovery.py` (`probe_recovers`): accept a causally newer reset as a new window when the observing credential's owner is proven to match the stored observation (single owner, or an attributed owner shared by every bound PAT).
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/gh_transport_budget.py` (`finish`, around the `min`/`max` clamp): do not extend a stale reset with `max()` while keeping the old `remaining`. When the incoming reset is newer, keep or replace the pair together; never combine a new reset with an old balance.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/gh_transport_identity.py`: optionally derive a trusted owner for PAT/OAuth tokens (cached authenticated login, never logged) so multi-PAT hosts become attributed. GitHub App installation tokens (`ghs_`) remain separate owners.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-transport-budget.py`: add regression cases (see Acceptance Criteria).
- `EDIT: .agents/reference/github-api-transport.md`: update the owner attribution and reconcile section.

### Implementation Steps

1. Reproduce in a test: bind two credentials to one scope, store `remaining=540` with a future reset, then feed an observation with a newer reset and `remaining=4999`.
2. Fix the `max(reset)` ratchet in `finish()`, then fix recovery for proven same-owner credentials.
3. Add `stale_multi_credential_scope` to `gh_transport_budget.py status` diagnostics.
4. Run `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-transport-budget.py` and the transport shell cases.

### Hazards

- Never merge credentials belonging to different GitHub users or installations, and never let one owner inherit another owner's balance.
- Keep secondary-limit cooldowns, reservations, uncertain-request debt and atomic admission unchanged.
- `/rate_limit` responses are still never a grant.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/gh_transport_recovery.py`
- `.agents/scripts/gh_transport_budget.py`
- `.agents/scripts/gh_transport_identity.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-transport-budget.py`
- `.agents/reference/github-api-transport.md`

</details>

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

The GitHub transport governor keeps a stale low `core` balance in the shared
`unresolved` quota scope whenever more than one credential is bound to it. It
also keeps pushing that balance's reset epoch forward, so the stale state never
expires. Until this is fixed, every REST read on the host (pulse, workers,
interactive merges) is paced to about one call per 6.5s.

## Why

- Observed 2026-10-05 23:10Z–00:00Z on a host running v3.38.12 (includes
  t18590 / PR #33688). Local admission DB, scope `unresolved`:
  `core remaining=540`, with the reset rising from 1791246218 to 1791247191
  while `remaining` stayed at 540. `pacing.core` slots were about 6.5s apart.
  The `binding` table holds 5 credentials for that scope.
- Live GitHub for the active `gh` keyring PAT showed `core 5000/5000, used=0`.
  No GitHub App is configured (`github-app-auth-helper.sh status` reports
  `gh-pat`).
- Impact: `full-loop-helper.sh merge` failed 4 times in a row with
  `github-api-read-deferred` (`local primary pacing from observed demand and
  reset`). It passed only with the documented per-process rollback
  `AIDEVOPS_GH_TRANSPORT_GOVERNOR_DISABLE=1`. The same pacing throttles pulse
  dispatch (GH#33647).
- Mechanism: `gh_transport_recovery.py` `probe_recovers()` accepts a newer
  window only when `owners == 1`. The serialized-probe path also requires
  `owners == 1 or budget.attributed`, and nothing sets
  `AIDEVOPS_GH_QUOTA_OWNER`. `gh_transport_budget.py` `finish()` then applies
  `available = min(incoming, stored)` and `reset_at = max(incoming, stored)`.
  An idle PAT reports a sliding reset of about now+3600, so `row[1] > now`
  never becomes false and the clamp renews indefinitely.

</details>

title: full-loop merge starved by local primary pacing while quota remains (30s admission recovery budget)
body:
## Observed

`full-loop-helper.sh merge <PR> <repo>` failed again and again for over 20 minutes with:

```
PR #N verification deferred ([gh-transport] error_kind=github-api-read-deferred ... reason="local primary pacing from observed demand and reset" operation=pull-request-identity-read)
Local GitHub read admission: waiting 7s before rechecking PR #N (30s recovery budget)
Merge deferred by GitHub read admission; retry_at=...
```

Local quota row (`~/.aidevops/state/gh-transport/admission.sqlite3`, table `quota`): core remaining 540 of 5000, about 50 minutes to reset. `primary_wait()` in `gh_transport_capacity.py` spaces requests about (reset - now) / available ≈ 4.6 s apart, and other local consumers (pulse) take the free slots. The pre-merge gate (`cmd_pre_merge_gate`) needs several sequential reads, so it can't finish within `_merge_pre_merge_gate_with_admission_retry()`'s 30 s budget (`full-loop-helper-merge.sh`, around line 2497). An interactive, user-requested merge is starved until the quota resets, although 540 points are left and the merge needs fewer than 20.

## Expected

An interactive merge or release (user-visible critical path) gets admitted ahead of background demand, or the recovery budget scales to the pacing interval × reads the gate needs, so a merge completes within a few minutes while quota remains.

## Possible fixes

- Priority classes in the governor: interactive and critical-path reads may use the slots that pacing holds back; background (pulse) yields.
- Or: `_merge_pre_merge_gate_with_admission_retry()` derives its budget from the gate's read count × the current pacing interval (capped, e.g. 5 min) instead of a fixed 30 s.

## Verification

- With a pacing row saved (remaining well below half the limit, other consumers active), `full-loop-helper.sh merge` on a green PR completes within the new budget.
- Existing tests: `tests/test-full-loop-merge.sh`, `tests/test-gh-shim-transport-cases.sh`.

title: planning-commit-helper reports RESULT=direct on detached HEAD without publishing
body:
## What

`planning-commit-helper.sh "<msg>"` run from a linked worktree on a **detached
HEAD at origin/main** printed `AIDEVOPS_PLANNING_COMMIT_RESULT=direct`, but
the commit was never published. It existed only as a local detached commit
(`[detached HEAD cd90633dd4] plan: add t18592 brief (GH#33701)`). `git ls-remote
origin main` still showed the previous SHA, and `git branch -r --contains
cd90633dd4` was empty.

Earlier the same session, the helper ran from a named branch and correctly
returned `RESULT=pr` (PR #33702).

## Why

Callers, and the reconciler that later reads the brief, treat `direct` as
"published to the default branch". Here the brief never reached main, and
GH#33701 stayed `publication:pending` until the brief was shipped manually
in PR #33705.

## How

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/planning-commit-helper.sh` (around the
  `_todo_branch_requires_planning_pr` / `todo_commit_push` branch, ~L593-598):
  print `RESULT=direct` only after verifying the remote default branch
  contains the published commit. Otherwise return non-zero with a diagnostic.
- Find which path committed on the caller's detached HEAD (`todo_commit_push`
  in the TODO commit library) instead of using the temporary-index
  publication described at L587-590.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/planning-commit-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/shared-todo-commit.sh`

`todo_commit_push()` is defined at `.agents/scripts/shared-todo-commit.sh:733`.

## Verification

From a linked worktree detached at `origin/main` with one new
`todo/tasks/tNNN-brief.md`, run `planning-commit-helper.sh "plan: test"`. It
must either publish (remote main or a PR contains the commit) or fail
non-zero. It must never print `RESULT=direct` while the commit exists only
locally.

title: full-loop merge: final head-SHA read swallows local-admission deferral and refuses merge
body:
## What

`full-loop-helper.sh merge` fails at the final pre-merge head-SHA read when the local GitHub read admission defers the request, even though every earlier gate (required checks, review-bot gate, authority preflight) has passed at the same head. GitHub's real budget was nearly full at the time (core 5000/5000, GraphQL 4992/5000); the deferral came from local admission pacing driven by demand from concurrent sessions.

## Observed (interactive session, managed project repo, 2026-10-06)

- Seven `merge` attempts on one PR over ~20 minutes, with 2- and 5-minute back-offs between some attempts.
- Most failed early with `error_kind=github-api-read-deferred attempted=false deferred_by=local_admission reason="local primary pacing from observed demand and reset"`; the readiness path's 30s recovery budget was insufficient.
- Two attempts passed every gate and then failed with:
  - `Could not retrieve PR #N head SHA for verification; refusing merge`
  - `Cannot bind merge to a remotely verified PR head SHA` / `Merge blocked: cannot bind the merge body to an exact remotely verified PR head.`
- `gh pr view` immediately afterwards returned the same head SHA, `mergeStateStatus: CLEAN`, `state: OPEN`.

## Root cause (deployed copy)

`.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh` `_merge_resolve_match_head` (around line 1191):

```bash
pre_merge_head_sha=$(_merge_fetch_head_sha_rest "$pr_number" "$repo" || true)
```

The `|| true` discards the local-admission deferral evidence, so the caller reports a generic SHA-retrieval failure instead of a deferral with `retry_at`, and no bounded recovery is attempted. The readiness path already has a bounded local-admission recovery (around line 2514, `Local GitHub read admission: waiting ...s (30s recovery budget)`), but this final read does not reuse it.

## Proposed fix

1. In `_merge_resolve_match_head`, capture stderr from `_merge_fetch_head_sha_rest`; when `_full_loop_local_admission_evidence` (in `full-loop-helper-readiness.sh`) matches, wait until `retry_at` within the same bounded recovery budget and re-read, keeping the exact-head equality check and refusing merge if the head changed.
2. If recovery is exhausted, emit the deferral diagnostic with `retry_at` (same shape as the readiness path) rather than the generic SHA error, so operators can tell pacing from a real failure.
3. Consider whether interactive merges, which are the last step of an already-verified critical path, should get admission priority over background demand, so a merge isn't starved by parallel sessions.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh` — `_merge_resolve_match_head`, `_merge_fetch_head_sha_rest`, and the bounded recovery near line 2514
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-readiness.sh` — `_full_loop_local_admission_evidence`
- Tests: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-cases.sh` (has `test_bounded_local_admission_recovery` and admission fixtures to extend)

## Verification

- Add a merge-case fixture where `_merge_fetch_head_sha_rest` first emits the local-admission deferral line and then succeeds: expect merge proceeds at the verified head.
- Fixture where the deferral persists past the budget: expect a deferral diagnostic with `retry_at`, not "Could not retrieve PR head SHA".
- Fixture where the re-read returns a different SHA: expect refusal (head-drift protection unchanged).
- `shellcheck` clean; `tests/test-full-loop-merge.sh` passes.

- Local admission DB, scope `unresolved`: `quota.core remaining=540 reset=1791246218`; `observed` advances on every response, but `remaining` never increases. `pacing.core` retry slots are about 6.5s apart.
- `binding` holds 5 credentials, all mapped to that one scope.
- Live GitHub for the active `gh` keyring PAT (`marcusquinn`): `core 5000/5000, used=0`, reset moving forward with each call. No GitHub App is configured (`github-app-auth-helper.sh status` → `gh-pat`). No credential that could be checked showed 540 remaining.

`.agents/scripts/gh_transport_recovery.py` `probe_recovers()` accepts a newer

budget.attributed`. `attributed` is false unless `AIDEVOPS_GH_QUOTA_OWNER` is
set, and nothing in setup or the pulse sets it. `gh_transport_budget.py`
`finish()` then clamps every fresh observation to
`min(incoming, stored)` / `max(reset)`, so the stale value is re-stamped until
the stored reset expires.

## How (recommended)

1. Make the multi-credential `unresolved` scope recoverable. Prefer automatic
   owner attribution: resolve the authenticated login (`gh api user`, cached,
   never logged) for PAT/OAuth tokens and use it as the quota owner. All PATs
   of one user share a single allowance, so this is the documented trusted

2. Otherwise, at minimum, let a newer reset observed by a credential whose

3. Diagnostics: `gh_transport_budget.py status` should report

   reset is older than a live observation.
4. Update `.agents/reference/github-api-transport.md` (owner attribution and
   reconcile section).

installations. Keep secondary-limit cooldowns, reservations and atomic
admission unchanged.

- Runtime: with more than one bound credential and a stale low balance, a

title: consolidated: auto owner attribution and stale_multi_credential_scope diagnostic for unresolved GH transport quota
body:
_Supersedes #33701 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Make the shared `unresolved` GitHub transport quota scope recover from a stale low `core` balance when more than one credential is bound to it. Remaining work after PR #33710 (merged as `d8dfb01e81`): automatic quota-owner attribution (brief item 1) and the `stale_multi_credential_scope` status diagnostic (brief item 3), plus the reference doc update (item 4).

## Why

The transport governor keeps a stale low `core` balance (`remaining=540`) for the `unresolved` scope when several credentials are bound to it. While the stored reset epoch is in the future, every REST read on the machine (pulse, workers, interactive merges) is paced to roughly one call per `seconds_left / 540`, about 6.5s. Impact: `full-loop-helper.sh merge` failed with `github-api-read-deferred` / `local primary pacing from observed demand and reset`; the REST-core progress gate reported "authoritative REST-core quota evidence unavailable" and blocked Pulse dispatch (GH#33647); `_gh_current_user_allows_repo_write` failed with `permission-lookup-failed:api-failure`, so the merge pass logged maintainer repos as "contributor/read-only" and skipped them.

Evidence (2026-10-05, v3.38.11 + hot-deployed #33688): scope `unresolved` `quota.core remaining=540 reset=1791246218`; `binding` held 5 credentials mapped to the one scope; live GitHub for the active PAT showed `core 5000/5000, used=0`. No GitHub App configured (`github-app-auth-helper.sh status` → `gh-pat`).

Root cause: `.agents/scripts/gh_transport_recovery.py` `probe_recovers()` accepts a newer reset window only when `owners == 1`. With multiple bound credentials, recovery needs the serialized probe path, requiring `owners == 1 or budget.attributed`. `attributed` is false unless `AIDEVOPS_GH_QUOTA_OWNER` is set, and nothing in setup or the pulse sets it.

## How

1. Automatic owner attribution: resolve the authenticated login (`gh api user`, cached, never logged) for PAT/OAuth tokens and use it as the quota owner. All PATs of one user share a single allowance (documented trusted case). GitHub App installation tokens (`ghs_`) must remain separate owners. Fallback at minimum: a newer reset observed by a credential whose owner is proven identical to the stored observation repairs the balance, with a newer reset and higher remaining replacing the stored pair instead of extending the old balance.
2. Diagnostics: `gh_transport_budget.py status` reports `stale_multi_credential_scope` when bound credentials > 1 and the stored reset is older than a live observation.
3. Update `.agents/reference/github-api-transport.md` (owner attribution and reconcile section).

Already done (do not redo): PR #33710 fixed the `max(reset)` ratchet in `finish()`; the conservative clamp keeps the lower balance paired with its own reset epoch (per @marcusquinn). Read `finish()` in `gh_transport_budget.py` first to avoid duplicating this.

Hard boundary: never merge credentials belonging to different GitHub users or installations. Keep secondary-limit cooldowns, reservations and atomic admission unchanged.

Rollout caveat: processes started from older runtime bundles still run the old `finish()` and may keep re-stamping the stale reset until they restart (about 50 such processes were seen on one runner). Not code-fixable here; mention in the reference doc.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Two bound credentials of one attributed owner, stored `remaining=540` with a future reset, then an incoming newer-reset `4999` observation is accepted.
- [ ] Two different owners stay isolated and do not inherit each other's balance (negative/regression).
- [ ] `ghs_` installation tokens remain separate owners; the resolved login is cached and never logged.
- [ ] `gh_transport_budget.py status` reports `stale_multi_credential_scope` under the stated condition.
- [ ] Runtime: with more than one bound credential and a stale low balance, a normal `gh api repos/OWNER/REPO` read clears pacing within one response; `full-loop-helper.sh pre-merge-gate` does not return `github-api-read-deferred` while live quota is healthy.
- [ ] Secondary-limit cooldowns, reservations and atomic admission behave unchanged.
- [ ] `.agents/reference/github-api-transport.md` documents owner attribution and reconcile behaviour.

## Verification

- `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-transport-budget.py`
- `shellcheck` is not needed (Python only); run the existing scoped Python lint if configured.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: .agents/scripts/gh_transport_recovery.py
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/gh-transport-governor.py
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/gh_transport_budget.py
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/gh_transport_identity.py
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-transport-budget.py
- EDIT: .agents/reference/github-api-transport.md

## Context & Decisions

- @marcusquinn (original brief): problem statement, root cause, recommended approach, hard boundary, verification.
- @marcusquinn (comment 1): the stale balance never expires on its own because `max(reset)` ratchets; the fix must also stop the ratchet. Verified workaround: `AIDEVOPS_GH_TRANSPORT_GOVERNOR_DISABLE=1` (per process only).
- @marcusquinn (comment 2): PR #33710 fixed the ratchet; items 1 (auto attribution) and 3 (status diagnostic) remain; rollout caveat above.

Related: GH#33647, GH#33651 (t18590, PR #33688), GH#31442, GH#31541.

cc @marcusquinn

title: pulse: PR backlog guardrail counts drafts and interactive PRs, starving worker dispatch
body:
## What

The repository PR backlog guardrail suppresses all ordinary dispatch for a repo once it has `PULSE_DISPATCH_GUARDRAIL_OPEN_PR_THRESHOLD` (default 12) open PRs of any kind. Count only the backlog workers can create or move (non-draft, worker-origin PRs awaiting merge), and allow a per-repo threshold in `repos.json`.

## Why

Observed on v3.38.11 (two runners, one managed private repo, 2026-10-06 ~01:00Z): both runners had 12 free worker slots, load 8/24, and 22 eligible candidates, yet every cycle logged

```text
Repository PR backlog guardrail: repo=<repo> open_prs=12 threshold=12 ordinary_candidates_suppressed=22 exempt_candidates=0
Dispatch path=max complete: implementation_dispatched=0 ... processed=1/1
```

and zero workers ran for hours. Of the 13 open PRs: 6 were the maintainer's interactive PRs (several DIRTY drafts from September), 4 were worker drafts (two stalled since 2026-09-28, see #33654), one an orphan-recovery checkpoint, and only 2 were non-draft worker PRs awaiting merge. Interactive and long-stalled draft PRs are not merge backlog the pulse can reduce, so counting them blocks throughput without protecting anything.

## How

1. In `_dispatch_filter_repo_pr_backlog_candidates` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-current-state-guardrails.sh`), fetch `number,isDraft,labels` and count only PRs that are not drafts and carry `origin:worker` / `origin:worker-takeover` and no `hold-for-review` / `needs-maintainer-review` label. Log both totals (`open_prs_total`, `open_prs_counted`).
2. Read an optional per-repo `"dispatch_open_pr_threshold"` from the repo's `repos.json` entry, falling back to the env var, then 12. `0` disables, as today.
3. Note the change where the guardrail is documented (`rg -n "PULSE_DISPATCH_GUARDRAIL_OPEN_PR_THRESHOLD" .agents/`).

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-current-state-guardrails.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-current-state-guardrails.sh`
- `.agents/reference/repos-json-fields.md`

Scope note (worker, GH#33243 integration recovery): `rg -n "PULSE_DISPATCH_GUARDRAIL_OPEN_PR_THRESHOLD" .agents/` matches only the script and its test; no doc currently describes the guardrail. The new per-repo `dispatch_open_pr_threshold` field is documented in the canonical repos.json field reference, `.agents/reference/repos-json-fields.md` ("PR Throughput Preferences").

## Verification

- Existing guardrail tests pass; one fixture with 12 drafts/interactive PRs no longer suppresses candidates, and 12 non-draft worker PRs still does.
- On a runner, the log shows `open_prs_counted` below `open_prs_total` and candidates are no longer suppressed by non-worker PRs.

   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)

The pulse holds `auto-dispatch` briefs whose scope fails `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check`, so prose after a path makes the successor undispatchable.

Use `EDIT:` when the path already exists on the default branch; use `NEW:` only after confirming it is absent. A stale checkout or failed API lookup is not proof of absence.

Keep all source lines (do not replace them with a summary): the runner capability gate unions comma/space-separated names across these lines. Never drop a prerequisite because this consolidation runner lacks the named secret; consolidation itself does not need those credentials.
   - `## Context & Decisions` — which commenter contributed which insight (attribution matters)
   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #33641 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`

3. **Validate before filing the new consolidated issue.** Save the inlined parent body verbatim to a local file, plus a separate body file for each additional superseded issue. Validate the merged body against ALL sources; a failed check stops publication and parent closure until the merged body is repaired:

```bash

  --source "<file containing the verbatim parent body>" \
```

- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.

## Parent body (verbatim)

## What

`full-loop-helper.sh merge` gives up on the first local GitHub read-admission deferral and reports it as a merge failure, even when GitHub quota is healthy.

## Evidence

- Interactive merge failed three times with `error_kind=github-api-read-deferred ... deferred_by=local_admission`; rerun with `AIDEVOPS_GH_LOCAL_ADMISSION_RETRY_DELAY_SECONDS=5` merged.
- `.agents/scripts/gh-transport-controls.sh` retries a local deferral once with a short delay; `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh` maps `github-api-read-deferred` straight to an error.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`: on `deferred_by=local_admission`, wait until `retry_at` (or bounded backoff) and retry the pre-merge gate within a bounded budget (60 s, at most 3 retries); fail closed otherwise and on real GitHub rate-limit/HTTP errors.
- Do not change pulse/worker admission policy.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-cases.sh`

Integration scope recovery: PR #33659 moved the existing admission regression cases into test-full-loop-merge-cases.sh, sourced by test-full-loop-merge.sh. Updating those existing cases is necessary to verify the authorized 60-second, three-retry behavior. Collision discovery found no open related PR; verification remains bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge.sh and ShellCheck on changed scripts.

## Acceptance

- A local-admission deferral whose window opens within the budget merges without operator action.
- A deferral beyond the budget still exits non-zero with the `retry_at` detail.
- Genuine GitHub quota exhaustion is not retried in a tight loop.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge.sh`
- `shellcheck` on changed scripts.

title: consolidated: bounded local-admission wait across full-loop merge GitHub reads
body:
_Supersedes #33641 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Make `full-loop-helper.sh merge` wait out a local GitHub read-admission deferral (`deferred_by=local_admission`) instead of failing on the first one. Apply the bounded wait to every pre-merge GitHub read path in `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`, and when a deferral still persists, report its `error_kind` and `retry_at` rather than a generic failure.

## Why

`full-loop-helper.sh merge` maps `github-api-read-deferred` straight to an error even when GitHub quota is healthy. `.agents/scripts/gh-transport-controls.sh` retries a local deferral only once with a short delay. Interactive merges failed repeatedly with `error_kind=github-api-read-deferred ... deferred_by=local_admission`; rerunning with `AIDEVOPS_GH_LOCAL_ADMISSION_RETRY_DELAY_SECONDS=5` merged. Several call sites additionally discard the deferral detail (`2>/dev/null) || return 1`), so operators see misleading generic errors.

## How

Edit `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`:

1. On `deferred_by=local_admission`, wait until `retry_at` (or a bounded backoff) and retry the pre-merge gate within a bounded budget: 60 s total, at most 3 retries. Fail closed (non-zero exit, `retry_at` detail) when the budget is exceeded, and on real GitHub rate-limit/HTTP errors. Never retry genuine quota exhaustion in a tight loop.
2. Cover the additional read paths reported in comments (use one shared deferral handler near the existing `github-api-read-deferred` mapping, around line 2446, rather than per-call-site logic):
   - Release-lane PR identity check (`gh api repos/<repo>/pulls/<N>` with `2>/dev/null`, around lines 2525-2526). Currently reports a hard `Merge blocked: cannot verify release-lane PR identity`.
   - `_merge_fetch_pr_refs_rest` (around line 646), which calls `_flm_gh_read gh api ... 2>/dev/null) || return 1`, and its caller `_merge_guard_prospective_todo` (around line 975), which maps any failure to `unable to pin fresh PR base/head evidence for prospective TODO validation`. Surface the deferral kind and `retry_at` in the error instead of the generic message.
   - Similar `2>/dev/null) || return 1` reads around lines 236, 294, 332 and 1882.
   - Required-check evidence read (`required-check evidence is indeterminate (exact check read exit 2)`).
3. Do not change pulse/worker admission policy.

Reference only (not in write scope): `.agents/scripts/gh-transport-controls.sh` (existing single local-deferral retry). Line numbers are from the reports; re-verify against current `main`.

Out-of-scope follow-up (per @marcusquinn, comment 1): other one-shot interactive helpers with several sequential reads (`interactive-session-helper.sh claim`, `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr`) hit the same pacing deferral; a shared read wrapper with a bounded wait until `retry_at` would fix them centrally. File a separate issue if not covered here.

Integration scope recovery: PR #33659 moved the existing admission regression cases into `test-full-loop-merge-cases.sh`, sourced by `test-full-loop-merge.sh`. Updating those existing cases is necessary to verify the authorized 60-second, three-retry behavior. Collision discovery found no open related PR. Prior PRs #33650 and #33682 conflicted with `main`; salvage via cherry-pick of `187f11b74e6af8ae4745188fe5d491fa2e2be6de` / `4546a500a2c9caf42e506e979d87f8f12b3a103d` onto a fresh branch off `origin/main` if still useful, else rewrite from this spec.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A local-admission deferral whose window opens within the budget merges without operator action.
- [ ] A deferral beyond the budget (60 s / 3 retries) still exits non-zero with the `retry_at` detail.
- [ ] Genuine GitHub quota exhaustion and real HTTP errors are not retried in a tight loop and still fail closed.
- [ ] The release-lane identity read and the prospective-TODO refs read (`_merge_fetch_pr_refs_rest`) wait for `retry_at` on a local deferral; if it persists, the error names the deferral kind and `retry_at`.
- [ ] A test case covers the prospective-TODO refs read returning a local-admission deferral once, then succeeding.
- [ ] `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge.sh` passes and ShellCheck reports zero violations on changed scripts.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-cases.sh

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge.sh`
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-cases.sh`

## Context & Decisions

- Original report and bounded-retry design (60 s, max 3 retries, fail closed on real errors, no admission policy change): parent #33641 body.
- @marcusquinn (comment 1): evidence that the failure also hits `interactive-session-helper.sh claim` and `commit-and-pr`, and that three merge runs were needed; suggests a shared read wrapper.
- @marcusquinn (comment 2): release-lane identity read (`2>/dev/null`) turns a deferral into a hard block; must be covered.
- @marcusquinn (comment 3): `_merge_fetch_pr_refs_rest` / `_merge_guard_prospective_todo` hide the deferral reason; apply bounded wait and surface `error_kind`/`retry_at`; add test case.
- Prior PRs #33650 and #33682 conflicted with `main`.

title: t18594: wp-plugin-parity-helper: inventory plugin version gaps across sibling sites and sync with health-checked swaps
body:
## Task


Add `.agents/scripts/wp-plugin-parity-helper.sh` with two subcommands that run **on the hosting account** (uploaded via `scp` or streamed with `ssh <alias> bash -s -- ...`):

- `inventory --target <domain> [--domains-root <dir>]`: list every WordPress install under the domains root (default `$HOME/domains/*/public_html`), collect `name,version,status` per plugin with `wp --skip-plugins --skip-themes plugin list`, and print TSV rows `slug  target_version  newest_version  source_domain  target_status` only where a sibling has a strictly newer version (`sort -V`). Exclude must-use and drop-in entries.
- `sync --target <domain> --stash <dir> [--check-path <path>] [--dry-run] <slug:source-domain>...`: for each pair, copy the source folder to `<slug>.new`, move the old folder into the stash, rename into place, and for **active** plugins request `https://<target><check-path>` (default `/`) expecting HTTP 200 with no "fatal error" or "critical error on this website" text; on failure restore the stashed folder and report `REVERTED`. Print `OK|SKIP|FAIL|REVERTED slug old -> new (status)` per plugin. Abort before any change if the target fails the health check.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Files to Modify

- NEW: `.agents/scripts/wp-plugin-parity-helper.sh` — model the structure (sourcing `shared-constants.sh`, `help` subcommand, `local var="$1"`, explicit `return 0/1`) on `.agents/scripts/wp-plugin-release-helper.sh`.
- EDIT: `.agents/tools/wordpress/premium-plugin-updates.md` — in "Refreshing Stale Plugins From Sibling Sites", point steps 1, 4 and 5 at the helper with a usage example using placeholders only.

### Implementation Steps

1. `inventory`: write all rows to a `mktemp -d` file, then filter with `awk`; do not use process substitution (`<(...)`), which fails on hosts without `/dev/fd`.
2. Compatibility hint: for slugs ending in `-pro`, `pro`, or known add-on pairs (`fluentformpro`→`fluentform`, `fluentcampaign-pro`→`fluent-crm`, `fluent-support-pro`→`fluent-support`, `seo-by-rank-math-pro`→`seo-by-rank-math`, `wp-social-ninja-pro`→`wp-social-reviews`), print a warning column when the target's base plugin version differs from the source site's base version.
3. `sync`: guard every `rm -rf` with `${var:?}`; never delete the stash; `--dry-run` prints the plan without copying.
4. Never read or print `wp-config.php` secrets; the helper does not take database backups (document running the backup first, see `services/hosting/hostinger.md` "Database backups without WP-CLI").

### Hazards and Compatibility

- Bash 3.2 compatibility and ShellCheck zero violations (`reference/bash-compat.md`).
- Swapping an active plugin briefly exposes a partial state; keep copy-then-rename ordering so the live folder is replaced by two `mv` calls.
- Do not run upgrade routines or activate plugins.

### Scope Boundaries

- No changes to `wp-fleet-helper.sh` / `wp-fleet-runner.py` (release-asset trust model is intentionally separate).
- No new test runner or CI gate.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/wp-plugin-parity-helper.sh
- .agents/tools/wordpress/premium-plugin-updates.md

</details>

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## Origin

Interactive session: stale premium plugins on two WordPress sites sharing one shared-hosting account were refreshed by ad-hoc scripts (version inventory across all installs on the account, then per-plugin folder swaps with health check and revert). 66 plugin folders were updated without regressions. The procedure is documented in `.agents/tools/wordpress/premium-plugin-updates.md` ("Refreshing Stale Plugins From Sibling Sites", added by t18593 / GH#33734); this task turns it into a reusable helper.

## What

Add `.agents/scripts/wp-plugin-parity-helper.sh` with two subcommands that run **on the hosting account** (uploaded via `scp` or streamed with `ssh <alias> bash -s -- ...`):

- `inventory --target <domain> [--domains-root <dir>]`: list every WordPress install under the domains root (default `$HOME/domains/*/public_html`), collect `name,version,status` per plugin with `wp --skip-plugins --skip-themes plugin list`, and print TSV rows `slug  target_version  newest_version  source_domain  target_status` only where a sibling has a strictly newer version (`sort -V`). Exclude must-use and drop-in entries.
- `sync --target <domain> --stash <dir> [--check-path <path>] [--dry-run] <slug:source-domain>...`: for each pair, copy the source folder to `<slug>.new`, move the old folder into the stash, rename into place, and for **active** plugins request `https://<target><check-path>` (default `/`) expecting HTTP 200 with no "fatal error" or "critical error on this website" text; on failure restore the stashed folder and report `REVERTED`. title: pulse: dispatch starved again: cache prime consumes cycle budget and stale enumeration estimate never decays
body:
## What

Pulse dispatch is starved again: worker runs per day fell 86 (Oct 1) → 87 → 53 → 74 → 23 (Oct 5) → 0 (Oct 6), from `~/.aidevops/logs/headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl`. Every recent cycle logs:

```
Dispatch_max skipped before candidate enumeration: cycle wall-clock budget below dispatch reserve (remaining=750s floor=600s enumeration=886s); refill trigger retained for a fresh-budget pass (GH#33560)
```

## Root cause (two coupled defects)

1. **Cache prime consumes the dispatch cycle budget.** `pulse-wrapper.sh:270` sets `PULSE_START_EPOCH` and `pulse-wrapper.sh:1648` runs `_pulse_prime_caches_if_stale` inside the same cycle. `_pulse_cycle_remaining_seconds` (`pulse-watchdog.sh:207`) gives ~1710s per cycle (min(stale, lock 1800) − 90 reserve). Cache prime now takes 822–1624s (`pulse-cache-prime.log`), and its 1800s sentinel is older than the cycle period, so it runs nearly every cycle and leaves too little budget for dispatch.
2. **Enumeration estimate ratchet.** `_dispatch_enumeration_expected_seconds` (`pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh:696`) reads `~/.aidevops/cache/pulse-dispatch-enumeration-seconds` (886s, unchanged since 2026-10-05T15:49Z). The value is only updated after enumeration runs; when the admission gate skips enumeration because of that estimate, the estimate never decays, a self-sustaining starvation loop (same class as GH#33710 reset ratchet).

Observability gap: `append_cycle_index` (`pulse-wrapper.sh:1766`) only records cycles that reach the end, and the duration excludes cache prime, so `pulse-cycle-index.jsonl` has 2 records since Oct 3 and cannot show this starvation.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` / `pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh`: do not charge cache-prime time to the dispatch cycle budget (rebase `PULSE_START_EPOCH` after prime, or bound prime to a share of the cycle), and keep lock/watchdog semantics intact.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh`: decay the persisted enumeration estimate toward the 300s floor when admission skips enumeration because of it, so a stale high value cannot block indefinitely.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-logging.sh`: record cycle outcome/prime time so starvation is visible in the cycle index.

## Verification

- `shellcheck` on changed scripts; existing `tests/test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh`, `tests/test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh`, `tests/test-pulse-dispatch-engine-stage-wiring.sh`, `tests/test-pulse-cycle-state-contract.sh` pass.
- After release + `aidevops update`: `pulse.log` shows `Dispatch_max` enumerating and launching workers; `headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl` shows new worker runs.

Related: GH#33647, GH#33560, GH#33569, GH#33710.

title: pulse: cycle index misses blocked/killed cycles and excludes pre-dispatch time, hiding dispatch starvation
body:
## What

`~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-cycle-index.jsonl` is meant to be the historical per-cycle throughput record, but it misses most cycles. It had 2 records from 2026-10-03 to 2026-10-06 while pulse cycles ran roughly hourly, and 711 records since 2026-09-01. The GH#33737 dispatch starvation (0 workers for 9h+) was therefore invisible in it and had to be reconstructed from `pulse.log`, `pulse-stage-timings.log` and `headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl`.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `jq -sc '[.[] | select(.ts >= "2026-10-03")] | length' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-cycle-index.jsonl`

**Actual output:** `2` (while `pulse-stage-timings.log` shows a pulse cycle roughly every 65 minutes over the same window)

**Expected:** one record per pulse cycle, including blocked or early-return cycles.

## Root cause

- `append_cycle_index` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-logging.sh:592`) is only called at `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` just before the LLM supervisor step. Cycles that return early (blocked, stop flag, dedup), are killed by the watchdog, or lose the lock never write a record.
- `duration_s` uses `_cycle_start_epoch`, which is set after cache prime and fix-the-fixer stages, so the recorded duration excludes pre-dispatch overhead (`PULSE_START_EPOCH` is the real cycle start).
- The record has no outcome/blocker field, so "0 dispatched" cannot be distinguished between empty queue, budget skip and blocked cycle.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-logging.sh` `append_cycle_index`: add `outcome` (progressed/idle/blocked/partial), `blocker` (from cycle state), `wall_s` (from `PULSE_START_EPOCH`), and `dispatch_budget_skips` (delta of `pulse_dispatch_cycle_budget_skipped` stat). Keep existing fields for compatibility.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`: write the index once per cycle from the terminal path (the same place `_pulse_cycle_state_write_terminal_if_current` / `_pulse_efficiency_cycle_finish` run, including the EXIT cleanup) with an idempotence guard so normal cycles are not double-counted.
- `.agents/reference/observability.md`: document the fields and the 10,000-line retention (`PULSE_CYCLE_INDEX_MAX_LINES`).

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-logging.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/observability.md`

## Verification

- `shellcheck` on changed files; existing `tests/test-pulse-cycle-state-contract.sh` and `tests/test-pulse-wrapper-characterization.sh` pass.
- After deploy: a blocked or early-return cycle appends exactly one record with `outcome` and `blocker`; a normal cycle still appends exactly one.

Related: GH#33737.
