title: pulse: runner_capability_unmet candidates retried every pass, misreported as no_recent_log_evidence, and can use up the first-wave fill
body:
## What

Candidates deferred pre-launch with `runner_capability_unmet` are retried on every dispatch pass with no backoff and are misreported as `no_recent_log_evidence`. In the live pulse, marcusquinn/cloudron-netbird-app #158 and #165 have been deferred this way on every pass for days (dozens of attempts at 6–68s each), and they were the only candidates the first-wave early dispatch reached in the latest cycles, so that wave launched 0 workers.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `rg -c "deferred: runner_capability_unmet" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` and `rg "pre-launch failure stage=dispatch_with_dedup rc=1 reason=no_recent_log_evidence" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`

**Actual output:** dozens of `[dispatch_with_dedup] #158 deferred: runner_capability_unmet` lines, each followed by `Dispatch_max: #158 (marcusquinn/cloudron-netbird-app) pre-launch failure stage=dispatch_with_dedup rc=1 reason=no_recent_log_evidence`.

**Expected:** the reason is recorded as `runner_capability_unmet`, and an unchanged unmet requirement is not re-probed on every pass (it should be cooled down until the issue body/labels or runner capability change).

## Root cause (from code reading)

- `.agents/scripts/runner-capability-helper.sh:28,32` logs `[dispatch_with_dedup] #N deferred: ...` without the repo slug, so `_dispatch_candidate_recent_lines` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh` does not match it and `_dispatch_candidate_failure_reason` falls back to `no_recent_log_evidence` (`.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh:1342`).
- `runner_capability_unmet` is missing from the low-cardinality reason allowlist at `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh:227`.
- No candidate-level cooldown exists for this deferral, so a runner that can never satisfy the requirement keeps paying for the probe and can use up the first-wave fill (`_preflight_early_dispatch`, `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-preflight-lib.sh:461`).

## How

- Emit the deferral as a structured `DISPATCH_BLOCK_REASON reason=runner_capability_unmet` line that includes the repo slug, and add the token to the allowlist so it is classified and counted.
- Add a per-candidate cooldown keyed on repo/issue plus a fingerprint of the requirement inputs (dispatch-class labels + `requires-secrets:` line), so unchanged unmet candidates are skipped at enumeration until the fingerprint changes or a bounded TTL (for example 6h) expires. Keep the fresh final gate unchanged (GH#33399).
- The first-wave fill should not count a repo whose candidates are all cooled down as its "first nonempty" repo.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/runner-capability-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`

### Scope note (worker integration recovery)

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`: `build_ranked_dispatch_candidates_json` is the enumeration point and owns the first-wave "first nonempty repo" break (GH#33647). The cooldown filter must run there, before the empty check, so a repo whose candidates are all cooled down is not counted as nonempty. One call to a filter defined in `pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh`.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh`: `_dispatch_record_and_cache_block` is the only caller of `_dispatch_record_nonzero_dispatch_result` holding the candidate JSON (labels/updatedAt) needed to record the fingerprint; it passes that JSON through as an optional argument.
- The enumeration snapshot has no issue body, so the fingerprint uses dispatch-class labels + the issue `updatedAt` (any body edit changes it, matching the existing negative-cache convention) + the repo's `.aidevops.json` requirement map.

## Verification

- `shellcheck` on changed files; existing `tests/test-runner-capability.sh`, `tests/test-dispatch-candidate-failure-reasons.sh`, `tests/test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh`, `tests/test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh` pass.
- Live: `pulse.log` shows `reason=runner_capability_unmet` instead of `no_recent_log_evidence`, and #158/#165 are not attempted again within the cooldown.

Related: GH#33737.

title: fix: reap orphaned Playwright/dev web servers that outlive their bounded operation
body:
## Observed

On a shared Linux runner host (24 vCPU, 125 GiB), a Playwright `webServer` process tree outlived its OpenCode session by 6 days:

- `/bin/sh -c pnpm dev` → `pnpm dev` → `sh -c next dev --webpack --port ${WEB_PORT:-3100}` → `next-server`, reparented to PID 1, own session/process group.
- stdin/stdout/stderr were sockets to the long-gone parent (no reader).
- Environment carried `PLAYWRIGHT_TEST`, `BASE_URL`, `AIDEVOPS_OPERATION_ID`, `OPENCODE_PID`, i.e. it was started by an aidevops bounded operation running Playwright in an interactive OpenCode session.
- `next-server` RSS grew to ~34 GiB and used ~120% CPU while the host was CPU-saturated by pulse workers. No connections to its port; no Playwright run alive.
- Terminating the process group freed 35 GiB (RAM used 94 → 59 GiB, swap 21 → 16 GiB). One child ignored SIGTERM and needed SIGKILL.

`process-guard-helper.sh` only classifies stale `playwright test --list` processes (`_classify_stale_playwright_list`); `orphan-worker-reaper.sh` only handles headless workers with no dispatch ledger. Nothing reaps orphaned test web servers.

## Proposed fix

1. `aidevops_bounded_operation` (OpenCode plugin) — on terminal state/cancel/expiry, kill any surviving descendants that carry its `AIDEVOPS_OPERATION_ID` even if they called `setsid` (scan `/proc/*/environ` on Linux; `ps -E`/`pgrep` fallback on macOS).
2. `.agents/scripts/process-guard-helper.sh` — add a classifier for orphaned dev/test servers: PPID 1, environment contains `PLAYWRIGHT_TEST` or `AIDEVOPS_OPERATION_ID` whose operation is no longer live, no established connections on its listening port, age > configurable limit (default 2h). Kill the whole process group, TERM then KILL. Report-only mode first if preferred.
3. Log each reap with pid/pgid/port/RSS.

Reference pattern: `_classify_stale_playwright_list` and `_has_aidevops_playwright_evidence` in `.agents/scripts/process-guard-helper.sh`.

## Verification

- Start a Playwright run with `webServer` inside a bounded operation, cancel it, confirm no `next`/`pnpm dev` descendants survive.
- Simulate an orphan (`setsid` + `PLAYWRIGHT_TEST=1` + idle port, aged via configurable limit) and confirm the guard reaps it, while a server with an established connection or a live operation ID is left alone.
- ShellCheck clean.

title: perf: setup_tabby spends 30-150s per setup on guarded git calls for worktree detection
body:
## What

`setup_tabby` costs 28–67s on every setup/update run (156s when it overlaps another setup), measured over recent rows of `~/.aidevops/logs/setup-stage-timings.log` (308 recorded runs). Most of the time goes to worktree detection in `.agents/scripts/tabby-profile-sync.py`, which shells out to `git rev-parse --git-dir` and `--git-common-dir` for every registered repo. With `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts` on PATH, `git` resolves to the canonical-git-command guard shim (`.agents/scripts/git`), which costs about 0.24s per call versus 0.02s for `/usr/bin/git`.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `rg "setup_tabby\t[0-9]" ~/.aidevops/logs/setup-stage-timings.log | tail -10`

**Actual output:** durations of 27.70, 27.86, 28.91, 36.69, 67.15, 67.52 and 156.36 seconds (2026-10-06).

**Expected:** a few seconds. With 85 registered repos, 2 calls × 85 × ~0.22s of shim overhead ≈ 37s, which matches the baseline.

Per-call timing: `/usr/bin/time -p ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/git -C <repo> rev-parse --git-common-dir` → real 0.24; `/usr/bin/time -p /usr/bin/git -C <repo> rev-parse --git-common-dir` → real 0.02.

## How

Detect linked worktrees from the filesystem in the worktree-detection function (the `_run_git(repo_path, "rev-parse", ...)` pair around `.agents/scripts/tabby-profile-sync.py:91-129`), without subprocesses:

- `<path>/.git` is a directory → main checkout, not a worktree.
- `<path>/.git` is a file whose `gitdir:` target resolves to a path containing a `/worktrees/<name>` segment under a `.git` directory → linked worktree.
- `gitdir:` pointing into `.git/modules/` (submodule) or anything unreadable → not a worktree (keep the current "never exclude normal repos" contract).

Do not bypass or modify the git shim; it is a deliberate safety guard. Keep a git fallback only if the filesystem result is ambiguous.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tabby-profile-sync.py`

## Verification

- Existing Tabby sync tests pass: `rg -l "tabby-profile-sync" .agents/scripts/tests` and run each.
- `python3 .agents/scripts/tabby-profile-sync.py --repos-json ~/.config/aidevops/repos.json --tabby-config <copy of config.yaml>` produces the same profiles as before on a copy of the live config. Use a temporary copy, never the live file.
- After deploy, the next `setup_tabby` row in `setup-stage-timings.log` is under 10s.

title: Pulse CPU gate closes on I/O-inflated macOS load average despite ~40% idle CPU
body:
## What

Pulse CPU admission (`_pulse_cpu_pressure`) closes on a macOS one-minute load average that is inflated by I/O-blocked threads, even when the CPU has substantial idle headroom. Corroborate the load signal with measured CPU idle before closing admission, so the gate keeps the #33578 intent: full CPU use is admitted and only severe run-queue thrash closes it.

## Observed (16-core Mac, v3.38.14, 2026-10-06 ~02:50–02:55Z)

- `pulse.log`: `max workers: 0, load=131.49/16 max_load_per_core=4 cpu_gate=closed` and `Dispatch_capacity: ... cpu_gate=closed active_workers=2 admission=closed`, with 15+ available auto-dispatch candidates queued. `cpu_gate=closed` appears 6 times in the current log.
- Same minute: `vm.loadavg` = `{ 128.59 129.12 107.44 }` while `top -l 2 -s 3 -n 0` reported `CPU usage: 42.75% user, 15.61% sys, 41.62% idle`.
- The load came from disk-bound background work: Backblaze `bztransmit -updatebackupstats` (31 min, 10 GB RSS), `fseventsd` (peaking at 201% CPU), and `iostat` showing about 30k tps on `disk0`. Darwin's load average counts threads in uninterruptible I/O wait, so load/core of 8 did not mean CPU oversubscription.
- Two minutes earlier, under real pressure (`41% sys, 17% idle`), closing would have been reasonable, so a corroborated gate still protects against thrash.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-capacity.sh:279-300` (`_pulse_cpu_pressure`): keep the load/core threshold as a pre-filter, but close only when a short CPU-idle sample also shows saturation (for example idle below a configurable `orchestration.min_cpu_idle_pct`, default ~10). On Darwin, sample with `top -l 2 -s 1 -n 0` (second sample) or `iostat -c 2 -w 1`; on Linux, two `/proc/stat` reads. If the sample is unavailable, fall back to today's load-only behaviour.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-capacity.sh:320-325` and `.agents/scripts/pulse-capacity-alloc.sh:294-304`: add the idle percentage to the existing `Dispatch_capacity` / `Available RAM` log lines so closures are diagnosable.
- Keep the output contract `"<load> <cores> <gate> <threshold>"` stable for existing callers. Append the new field only if all callers tolerate it.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-capacity.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-capacity-alloc.sh`

## Acceptance

- [ ] With load/core above the threshold and measured idle at or above the configured minimum, the gate stays `open` and logs both values.
- [ ] With load/core above the threshold and idle below the minimum, the gate closes as today.
- [ ] With CPU-idle telemetry unavailable, behaviour is unchanged.
- [ ] ShellCheck clean; Bash 3.2 compatible; explicit `return 0`/`return 1`.

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-capacity.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-capacity-alloc.sh
rg -a "cpu_gate=" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | tail -5   # after deploy, on a host with background disk load
```

title: full-loop merge: Git 2.44 gate blocks every TODO.md merge on Ubuntu 24.04 LTS (distro Git 2.43)
body:
## What happened

In v3.38.13, `full-loop-helper.sh merge` blocked the merge of every PR that changes `TODO.md` on Ubuntu 24.04 LTS:

```
Merge blocked: native Git 2.43.0 at /usr/bin/git predates GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH (Git 2.44+ required for prospective TODO validation); set AIDEVOPS_REAL_GIT_BIN to a newer Git (for example Homebrew git)
```

Ubuntu 24.04 (noble) ships Git `1:2.43.0-1ubuntu7.3` as its newest version (noble-updates/noble-security). So on the current Ubuntu LTS, every interactive full-loop merge that touches `TODO.md` stops until the user installs a newer Git with sudo (here: the git-core PPA, 2.55.0). v3.38.11 had the guard but no version gate. The update arrived during a live session, so a merge that had just worked started failing.

## Where

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`, `_merge_guard_prospective_todo`: version gate added near the `git_major`/`git_minor` comparison (`git_minor < 44`).
- `_merge_run_config_isolated_git` already sets `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` and comments that pre-2.44 Git "must still fail instead of waiting on a credential prompt", so a non-blocking fallback looks intended.

## Suggested fix (pick one)

1. On Git < 2.44, run prospective TODO validation in an object store that has no promisor remote (or with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` plus the existing bounded timeouts). Treat a missing object as indeterminate instead of rejecting the Git version outright.
2. Or keep the gate but detect it in `setup.sh` / `aidevops status`. Tell the user before a merge on Debian/Ubuntu LTS, with a distro-specific fix (`ppa:git-core/ppa` on Ubuntu) instead of the Homebrew hint.

## Verification

- On Ubuntu 24.04 with distro Git 2.43, `full-loop-helper.sh merge <PR>` for a PR that changes `TODO.md` either merges with validation intact or fails before the merge attempt with a distro-correct fix.
- Existing `tests/test-full-loop-merge-planning.sh` prospective TODO cases still pass.

title: pulse: CPU gate closes admission on load average while cores are idle; admit up to idle-core headroom
body:
## What

The Pulse CPU admission gate (`_pulse_cpu_pressure`, `.agents/scripts/pulse-capacity.sh:279-300`, from #33570) closes on the one-minute load average alone. On macOS, load average also counts threads blocked on I/O and locks, so it can be far above the threshold while CPU cores are idle. When that happens the gate sets max workers to 0 and stops all new launches.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command:** `rg "cpu_gate=closed" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` and `top -l 2 -n 0 -s 2 | rg "CPU usage|Load Avg"` at the same time.

**Actual output (2026-10-06):** `Available RAM: 44866MB ... max workers: 0, load=131.49/16 max_load_per_core=4 cpu_gate=closed` and `Dispatch_max skipped: no available worker slots (max=0, active=2, available=0)`, while `top` reported `Load Avg: 127.16` with `CPU usage: 42.62% user, 20.19% sys, 37.18% idle`. macOS memory pressure was normal (level 1, 70% free). The load came from a Backblaze rescan plus Brave renderers after setup rewrote ~8k files.

**Expected:** while CPU cores are measurably idle, new workers are still admitted, up to the idle-core headroom.

## How

- When load/core is above `max_load_per_core`, sample CPU idle once (macOS `iostat -n 0 -c 2 -w 1`, about 1s wall and negligible CPU; Linux `/proc/stat` delta, idle only and not iowait). If idle is at least `orchestration.cpu_idle_admit_percent` (default 25, 0 disables), report the gate as `open_idle` instead of `closed`.
- In `pulse_apply_provider_load_capacity_cap`, cap total workers in `open_idle` to `active + floor(cores × idle% / 100)` (at least 1 new), so each pass only uses idle cores and re-samples next pass.
- Keep `closed` when idle is below the threshold or the sample is unavailable.
- Add the config key to the defaults, the schema, the `config-helper.sh` env mapping and `reference/configuration.md`.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-capacity-alloc.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-config.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/config-helper.sh`

## Verification

title: feat(observability): lossless bounded retention for worker metrics ledgers and pulse cycle index
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `metrics jsonl rotation retention headless-runtime-metrics` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: 5 commits in the last 48h touch `pulse-logging.sh`/`pulse-wrapper-config.sh` (GH#33739 cycle index, GH#33754 CPU admission, GH#33737, GH#33578, GH#33570); 0 open PRs touch the retention paths below
- [x] File refs verified: 9 refs checked, all present at `main` `7a4aeb9496`
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — design decisions resolved below; worker implements known pattern with local error handling
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — the brief carries the decided design; no code was drafted

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-06
- **Created by:** ai-interactive (maintainer-approved filing)
- **Conversation context:** During the GH#33647/GH#33754 throughput work the maintainer asked whether aidevops keeps the data needed for future throughput evaluation and optimisation. Pulse logs have hot/cold rotation, but the worker metrics ledgers do not, and the cycle index discards its oldest rows.

## What

Bounded, lossless retention for the three throughput ledgers in `~/.aidevops/logs/`:

1. `headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl` (per-worker outcomes) and `resource-metrics.jsonl` (per-worker CPU/RSS) get size-capped hot files. Rotated segments are gzip-archived under `~/.aidevops/logs/metrics-archive/`, and the archive has its own size cap.
2. `pulse-cycle-index.jsonl` keeps its 10,000-line hot cap. Lines pruned from the head are archived as gzip instead of discarded.
3. Storage inventory and observability docs describe the retention, and how to read archives (`gzip -dc ... | jq`).

## Why

- Both metrics files grow without bound. Today they are 7.2 MB (12,906 rows since 2026-03-31) and 3.5 MB (10,469 rows since 2026-05-02), roughly 1.2 MB and 0.7 MB per month. That is not urgent, but more workers mean faster growth. At least 10 readers parse these files in full on hot paths: `pulse-capacity.sh:137`, `pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh:747`, `pulse-dispatch-current-state-guardrails.sh:224`, `dispatch-backoff-helper.sh`, `worker-activity-helper.sh`, `pulse-diagnose-helper.sh`, `stats-health-dashboard-data.sh`, `orchestration-efficiency-collector.sh`, `pulse-current-state.py` and `model-replay-evidence.mjs`. Per-cycle read cost scales with file size.
- `append_cycle_index` (`pulse-logging.sh:765-785`) runs `tail -n 10000` and drops older cycles permanently, about 14 days of history. Long-horizon throughput evaluation (the maintainer's stated aim) needs those rows.
- `storage-inventory-helper.sh:776-789` inventories pulse logs but none of these three ledgers, so storage reports cannot show their retention policy.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** Reuses the verified `rotate_pulse_log`/`_prune_cold_archive` pattern with every retention decision fixed below. The worker writes local code and error handling. No trust boundary is involved, and the dispatch-path file `headless-runtime-lib.sh` stays untouched.

## How (Approach)

### Worker Quick-Start

```bash
# Reference pattern (hot/cold rotation, archive prune):
rg -n "^_rotate_single_log|^_prune_cold_archive|^rotate_pulse_log|^append_cycle_index" .agents/scripts/pulse-logging.sh
# Writers are append-per-write (rename-safe; no long-lived fds):
#   headless-runtime-lib.sh append_runtime_metric: python open(path, 'a') per record
#   resource-metrics-helper.sh:328: printf ... >>"$out_file" once per worker
# Config globals live beside PULSE_LOG_* in pulse-wrapper-config.sh:473-477
```

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-logging.sh` — add `_rotate_metrics_jsonl` + `_prune_metrics_archive`; call from `rotate_pulse_log`; extract the cycle-index prune into `_prune_cycle_index` and archive the pruned head
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-config.sh:473-477` — new config globals
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/storage-inventory-helper.sh:782-785` — records for the three ledgers + `metrics-archive`
- `EDIT: .agents/reference/observability.md:492` — retention + archive-read recipe
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-cycle-state-contract.sh` — only if needed to assert archive-on-prune (it already sets `PULSE_CYCLE_INDEX_MAX_LINES=100` at line 49)

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** the readers listed under Why (e.g. `pulse-capacity.sh:137`, `worker-activity-helper.sh`, `dispatch-backoff-helper.sh`) read only the hot file. With a 25 MiB hot cap (about 20 months at the current rate) their windows (hours to days) are unaffected. No reader change.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `append_runtime_metric` (`headless-runtime-lib.sh:408`), `resource-metrics-helper.sh:328` via `headless-runtime-attempt.sh:332`, and `append_cycle_index` (`pulse-logging.sh:699`). Only the Pulse-side rotation is new; writers stay unchanged.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `test-pulse-cycle-state-contract.sh`, `test-pulse-wrapper-characterization.sh` (lists `rotate_pulse_log`), and `test-storage-inventory-helper.sh`.
- **Schemas/config:** shell env globals only. Not added to `aidevops.defaults.jsonc`, consistent with the existing `PULSE_LOG_*` caps, which are env-only.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** deployed by `setup.sh` to `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/`; no generated files.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A because no stored format changes. The first cycle after deploy rotates `headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl`/`resource-metrics.jsonl` only if already over the cap; today's files (7.2 MB / 3.5 MB) are under it.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert the PR. Archives remain as plain `.jsonl.gz` and are readable without aidevops.

### Implementation Steps

1. **Config** (`pulse-wrapper-config.sh`, beside `PULSE_CYCLE_INDEX_MAX_LINES`):

   ```bash
   PULSE_METRICS_ARCHIVE_DIR="${PULSE_METRICS_ARCHIVE_DIR:-${HOME}/.aidevops/logs/metrics-archive}"
   PULSE_METRICS_HOT_MAX_BYTES="${PULSE_METRICS_HOT_MAX_BYTES:-26214400}"   # 25 MiB per ledger hot file
   PULSE_METRICS_COLD_MAX_BYTES="${PULSE_METRICS_COLD_MAX_BYTES:-524288000}" # 500 MiB combined archive cap
   ```

2. **`_rotate_metrics_jsonl <file> <base>`**: rotate by rename, not by gzip-then-truncate. `_rotate_single_log` truncates after gzip, which loses rows appended between the two steps.
   - Return 0 if the file is missing or under `PULSE_METRICS_HOT_MAX_BYTES` (`_file_size_bytes`).
   - `mv` the file to a staged name in the **same directory** (`.${base}-rotating-${ts}-$$`) so the rename is atomic. The next writer append recreates the hot file.
   - `gzip -c staged > mktemp-in-archive-dir`, then `mv` to `${base}-${ts}.jsonl.gz`. If that name already exists, append `-$$`. Then `rm` the staged file.
   - On gzip failure, move the staged file uncompressed into the archive dir and log it. Never delete data on a failure path.
   - Log every action to `$WRAPPER_LOGFILE`; always `return 0`.

3. **`_prune_metrics_archive`**: copy `_prune_cold_archive`, but glob `"${PULSE_METRICS_ARCHIVE_DIR}"/*.jsonl*` and cap at `PULSE_METRICS_COLD_MAX_BYTES`. Delete the oldest first by timestamped name, sorting on the timestamp part because several base names share the directory. Bash 3.2: no `mapfile`.

4. **Wire into `rotate_pulse_log`** (currently 41 lines), after the wrapper-log block:

   ```bash
   mkdir -p "$PULSE_METRICS_ARCHIVE_DIR" 2>/dev/null || true
   _rotate_metrics_jsonl "${AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS_METRICS_FILE:-${HOME}/.aidevops/logs/headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl}" "headless-runtime-metrics"
   _rotate_metrics_jsonl "${AIDEVOPS_RESOURCE_METRICS_FILE:-${HOME}/.aidevops/logs/resource-metrics.jsonl}" "resource-metrics"
   _prune_metrics_archive
   ```

5. **Cycle index**: first extract lines 765-785 of `append_cycle_index` into `_prune_cycle_index` (see Complexity Impact). Inside it, before the `tail -n` rewrite, run `head -n "$excess" "$PULSE_CYCLE_INDEX_FILE" | gzip -c` into a mktemp in the archive dir, then `mv` it to `pulse-cycle-index-${ts}.jsonl.gz`. If archiving fails, **skip the prune this cycle** (log it) rather than discard rows. The next cycle retries, and the hot file only grows by one line per cycle in the meantime. Each prune removes only one or two lines, so add hysteresis: prune only when `line_count > MAX + 500`, trimming back to `MAX`, to avoid one tiny archive per cycle.

6. **Storage inventory**: add `_storage_emit_record` lines modelled on `storage-inventory-helper.sh:782-785` for `headless-runtime-metrics`, `resource-metrics`, `pulse-cycle-index` (active class; "25 MiB active-file cap with gzip archive rotation", or "10,000-line hot cap; pruned head archived") and `metrics-archive` (archive; "500 MiB combined cap; oldest first"). The disposition text should read "Use pulse-owned rotate_pulse_log; never unlink the active file".

7. **Docs**: in `observability.md:492`, replace "Retention keeps the newest 10,000 lines" with the archive behaviour. Add one line covering both metrics ledgers and an archive-read recipe: `gzip -dc ~/.aidevops/logs/metrics-archive/headless-runtime-metrics-*.jsonl.gz | jq -c ...`.

8. Run `shellcheck` on changed scripts, then the verification below.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** `rotate_pulse_log` runs under the Pulse instance lock (single rotator). Workers append concurrently. Rename-then-gzip is safe because every writer opens per append: a row lands either in the staged file, which gets archived, or in the new hot file. Do **not** use truncate, and do not rotate from the writers.
- **Migration/rollback:** none needed. Old code ignores the archive dir, and reverting leaves the archives readable.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** readers only see the hot file. Any analysis that needs history before rotation must read the archives explicitly (document this; no reader changes).
- **Idempotency/retry:** rotation triggers only above the cap. Archive names carry a UTC timestamp, plus `$$` on collision. A leftover `.*-rotating-*` file from a crash should be archived on the next run: glob for it at the start of `_rotate_metrics_jsonl`.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** every failure path keeps the data, either as the staged file or as an uncompressed archive, and logs to `$WRAPPER_LOGFILE`. The Pulse cycle is never blocked: all helpers return 0.

### Complexity Impact

- **Target function:** `append_cycle_index` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-logging.sh` (lines 699-788)
- **Current line count:** 90 lines (threshold 100)
- **Estimated growth:** +12 lines
- **Projected post-change:** 102 lines without extraction
- **Action required:** extract helpers first. Move lines 765-785 into `_prune_cycle_index` (about 30 lines with archiving) so `append_cycle_index` drops to about 70. `rotate_pulse_log` goes from 41 to about 46: no action. (GH#33754 hit this exact gate.)

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-logging.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-config.sh .agents/scripts/storage-inventory-helper.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-cycle-state-contract.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-characterization.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-storage-inventory-helper.sh
# Runtime proof in a sandbox HOME: create a >cap metrics file with PULSE_METRICS_HOT_MAX_BYTES=1024,
# source pulse-wrapper-config.sh + pulse-logging.sh, call rotate_pulse_log, then assert:
#   hot file absent or small; one *.jsonl.gz in metrics-archive; gzip -dc | wc -l == original row count
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Surface mapping:** shellcheck/linters cover the changed scripts. The cycle-state contract covers `append_cycle_index`/`_prune_cycle_index`, the characterization test covers the `rotate_pulse_log` symbol, the storage test covers the inventory records, and the sandbox run covers the lossless-rotation criterion.
- **Broad verification trigger:** not required; there are no shared contracts or release infrastructure changes.

### Recoverability Checkpoint

- [ ] Focused functional verification passes: the sandbox rotation run plus `test-pulse-cycle-state-contract.sh`
- [ ] WIP commit created before broad gates: `wip: metrics ledger rotation`
- [ ] Evidence-triggered broad verification: not required (see above)

### Scope Boundaries

**Hard boundaries:** do not modify `headless-runtime-lib.sh` (dispatch-path file) or any reader; do not change the `pulse.log`/`pulse-archive` caps; do not delete or rewrite existing metric rows. Two historical future-dated fixture rows (`"ts":4102444800`, lines 1-2 of the live `headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl`) are out of scope; leave them.

**AI brief owner:** interactive maintainer session that filed this issue.

**Recovery:** preserve the current PR and use the structured runtime request and Pulse intake in `reference/worker-discipline.md` when local recovery is unsafe.

### Files Scope

Integration recovery: the existing storage inventory test hard-codes 16 stores at lines 94 and 112; the four authorized ledger/archive records require 20. Update only those expectations and assert the new retention records; verify with bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-storage-inventory-helper.sh. Trusted brief author has admin access; collision discovery found only this PR.

- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-storage-inventory-helper.sh`

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-logging.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-config.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/storage-inventory-helper.sh`
- `.agents/reference/observability.md`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-cycle-state-contract.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] When a metrics ledger exceeds `PULSE_METRICS_HOT_MAX_BYTES`, `rotate_pulse_log` moves it into `metrics-archive/<base>-<UTC>.jsonl.gz`, and the decompressed archive contains every original row (lossless).

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "_rotate_metrics_jsonl"
    path: ".agents/scripts/pulse-logging.sh"
  ```

- [ ] Cycle-index rows beyond the hot cap are archived to `metrics-archive/pulse-cycle-index-<UTC>.jsonl.gz` before removal; if archiving fails, no rows are removed that cycle.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "_prune_cycle_index"
    path: ".agents/scripts/pulse-logging.sh"
  ```

- [ ] Negative: rotation never truncates an active metrics ledger in place (no `: >` / `>` truncation of the metrics files), and `headless-runtime-lib.sh` is unchanged.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "git diff --quiet origin/main -- .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh"
  ```

- [ ] `metrics-archive` stays within `PULSE_METRICS_COLD_MAX_BYTES`, pruning the oldest archives first.
- [ ] `storage-inventory-helper.sh` reports the three ledgers and `metrics-archive` with their retention policy.
- [ ] `observability.md` documents retention and the archive-read recipe.
- [ ] Shellcheck is clean; `append_cycle_index` stays under 100 lines; the existing tests listed above pass.

## Context & Decisions

- Rename-based rotation was chosen over the existing gzip-then-truncate because metric rows are evidence, and truncation drops rows appended during compression. Writers open the file per append, so a rename is safe.
- Rotation is Pulse-owned (`rotate_pulse_log` is already called every cycle under the instance lock), not writer-owned. This keeps the dispatch-path file `headless-runtime-lib.sh` out of scope and avoids concurrent rotators.
- The 25 MiB hot cap keeps about 20 months of rows at current volume, so no reader windows change. The 500 MiB cold cap is half the pulse-log cold cap because these ledgers compress well and are small.
- Non-goals: compaction/aggregation, a query CLI over archives, and changing reader time windows.

## Relevant Files

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-logging.sh:445` `_rotate_single_log`, `:485` `_prune_cold_archive`, `:530` `rotate_pulse_log`, `:699` `append_cycle_index`: reference pattern and targets
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-config.sh:466-477`: retention config globals
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh:408`: `append_runtime_metric` writer (read-only reference)
- `.agents/scripts/resource-metrics-helper.sh:328`: resource writer (read-only reference)
- `.agents/scripts/storage-inventory-helper.sh:782-785`: inventory record pattern
- `.agents/reference/observability.md:492`: cycle-index retention doc

## Estimate Breakdown

| Phase | Time | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| Research/read | 15m | `pulse-logging.sh` 430-790, inventory 770-790 |
| Implementation | 1h | 3 helpers, wiring, config, inventory, docs |
| Verification | 30m | sandbox rotation, 3 existing tests, shellcheck |
| **Total** | **~1h45m** | |

title: Pulse main dispatch skipped every cycle: in-cycle merge pass overruns its budget and GH#33569 skip never applies to busy repos
body:
## What

Main `dispatch_max` is skipped in consecutive Pulse cycles because pre-dispatch stages consume the cycle wall-clock budget. The in-cycle deterministic merge pass overruns its 300s graceful budget (GH#33569) to about 580s, and the GH#33569 unchanged-PR skip never applies to the repos that cost the most. Only narrow refill passes then run, with 1–2 candidates each, while 19 slots stay free and actionable backlog exists.

## Observed (16-core Mac, v3.38.16, 2026-10-06 03:00–03:57Z, CPU gate open)

- `pulse.log`: `Dispatch_max skipped before candidate enumeration: cycle wall-clock budget below dispatch reserve` at lines 288054, 289220, 290588 and 291051 (remaining 504–757s against floor 600s plus enumeration 300–886s). Refill passes then logged `Dispatch_max: available=19, candidates=1` and `processed=1/1`/`2/2`.
- In-cycle stage costs before the skip at line 291051: `deterministic_merge_pass timing: total_s=583` (graceful budget 300s, `PULSE_MERGE_IN_CYCLE_BUDGET_SECONDS` default), `fix_the_fixer_detector (0, 208s)`, then a second merge pass `total_s=296` and `dispatch_candidate_115 (0, 221s)`. `preflight_cleanup_and_ledger` takes 83–93s per cycle.
- Per-repo merge-pass costs: `marcusquinn/aidevops` 290–315s for 6–7 PRs (`slowest_pr=#33686` at 74–100s); a private app repo (`<busy-private-repo>`) 129–179s for 10–11 PRs. A single slow PR runs past the graceful deadline because the deadline is only checked between PRs or repos.
- The GH#33569 skip has never fired here: 0 `PR set unchanged` lines in any log. A read-only probe calling `_pmu_should_skip_repo` with `PULSE_MERGE_UNCHANGED_SKIP=1` shows the mechanism works for a quiet repo (`<quiet-private-repo>`: streak 59, `would_skip=yes`). For the expensive repos it can't apply: `marcusquinn/aidevops`'s PR fingerprint changes every cycle (streak stays 1), and `<busy-private-repo>` has no state file at all because each pass pauses mid-repo at a cursor (`graceful time budget exhausted during enrichment … pausing at enrichment cursor`), so `_pmu_record_repo_evaluation` never records a complete from-index-0 evaluation.
- The standalone `pulse-merge-routine.sh` already evaluates every repo each pass, so the in-cycle pass is defence-in-depth (per its GH#33569 comment) yet still costs about 580s per cycle.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh:1132-1144`: when the standalone merge routine is installed and healthy, make the in-cycle pass skip entirely, or cap it at a small share such as 60–120s, so dispatch keeps its reserve. Keep it as a fallback only when the routine is absent or stale.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-pass.sh` (`_pmp_process_merge_repo_for_pass`, from line 810) and `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh:714-770`: enforce the graceful deadline inside per-PR evaluation and enrichment, not only between PRs, so one slow PR cannot double the budget.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-unchanged-skip.sh:52-76`: consider fingerprinting per PR (head SHA, labels, check-state digest) instead of the whole-list `updatedAt`, and recording per-PR no-op results, so busy repos skip unchanged PRs even when one PR changed or the pass resumed from a cursor.
- Identify why `fix_the_fixer_detector` sometimes takes 208s (other cycles take 2s) and bound it below the dispatch reserve.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-pass.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-unchanged-skip.sh`

## Acceptance

- [ ] With the standalone merge routine healthy, a Pulse cycle reaches `Dispatch_max: available=N, candidates=M` with a full enumeration in consecutive cycles on a runner with 10+ open PRs across repos.
- [ ] The in-cycle merge pass never exceeds its configured budget by more than one bounded API call.
- [ ] Busy repos (PR set changing every cycle) still skip unchanged individual PRs.
- [ ] ShellCheck clean; Bash 3.2 compatible.

## Verification

```bash
rg -a -c "skipped before candidate enumeration" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log   # should stop growing
rg -a "deterministic_merge_pass timing: total_s=" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | tail -5
rg -a "PR set unchanged" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | tail -5
```

Related closed starvation fixes: #33560, #33647, #33737.

title: Merge pass drops For-#/Ref-# checkpoint PRs on conflict: no carry-forward or repair routing
body:
## What

The deterministic merge pass closes conflicting checkpoint PRs that use a non-closing `For #NNN` / `Ref #NNN` reference without carrying their diff forward or routing conflict repair. If the referenced issue is `status:blocked` (which is common for checkpoint PRs), no worker is re-dispatched, and the checkpoint evidence is effectively lost from the repo.

## Root cause

`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh:1890` `_extract_linked_issue` intentionally returns only GitHub-native closing targets (`close[sd]`, `fix(es|ed)`, `resolve[sd]`), per t2108/GH#18098. That is correct for post-merge issue closing. But `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-conflict.sh:1105` reuses it to choose the carry-forward target (`_carry_forward_pr_diff`, t2118), and `_route_pr_to_fix_worker` uses it as well. Worker checkpoint PRs use `For #NNN` by design, so they never close the issue. These paths then find no target.

## Observed (v3.38.16, 2026-10-06 ~04:02Z, private app repo)

1. A worker opened checkpoint PR `For #<issue>` (single ledger file, data-only, CLEAN, checks green).
2. A sibling split PR edited the same ledger file and merged first. Both appended to the end of the file, so the conflict was trivial.
3. Merge pass log:
   - `update-branch failed, falling through to close (t2116): merge conflict between base and head`
   - `_route_pr_to_fix_worker: PR #<pr> ... has no linked issue for conflict repair routing`
   - `Deterministic merge: closed conflicting PR #<pr> ...`
4. No `_carry_forward_pr_diff` line was logged, and the referenced issue body has no diff marker for the PR. That issue is `status:blocked` (beta auth blocker), so the closing comment's promise that "a worker will be dispatched" does not hold.
5. A maintainer recovered it by hand: merged the closed head into develop, resolved the append-only conflict and opened a replacement PR.

## How

- Add a conflict-routing resolver, e.g. `_extract_pr_work_issue` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh` beside `_extract_linked_issue`. It returns the single closing target first; otherwise a single same-repo `For #NNN` / `Ref #NNN` / title `tNNN`/`GH#NNN` target. If there are several or none, it stays ambiguous and returns empty. Do **not** change `_extract_linked_issue`; post-merge closing must still ignore `For`/`Ref`.
- Use the new resolver at `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-conflict.sh:1105` (carry-forward) and in `_route_pr_to_fix_worker`.
- When the resolved issue carries `status:blocked`, make the close comment say the diff was carried forward to the issue and that no automatic redispatch will happen. Do not say a worker will be dispatched.
- Optional: for `origin:worker` data-only PRs (only `todo/**` paths), mark the PR `needs-conflict-repair` instead of closing it, or let the conflict-repair worker attempt a union merge of append-only Markdown ledgers.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-conflict.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh`

Integration scope recovery: `_route_pr_to_fix_worker` is defined in `pulse-merge-process.sh:1448`, not the original two-file map. Add only that integration path to resolve conflict work targets before its existing routing guards; preserve all ownership and dispatch protections. No conflicting open PR was found by scoped prework discovery. Verify with ShellCheck, bash syntax checks, and existing linked-issue, carry-forward, close-wording and conflict-routing regressions.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A conflicting PR whose body contains only `For #N` has its diff carried forward to issue N before closing, with a log line saying so.
- [ ] Post-merge closing still never closes an issue referenced only by `For`/`Ref`. Existing t2108/GH#18098 behaviour is unchanged.
- [ ] The close comment does not promise redispatch when the issue is blocked.
- [ ] ShellCheck clean; Bash 3.2 compatible.

## Verification

```bash
rg -a "_carry_forward_pr_diff: appended diff from PR" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | tail -5
rg -a "no linked issue for conflict repair routing" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | tail -5   # should stop for For-# PRs
```

Related: #19142 (carry-forward), #18815 (conflict-close misfire), #19779/#19948 (rebase-or-close sweep).

title: consolidation-task: merge thread on #27171 into single spec
body:
## Consolidation target: #27171

**Parent issue:** #27171 in `marcusquinn/aidevops`
**Parent title:** file-size-debt: .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh exceeds 2000 lines
**Parent labels:** `status:available,auto-dispatch,tier:thinking,origin:worker,consolidation-in-progress,file-size-debt`

> You do **NOT** need to read #27171. Everything required is inlined below.
> Reading the parent wastes the token budget and is explicitly disallowed for this task.

## What to do

1. **Read the parent body and substantive comments inlined below.** Identify:
   - The original problem statement
   - Scope modifications added by commenters (additions, corrections, clarifications)
   - Resolved questions, rejected ideas, or superseded decisions
   - The final agreed-upon approach

2. **Compose a single coherent issue body** in the aidevops brief format (see `~/.aidevops/agents/templates/brief-template.md`):
   - `## What` — the deliverable
   - `## Why` — the problem and rationale
   - `## How` — approach with explicit file paths and line references
   - `## Acceptance Criteria` — testable checkboxes
   - `### Files Scope` — the successor's write surface, one repo-relative path per line and nothing else on the line (`- EDIT: path/to/file` or `- NEW: path/to/file`). Carry over the parent's scope when present. Read-only references belong in `## How`, not here. The pulse holds `auto-dispatch` briefs whose scope fails `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check`, so prose after a path makes the successor undispatchable.
     Preserve every wildcard scope entry verbatim from every superseded issue, including tool-generated paths such as `- NEW: todo/<area>/log/*/*/<slug>-*.jsonl`. Never invent a concrete machine, date, timestamp or filename in place of a pattern. Never change an existing `EDIT:` entry to `NEW:`.
     Check each path against the current default branch before copying its scope marker: use `git ls-files` in an up-to-date default-branch checkout or `gh api` for that branch's contents. Use `EDIT:` when the path already exists on the default branch; use `NEW:` only after confirming it is absent. A stale checkout or failed API lookup is not proof of absence.
   - **Runner prerequisites** — copy verbatim every line matching `^requires-secrets:` and its runner-prerequisite paragraph from every superseded issue. Keep all source lines (do not replace them with a summary): the runner capability gate unions comma/space-separated names across these lines. Never drop a prerequisite because this consolidation runner lacks the named secret; consolidation itself does not need those credentials.

   - `## Contributors` — a cc line @-mentioning every author from the list below

   Start the merged body with: `_Supersedes #27171 — this issue is the consolidated spec._`

3. **Validate before filing the new consolidated issue.** Save the inlined parent body verbatim to a local file, plus a separate body file for each additional superseded issue. Validate the merged body against ALL sources; a failed check stops publication and parent closure until the merged body is repaired:

```bash
python3 ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/consolidation-contract-validator.py \
  --source "<file containing the verbatim parent body>" \
  --successor "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
# Repeat --source for each additional superseded issue body.
```

The validator must pass before running the signed creation command below. It checks verbatim secret lines and prerequisite paragraphs, wildcard scope preservation, and EDIT-to-NEW regressions. Also run `pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh scope-check` on the merged body for ordinary scope syntax validation.

```bash
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/gh-write-helper.sh issue create --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --title "consolidated: <concise description derived from the merged spec>" \
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,auto-dispatch,status:available,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding all status:* labels, needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body-file "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Use the signed wrapper above rather than the raw GitHub CLI so the successor retains the managed signature and origin metadata.

**Dispatch handoff:** `auto-dispatch` and `status:available` are also mandatory. Keep exactly one `status:*` label on the successor: `status:available`, never the parent's lifecycle status. The consolidated successor marker and this explicit handoff must both be present before `_has_consolidated_label` permits implementation dispatch; the fill-floor enumerator also needs the available status.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close the parent #27171:**

```bash
gh issue comment 27171 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 27171 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 27171 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
```

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #27171 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @marcusquinn."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

title: wp-plugin-new-helper.sh create is blocked by the canonical Git guard and rejects the starter's .aidevops.json
body:
## Observed

`wp-plugin-new-helper.sh create` (aidevops v3.38.15, starter v1.0.24) cannot finish in an interactive session:

1. `_copy_starter` runs `git -C "$P_DEST" init`, then `git -C "$P_DEST" add -A`. The canonical Git guard (`canonical_git_policy.py` → `canonical_git_repository.is_canonical`) treats every primary checkout as canonical, including one created a moment ago, so `git add` is blocked: `BLOCKED by canonical Git guard: canonical worktree mutation via 'git add'`. The helper then removes the folder, so no plugin is created.
2. Even past that, `_publish` registers with `aidevops repos add --slug OWNER/SLUG --confirm REGISTER_CANONICAL_REPOSITORY`. The starter ships `.aidevops.json`, and that form fails with `The --slug bootstrap form is only valid when .aidevops.json is absent`. Plain `aidevops repos add` in the clone works.
3. Smaller: `aidevops init code-quality` in the linked worktree commits whatever is already staged. `rename-plugin.sh`'s renames were staged, so the init commit held them at 100% similarity, and the content edits stayed unstaged.

## Route that worked (no guard bypass)

1. `gh repo create OWNER/SLUG --private --template wpallstars/wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding --description …` (the starter is a template repo; check that its `main` equals the release tag with `gh api repos/…/compare/TAG...main`).
2. `git clone` from the destination's parent folder (allowed), then `aidevops repos add` inside the clone.
3. `worktree-helper.sh add chore/<slug>-identity`; in the worktree, run `scripts/rename-plugin.sh …`, `wp_plugin_quality.py strip-badges README.md`, `composer update --lock`, `aidevops init code-quality`, then commit the rest.
4. PR, then `full-loop-helper.sh merge`, which fast-forwards canonical `main`.

## Proposed fix

- `.agents/scripts/wp-plugin-new-helper.sh`: replace `_copy_starter`/`_rename`/`_publish` with the route above (template repo or a pushed orphan branch, created outside the canonical checkout). Do the rename in a linked worktree through a first PR, or push the history from a guard-allowed private temp clone, like `_is_isolated_routines_publisher` in `canonical_git_policy.py`. Do not add a general canonical-init exemption.
- Registration: use `aidevops repos add` without `--slug` when `.aidevops.json` exists.
- `.agents/tools/wordpress/wp-plugin-new.md`: update Result ("fresh history of two commits") to match.

## Verification

- `wp-plugin-new-helper.sh create --name "Guard Test" --no-github --dest <temp>` and a private GitHub run both finish under the canonical guard, with no `BLOCKED` output.
- `aidevops repos list` shows the new repo with `features: ["code-quality"]`; the new plugin's `scripts/lint.sh` passes.

title: Pulse: co-located runners on one host each claim the full machine; default load gate allows 4x oversubscription
body:
## What

When two or more aidevops runners (separate OS users, each with its own Pulse) share one host, each sizes its simultaneous workers as if it owned the whole machine. The default `orchestration.max_load_per_core` of 4.0 then lets combined load reach 4× the core count before either gate closes. The result is real CPU thrash that breaks latency-sensitive worker steps.

## Observed (v3.38.17, 2026-10-06)

- One 24-core / 128 GB Linux host runs two runners as separate users. Each Pulse logged `max workers: 12 … max_load_per_core=4.0 cpu_gate=open`, so the combined target was 24 workers and the gate threshold was load 96.
- `sar -q` showed run-queue 62–77 and load ~76 at 03:30–03:40Z. Browser-based worker steps (Playwright sign-in under a request-interception guard) timed out at 180s with no HTTP response during that window, on six unrelated issues. The same step took 4.3s on an unloaded host.
- Mitigation: per user, `aidevops config set orchestration.max_load_per_core 2` plus a per-repo `dispatch_classes` cap. Afterwards both Pulses logged `load=53.5/24 max_load_per_core=2 cpu_gate=closed cpu_idle_pct=0 … admission=closed`. The GH#33754 idle corroboration correctly kept the gate closed because idle was 0–1%.

## How

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-capacity.sh` (load gate, `_pulse_cpu_pressure`) and the worker-target computation in `.agents/scripts/pulse-capacity-alloc.sh`: detect co-located runners. For example, count distinct users running `pulse-wrapper.sh` / `headless-runtime-helper.sh` via `ps -eo user=,args=`, or use a shared host-level registry under `/tmp`/`/run` with per-user heartbeat files. Then divide the core-derived worker target by the number of active runners, unless explicitly overridden.
- Alternatively or additionally: when co-location is detected and `max_load_per_core` is unset, default it to ~2.0 instead of 4.0. Log `colocated_runners=N` in the `Dispatch_capacity` line.
- Document the shared-host case in the runner setup reference (`reference/github-self-hosted-runners.md` or the Pulse capacity docs), including where the setting lives: `~/.config/aidevops/config.jsonc` via `aidevops config set`, not `settings.json`.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-capacity.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-capacity-alloc.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/configuration.md`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-config.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-cpu-admission.sh`

Integration evidence: pulse-wrapper-config.sh resolves auto/core-derived and explicit caps into the same MAX_WORKERS_CAP variable before sourcing capacity helpers. Preserve that distinction to honor explicit overrides. Extend the existing CPU admission test to verify runner detection, shared preflight/refill limits and minimum-floor safety.

Scoped verification: shellcheck the changed shell files; bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-cpu-admission.sh; bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-min-concurrency.sh; time the live runner detector (under 100ms).

## Acceptance

- [ ] With two runner users active on one host, each Pulse logs `colocated_runners=2` and a worker target of about half its solo value, or an explicitly configured override.
- [ ] Single-runner hosts behave exactly as today (no regression to the GH#33754 full-CPU policy).
- [ ] ShellCheck clean; Bash 3.2 compatible; detection costs under 100ms per cycle.

## Verification

```bash
rg -a "Dispatch_capacity:.*colocated_runners=" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | tail -3
```

title: bug(scheduler): Linux hosts run pulse and pulse-merge from both cron and systemd timers (regression of #17695)
body:
## Problem

On a Linux host, `setup.sh`/`aidevops update` left BOTH schedulers active for the same jobs:

- crontab: `*/2 * * * * ... pulse-wrapper.sh  # aidevops: supervisor-pulse` and `* * * * * ... pulse-wrapper.sh --merge-only  # aidevops: pulse-merge (--merge-only)`
- systemd user timers: `aidevops-supervisor-pulse.timer` (OnUnitActiveSec=120) and `aidevops-pulse-merge.timer` (OnUnitActiveSec=60), both enabled and firing.

This is a regression of the dual-execution bug fixed in #17695 / #17447 (centralized Linux scheduler installation).

## Observed impact (logs in `~/.aidevops/logs/`)

- `pulse-wrapper.log`: 6735 "another instance running" lines plus repeated `Terminated` lines — every 2 min two launchers race for `pulse-wrapper.lockdir`.
- `pulse-merge.log`: continuous `merge_pass already in flight (PID …), skipping` from the second scheduler.
- `pulse-cycle-index.jsonl`: repeated `outcome: partial, blocker: interrupted` and "skipped terminal publish for cycle … because a newer cycle owns the instance lock".
- The cron-launched instance is invisible to the systemd-aware watchdog (see the companion watchdog issue), which amplifies the collision into a revive loop.

## Root cause to fix

The scheduler installer does not reconcile: when it installs/keeps systemd units it must remove the matching `# aidevops: supervisor-pulse` / `# aidevops: pulse-merge` cron entries (and vice versa). There is also no runtime guard detecting the duplicate.

## Files to inspect/modify

- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers.sh` (Linux scheduler install/reconcile; `_read_pulse_interval_seconds` lives here)
- `.agents/scripts/routine-helper.sh` (`install-systemd`, t1909)
- Whatever `aidevops update` path regenerates schedulers (see #17381)

## Acceptance

1. After `setup.sh --non-interactive` on a host with systemd user units loaded, `crontab -l` contains no pulse/pulse-merge entries; on cron-only hosts no aidevops pulse timers are enabled.
2. Reconcile runs on every update, not only first install, so already-affected hosts self-heal.
3. `aidevops status` (or doctor) reports a dual-scheduler condition explicitly.

## Verification

`crontab -l | rg 'aidevops: (supervisor-pulse|pulse-merge)'` returns nothing while `systemctl --user list-timers 'aidevops-*pulse*'` shows the timers; after 30 min `rg -c 'another instance running' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-wrapper.log` stops growing at ~30/hour.

title: bug(pulse-watchdog): revive loop — cycle-start stamp and cron-blind process discovery declare live long cycles dead
body:
## Problem

`pulse-watchdog-tick.sh` logged `pulse dead for N s (threshold 240s = interval 120 + grace 120) — reviving` 1934 times since 2026-08-24, with ages up to ~1900s, while a pulse cycle was actually alive and holding `pulse-wrapper.lockdir`. Each revive starts `aidevops-supervisor-pulse.service`, which immediately exits with "another instance running" — an endless no-op revive loop that also produces `partial/interrupted` cycles.

## Root causes (from reading the code)

1. **Liveness signal is a cycle-START stamp.** `pulse-wrapper.sh:1496` writes `pulse-wrapper-last-run.ts` when a cycle starts. Real cycles take 260–1533s (`pulse-cycle-index.jsonl`), so any healthy long cycle exceeds `interval + grace` and is declared dead. There is no heartbeat during the cycle.
2. **Process discovery misses cron-launched pulses.** `pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh` `_pulse_pids` (≈ lines 601–632) skips any PID whose parent command contains `pulse-wrapper.sh` (Layer 2 "subshell" guard). A cron launch is `/bin/sh -c '/bin/bash -lc "…/pulse-wrapper.sh"'`, so the real top-level wrapper's parent command matches and the instance is filtered out → `is-running` returns 1. (Hypothesis consistent with the logs; confirm with `pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh is-running` while a cron-started cycle holds the lock.)
3. `_systemd_pulse_alive` only checks the systemd unit, so a lock held by any other launcher is not considered.

## Fix direction

- Watchdog should treat a live `pulse-wrapper.lockdir` owner (PID alive, matching command) as alive before age checks, and/or the cycle should refresh a heartbeat stamp per stage.
- Fix `_pulse_pids` Layer 2 so a wrapper whose parent is a `-c` launcher (cron/systemd `bash -lc`) is counted as top-level.
- Revive must be idempotent: if the lock is held, do not start a new unit; log once per stale episode, not every minute.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-watchdog-tick.sh` (lines 115–166)
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh` (`_pulse_pids`, `_is_running`)
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` (stamp write ≈1465–1496; instance-lock logic)
- Existing tests to extend if needed: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-defense-restart.sh`

Related: #27174 (watchdog race, closed), companion dual-scheduler issue.

## Verification

During a cycle longer than 240s, `pulse-watchdog.log` gets no "reviving" lines and `pulse-wrapper.log` gets no "another instance running" lines caused by watchdog starts.
### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-watchdog-tick.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-defense-restart.sh`

Implementation: validate the live wrapper lock owner before timestamp-based revival, recognize shell -c launchers without counting wrapper subshells, and extend the existing isolated regression suite. No wrapper heartbeat change is needed because live ownership is authoritative regardless of cycle age.

Verification: bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-defense-restart.sh; shellcheck the three scoped files.

title: bug(recovery): maintenance fails closed silently and a stuck pending transaction blocks all later passes
body:
## Problem

`cleanup_worktrees.log` contains `[cleanup-worktrees-async] recovery maintenance failed closed; continuing` 173 times (646 more in `.log.1`) with **no reason** before or after it. Meanwhile a pending transaction under `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/.../worktree-recovery-maintenance/pending/` stayed unfinished for ~4 hours (receipt `reserved_at` 10:59Z) until a manual `worktree-recovery-maintenance-helper.sh run` completed it in 27s with rc 0.

## Root cause

`worktree-recovery-maintenance-helper.sh` `worktree_recovery_maintenance_run` (≈ lines 1536–1636) has ~15 bare `return 1` paths (jq missing, state dir, resume_pending non-2 status, store root, limits, selection, defer, diagnostics, pending dir collision, apply, finalize, lock release) that emit nothing on stderr or stdout. The caller `cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh` `_maintain_worktree_recovery` (lines 209–223) captures stdout and only logs a fixed string on failure, discarding the exit code. Failures are therefore undiagnosable, and a failed `_worktree_recovery_maintenance_resume_pending` silently blocks every later pass (it returns before new selection), so the store keeps growing.

## Fix direction

1. Every failure path emits one structured JSON line (`{"outcome":"failed","stage":"<name>","reason":"…"}`) on stdout — the caller already logs stdout on success; log it on failure too, plus the exit code.
2. Distinguish "pending transaction cannot be resumed" and make it self-healing (bounded retry, then quarantine the pending dir with a receipt) instead of blocking all future passes.
3. Caller: `printf '%s\trc=%s\t%s'` with stage/reason rather than a fixed string.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/worktree-recovery-maintenance-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/cleanup-worktrees-async-helper.sh`
- `.agents/reference/storage-lifecycle-worktree-recovery.md`

title: bug(recovery): Linux recovery store grows to 57 GB — size-unaware selection reclaims ~1 MB per pass (regression of #32832)
body:
## Problem

Linux recovery store `~/.aidevops/recovery/worktrees` reached **57 GB** (1605 archive dirs, 474 `.archive-attempt-*.json`) and grows daily (177 archives created on a single day). Archives are 300 MB–3.3 GB each (mostly `node_modules`), yet each maintenance pass reclaims ~1 MB. Regression of #32832 / #32292 (store grows unbounded).

## Evidence (maintenance plan/receipt JSON)

- `pressure_reason: "aggregate-size-unavailable"`, `store_bytes: null`, `pressure_active: true`.
- `max_scan: 50`, `max_candidates: 20`, 120s deadline with `deadline_exhausted: true`, `coverage_percent: 0`, inventory 1828.
- Each pass selects only 5–9 candidates of ~1 MB; the large archives are never reached.
- Completed receipt example: `observed_allocated_bytes: 1126400`.

## Root causes

1. Aggregate store size is never computed within the deadline, so pressure runs on a fallback signal and selection is not size-aware.
2. Selection scans in an order that favours small/cheap entries and the 120s deadline is consumed by scanning; big archives are never selected.
3. There is no age-based expiry that keeps reclaim rate ≥ creation rate; creation (per worker worktree removal) is unbounded relative to reclaim.
4. Archiving `node_modules` / reproducible dependency trees at all is the dominant cost — they are regenerable and should be excluded or pruned first (cache-prune operation exists: `WORKTREE_RECOVERY_MAINTENANCE_OPERATION_CACHE_PRUNE`).

## Fix direction

- Maintain an incremental size index (written at archive time) so `store_bytes` is always known without a full scan.
- Select by largest-reclaimable-first among eligible archives; prune dependency caches (`node_modules`, `.next`, `.turbo`, pnpm stores) inside archives before anything else.

title: bug(pulse-merge): terminal-cancelled non-required checks deadlock merge — never re-run, never routed to CI repair
body:
## Problem

PR #33686 (approved, `MERGEABLE`, review-bot gate PASS, "passed all gates") has been re-evaluated by `pulse-merge` every pass for many hours without ever merging or being repaired:

```
[pulse-merge] pre-merge snapshot: unclassified non-required check 'GH wrapper guard scan' is terminal-cancelled for PR #33686 … — merge blocked (GH#27137)
… (Planning PR Keyword Check, Shell Init Pattern Lint, Stat Portability Lint, Task-ID Collision Guard)
[pulse-merge] pre-merge snapshot: PR #33686 … not ready (active=0, blocking_failures=5, advisory_failures=0)
[pulse-wrapper] _dispatch_ci_fix_worker: PR #33686 … has no actionable failed checks with URLs — skipping CI repair routing
```

964 log references to this PR. Each evaluation costs 73–212s (`deterministic_merge_pass timing … slowest_pr=#33686:212s`), making the merge pass 150–345s and contributing to pulse cycle overruns.

## Root cause

Deadlock between two components:

1. The pre-merge snapshot (GH#27137) treats **terminal-cancelled** non-required checks as blocking failures.
2. The CI-fix router only acts on failed checks with URLs, so cancelled checks are never re-run and never routed.

Nothing re-runs cancelled workflow runs (they were cancelled by concurrency/superseding), so the PR is permanently stuck, and the merge pass has no backoff for an unchanged head SHA + unchanged check state.

## Fix direction

- On terminal-cancelled checks for the current head: re-run the cancelled workflow runs once (`gh run rerun <id>` via the wrapper), record the attempt keyed by head SHA, and re-evaluate after completion; if they cancel again, escalate once.
- Or classify cancelled checks that have a newer successful run of the same name on the same SHA as superseded (not blocking).
- Cache "not ready" verdicts by (PR, head SHA, check-state hash) so unchanged PRs are skipped cheaply on subsequent passes.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh` (pre-merge snapshot, GH#27137)
- `_dispatch_ci_fix_worker` (locate with `rg -n "_dispatch_ci_fix_worker" .agents/scripts`)
- Related closed: #28318 (historical cancelled checks in post-PR handoff), #28164 (merge throughput collapse)

## Verification

A PR whose only blockers are cancelled non-required checks gets one automatic re-run and then merges (or escalates once); `deterministic_merge_pass timing` no longer reports the same PR as slowest across consecutive passes.

title: bug(cleanup): orphan-dir cleanup retries trash-failed forever on root-owned files (no foreign-owner classification)
body:
## Problem

Orphan-dir cleanup retries the same directory forever: 254 `trash-failed` occurrences in cleanup_worktrees.log (+105 in .log.1), every cleanup pass for weeks. A Docker-created root-owned subtree prevents unprivileged cleanup.

## Root causes

1. `pulse-cleanup-worktree-removal.sh` treats `trash-failed` as transient, with no classification, retry limit, or operator surfacing.
2. Containers bind-mount worker worktrees without matching the host UID/GID.

## Authorized outcome

- Pre-check ownership without following symlinks; classify `foreign-owner` as terminal, persist once, skip silently thereafter, and surface the path and operator recovery command in `aidevops status`.
- After a bounded number of identical `trash-failed` results for a path, stop retrying and escalate once.
- Document non-root Docker for worker worktrees. Never run privileged ownership repair automatically.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup-worktree-removal.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup-fixture-orphans.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/orphan-cleanup-state.py`
- `.agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/aidevops-status-lib.sh`
- `.agents/tools/ai-assistants/headless-dispatch.md`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-cleanup-orphan-sibling-dirs.sh`

### Integration scope recovery evidence

The existing two cleanup callers need one shared persistent-state implementation. `aidevops-status-lib.sh` owns status output; cleanup modules are not sourced by that command. `headless-dispatch.md` owns worker guidance. The existing orphan-sibling runtime test exercises the affected cleanup caller. These adjacent paths implement the originally requested reporting, prevention, and verification; no authority or safety boundary changes. Author write permission, assigned in-progress issue, default branch history, issue PR/branch deduplication and scoped collision discovery were checked before editing.

## Verification

Verify retry exhaustion, successful cleanup state reset, and non-following of symlinks. Run the existing orphan-sibling runtime test, Python compilation and scoped ShellCheck.

title: t18595: fix(pulse): CI-drift update-branch loops on same failing required checks and never routes to CI fix-worker
body:
## Task


Stop Pulse from repeatedly running the CI-drift `update-branch` rebase on a PR whose
same required checks keep failing on every rebased head. After one drift rebase has
been tried for a given set of failing required contexts, the next cycle must route the
PR to the CI fix-worker (`_route_pr_to_fix_worker ... "ci"`) instead of rebasing again.

## Done when

- [ ] Positive: when a ledger entry for PR N records a prior drift rebase with the same failing required-context signature and the current head differs from the recorded prior head, `_pmp_stage_required_checks` does not call `_attempt_pr_ci_rebase_retry` and does call `_route_pr_to_fix_worker ... "ci"`; the new log line names the failing contexts.
- [ ] Regression: a PR with no ledger entry, or with a different failing-context signature, still gets exactly one drift rebase attempt and the ledger records it.
- [ ] Regression: pending/in-progress required checks still never trigger update-branch or fix-worker routing (GH#26406 behaviour unchanged); `DRY_RUN=1` still returns before any rebase.
- [ ] Unclassifiable check state keeps current behaviour (fail-open to one rebase) and logs the reason.
- [ ] All listed verification commands pass.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Worker Quick-Start

- Caller: `_pmp_stage_required_checks` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh:1570-1602`
  calls `_attempt_pr_ci_rebase_retry` (line 1585); a 0 return skips
  `_route_pr_to_fix_worker` (line 1589).
- Rebase function: `_attempt_pr_ci_rebase_retry` in
  `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh:1047-1145` (~99 lines — at the 100-line
  function-complexity gate; do NOT add logic inside it).
- Failing-context classification: `_check_required_checks_has_terminal_failure` in
  `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-required-checks.sh:1778` (counts terminal failed
  required contexts; extend or add a sibling that emits their sorted names).
- Sub-library sourcing pattern: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh:302-324`
  (`source "${_PULSE_MERGE_DIR}/pulse-merge-*.sh"`).
- State-dir precedent: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-feedback-ci-repair.sh:1191`
  (`AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS_RUNTIME_DIR` default) and `_ci_repair_write_state` at line 520.

### Files to Modify

- `NEW: .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-ci-drift-ledger.sh` — small sourced lib: record and query per-PR drift-rebase attempts.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh:300-325` — source the new lib alongside the other `pulse-merge-*.sh` libs.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh:1585-1588` — consult the ledger before `_attempt_pr_ci_rebase_retry`; record after a successful rebase.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-required-checks.sh:1778-1850` — expose the sorted names of terminal failed required contexts (new sibling function preferred over growing the existing one).
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-ci-repair-routing.sh` — add focused cases to the existing suite (it already stubs `_attempt_pr_ci_rebase_retry` at line 497); no new harness.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** only `_pmp_stage_required_checks` (pulse-merge.sh:1585). The review-repair caller at pulse-merge-process.sh:1260 uses strict `review-repair` policy and is out of scope — leave unchanged.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** new ledger file writes only; GitHub writes unchanged (update-branch or existing fix-worker routing).
- **Existing verification/tests:** `test-pulse-merge-ci-repair-routing.sh`, `test-pulse-merge-pr-context.sh`, `test-pulse-merge-update-branch.sh`, `test-pulse-merge-routine-standalone.sh` (asserts the dry-run guard precedes the rebase call — keep it true).
- **Schemas/config:** none required; an env override for the ledger TTL is optional (`PULSE_CI_DRIFT_LEDGER_TTL_S`, default 7 days).
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** deployed to `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/` by `setup.sh`; no generated output.
- **Migrations/backfills:** none — absent ledger = current behaviour (one rebase allowed).
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** prune entries older than TTL on write; deleting the ledger file restores current behaviour.

### Implementation Steps

1. Add a sibling in `pulse-merge-required-checks.sh` that prints the sorted, newline-separated names of terminal failed required contexts for `repo pr [head]`, reusing the data `_check_required_checks_has_terminal_failure` already fetches. Return non-zero when state cannot be classified.
2. Create `pulse-merge-ci-drift-ledger.sh` with two functions (explicit `return 0/1`, `local var="$1"`):

```bash
# Ledger: one line per PR: "<repo>#<pr>\t<signature>\t<prior_head>\t<epoch>"
# signature = sha of sorted failing required context names
_ci_drift_ledger_should_skip() {   # repo pr head signature -> 0 = skip rebase
	# skip when an entry exists for repo#pr with the same signature and
	# prior_head != current head (Pulse already rebased; same contexts still fail)
}
_ci_drift_ledger_record() {        # repo pr prior_head signature
	# replace any line for repo#pr; prune lines older than TTL; atomic write via mktemp+mv
}
```

3. In `_pmp_stage_required_checks`, before the rebase call: compute the signature; if `_ci_drift_ledger_should_skip` returns 0, log
   `[pulse-merge] PR #N in repo: CI-drift rebase already tried for the same failing required contexts (<names>); routing to CI fix-worker`
   and fall through to `_route_pr_to_fix_worker`. After a successful rebase (rc 0), call `_ci_drift_ledger_record` with the pre-rebase head. If the signature cannot be computed, keep current behaviour (fail-open to one rebase).
4. Add focused cases to `test-pulse-merge-ci-repair-routing.sh` (see Acceptance Criteria).
5. `shellcheck` changed files; run the verification commands below.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** Pulse runs one merge pass per runner at a time; write the ledger via `mktemp` + `mv` in the same dir. Ledger is runner-local, so another runner may still try one rebase — bounded at one per runner per signature, acceptable.
- **Migration/rollback:** absent/empty ledger = existing behaviour; revert is file deletion plus code revert.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** older runners keep looping; newer runners route to the fix worker. No shared format.

## Task Brief

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-06, interactive session (maintainer-approved filing)
- **Evidence source:** live Pulse log `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` and PR #33755 commit/check history

## What

Stop Pulse from repeatedly running the CI-drift `update-branch` rebase on a PR whose
same required checks keep failing on every rebased head. After one drift rebase has
been tried for a given set of failing required contexts, the next cycle must route the
PR to the CI fix-worker (`_route_pr_to_fix_worker ... "ci"`) instead of rebasing again.

## Why

Throughput: a deterministic code failure (static analysis, complexity, lint) cannot be
fixed by merging the base branch, but on a busy repo the base is always ahead
(`behind_by>0`), so `_attempt_pr_ci_rebase_retry` succeeds every cycle, returns 0, and
the caller returns before fix-worker routing. The PR is never repaired by automation.

Observed on PR #33755 (issue #33750), worker commit `2089e6cc97` at 03:14Z:

| Time (UTC) | Event |
|---|---|
| 03:32 | Pulse update-branch → merge commit `f836c8d8ee` |
| 03:55 | Pulse update-branch → `014798459e`; `Qlty Regression Gate` + `Qlty Smell Regression` failed again |
| 04:18 | Pulse update-branch → `0f3124e5ad`; same two required contexts failed again (04:20) |
| 04:34 | Interactive maintainer pushed the actual fix `f1d52de4e4`; merged next cycle |

Pulse log pattern (repeats three times, never followed by a `_dispatch_ci_fix_worker` line):

```text
[pulse-merge] _check_required_checks_has_terminal_failure: 1 terminal failed required context(s) for PR #33755 ... (t3567)
[pulse-merge] PR #33755 in marcusquinn/aidevops: attempting CI-drift rebase via update-branch (t2805)
[pulse-merge] PR #33755 in marcusquinn/aidevops: CI-drift rebase succeeded via update-branch, deferring to next cycle (t2805)
```

Cost: ~80 minutes of blocked merge, three wasted full CI runs, and a human intervention
for a failure the CI fix-worker path (`pulse-merge-feedback-ci-repair.sh`) exists to handle.

## Tier

`tier:standard` — bounded change on the Pulse merge path with a clear reference pattern;
the design decision (per-PR ledger keyed by failing-context signature) is resolved below.

## Context & Decisions

- Chosen: signature-keyed per-PR ledger over a blanket "max N rebases" counter — a genuinely new failure after a base change still deserves one drift rebase, and a same-signature repeat is strong evidence the PR's own code is at fault.
