title: Per-repo 'GitHub Actions unavailable' capability: local verification path for full-loop and workers
body:
## Goal

Let a repository record that its GitHub Actions don't run, for example a private repo on an account with billing or spending blocked. Workers and interactive full-loops then verify locally from the start, instead of discovering it from a failed run. Follow-up to #32869, which (via PR #32891) only covered classifying the failure: `ci-infra-signature-lib.sh` → `CI_BILLING_OUTAGE_PATTERN`, with no CI repair dispatch. The capability part of #32869 ("represent zero-minute Actions availability as a repository/runtime capability; prevent worker completion contracts from requiring remote checks when unavailable; support a local-verification plus trusted-merge path") has not shipped. `reference/repos-json-fields.md`, `reference/ci-gate-policy.md` and `workflows/full-loop.md` have no such field or path.

## Observed (2026-10-06)

A new private plugin repo on an organization whose Actions jobs fail with "The job was not started because recent account payments have failed or your spending limit needs to be increased". The owner chose to rely on local checks. The PR merged through `full-loop-helper.sh merge` only because the repo had no required checks. Nothing told the session ahead of time to run local checks and record them; that was manual. The only durable record today is a per-repo `AGENTS.md` rule written by hand (a prose rule, not machine-readable).

## Proposed change

1. `.agents/reference/repos-json-fields.md`: add a field such as `actions: "unavailable"` (default absent = available), with an optional `actions_reason`. Settable with `aidevops repos` (e.g. `aidevops repos actions <on|off> [repo]`, modelled on `aidevops repos maintenance <on|off>`).
2. `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md` + `.agents/reference/ci-gate-policy.md`: when the field is set, the completion contract requires the repo's configured local checks (lint/typecheck/unit, or the repo's documented scripts such as `scripts/lint.sh` and `scripts/smoke-test.sh`). Their results are recorded in the PR body or a PR comment. Don't poll or wait for remote checks.
3. `full-loop-helper.sh merge` / `wait-checks`: with the field set, treat terminal billing-blocked failures matching `CI_BILLING_OUTAGE_PATTERN` as non-blocking only when the PR records local verification for the exact head. Any non-billing failure still blocks. Keep #aidevops:trust-boundary checks unchanged for external authors.
4. Worker dispatch brief: include the capability so headless workers know before pushing.
5. Optional: when the pulse sees billing-blocked failures on a repo without the field, add one deduplicated advisory suggesting it (no comment storms).

## Verification

- Fixture repo with `actions: "unavailable"` and a billing-blocked failed check: `full-loop-helper.sh merge` succeeds when the PR records local verification for its head SHA, and blocks when it doesn't, or when a failure is not billing-related.
- `wait-checks` returns without polling for that repo.
- Existing `tests/test-pulse-merge-ci-repair-routing.sh` still passes; extend it, or add a sibling test, for the merge path.

### Files Scope
- `aidevops.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/aidevops-repos-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/repo-actions-capability-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-readiness.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/gh-checks-wait-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-prompt.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-repo-actions-capability.sh`
- `.agents/reference/repos-json-fields.md`
- `.agents/reference/ci-gate-policy.md`
- `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md`
- `README.md`

Implementation map: use the existing registry mutation pattern, shared billing annotation classifier, readiness gate and required-check waiter. Local evidence must be trusted and bound to the current PR head; classify all terminal failures, not only required contexts. Native protection, external-author authority and bot-review gates remain unchanged. Verify with ShellCheck, a focused fixture regression, existing merge/waiter tests and CI-repair routing regression. Optional Pulse advisory is not part of this implementation.

Integration scope recovery: `_merge_admin_fallback_required_checks_clear` calls the same waiter before an implicit admin retry. It must request native-only evidence so local verification cannot authorize a protection bypass. This directly necessary integration adds only `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`; verify with the existing merge cases and the capability fixture. The assigned issue remains open and owned by this worker; no related open PR or pushed issue branch was found.

title: wp-plugin-new: include LAUNCH.md when making a new plugin its own
body:
## Problem

`/new-wp-plugin` step 6 ("Make it the plugin's own") lists `README.md`, `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`, `AGENTS.md` and the banner, but not `LAUNCH.md`. Plugins made from WP Plugin Starter inherit the starter's own `LAUNCH.md`, which says the repository is public, the plugin is not meant for WordPress.org and has no features, and that a `main` ruleset, CodeQL and Scorecard are on. For a new private plugin this is wrong, and agents read it as current state. Seen on a plugin made from starter v1.0.24 (`LAUNCH.md` rewritten by hand after the first feature PR).

The starter side is wpallstars/wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding#390: `rename-plugin.sh` is to write a fresh pre-launch `LAUNCH.md`.

## Change

- `.agents/tools/wordpress/wp-plugin-new.md` → Workflow step 6: add `LAUNCH.md` to the files made the plugin's own. Check that it states the real launch state: private, no release, no protection/rulesets, hosted reviewers deferred to public launch, WordPress.org not submitted. Note that starters with #390 write this; older ones need a rewrite.
- `.agents/scripts/commands/new-wp-plugin.md` step 4: add `LAUNCH.md` to the list.

title: t18596: fix(pulse): malformed .aidevops.json silently blocks every candidate in a repo via runner-capability invalid_requirements cooldown
body:
## Task


Stop a malformed repo-local `.aidevops.json` from silently starving every dispatch
candidate in that repository. The runner-capability gate must (1) not parse the repo
config at all when the issue has no `dispatch-class:` label, and (2) when it does need
the config and cannot parse it, report a distinct, non-cooldown signal
(`config_unreadable path=.aidevops.json`) instead of the generic `invalid_requirements`.

## Done when

- [ ] Positive: an issue with no `dispatch-class:` label in a repo whose `.aidevops.json` is malformed passes `runner_capability_check` (exit 0).
- [ ] Positive: an issue with a `dispatch-class:` label in a repo with malformed `.aidevops.json` fails with `runner_capability_unmet reason=config_unreadable path=.aidevops.json`, logged as `signal=config_unreadable cooldown=none`.
- [ ] Regression: valid config + `dispatch-class:` label with an unmet secret/probe still yields the existing signals and cooldown eligibility.
- [ ] All verification commands pass.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Worker Quick-Start

- `.agents/scripts/runner-capability-helper.sh:185-281` — embedded Python requirements check.
- `.agents/scripts/runner-capability-helper.sh:44-68` — shell signal/cooldown mapping.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh:965-1079` — cooldown fingerprint includes a config fingerprint, so a repaired file already clears the cooldown; no change needed there.
- Existing suite: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-runner-capability.sh`.

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/runner-capability-helper.sh:187-204` — collect `dispatch-class:` labels first; read/parse `.aidevops.json` only when at least one is present. On parse failure call `unmet('config_unreadable path=.aidevops.json')`.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/runner-capability-helper.sh:53-64` — leave `config_unreadable` out of the cooldown-eligible set (operator-fixable, cheap to re-check; fingerprint changes on repair anyway). Keep bare-verdict mapping unchanged otherwise.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-runner-capability.sh` — add cases below to the existing suite (no new harness).

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `runner_capability_check` is called from the `dispatch_with_dedup` path via `_runner_capability_*` wrapper at `runner-capability-helper.sh:20-37`; cooldown consumers in `pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh` parse only the `signal=` and `cooldown=` fields.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** none beyond log lines and the existing cooldown file (not written for the new signal).
- **Existing verification/tests:** `tests/test-runner-capability.sh`; `tests/test-pulse-wrapper-worker-detection.sh` and `tests/test-dispatch-max-parallel.sh` stub ranked candidates and should stay green.
- **Schemas/config:** none.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** deployed copy via `setup.sh`; no generated output.
- **Migrations/backfills:** none; existing cooldown files keyed on the old fingerprint expire or are invalidated on config repair.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** code revert only.

### Implementation Steps

1. In the Python block, compute `class_names = [label[len('dispatch-class:'):] ...]` from issue labels before touching config. If empty, set `classes = {}` and skip reading `.aidevops.json` (symlink check included).
2. When `class_names` is non-empty, read and parse the config inside a narrow `try`; on `ValueError`/`OSError` call `unmet('config_unreadable path=.aidevops.json')`.
3. In `_runner_capability_log_deferral`, the existing `reason=([a-z_]+)` extraction yields `signal=config_unreadable`; confirm it is NOT in the `cooldown=eligible` case list.
4. Add test cases; run verification.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** read-only check; no new shared state.
- **Migration/rollback:** none; behaviour for valid configs and labelled issues unchanged.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** older runners keep the 6 h cooldown; newer runners dispatch unlabelled issues regardless of config validity.
- **Idempotency/retry:** `config_unreadable` re-checks every cycle (cheap file parse).
- **Partial failure/recovery:** an unparseable config still blocks only issues that genuinely need class requirements, with an actionable reason.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-runner-capability.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/runner-capability-helper.sh
.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed
```

- **Surface mapping:** suite proves both acceptance paths and the unchanged valid-config path; shellcheck/linters cover the shell wrapper.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required.

### Scope Boundaries

**Hard boundaries:** do not change secret, probe, or SSH requirement handling; do not repair other repositories' `.aidevops.json` files in this PR (separate operator action).

**AI brief owner:** interactive maintainer session that filed this issue.

**Recovery:** preserve the current PR and use the structured runtime request and Pulse intake in `reference/worker-discipline.md` when local recovery is unsafe.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-runner-capability.sh`

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-06, interactive throughput review (maintainer session)
- **Evidence source:** live `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log`, local repo configs, `runner-capability-helper.sh`

## What

Stop a malformed repo-local `.aidevops.json` from silently starving every dispatch
candidate in that repository. The runner-capability gate must (1) not parse the repo
config at all when the issue has no `dispatch-class:` label, and (2) when it does need
the config and cannot parse it, report a distinct, non-cooldown signal
(`config_unreadable path=.aidevops.json`) instead of the generic `invalid_requirements`.

## Why

Throughput: on this runner, every available issue in two pulse-enabled repos is blocked
for 6 hours at a time, indefinitely, with a misleading reason.

- Five issues in `<private-managed-repo>` and `marcusquinn/cloudron-netbird-app` #158 #165 —
  all `status:available` + `auto-dispatch`, unassigned, no `dispatch-class:` labels, no `requires-*` body lines.
- Pulse log, repeating since at least line 295623:
  `Dispatch_max: #N (<private-managed-repo>) runner_capability_unmet cooldown recorded signal=invalid_requirements ttl=21600s`
  then `Dispatch enumeration: <private-managed-repo> runner_capability_unmet cooldown skipped #N ...` (five issues).
- Both repos' `.aidevops.json` are invalid JSON (an extra `}` closes the root object before `"plugins": []`):
  Python `json.loads` → `Extra data: line 34 column 4`.
- Mechanism: `.agents/scripts/runner-capability-helper.sh:193` parses config unconditionally;
  `json.JSONDecodeError` is a `ValueError`, caught at line 279 → bare `unmet()` → shell maps a
  reason-less verdict to `signal=invalid_requirements` (lines 56-57) → `cooldown=eligible` (line 63)
  → 6 h cooldown recorded by `_dispatch_capability_cooldown_record` (`pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh:994`).
- Scan of this runner's pulse repos: 11 valid configs, 2 malformed, 41 without a config.

## Tier

`tier:standard` — small, well-located change in one helper plus focused test cases in its existing suite.

## Context & Decisions

- Chosen: skip config parsing when no class label requests it — the config is only consulted for `dispatch_class_requirements`, so validity is irrelevant otherwise.
- Rejected: auto-repairing malformed `.aidevops.json` from the dispatch path — writes to canonical checkouts belong to the audited project-config migration path (`repo-aidevops-health-helper.sh`), not dispatch.
- Follow-up candidate (not this task): `repo-aidevops-health-helper.sh` could report malformed `.aidevops.json` in its health output.

- `.agents/scripts/runner-capability-helper.sh:44-68,185-281`

## Worker Guidance


### Files to Modify

## Task Brief

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-06, interactive throughput review (maintainer session)
- **Evidence source:** issue-sync run `37495532410` log; t18583 TODO entry and planning PR #33521; framework docs listed below

## What

Make the "save for later" guidance match what issue-sync actually does, and stop the
false task-ID collision warning on planning PRs.

1. Guidance says saved/later work is "a local TODO/plan without creating an implementation
   issue", but `issue-sync-helper.sh push` creates an issue for every open `- [ ] tNNN`
   TODO row without `ref:GH#` (`_push_build_task_list`,
   `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper-push.sh:55-67`), and the `/save-todo` "simple"
   template itself writes a `tNNN` row. Align the docs with the mechanics: an ID-bearing
   saved task becomes a **non-dispatched tracking issue** (no `auto-dispatch`); only the
   ID-less plan-line form (`- [ ] {title} #plan → [...]`) stays issue-less.
2. `_push_warn_if_task_id_collides` (`issue-sync-helper-push.sh:297-307`) matches any merged
   PR whose title contains the task ID, so every task's own planning PR (`tNNN: plan ...`)
   triggers `TASK ID COLLISION ... will be blocked by the dedup guard`. Ignore merged PRs
   whose title starts with `tNNN: plan` (or whose only changes are planning files).

t18583 was saved on 2026-10-04 as "deferred capability brief only; no implementation
issue" (#33521). Issue-sync then tried to create its issue on every push to `main`; that
attempt failed (privacy guard on a placeholder path), and the failure skipped planning
publication for all other tasks until 2026-10-06. Doc/mechanics mismatch led the author to
expect no issue; the false collision warning added misleading noise to the same log.

## Tier

`tier:standard` — doc wording in three files plus one small warning-filter change.

## Context & Decisions

- Chosen: align docs with existing mechanics (tracking issue, no dispatch) over a new issue-less tag — maintainer chose this for t18583 on 2026-10-06; avoids a second publication path.
- Out of scope: privacy guard flags tilde-prefixed placeholder paths (home-relative `Git/<owner>/<repo>`) as local paths (`privacy-guard-helper.sh:389`). Treat as a separate finding only if it recurs.

title: t18583: Reusable Hostinger fleet onboarding and drift sync
body:
**Task ID:** `t18583` | **Status:** open
**Logged:** 2026-10-03
**Tags:** `enhancement` `hosting` `interactive`

## Outcome

Reusable Hostinger fleet onboarding and drift sync — phased: inventory/plan/drift PR #34379, readiness PR #34445, provisioning PR #34447, layout-move wrapper PR #34448.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief


Status: All four phases implemented. Production repairs (repo creation,
registration, layout moves) still need explicit operator authority each time
they run.

## Progress

- [x] Phase 1 — read-only inventory, plan and drift (`hostinger-helper.sh fleet`),
  multisite network discovery, fleet-scoped `migrate-layout plan --source`.
- [x] Phase 2 — provisioning (`fleet provision`): preview by default; `--apply`
  bound to the reviewed plan hash, refusing stale or config-contradicted plans;
  create or adopt private repos, clone, native init (registers), deliver the
  init commit as issue + PR without merging; resumable, per-step private receipt,
  explicit per-repository partial results.
- [x] Phase 3 — readiness verification (`fleet ready`): visibility, owner,
  default-branch heads, effective features, Pulse/maintenance flags and worker auth;
  configured readiness, with optional merged-worker-PR evidence kept separate.
- [x] Phase 4 — fleet layout-move wrapper (`fleet move`): named misplaced sites
  only; confirm the fleet plan hash; snapshot, pause, scoped native plan (after
  pausing) and apply; restore maintenance and Pulse by slug with read-back proof
  (new native `aidevops repos pulse on|off`); partial moves stay paused until
  `--restore`.

The new `hosting_fleet_*.py` modules avoid the `.gitignore` credential pattern
`hostinger_*`. `aidevops.sh` gained `repos pulse`.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/hosting_fleet.py`
- `.agents/scripts/hosting_fleet_inventory.py`
- `.agents/scripts/hosting_fleet_plan.py`
- `.agents/scripts/hosting_fleet_remote.py`
- `.agents/scripts/hosting_fleet_ready.py`
- `.agents/scripts/hosting_fleet_checks.py`
- `.agents/scripts/hosting_fleet_provision.py`
- `.agents/scripts/hosting_fleet_steps.py`
- `.agents/scripts/hosting_fleet_deliver.py`
- `.agents/scripts/hosting_fleet_move.py`
- `.agents/scripts/hosting_fleet_automation.py`
- `.agents/scripts/hostinger-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/repo_layout_migrate.py`
- `.agents/scripts/repo-layout-migrate-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/aidevops-repos-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/repo-discovery-lib.sh`
- `aidevops.sh`
- `.agents/services/hosting/hostinger.md`
- `.agents/reference/repo-organization.md`
- `.agents/reference/repos-json-fields.md`
- `tests/test-repo-layout-migrate.py`

## Goal and observed evidence

Turn a successfully completed 30-site onboarding into a reusable capability:
inventory the hosting account, map shared WordPress networks, provision private
repositories, initialize aidevops, and verify background readiness without
modifying production. The observed fleet comprised 25 hosting-panel entries,
30 distinct sites, and 17 shared WordPress codebases.

The one-off process required materially adapted inventory, initialization,
delivery, verification and completion-receipt scripts. It encountered legacy
feature opt-outs, missing remote default-branch references, inherited source
whitespace, owner transfers, and onboarding-document artifact restrictions.
Fleet verification ultimately passed 30/30. Keep customer identities, local
paths and credentials out of shared examples and public diagnostics.

## Reference patterns and candidate files

- `.agents/scripts/hostinger-helper.sh`: existing hosting command surface;
  evaluate authenticated API discovery versus its configured-site inventory.
- `.agents/scripts/aidevops-cli/aidevops-repos-lib.sh`: registry integration.
- `.agents/scripts/repo-layout-migrate-helper.sh` and
  `.agents/reference/repo-organization.md`: owner-aware canonical locations and
  reviewed, receipt-backed migrations; never improvise directory moves.
- `.agents/scripts/repo_layout_migrate.py`: native scoped repository planning,
  consumer inventory, before-state validation, content hashes and receipts.
- `.agents/scripts/canonical-recovery-helper.sh`: audited mirror convergence.
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh`: worker runtime/canary checks.
- Existing native init, GitHub write, secret scanning and PHP lint interfaces:
  reuse their current supported contracts rather than duplicating them.
- New fleet-helper module and reference-document paths are not finalized;
  discover the current integration points before choosing them.

## Proposed behavior

1. Provide a non-mutating inventory/plan mode with explicit account, owner and
   site scope. Separate hosting-panel entries, WordPress networks, blogs and
   aliases. Associate shared code with its primary network repository.
2. Default organization clones to `<git-root>/<owner>/<repo>` and personal clones
   to `<git-root>/<repo>` (`<git-root>` = the home `Git` directory; see
   `reference/repo-organization.md`), respecting explicit exceptions and collisions. Support a
   caller-specified personal-owner exception. Never include unrelated repos in
   an approved fleet transaction.
3. Use existing authenticated interfaces and secure credential storage. Do not
   emit credentials or copy production configuration, databases, uploads or
   backups. Optional custom-code imports need scanning and scoped syntax checks.
4. Reuse native initialization for planning, Git workflow and code quality.
   Check effective feature flags, not only requested-feature output or registry
   labels. Treat inherited source-formatting debt separately from authored
   onboarding metadata, without disabling relevant native gates.
5. Verify private visibility, intended remote ownership, permissions, canonical
   registration, default-branch heads, initialization, Pulse/maintenance flags,
   worker authentication and full-loop prerequisites. Distinguish configured
   readiness from actual successful worker runs.
6. Support resumable, per-site receipts and explicit partial/failure results.
   Validate GitHub targets before writes; handle existing repos, transfers,
   drafts and pending versus terminal CI states without blind retries or merges.
7. Offer read-only drift checks for new, missing, moved or misregistered sites.
   Require explicit execution authority for repairs. Do not create a recurring
   schedule, dispatch implementation, or deploy merely because a brief exists.

## Owner-layout migration workflow

Observed operational evidence: a later, explicitly authorized layout transaction
moved 24 fleet repositories with exact Git state preserved. Native processing
included 39 runtime databases, including an approximately 83 GB database; guarded
apply completed in approximately 13.5 minutes. Live terminal configuration drift
required a separately hashed plan revision. These measurements are evidence for
budgeting on that installation, not universal timeout defaults.

1. Select only the approved fleet and reuse native `plan_repository` and consumer
   contracts. Do not use a whole-workspace migration to accomplish a fleet-only
   request. Preserve personal-owner exceptions and unrelated registrations.
2. Probe source, destination and linked-worktree consumers. Leave active sites in
   place with automation enabled until their owners checkpoint and exit. Never
   kill unowned sessions, create compatibility symlinks or bypass active-path gates.
3. Reconcile missing local clones and registrations separately from eligible
   moves. Do not silently recreate deliberately removed previews. Remote deletion
   requires its own explicit authority, exact identity/admin checks, high-stakes
   verification and owner-private backups of needed Git/API evidence.
4. Snapshot each eligible site's exact maintenance and Pulse settings before
   pausing it through the supported maintenance command. Restore both settings
   after success or an unmoved abort: maintenance-on alone does not restore Pulse.
   Preserve unrelated registry edits and record restoration proof.
5. Inventory and retain every native database integrity, schema/row drift and
   backup guard. Budget from observed database sizes and provide bounded progress;
   a long integrity check is not evidence of corruption or permission to skip it.
6. Snapshot mutable regular-file consumers after lengthy database inventory.
   If a file drifts, revalidate the exact scope and native file contract; write a
   new plan ID/hash while preserving the old receipt. A receipt with mutation
   steps requires native resume/rollback, never in-place plan replacement. Apply
   must continue to recheck all repository and consumer before-states.
7. Apply only the exact confirmed native plan hash. Inspect the append-only
   receipt before declaring completion, and keep pending sites explicit. A
   safety refusal pauses the unsafe path, not the entire objective.
8. Verify physical locations, exact Git fingerprints, linked common-directory
   pointers, registry paths, terminal/runtime retargeting, private remote identity
   and restored automation. Resolve current fleet paths by slug; preserve the
   historical onboarding inventory and write a distinct post-layout report.
9. Keep rollback receipts and backups private. Flag restoration deliberately
   changes registry content after native completion; any later rollback must
   reconcile this intended drift rather than overwrite unrelated configuration.

Operational adapters were installation-local; do not copy customer paths, names,
credentials or raw terminal configuration into this shared brief. A future
implementation should expose these bounded selection/progress/restoration
contracts through the native fleet CLI rather than accumulating one-off scripts.

## Verification and acceptance

- Exercise native inventory/plan and supported CLI paths on an authorized,
  explicitly scoped account; verify repeat runs make no unnecessary changes.
- Reconcile counts and per-site receipts against live hosting/GitHub facts.
- Include shared-network children, an existing repo, an owner exception, a
  destination collision, disabled effective features and interrupted delivery
  when they are available through existing fixtures or operational checks.
- Inspect effective configuration, Git capture state, mirror heads, registry
  values and scheduler health. Canary success alone is not fleet job success.
- A partial fleet cannot produce an all-ready receipt or close failed audit
  issues. No production mutation or accidental publication is acceptable.
- For an authorized owner-layout move, prove exact scope and preserved Git state,
  truthful active/absent/retired classifications, receipt completion and exact
  automation restoration through native runtime paths. Exercise drift and refusal
  recovery with existing checks; never weaken guards to obtain a green result.
- Run existing scoped lint/type/syntax checks for touched files. Add focused
  coverage only when needed to resolve material uncertainty; do not introduce
  new runners, mocks, test-only interfaces or CI gates by default.

</details>

body:
**Task ID:** `t18599` | **Status:** open
**Tags:** `bug`

## Outcome

fix(issue-sync): concurrent planning-publication reconcile reports silent failure for issues another reconciler already published

## Done when

- [ ] Positive: an issue listed as pending whose label is gone by the time it is processed counts as reconciled and logs `already reconciled concurrently`.
- [ ] Regression: an issue that still has `publication:pending` and fails validation still counts as failed.
- [ ] All verification commands pass.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/planning-publication-reconcile.sh:266-298` — add `_publication_concurrently_reconciled` (pending label absent on a fresh issue view) and use it at the pre-mutation and post-mutation pending checks: print an info line and return 0.
- Silent `return 1` at those two points becomes the concurrent-success path; other failure paths unchanged.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `cmd_reconcile` (CI step `Reconcile pending planning publication`, `full-loop-helper.sh merge`, manual `reconcile --task`).
- **Writers/mutation paths:** no new writes; fewer redundant label edits.
- **Existing verification/tests:** `tests/test-planning-publication-reconcile.sh`, `tests/test-planning-publication-lifecycle.sh`.
- **Schemas/config/mirrors/migrations:** none. **Rollback:** revert.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency:** `publication:pending` removal is the reconciler's final mutation (comment at line 308), so its absence means another reconciler finished every earlier step.
- **Partial failure:** issues whose pending label is still present keep the existing fail-closed checks.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-planning-publication-reconcile.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-planning-publication-lifecycle.sh
shellcheck .agents/scripts/planning-publication-reconcile.sh
```

- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/planning-publication-reconcile.sh`

</details>

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

title: t18600: Decision asks and completion summaries include clickable links to evidence
body:
## What

When an interactive session asks the user to decide something (the `What next` block's **Needed from you** asks) or reports what was delivered, every named object must be a clickable link: PRs, issues, commits, changed files, previews and dashboards.

## Why

Users run many parallel sessions. Asks like "Merge PR #123?" or "Review the change in `session.md`?" force an extra turn ("send me links") or make the user remember the session and search for the object. A link lets them inspect and answer in one step.

Current guidance (`.agents/reference/session.md` "What Next Block" / "Numbered Asks") requires naming the concrete object but never requires a link, and terminal runtimes do not autolink bare `#123`.

## How

- `.agents/reference/session.md`: add a link rule to the What Next rules and Numbered Asks; update the template and example; require linked delivery bullets in Session Lifecycle.
  - Full `https://` URLs from tool output (`gh pr view --json url`, `gh issue view --json url`, `gh browse --no-browser <path>`), never guessed/constructed.
  - Local files as absolute `path:line`; local previews as their `localhost` URL.
  - Print the bare URL (optionally after the label) so it stays clickable when Markdown is not rendered.
- `.agents/AGENTS.md`: append a short pointer to the always-loaded What next rule, net-neutral on the 24000-byte CI size ratchet.

title: t18604: feat(pulse): dormant repos skip candidate scans until woken by new work or an...
body:
**Task ID:** `t18604` | **Status:** open
**Tags:** `auto-dispatch` `feat`

## Outcome

feat(pulse): dormant repos skip candidate scans until woken by new work or an interactive session

**Blocked by:** `t18603`

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-06, interactive throughput review (maintainer session); maintainer proposal
- **Depends on:** t18603 / GH#33844 (conditional 304s must work before "nothing changed" signals can be trusted)
- blocked-by: t18603

## What

Pulse stops scanning repos that have no dispatchable work on every pass. A repo whose only open issues are persistent, non-dispatchable ones (reporting, parent and held issues) enters a **dormant** state and is skipped for candidate discovery and prefetch. It wakes only on an explicit signal: new or relabelled issues/PRs, a push to its planning files, or an interactive session starting or claiming work in it.

## Why

Most managed repos are not under active development; many hold only persistent reporting issues. Today every enabled repo is rechecked on a timer:

- `pulse-prefetch-orchestration.sh:517-570` `check_repo_tier_skip` gates only the prefetch stage (`pulse-prefetch-repo.sh:397`). Tiers come from `pulse-repo-tier.sh` (7-day GitHub event counts: hot ≥30, warm ≥5, cold <5) and the longest skip is `PULSE_TIER_COLD_INTERVAL=600`s (`pulse-wrapper-config.sh:243-246`). An event-quiet repo with no dispatchable work is still refetched every ~10 minutes, indefinitely.
- Tier reflects event volume, not whether dispatchable candidates exist. A busy repo with only reporting-issue churn stays hot; a quiet repo with one new `auto-dispatch` issue waits for its cold interval.
- `pulse-events-tickle.sh` keeps one ETag per **owner**, so any event anywhere under an owner marks all its repos stale.
- `interactive-session-helper.sh` and `interactive-start-helper.sh` emit no wake signal.

## Tier

`tier:thinking` — new scheduling state with cross-stage correctness constraints; a missed wake causes silent starvation.

## How (Approach)

### Verify first (findings decide the design)

1. Map which pulse stages enumerate repos: prefetch (`pulse-prefetch-repo.sh`, `pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh`), candidate discovery/dispatch fill, stale-PR/checkpoint continuation and sweeps. Record which stages would be gated by dormancy and which must keep running (open PRs, active workers, checkpoint recovery, CI repair must never sleep).
2. Define "no dispatchable work" from existing dispatch eligibility (labels such as `auto-dispatch`, `status:available`, `parent-task`, hold labels), reusing the existing predicate rather than inventing a second one.
3. Confirm which per-repo change signal is cheapest: per-repo events or issues `since=` with an ETag (after t18603) versus the owner-level tickle.

### Expected shape (adjust to findings)

title: Worktree ownership error recommends adopt after reboot when the same session can re-claim via pre-edit check
body:
## Problem

After a host reboot, an interactive OpenCode session resumes with the **same** session ID, but its registered worktree still records the pre-reboot owner PID. `aidevops_bounded_operation start` (and other tools that use `verifyRegisteredOwnership`) then fails with:

> Operation workdir is not owned by the current OpenCode session. For a registered previous-session worktree, run worktree-helper.sh adopt <path> <session> <task> after its owner exits; live owners cannot be adopted.

That guidance does not fit this case:

- The recorded `owner_session` equals the current `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID`; only `owner_pid` is stale (dead process). It is not a previous session's worktree.
- `worktree-helper.sh adopt` cannot succeed when the registry row has an empty `task_id` (the worktree was created without one), because `cmd_adopt` requires `old_task == task_id` and rejects an empty `task_id` argument. It exits 1 with no message.
- The path that does work is running `pre-edit-check.sh` (or the `aidevops_pre_edit_check` tool) in the worktree: `claim_worktree_ownership` re-claims it for the current session with a fresh PID, after which the bounded operation starts normally.

## Evidence (aidevops v3.38.17, OpenCode v1.18.34, Linux)

1. Before reboot: the registry row for the worktree had `owner_session=ses_<current>`, `task_id=''`, `owner_pid=<pre-reboot pid>`.
2. After reboot, same session resumed: `aidevops_bounded_operation start` returned the error above.
3. `worktree-helper.sh adopt <worktree> ses_<current> <task>` exited 1, silently.
4. `aidevops_pre_edit_check` with `workdir=<worktree>` passed. The registry row then showed a new `owner_pid` and `created_at`, with the same session.
5. `aidevops_bounded_operation start` succeeded.

## Proposed fix (small, no change to the trust boundary)

Files:

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/gpt-image-worktree.mjs` (`verifyRegisteredOwnership`, error text around line 45).
- Optionally `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper.sh` (`cmd_adopt`) and `.agents/scripts/shared-worktree-registry.sh` (`registry verify-owner`).

Change:

1. When verification fails, make the error tell the user what to do next. If the registry row's `owner_session` equals the current session ID and its `owner_pid` is dead, say to run `pre-edit-check.sh` (or `aidevops_pre_edit_check`) in that worktree to re-claim it. Recommend `adopt` only for a different, exited session.
2. Optional: have `cmd_adopt` print one line explaining why it refused (for example "registry task_id is empty; adopt requires a matching task ID"), instead of exiting 1 silently.

Out of scope: relaxing `adopt`'s task-ID match. It may be intentional as a safety check against taking another session's work.

## Verification

- Register a worktree for session S with a PID that has exited and an empty `task_id`. Run a bounded operation as session S: the error should name the pre-edit re-claim path, not `adopt`.
- Run `pre-edit-check.sh` in that worktree as S, then the bounded operation: it should start.
- Run `worktree-helper.sh adopt` with a mismatched or empty task: it should print a one-line reason and exit 1.

<!-- aidevops:sig -->

title: Canonical Git guard blocks read-only git check-ignore, breaking child build tools in canonical checkouts
body:
## Observed

The canonical Git guard (`.agents/scripts/git` PATH wrapper → `canonical-git-command-guard.py`) treats `git check-ignore` and `git ls-files` style read-only queries as canonical mutation. `git check-ignore` in a canonical checkout is blocked with:

```text
BLOCKED by canonical Git guard: canonical worktree mutation via 'git check-ignore'.
```

Because the wrapper is on PATH, child processes are affected too. A Node build tool run against a clean, up-to-date canonical `main` checkout runs `git check-ignore --quiet --no-index -- <dir>/<probe>` to confirm its temporary output directory is ignored by Git. The guard's non-zero exit is indistinguishable from a real git error, so the tool aborts with "could not be checked against Git safely". The documented workflow ("publish from a clean checkout of main") therefore fails from the canonical checkout. The workaround was to create a linked worktree at `origin/main`.

The same guard also blocks `git fetch` in canonical checkouts. That may be intentional (it updates refs), but `check-ignore` only reads `.gitignore` and the index; with `--no-index` it does not read the index at all.

## Expected

Read-only Git subcommands (`check-ignore`, `ls-files`, `rev-parse`, `status`, `log`, `diff`, `show`, `cat-file`) pass through the canonical guard unchanged, both in agent shells and in child processes.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/git` (PATH wrapper)
- `.agents/scripts/canonical-git-command-guard.py` (classification of subcommands as mutating/read-only)
- Regression test alongside existing guard tests under `.agents/scripts/tests/` (path to confirm).

## Verification

In a canonical checkout with the wrapper on PATH: `git check-ignore --no-index -v -- node_modules/x` prints the matching rule and exits 0, and `git check-ignore --quiet -- tracked-file` exits 1 (not the guard's block code). Mutating commands (`checkout`, `reset`, `commit`, `fetch` if intentionally blocked) remain blocked.

title: privacy-guard blocks claim-task-id counter push with an empty findings list
body:
## Observed

`claim-task-id.sh` in a public project repo (counter branch `task-id-counter`, auto-selected) failed on both CAS attempts. The privacy guard's pre-push hook blocked the counter push, but its findings list was **empty**:

```text
[privacy-guard][BLOCK] Push to origin contains private references in public-repo content:



  Remove the private material from the committed content and amend/rewrite the commit before pushing.
...
[ERROR] Pre-push hook failed after 2s with rc=1; remote push was not attempted
[ERROR] UNRECOVERABLE_COUNTER_DESYNC: allocation still failed after refetch/reconcile
```

The commit being pushed contains only `.task-counter` (an integer: 2 → 3), so it has no private content. The helper then reports this as an `UNRECOVERABLE_COUNTER_DESYNC`, which misnames a hook rejection as counter contention.

Workaround used: the issue was created with `gh_create_issue` (no task ID).

## Expected

1. The privacy guard never blocks without naming at least one finding. A block with an empty list is a guard bug: fail open with a warning, or print the matching rule and path.
2. Counter-only commits on the counter branch (`.task-counter` diff only) pass the privacy guard.
3. `claim-task-id.sh` reports a pre-push hook rejection as a hook failure (with the hook's name), not as `UNRECOVERABLE_COUNTER_DESYNC`.

## Likely files

- `.agents/scripts/` privacy-guard pre-push hook (the source of `[privacy-guard][BLOCK]`; locate with `rg -l "privacy-guard\]\[BLOCK" .agents`)
- `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id-counter.sh` (CAS push and the error classification for hook failures)

## Verification

- Reproduce: in a public repo whose counter is on a dedicated `task-id-counter` branch, run `claim-task-id.sh --title "x" --no-issue --dry-run` and then a real claim; the counter push succeeds.
- Force a real privacy finding in a test commit: the block names the finding.
- `shellcheck` on the changed scripts.

title: fix: retry transient GitHub reads in release snapshot provenance verification
body:
## What

Make `release_snapshot_sources` in `.agents/scripts/release-snapshot-helper.sh` retry transient GitHub read failures (bounded, fail-closed), so `aidevops release reconcile` does not fail on one truncated or empty API response.

## Why

During the v3.38.22 release, `aidevops release reconcile 33860` failed in the `release-tag-signature-verification` phase after the Publish Release workflow had already succeeded:

```text
Preparing worktree (detached HEAD 692d907f0c)
unexpected end of JSON input
RELEASE_TIMING phase=release-tag-signature-verification state=finish elapsed_seconds=14 result=failed items=1
```

A read-only `aidevops release status 33860` run immediately afterwards passed the same verification, and a second `reconcile` completed with `release:published tag=v3.38.22`. API budget was not the cause: core 5000/5000 and GraphQL 4960/5000 remaining. The failure was transient, but it used up the workflow's single allowed recovery attempt (`workflows/release.md`).

`unexpected end of JSON input` is Go's `encoding/json` error, so `gh` itself got a truncated or empty body. It did not come from `jq`, and the `release-provenance:` diagnostics from `_release_provenance_read_json` were absent.

Call path (verified):
`full-loop-release-reconcile.sh:401` `_full_loop_release_verify_candidate_tag_provenance` → `:90` `release-provenance-helper.sh verify` → `release-provenance-helper.sh:688` `_release_provenance_verify_aggregate_manifest` → `release_snapshot_sources`.

That function makes two raw `gh` reads per commit in the release range, with no retry:

- `release-snapshot-helper.sh:30`: `gh api --paginate --slurp "repos/${repo}/commits/${commit}/pulls?per_page=100"`
- `release-snapshot-helper.sh:47`: `gh pr view "$pr_number" --repo "$repo" --json state,mergedAt,mergeCommit,baseRefName`

v3.38.22 aggregated 5 PRs, so verification made about 10 such reads.

## Reproducer

Observed once in production; it is a transient, so a live replay is not deterministic. Deterministic reproduction for the fix: stub `gh` in `tests/test-release-snapshot-helper.sh`. On the first call for `repos/<repo>/commits/<sha>/pulls`, print `unexpected end of JSON input` to stderr and exit 1. Then call `release_snapshot_sources`. Current behaviour: it returns 1 immediately with no retry. Expected: it retries, then succeeds on the second attempt.

## Tier

`tier:standard`: the files and reference pattern are verified below.

## How

Reference pattern: `_release_provenance_read_json` in `.agents/scripts/release-provenance-helper.sh:66-109`. It makes 3 attempts with `sleep $attempt` backoff, retries only on HTTP 5xx or an empty response, prints a `retrying after attempt N/3` diagnostic, fails closed after exhaustion, and treats other failures as non-retryable. You can't call it directly here:

- it requires a single JSON object, but `--paginate --slurp` returns an array;
- `release-snapshot-helper.sh` is sourced on its own by `tests/test-release-snapshot-helper.sh`.

1. In `release-snapshot-helper.sh`, add a small local helper (for example `_release_snapshot_gh_read <purpose> <jq-shape-filter> -- gh-args...`) that mirrors that pattern:
   - retries empty stdout, `HTTP 5xx`, and `gh` JSON decode errors on stderr (`unexpected end of JSON input`, `invalid character`) up to 3 attempts;
   - validates the response shape (array for line 30, object for line 47) before returning;
   - fails immediately on auth, 404 or permission errors.
2. Route both reads (lines 30 and 47) through it. Keep every existing `|| return 1` fail-closed path and the `#aidevops:trust-boundary` jq filter unchanged.
3. Add the same decode-error pattern to the retryable classification in `_release_provenance_read_json` (line 92 branch) so both readers behave the same way.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/release-snapshot-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/release-provenance-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-release-snapshot-helper.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-release-provenance-helper.sh`

Complexity impact: `release_snapshot_sources` is 50 lines today and should shrink slightly. Keep the new helper under the 100-line function gate.

## Acceptance

- A one-off truncated or empty `gh` response in `release_snapshot_sources` is retried and the call succeeds. A persistent one fails closed after 3 attempts with a diagnostic that names what was being read.
- Auth, 404 and permission failures still fail on the first attempt.
- `_release_provenance_read_json` retries `unexpected end of JSON input`.
- Coverage: extend `.agents/scripts/tests/test-release-snapshot-helper.sh` with a `gh` stub (once-transient → success; always-transient → fail after 3; auth → fail after 1). Extend `assert_read_transport` in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-release-provenance-helper.sh` (around lines 170-176) with a decode-error case.
- Checks pass: `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-release-snapshot-helper.sh`, `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-release-provenance-helper.sh`, `shellcheck .agents/scripts/release-snapshot-helper.sh .agents/scripts/release-provenance-helper.sh`, and `complexity-regression-helper.sh check --base origin/main`.

## Context and decisions

- Non-goals: no change to release authority, provenance rules, the trust-boundary filters, or the single-recovery rule in `workflows/release.md`. Retries stay bounded and fail-closed.
- Do not treat every non-zero `gh` exit as transient. Only empty bodies, 5xx, and JSON decode errors qualify.
- Session origin: interactive session releasing v3.38.22 (PRs #33857, #33860; release PR #33862).

title: reap-dead-stamps never reaps dead stamps on closed no-auto-dispatch issues and reports 'No stale interactive claims'
body:
## Observed

On one Linux host, `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/interactive-claims/` holds 60 claim stamps from interactive sessions that ended weeks ago, across three managed repos. Every stamp has a dead owner PID. Most belong to issues that are already **closed**. Spot checks show the closed issues carry `no-auto-dispatch` (an interactive-origin convention in those repos).

The pulse runs `interactive-session-helper.sh reap-dead-stamps` every cycle (`substage:normalize/reap_dead_stamps`). Each cycle `pulse.log` prints `No stale interactive claims.` while the 60 stamps remain. Manual `scan-stale --no-auto-release` lists all 60 as stale.

`interactive-session-helper.sh status` lists all 60 as active claims, with no liveness indication.

## Root cause

`.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper-scan.sh`, `_isc_scan_dead_stamps_phase` (auto-release branch):

```bash
_isc_has_label "$issue" "$slug" "no-auto-dispatch" || label_rc=$?
[[ $label_rc -eq 0 || $label_rc -eq 2 ]] && continue
```

The `no-auto-dispatch` lockdown gate fails closed for every issue, including **closed** issues. A dead-owner stamp on a closed issue protects nothing, but it is never reaped. These `continue` skips are not counted, so the summary line reports `No stale interactive claims.` even when every stamp was skipped.

## Proposed fix

1. In the auto-release branch, check issue state first using the existing `_isc_issue_is_closed` in `interactive-session-helper.sh`. For a closed issue with a dead owner and no recoverable worktree progress (`_isc_worktree_has_recoverable_progress` returns 1), delete the stamp with `_isc_delete_stamp`. Do not change labels or assignees, so a closed issue's `no-auto-dispatch` and status labels stay as they are.
2. Keep the existing fail-closed `no-auto-dispatch` skip for **open** issues.
3. Count skipped stamps and report them, e.g. `No releasable stale claims (N skipped: no-auto-dispatch=X, progress=Y, lookup-failed=Z).`, so the pulse log stops implying zero stale stamps.
4. Optional: in `status`, mark entries whose PID is dead (reuse `_is_process_alive_and_matches`) instead of presenting them as active.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper-scan.sh` — `_isc_scan_dead_stamps_phase`, `_isc_cmd_reap_dead_stamps`
- `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper.sh` — `_isc_issue_is_closed` (reuse)
- `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper-stamp.sh` — `_isc_delete_stamp` (reuse)
- `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper-commands.sh` — `status` output (optional item 4)
- Existing test to extend: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-scan-stale-auto-release.sh`

## Verification

- Extend `test-scan-stale-auto-release.sh`: a dead-PID stamp on a closed `no-auto-dispatch` issue is deleted. A dead-PID stamp on an open `no-auto-dispatch` issue is preserved. Neither run edits labels.
- Run `reap-dead-stamps` on a host with stale closed-issue stamps. The stamp directory shrinks, and the summary reports skipped counts.
- ShellCheck clean on the changed files.

title: Bug: full-loop merge refuses authority-metadata read after 60s admission deadline expires on slow but healthy gates
body:
## What

`full-loop-helper.sh merge` fails closed on green, collaborator-authored PRs when the earlier pre-merge gate steps (required-check verification + review-bot gate) take longer than 60 seconds. No GitHub read is attempted; the read is refused locally because a recovery deadline has already expired. Two observed failure messages share this root cause:

- `Merge blocked: unable to verify PR #N authority metadata`
- `Merge blocked: unable to pin fresh PR base/head evidence for prospective TODO validation` (from `_merge_guard_prospective_todo` → `_merge_fetch_pr_refs_rest`)

## Evidence (observed 2026-10-07 by the supervisor pulse, v3.38.23, also present on `main` at 600b2cbaa)

Run 1 and 2 (PR #A in a managed private repo, ~70-80 s after start):

```
[SUCCESS] Remote PR evidence verified at head d5e885ab...; required checks are terminal-success
[INFO] Running review bot gate for PR #A ...
[SUCCESS] Review bot gate: PASS — safe to merge PR #A
[ERROR] Merge blocked: unable to verify PR #A authority metadata
[ERROR] Merge blocked by the pre-merge safety gate.
```

Run 3 (daily sweep, PR #B in a managed private repo, ~110 s after start):

```
[SUCCESS] Remote PR evidence verified at head 70f16865...; required checks are terminal-success
[SUCCESS] Review bot gate: PASS — safe to merge PR #B
[SUCCESS] External/fork authority preflight: no external authority targets for PR #B
[INFO] Merging PR #B (--squash --subject <validated>)...
[ERROR] Merge blocked: unable to pin fresh PR base/head evidence for prospective TODO validation
```

The exact REST read that `_merge_fetch_pr_refs_rest` performs (`gh api repos/<slug>/pulls/<B> --jq '[.base.ref, .base.sha, .head.sha, .base.repo.full_name, .base.repo.clone_url] | @tsv'`) succeeds immediately when run directly. `gh api rate_limit` showed full core quota, so this is not a quota or transport error.

Impact: deterministic auto-merge skips `For #NNN` checkpoint PRs (no closing issue, t2449), so the daily sweep's `full-loop-helper.sh merge` is the only merge path for them, and it fails on every green PR whose gates take > 60 s. Green PRs accumulate unmerged.

## Root cause

`.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh` (line numbers at `main` 600b2cbaa):

- `_merge_pre_merge_gate_with_admission_retry()` (line 2706) wraps the whole pre-merge gate in `_merge_with_admission_retry`, which sets `local _FULL_LOOP_ADMISSION_DEADLINE=$((SECONDS + budget))` with `budget` capped at 60 (lines 65-69, added in c18a3e8a5 / #33774).
- Every nested `_flm_gh_read_once()` (lines 40-55) computes `remaining = _FULL_LOOP_ADMISSION_DEADLINE - SECONDS` and does `[[ "$remaining" -gt 0 ]] || return 1` **before** attempting the read.
- Any read reached after the checks wait and review-bot gate (authority metadata at `_merge_collect_external_authority_gaps`, line 593; PR refs at `_merge_fetch_pr_refs_rest`, line 754) returns 1 without ever calling `gh`.

The 60 s budget was intended to bound *retry waiting after a local-admission deferral*, but it is applied as a wall-clock deadline for the entire gate, including reads that were never deferred.

## Proposed fix

In `_flm_gh_read_once`, only enforce the shared deadline for waiting/retry, not for the first attempt of a fresh read; or scope the deadline in `_merge_with_admission_retry` so it starts counting at the first observed `deferred_by=local_admission` record rather than at gate entry. Either way, a gate that has not seen any deferral must not refuse reads due to elapsed time. Keep the 60 s cap on total *sleep* time. The fix belongs in the shared read path, so both call sites above are covered without per-caller changes.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh:35-114` — `_flm_gh_read`, `_flm_gh_read_once`, `_merge_with_admission_retry` only. Do not read or restructure the rest of the 2822-line file; it is tracked separately by file-size-debt #30748.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-authority-guard.sh` — only if extending it is the cheapest way to prove the fix (it already stubs `_flm_gh_read`).

Context only (do not edit): `full-loop-helper-merge.sh:2706` (`_merge_pre_merge_gate_with_admission_retry`) shows where the outer deadline is entered.

## Verification

1. `shellcheck .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`
2. Reproduce: with `SECONDS` advanced past the deadline inside `_merge_with_admission_retry` (e.g. stub the gate to `sleep 61` before the read), a fresh read must still execute once.
3. Existing `tests/test-full-loop-merge-authority-guard.sh` and merge admission tests still pass.
4. Live: `full-loop-helper.sh merge <green collaborator PR> <slug> --squash` where checks+review gate take > 60 s now proceeds past the authority and prospective-TODO reads.

title: scope-guard-pre-push: exact bracketed Files Scope paths (Astro [slug] routes) never match themselves
body:
## Problem

`scope-guard-pre-push.sh` and the canonical Files Scope rule disagree about bracketed paths.

- `.agents/scripts/brief_scope.py` `exact()` accepts `[` and `]` in canonical Files Scope paths and rejects `*`. The readiness gate (`brief-readiness-helper.sh`, `files-scope:canonical`) therefore requires exact paths such as `apps/site/src/pages/[practice]/services/[slug].astro`, the normal file names for Astro, Next.js and SvelteKit dynamic routes.
- `.agents/hooks/scope-guard-pre-push.sh` `_file_in_scope()` (around line 250) compares with `[[ "$_file" == $_pattern ]]`. Bash treats `[practice]` as a character class, so an exact bracketed path never matches itself. Any worker whose canonical-valid scope lists a dynamic route gets its push blocked as out of scope when the scope guard is installed.

## Evidence

A standalone reproduction of `_file_in_scope` matching:

```text
NO MATCH pattern=apps/x/[practice].astro          file=apps/x/[practice].astro
match    pattern=apps/x/\[practice\].astro        file=apps/x/[practice].astro
```

A brief using escaped or glob forms (`\[practice\]`, `?practice?`, `dir/*`) fails `check-readiness` with `files-scope:canonical`. No Files Scope form passes both gates for bracketed paths.

## Proposed fix

In `_file_in_scope`, test a literal match first (`[[ "$_file" == "$_pattern" ]]`, quoted), then keep the existing glob match for patterns that contain `*` or `?`. This keeps glob support and makes every canonical exact path match itself.

## Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/hooks/scope-guard-pre-push.sh` — `_file_in_scope`.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-scope-guard-pre-push.sh` — add a case where the Files Scope lists a bracketed dynamic-route path: pushing that exact file passes, and a same-length plain path stays out of scope.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/hooks/scope-guard-pre-push.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-scope-guard-pre-push.sh`

## Verification

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-scope-guard-pre-push.sh
shellcheck .agents/hooks/scope-guard-pre-push.sh
```

## Acceptance

- [ ] An exact bracketed path in Files Scope matches the same file in the push diff.
- [ ] A literal bracket pattern no longer matches single-character file names (for example `apps/x/p.astro` against `apps/x/[practice].astro`).
- [ ] Existing glob patterns (`.agents/hooks/*.sh`) still match.

Observed while filing schema-v2 briefs for Astro template work in a managed project repo; that repo does not install the scope guard, so it was not blocked there.

## Task

  - release the worktree afterwards.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-quality-debt.sh:166-179` — `_enrichment_resolve_repo_path` keeps returning the canonical path, used only as the worktree source.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `dispatch_enrichment_workers` (`pulse-quality-debt.sh:403`), called from `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh:147` and `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh:845`.

Rollback: revert the PR; no state to undo, because `fast-fail-counter.json` keys are unchanged.

1. Choose the worktree mechanism used by pulse worker launch (reuse, do not invent). Record the choice in the PR body.
2. Wrap the `headless-runtime-helper.sh run` call with the env contract and the worktree `--dir`.

title: t18608: fix(fast-fail): worker-side failures never flag enrichment_needed
body:
**Task ID:** `t18608` | **Status:** open
**Tags:** `auto-dispatch` `bug` `pulse`

## Outcome

fix(fast-fail): worker-side failures never flag enrichment_needed

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## Task


When a worker records its own first non-rate-limit failure for an issue through `_report_failure_to_fast_fail`, the fast-fail entry must get `enrichment_needed=true` for enrichment-relevant reasons. This matches the pulse-side `fast_fail_record` behaviour. The pulse enrichment pre-pass then analyses these issues.

## Done when

- [ ] A first worker-side failure with an allow-listed reason sets `enrichment_needed=true` in the fast-fail state.
- [ ] The worker-side writer carries the enrichment flag.
- [ ] Negative: `worker_post_pr_handoff_unverified` never sets the flag, and an entry with `enrichment_done=true` is never re-flagged (covered by the new test case).
- [ ] `shellcheck` is clean; the existing fast-fail tests pass.

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/headless-runtime-failure.sh:1668-1720` — `_fast_fail_write_state`: accept an optional 10th argument `set_enrichment` (`true|false`, default `false`). When `true`, add `| .[$k].enrichment_needed = true` to the jq program, but only if `.[$k].enrichment_done != true`.

title: pulse dep-graph: structured 'Blocked by:' line extracts task IDs from prose (e.g. 'nothing … (t1–t9) are independent'), creating dependency cycles; edited-away blockers never re-promote
body:
## What happened

A batch of 11 independent auto-dispatch tasks in a managed private repo never dispatched. Every brief (and so every composed issue body) contained:

```markdown
- **Blocked by:** nothing. The 11 template tasks (t139–t149) are independent and may run in parallel.
- **Blocked by:** none (t136 and t138 merged).
```

`_blocked_by_structured_lines` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph.sh:57`) accepts any line that starts with the `**Blocked by:**` field label. `task_identity_extract_all` then collects **every** task ID on that line. So each issue parsed as blocked by `t139 t149 t136 t138`. After self-edge removal, t139 waited on t149, t149 waited on t139, and t140–t148 waited on both: a permanent cycle.

`pulse.log`, repeated every cycle:

```text
is_blocked_by_unresolved: #A blocked by t149 (live: open) — skipping dispatch (t1927)
is_blocked_by_unresolved: #B blocked by t139=#A (cache: open) — skipping dispatch (t1935)
```

`_refresh_ensure_unresolved_is_blocked` then moved the issues from `status:available` to `status:blocked`.

Related: GH#33166 (structured-line parser introduced), GH#33414 (closed; prose `Blocked by #N` treated as an edge). This is a new variant: the field label is structured, but the value is prose.

## Second defect: no re-promotion after blockers are edited away

After the brief and body text were fixed (`Blocked by:` → `none.`), the issues had no body blockers, no `blocked-by:*` labels and 0 native `blocked_by` relationships. They still stayed `status:blocked`. `refresh_blocked_status_from_graph` (and so `normalize_repo_dependency_readiness`) only iterates `blocked_by` map keys. An issue with no remaining blockers drops out of the map and is never promoted back. A guarded manual label edit was needed.

## Suggested fix

1. In `_blocked_by_structured_lines` / `_blocked_by_extract_tids`, treat the field value as a reference list only:
   - Stop at the first token that is not a task ID, `#N`, a separator (`,`, `and`, whitespace) or backticks.
   - Or explicitly yield nothing when the value starts with `none|nothing|n/a|—`.
   - Prose after the list should not contribute edges.
2. Make the refresh pass also visit open issues labelled `status:blocked` with `auto-dispatch` whose fresh graph entry has no blockers. Promote them to `status:available` through the existing `_refresh_try_unblock_issue` gate, which keeps the non-dependency defer markers authoritative.
3. Optionally, have `verify-brief-helper.sh check-readiness` warn when a `Blocked by:` value contains task IDs alongside negation words.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph.sh`: `_blocked_by_structured_lines` (line 57), `_blocked_by_extract_tids` (line 947), `refresh_blocked_status_from_graph` (line 792), `_dep_graph_process_issue_json` (line 89).
- Reference pattern: the GH#33414 fix in the dep-graph reducer.

## Verification

- Source `pulse-dep-graph.sh` and run `_blocked_by_extract_tids` on a body containing the two lines above. It should return nothing (currently `t139 t149 t136 t138`).
- `**Blocked by:** \`t123\`, #4` and `blocked-by:t1,t2` must still parse as today.
- Fixture: an issue labelled `status:blocked` + `auto-dispatch` with no blockers in its body or natively becomes `status:available` after one `refresh_blocked_status_from_graph` pass. One with a non-dependency defer marker stays blocked.

title: brief-readiness-helper.sh is nondeterministic: pipefail + 'printf | grep -q' SIGPIPE flips readiness (WORKER_READY=false, SCHEMA=legacy) on large briefs
body:
## What happened

On the merge push, the `issue-sync` workflow (Ubicloud standard-2 runner, aidevops `main`) failed planning publication for one of 11 tasks:

```text
[WARNING] tNNN/#N: auto-dispatch brief is not worker-ready; retaining publication:pending
PUBLICATION_RECONCILE_SUMMARY reconciled=7 deferred=0 stale=0 failed=1 unmapped=0
```

The same brief passed `verify-brief-helper.sh check-readiness` locally every time it was checked (score 5/4, schema v2, no validation errors). The upstream and installed copies of the brief-validation scripts were identical (`compare v3.38.23...main` showed no changes to brief/readiness/scope/publication files).

## Root cause: `pipefail` + `grep -q` SIGPIPE race

`.agents/scripts/brief-readiness-helper.sh:35` sets `set -euo pipefail`. The helper then tests the whole ~48 KB brief body with patterns like:

```bash
printf '%s\n' "$body" | grep -qiF "$heading"           # line 102 (_score_body)
printf '%s\n' "$unfenced" | grep -qF "$BRIEF_SCHEMA_V2_MARKER"   # line 117 (_is_schema_v2_brief)
printf '%s\n' "$acceptance" | grep -E ... | grep -qiE ...        # lines 375-376
```

When `grep -q` matches early (the schema marker is near the top) and exits, a `printf` that is still writing receives SIGPIPE. Under `pipefail` the pipeline returns 141, which is read as "no match". The result depends on scheduling, so slow or shared runners hit it more often.

## Local reproduction

60 identical runs of `brief-readiness-helper.sh check --body "$(<brief)"` on one unchanged brief:

```text
  58  WORKER_READY=true  SCORE=5 THRESHOLD=4 SCHEMA=v2     VALIDATION_ERRORS=none
   1  WORKER_READY=true  SCORE=4 THRESHOLD=4 SCHEMA=v2     VALIDATION_ERRORS=none
   1  WORKER_READY=false SCORE=3 THRESHOLD=4 SCHEMA=legacy VALIDATION_ERRORS=not-applicable
```

A second brief over 80 runs gave 75 correct, 4 × score 4 and 1 × `SCHEMA=legacy`. Across an 11-brief publication batch, the chance that some brief flips is substantial. The same helper also gates dispatch, so a flip there would block a worker spuriously.

## Suggested fix

Avoid early-exit readers on a pipe under `pipefail`. Use here-strings or `[[ ... ]]` matching instead:

```bash
grep -qF "$BRIEF_SCHEMA_V2_MARKER" <<<"$unfenced"
```

Alternatively, drop `-q` and redirect to `/dev/null` so `grep` reads all input. Apply this to every `printf … | grep -q` in `brief-readiness-helper.sh`, and audit sibling validators (`verify-brief-helper.sh`, `planning-publication-reconcile.sh` callers) for the same pattern. A ShellCheck-adjacent ratchet for `| grep -q` under `pipefail` would stop it returning.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/brief-readiness-helper.sh`: lines 35, 102, 117, 199, 216, 219, 252, 262, 272, 375–376, 642.
- Reference: `reference/shell-style-guide.md` (pipeline safety).

## Verification

Run the helper 200× on a large (~50 KB) schema-v2 brief. Every run should produce identical output (currently ~3% vary). Add a load source (`stress` or parallel invocations) to make the race visible before the fix.

#33875 (`origin:worker`, assigned to the runner after a 06:31 dispatch attempt):

- 06:21:55: `needs-simplification` was added by the large-file gate.
- 06:48:41: `_post_simplification_gate_cleared_comment` posted "The `needs-simplification` label has been removed".
- The timeline has no `unlabeled needs-simplification` event. The label was still present 3 h later and blocked dispatch, and pulse.log shows only the idempotent marker skip on later cycles.

## Root cause

`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-large-file-gate.sh:141-150`: the precheck short-circuits `origin:worker` issues that have an assignee with `return 1` ("no gate"). The GH#31678 guard at lines 133-140 already returns 2 during `force_recheck` when the label is present, but only for `status:queued` / `status:in-progress`. The assigned branch has no equivalent guard.

`.agents/scripts/pulse-triage-evaluation.sh:644-648` (`_reevaluate_simplification_labels`) treats any return 1 from `_issue_targets_large_files` as "label cleared" and posts the CLEARED comment, but `_large_file_gate_clear_stale_label` never ran on this path.

## Fix

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-large-file-gate.sh:141-150` — apply the same rule as lines 135-138: when `force_recheck == true` and the label is present, return 2 instead of 1 for assigned `origin:worker` issues. This branch then matches the documented GH#31678 contract.
- Optional hardening: EDIT `.agents/scripts/pulse-triage-evaluation.sh:644-648` to post CLEARED only after the label is verified absent (the same check as `_large_file_gate_clear_stale_label` at `pulse-dispatch-large-file-gate.sh:918-926`).

1. `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-large-file-gate.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-triage-evaluation.sh`
2. `tests/test-reeval-stale-continuation.sh` and `tests/test-dispatch-lifecycle-comms.sh` pass.
3. Case to cover: an assigned `origin:worker` issue with `needs-simplification` under forced re-eval gets no CLEARED comment and keeps its label unless `_large_file_gate_clear_stale_label` succeeds.

In a private project, the primary repeatedly reported a dependency-audit blocker while a reviewed, narrow lockfile repair was already available. # GH#33891: Fix NixOS PATH and native tool discovery

Issue: https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/33891

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: NixOS PATH/native binary — no matching lessons.
- [x] Discovery pass: native-Git merge checks recently changed; current patch preserves them. No matching open PATH PR was found by prework discovery. Existing source-access changes fix approvals, not NixOS executable selection.
- [x] File refs verified: existing targets read in the linked worktree; new runtime helpers have verified parent directories.
- [x] Tier: thinking — shared launch plumbing and privileged source-access tool selection require a trust-preserving cross-runtime review.
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision: skipped; implement in the owning interactive session, then publish the verified patch.

## Origin

- Created: 2026-10-07
- Created by: interactive session, at the operator's request
- Target repository: marcusquinn/aidevops
- Assignee: vladimirdulov
- Conversation context: a screenshot showed native Git at `/run/current-system/sw/bin/git`, while the merge helper defaulted to `/usr/bin/git`. The operator requests TODO, brief, assigned issue, implementation, commit, push, PR loop, and merge. No release publication is requested.

## Reproducer

On NixOS, `type -a -p git` lists aidevops Git wrappers followed by
`/run/current-system/sw/bin/git`, with no `/usr/bin/git`. The full-loop merge
helper's default native-Git path fails even though Git is installed. Starting a
helper with a minimal scheduler PATH similarly loses Nix-installed tools.
`test-runtime-env.sh` reproduces a shim-only inherited PATH and proves recovery
from synthetic Nix profiles without changing the host filesystem.

## What

Recover stable Nix profile PATH entries at shared shell, OpenCode plugin, and scheduler/service boundaries. Discover native Git without selecting framework wrappers. Remove FHS-only executable assumptions from the identified source-access and team-interface entrypoints, keeping approval and project-root validation unchanged.

## Why

Per-command native-Git overrides only hide the immediate failure. Non-login processes also lose other Nix-installed tools, and privileged code must not solve portability by trusting caller-controlled executables.

## How

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/runtime-env.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/git`
- `.agents/scripts/canonical-recovery-helper.sh`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/runtime-path.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/shell-env.mjs`
- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/schedulers-pulse.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/opencode_service_lifecycle.py`
- `.agents/scripts/source_access_core.py`
- `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/source-access.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/team-interface-buzz-worktree.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/team-interface-opencode-project-root.mjs`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-runtime-env.sh`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-shell-env-origin.mjs`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test_opencode_service.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-source-access-helper.py`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-setup-source-access-broker.sh`
- `.agents/reference/platform-support.md`
- `TODO.md`
- `todo/tasks/gh33891-brief.md`
- `todo/research/nixos-command-lookup.md`

### Reference Pattern

Follow `shared-constants.sh` shared initialization, `shell-env.mjs` guard/project PATH precedence, and `opencode_service_lifecycle.py` isolated service environments. The source-access setup module is signed standalone code: keep its system-tool lookup self-contained, and preserve its signed-release verification and non-TTY privilege refusal.

### Files to Modify

- `NEW: .agents/scripts/runtime-env.sh` — stable profiles and shim-safe native Git resolution.
- `NEW: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/runtime-path.mjs` — shared plugin subprocess PATH recovery.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/source_access_core.py` — fixed trusted system roots for Git and SSH keygen, never caller PATH.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/setup/modules/source-access.sh` — self-contained trusted system lookup for signed broker setup commands.
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/team-interface-buzz-worktree.sh` and `.agents/scripts/team-interface-opencode-project-root.mjs` — trusted Nix system Git probes.
- Other explicitly listed Files Scope targets integrate those helpers, provide scoped regression evidence, and record the issue/PR lifecycle.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `full-loop-helper-merge.sh`, `canonical-recovery-helper.sh`, `shell-env.mjs`, `schedulers-pulse.sh`, `opencode_service_lifecycle.py`, `source_access_core.py`, source-access setup and team-interface validators.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `shell-env.mjs` and service/scheduler environment construction; source-access setup writes stay behind existing signature, ownership, consent and privilege checks.
- **Existing verification/tests:** listed `.agents/scripts/tests/` and plugin tests exercise command discovery, Git guards, service isolation, approval security and project/worktree bindings.
- **Schemas/config:** `opencode_service_state.py` retains its current service schema and identity; source-access approval formats are unchanged.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** `.agents/` ships to deployed agents/runtime bundles; existing services require definition regeneration and running processes retain original environments. No deployed files are hand-edited.
- **Migrations/backfills:** no schema migration; regenerate definitions from `schedulers-pulse.sh` and `opencode_service_lifecycle.py` only after authorized deployment.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert this patch and regenerate service definitions; retain `source-access.sh` staged cleanup. Do not revoke consent, delete databases, or alter privileged trust material.

### Implementation Steps

1. Finish shared profile recovery and shim-safe Git selection in `runtime-env.sh`; integrate it at shared shell, plugin and scheduler/service boundaries without changing precedence.
2. Replace security-sensitive FHS executable literals with fixed-system-root lookup in source-access and team-interface code, keeping caller PATH/overrides out of privileged selection.
3. Run the focused commands below, review trust-boundary changes independently, and record coverage limits. Commit, push, open the linked PR, resolve actionable findings, and merge without publishing a release.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** preserve source-access staged signed-byte verification, worktree ownership checks, and isolated service environments. No new persistent coordination or concurrent state mutation is introduced.
- **Migration/rollback:** service schemas and approval formats remain unchanged; revert source and regenerate PATH definitions for rollback, leaving trust material and history intact.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** runtime bundles must include new sibling helpers; preserve macOS/FHS system precedence and use stable Nix profile aliases rather than generation paths.
- **Idempotency/retry:** repeated profile recovery adds no duplicates; preserve explicit native-Git overrides, guard/project precedence, and current retry behavior.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** missing trusted system tools fail closed. Preserve staging cleanup and non-TTY sudo refusal; do not install packages, create compatibility symlinks, or select privileged tools through caller PATH.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-runtime-env.sh
python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test_opencode_service.py
node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/test-shell-env-origin.mjs
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-canonical-git-command-guard.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-systemd-timeout.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-launchd-sanitized-path.sh
python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-source-access-helper.py
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-setup-source-access-broker.sh
node --test .agents/scripts/tests/test-team-interface-buzz-worktree.mjs .agents/scripts/tests/test-team-interface-opencode-overlay.mjs
bash .agents/scripts/linters-local.sh
```

- **Surface mapping:** runtime-env and plugin tests prove profile recovery/precedence; service tests prove serialization and isolated launch; Git guard tests prove policy preservation; scheduler tests prove PATH defaults; source-access tests prove signed/privileged boundaries; team-interface tests prove project/worktree binding. Changed-file lint covers every edited source.
- **Coverage limit:** a real NixOS host is not available in this runner. Verify minimal-PATH/profile behavior and trusted system-tool selection with focused regressions and record that limitation. Run independent trust-boundary review before PR readiness.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Shared launch environments recover installed tools from stable Nix profile roots without replacing guards or project-selected versions; repeated initialization does not duplicate roots.
- [ ] Merge/recovery native Git resolution skips framework wrappers and preserves explicit operator overrides and all Git policy gates.
- [ ] Source-access tooling works with trusted Nix system binaries and never chooses caller-controlled PATH executables or expands automatic sudo authority.
- [ ] Team-interface project/worktree validation no longer requires `/usr/bin/git`, retaining repository and host/agent ownership validation.
- [ ] Focused checks, changed-file quality gates, and independent trust-boundary review pass; baseline-only failures and real-host coverage limits are recorded honestly.
- [ ] TODO and brief link the issue assigned to vladimirdulov; a verified PR is committed, pushed, reviewed and merged, without release publication.

## Recoverability

Commit a recoverable implementation checkpoint before broad gates. On a safety stop preserve exact head, unfinished criteria, next safe command and the linked issue/PR. Keep the issue open until the scoped fix is verified and merged.

## Out of Scope

Full NixOS packaging support for every third-party downloaded application, installation of missing tools, global NixOS configuration changes, publication/release, and unrelated baseline runtime-discovery test repairs.
