title: interactive claim fails and leaves mixed ownership when status:available issue keeps a stale foreign assignee
body:
## What

`interactive-session-helper.sh claim` (via `interactive-start-helper.sh --issue N`) fails closed with
`claim: ownership transition on #N could not be verified; no stamp written` when an issue is
`status:available` (no active status label) but still lists a **stale foreign assignee** — and it
leaves the issue half-mutated (`status:claimed` + two assignees).

## Observed (2026-10-07, #30748)

- Before: labels `status:available`, assignees `[vladimirdulov]` (worker claim released 2026-08-25).
- `interactive-start-helper.sh --issue 30748 --repo marcusquinn/aidevops ...` → error above.
- After: labels `status:claimed`, assignees `[vladimirdulov, marcusquinn]`.
- Recovery: `interactive-session-helper.sh claim 30748 marcusquinn/aidevops --implementing` classified it
  `foreign-worker` and removed the stale assignee; the start helper then succeeded.

## Root cause

`.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper-commands.sh`:

- `_isc_claim_ownership_class` (~L161) returns `unclaimed` whenever no active status label is present,
  even if foreign assignees remain.
- The `unclaimed` path (caller ~L452) calls `_isc_apply_new_claim` with only `--add-assignee "$user"`;
  stale assignees are never removed.
- `_isc_verified_caller_owns_claim` (~L188) then requires `assignees == [$user]` and fails.

## How (worker guidance)

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper-commands.sh`
- In the `unclaimed` path, when assignees other than `$user` remain on an issue with no active status
  label and no live interactive claim comment (same 2h window `_isc_claim_ownership_class` already
  computes), pass `--remove-assignee <login>` for each, mirroring `_isc_take_over_worker_claim` (~L227).
  Keep `foreign-interactive:*` refusal unchanged.
- Alternatively roll back the partial label/assignee mutation when verification fails, so the issue is
  not left `status:claimed` with mixed ownership.
- Verify: existing claim tests (`rg -l "_isc_claim_ownership_class|interactive-session-helper" .agents/scripts/tests`)
  plus a reproduction on a fixture issue state `status:available` + foreign assignee.
### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper-commands.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-interactive-session-claim.sh`

Verification: existing claim and interactive-start fixture suites plus ShellCheck on both scoped files.

title: Prospective merge HTTPS fetch falls through to macOS Keychain instead of managed credentials
body:
## What

Fix managed GitHub authentication for the prospective TODO merge guard so its native HTTPS fetches do not fall through to macOS Keychain or other interactive credential helpers. Use the approved managed credential source, including gopass-backed credentials, and fail clearly and non-interactively when authentication is unavailable.

## Origin and environment

- Reported by an operator after a macOS dialog said `git-credential-osxkeychain` wanted access to the `github.com` Keychain item during a full-loop merge.
- Observed on aidevops v3.38.23 in OpenCode v1.18.35 on macOS, 2026-10-07.
- The application worktree uses an SSH origin; GitHub CLI configuration also selects SSH. GitHub API reads already work.
- Native Git inherits Apple's system `credential.helper=osxkeychain`; there is no GitHub-specific credential-helper override in the inspected configuration.
- Gopass is installed and initialized. The operator expects managed credentials to come from gopass. This investigation did not decrypt or independently verify a GitHub token entry; the confirmed defect is the native fetch's uncontrolled credential routing, not proof that a particular gopass token is valid.
- Application repository names, PR numbers, local account paths, customer details, and credentials are deliberately omitted.

## Evidence

The recorded session establishes the following sequence:

1. `full-loop-helper.sh merge <PR> <OWNER/REPO> --squash` passes the review/check gates, prints `Merging PR ...`, then stalls. The interactive shell terminates it after 120 seconds.
2. A bounded retry fails before the merge write with:

```text
fatal: failed to get: -128
fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': Device not configured
[ERROR] Merge blocked: unable to materialize pinned PR commits for prospective TODO validation
```

3. The same session retries with a process-local Git configuration that first resets the inherited credential-helper list, then installs the existing native `gh auth git-credential` helper:

```text
GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0
GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=2
GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=credential.helper
GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=
GIT_CONFIG_KEY_1=credential.helper
GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_1=!<NATIVE_GH_BIN> auth git-credential
```

The merge and subsequent canonical synchronization then succeed. No persistent Git credential configuration was changed by that workaround. This validates the credential-routing failure; it does not establish that gh's existing credential is gopass-backed.

## Root cause and current upstream verification

The deployed generation contains the prospective-fetch functions in `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`. Current upstream has extracted them into `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge-prospective.sh`; the relevant behavior remains present in the upstream source inspected during reporting.

Current upstream references:

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge-prospective.sh:54-77`: `_merge_fetch_pr_refs_rest` reads `.base.repo.clone_url`, and `_merge_validate_target_remote_url` requires an HTTPS URL for the exact target host/repository. This is independent of the caller's SSH origin and gh's configured Git protocol.
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge-prospective.sh:224-239`: `_merge_fetch_partial_objects` invokes native Git through `_merge_run_bounded_isolated_git` to fetch into a separate bare object store.
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge-prospective.sh:381-399`: the native fetch wrappers preserve ambient system/global credential configuration and do not establish managed authentication.
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge-prospective.sh:402-413`: `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` exists in the config-isolated wrapper, but that wrapper is for non-transfer commands, not these explicit fetches. Even on the fetch path, this variable alone would not suppress an OS credential helper's GUI dialog.
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`: `_merge_guard_prospective_todo` creates the object context and calls the pinned-commit fetch during transport-authority revalidation, before the actual merge mutation.

Consequently, the native HTTPS fetch can invoke `git-credential-osxkeychain` despite successful SSH and GitHub API authentication. It also bypasses the PATH Git shim, so a change only in `.agents/scripts/git` cannot fully fix this defect.

## Pre-flight and deduplication

- Memory recall for prospective merge / HTTPS / osxkeychain / gopass returned no relevant entries.
- All-state upstream issue searches for `osxkeychain` and `prospective credential` found no matching credential-routing fix. An all-state PR search for `credential prospective` found the prior object-transfer fix, not an authentication fix.
- Related prior work: issues #32641, #33513, and #33752; merged PR #32659. Preserve their object-transfer bounds, missing-object handling, and supported-Git-version behavior.
- Verified the current upstream prospective library and the existing merge/secret test filenames through the repository contents/tree API, rather than assuming the deployed monolithic layout still matches HEAD.
- Seeded draft PR: skipped; this is an upstream bug report with observed evidence, not a locally implemented fix.
- Tier: thinking. Credential-source precedence and host/account scoping need explicit security review, and this code is on the worker/merge execution path.

## How

### Files to Modify

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge-prospective.sh`: establish explicit managed authentication for native HTTPS fetches.
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`: adjust orchestration only if needed to supply that authentication context.
- `.agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh`: verified reference for managed secret injection and unavailable-secret behavior; modify only if an actual shared capability gap requires it.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-authority-guard.sh` and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge.sh`: existing verification entry points; select the narrowest appropriate current test file after inspecting fixtures.
- Any new shared credential-bridge path is not yet known; discover and name it in the implementation PR. Do not patch installed runtime bundles directly.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** interactive full-loop merges and Pulse/non-repository callers of the prospective guard; native Git fetch children must receive the managed auth context.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** Git fetch materializes temporary objects; the credential bridge must not persist tokens or invoke credential `store`/`erase` against OS Keychain.
- **Existing verification/tests:** existing merge-authority/merge tests and secret-helper tests; no new runner or broad test infrastructure is needed.
- **Schemas/config:** prefer process-local, host-scoped configuration. No automatic global Git rewrite, SSH migration, credential migration, or deletion of Keychain items.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** normal aidevops deployment/runtime-bundle generation owns installed copies; source changes belong in the framework repository.
- **Migrations/backfills:** none required for the observed bug; do not turn this fix into a token migration.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** retain existing temporary-store cleanup and cancellation handling; make authentication state process-owned and disposable. Reverting the source change must not leave altered user Git configuration.

### Implementation Steps

1. Reverify the current split source and existing managed-auth patterns before editing.
2. Supply explicit managed credentials for the validated target host/repository on every prospective-fetch path, using environment/subprocess injection rather than secrets in arguments or URLs.
3. Reset inherited credential helpers before installing the approved helper, so `osxkeychain` cannot run first or receive a token through credential approval/storage.
4. Fail promptly with an actionable, redacted diagnostic if the managed credential is missing, locked, or unusable. Never silently fall back to an OS keyring or interactive prompt.
5. Preserve exact repository/host/head binding, authority/review gates, bounded partial fetches, and lazy-fetch prevention. Do not bypass prospective validation as an authentication workaround.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** process-local auth must not alter credentials for sibling sessions or other repositories.
- **Migration/rollback:** no persistent user configuration or secret-store changes as a side effect of merging.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** retain supported Git versions, Linux behavior, public-repository fetches, and explicit GH_HOST handling. Do not assume a fixed Homebrew installation path.
- **Idempotency/retry:** authentication errors must not trigger blind merge-write retries or credential-helper loops.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** preserve temporary-object cleanup, cancellation, and missing/locked-secret fail-closed behavior.
- **Security/privacy:** do not emit tokens in logs, argv, tracing, URLs, public issue comments, or test fixtures. The gh helper workaround is not sufficient by itself unless gh explicitly receives the managed token instead of sourcing its own OS keyring.

### Verification Before Dispatch

Reporting verified the installed code, current upstream source, safe credential configuration, and the failed/successful commands from the same recorded session. No new live merge or credential decryption was performed by the reporting session.

## Acceptance and Verification

- With an inherited `osxkeychain` helper and an SSH application origin, a prospective private-repository fetch uses the approved managed credential and never invokes the OS helper.
- Focused coverage in the existing shell test suite proves the inherited helper is not executed, including credential approval/storage; use fake helpers and synthetic tokens, not a GUI prompt or a live merge mutation.
- A missing/locked managed credential yields a bounded, redacted failure with no terminal or Keychain prompt.
- The explicit native-Git path works from both a linked worktree and a non-Git Pulse workspace.
- Existing host/repository pinning, exact-head authority, partial-fetch bounds, lazy-fetch prevention, and cleanup checks remain passing.
- Run ShellCheck on changed shell sources and the narrowest existing affected tests. Document actual commands/results in the PR.

title: gh-checks-wait-helper: name missing required contexts and hint rerun when GitHub never created the job
body:
### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/gh-checks-wait-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-checks-wait-helper.sh`

### Integration scope recovery

The existing test at `.agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-checks-wait-helper.sh` already covers configured-but-unreported contexts (the `configured_missing_output` fixture). Include this adjacent path to implement the requested extension without introducing a harness. The assigned worker verified the issue remains open and assigned, the brief has no explicit hard exclusion, and prework discovery found no colliding open PR for this test. Preserve PR #33941. Verify with `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-gh-checks-wait-helper.sh`, ShellCheck on the changed scripts, and `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed`.

## Reproducer

1. A PR whose base branch requires context `X`, where the workflow run producing `X` completes without ever creating the job named `X` (observed: run 37642182581, workflow `qlty-regression.yml`, job `Qlty Regression Gate` absent, run conclusion `failure`).
2. All other required contexts pass.
3. Run `full-loop-helper.sh merge <PR> <repo>`: plain merge fails with "base branch policy prohibits the merge", then the admin-fallback re-check prints `TIMEOUT: required checks remain non-terminal after 5s (pass=5)` and `LIFECYCLE_STATE=CHECKS_PENDING`, without naming `X`.
4. `full-loop-helper.sh wait-checks <PR>` stays pending until its budget expires.

## Observed

PR #33906 merge via `full-loop-helper.sh merge` failed twice with:

```
TIMEOUT: required checks remain non-terminal after 5s (pass=5)
LIFECYCLE_STATE=CHECKS_PENDING required checks are not terminal on the verified PR head; refusing admin fallback
```

All five *reported* required checks passed. The real cause: branch protection on `main` also requires `Qlty Regression Gate`, and that context never existed on the PR head. Workflow run 37642182581 (`.github/workflows/qlty-regression.yml`) ran `Detect PR scope` and `Qlty Smell Regression` successfully, but GitHub never created the `required-check` job (name `Qlty Regression Gate`) and concluded the run `failure` with only two jobs (`jobs?filter=all` total_count=2). `full-loop-helper.sh wait-checks` would have waited until timeout. `gh run rerun 37642182581` created the job, it passed, and the merge then succeeded.

The decision is correct (fail closed). The diagnostics are not: `pass=5` with no missing name reads as a contradiction and hides the one-command recovery.

## Fix

In `.agents/scripts/gh-checks-wait-helper.sh`:

1. When `classify_state` returns `pending` because of `configured_context_missing_from_checks` (around `classify_state`, lines ~316-336), surface the missing context names in the initial state, heartbeat, and `TIMEOUT` messages (e.g. `missing=Qlty Regression Gate`). `state_counts` currently counts only reported checks.
2. Optionally, for each missing context, look up the latest workflow run on the PR head whose workflow defines a job with that name. If that run is `completed` and the job is absent, print a recovery hint: `required context '<name>' was never created; workflow run <id> concluded <conclusion> without it - rerun: gh run rerun <id> --repo <repo>`. Keep it a hint; never rerun automatically from the admin-fallback path.

`.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh` `_merge_admin_fallback_required_checks_clear` (around line 1104) only needs to pass through the improved message.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/gh-checks-wait-helper.sh`
- Use the existing test override `AIDEVOPS_GH_CHECKS_TEST_REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` with a stubbed rollup lacking one configured context, and confirm the output names the missing context. Extend an existing gh-checks-wait test if one covers `configured_context_missing_from_checks`; do not add a new harness.
- `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed`

- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** delete `.github/workflows/pipe-early-exit-check.yml` to disable the gate; `.agents/scripts/pipe-early-exit-check.sh` and the style-guide section are inert without it.

### Implementation Steps

1. Read `.agents/scripts/counter-stack-check.sh` and `.github/workflows/counter-stack-check.yml`; copy their structure and option names.
2. Detection (line-based is acceptable): flag a line that pipes into `grep` with `-q`/`--quiet`/`-m 1`, or into `head`, when the file enables pipefail (`set -o pipefail` or a `set -…o pipefail` combined flag). Skip comment lines, here-string forms (`grep -q … <<<"$x"`), and files with the disable directive.
3. `--fix-hint` prints the allowed patterns: `grep -qF -- "$needle" <<<"$haystack"`; or capture to a variable first, then test; or `{ writer || true; } | grep -q` only when the writer's status is genuinely irrelevant.
4. Workflow: run on `pull_request` for changed `*.sh` files only; fail only on findings on lines the PR adds (`git diff -U0` against the base); post/update one sticky comment.
5. Style-guide section: banned pattern, allowed patterns, one-paragraph mechanism, enforcement pointer, and originating incidents #27981, #30824, #33882.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** N/A with evidence: read-only scanner; concurrent PR runs only update their own PR's sticky comment.
- **Migration/rollback:** the workflow, checker and doc section land in one PR; reverting it removes the gate with no residual state.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** judge added lines only (`git diff -U0` against the PR base), so touching a legacy file does not fail on its pre-existing matches. Files without pipefail are ignored. Short writers (`printf '%s' "$small"`) are still flagged on new lines; that is intended because the here-string form is always safe, and the disable directive covers fixtures.
- **Idempotency/retry:** reruns update the same sticky comment in place via the marker, as counter-stack-check does; findings are deterministic for a given diff.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** a scanner error fails the job closed with its error text; no repository state changes, so a rerun is the recovery.

The style-guide section is checked by Markdown Lint in CI (criterion 4).
- **Broad verification trigger:** Not required; no shared library, root tooling or release path changes.

## Origin

- Created from the maintainer review of #33882 (fixed by PR #33903). The review marked this as a separate follow-up, not part of that PR.
- Class is recurring: #27981 (worktree branch lookup SIGPIPE), #30824 (issue-sync first-match pipelines), #33882 (brief readiness flips on large briefs).

## What

Add a documented rule plus a diff-scoped check that flags new `<writer> | grep -q…` (and the same early-exit reader shape: `grep -m1`, `head -n…`) inside scripts that enable `pipefail`. Model it on the existing counter-stack gate so only PR-changed lines are judged; historical occurrences are not blocked.

## Why

Under `set -o pipefail`, an early-exit reader closes the pipe after its first match. A writer still producing output gets SIGPIPE (exit 141), and `pipefail` reports 141 instead of the reader's 0. The result is a false "no match" that depends on input size and pipe buffer timing. In #33882 a 256 KB body gave 100/100 false negatives on macOS, and a Linux runner flipped ~3% of runs. `reference/shell-style-guide.md` has no SIGPIPE rule and no gate exists, so each instance is found by incident.

## Tier

`tier:standard` — new checker and workflow copied from an existing gate pattern; no shared-library changes.

## Context & Decisions

- Diff-scoped rather than a `ratchets.json` count, because most of the 966 existing matches are harmless short writers and counting them would trap unrelated edits (see "Gate design — ratchet, not absolute" in the style guide).

title: planning-publication-reconcile ignores native blockedBy (cross-repo blockers get status:available)
body:
## What

Planning publication reconciliation labels a task `status:available` when its only blocker is a native GitHub `blockedBy` relationship (for example, a cross-repository blocker that cannot be written as a TODO `blocked-by:tNNN` marker). It must project `status:blocked` while any native blocker is open.

## Evidence (observed 2026-10-07)

- A child issue in a private project repo had one native `blockedBy` edge to an open parent issue in another private repo (verified with GraphQL `issue.blockedBy`). Its TODO line had no `blocked-by:` marker, because cross-repo task IDs cannot be expressed there.
- `planning-publication-reconcile.sh reconcile --repo <owner/repo> --sha <published-sha>` reported `reconciled=6` and applied `auto-dispatch` + `status:available` to that child. Same-repo children with TODO `blocked-by:` markers correctly received `status:blocked`.
- Dispatch was not actually exposed: `pulse-dep-graph.sh` `_blocked_by_check_native_relationships` reads all native `blockedBy` nodes regardless of repository and blocks dispatch. The label was misleading, not unsafe. It was corrected manually to `status:blocked`.

## Root cause

`.agents/scripts/planning-publication-reconcile.sh` `_publication_task_has_dependency` (lines ~140-156) only checks:

1. parsed `blocked_by` from the TODO line,
2. a raw `blocked-by:` token on the TODO line,
3. existing `status:blocked` / `blocked-by:#N` labels.

It never consults native `blockedBy` relationships.

## How

- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/planning-publication-reconcile.sh` — in `_publication_task_has_dependency`, after the TODO-marker checks, query native `blockedBy(first: 50) { nodes { state } }` for the issue and return 0 when any node is `OPEN`. Reuse the existing GraphQL pattern in `.agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph.sh` `_blocked_by_check_native_relationships` (route through the same gh wrapper/cost accounting). Fail closed: if the lookup errors, treat the task as dependent (`status:blocked`), never available.
- Keep the function short; extract a helper if it would exceed the complexity gate.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/planning-publication-reconcile.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-planning-publication-reconcile.sh`, adding fixtures only if the existing suite cannot represent "native open blocker, no TODO marker → status:blocked" and "native lookup failure → status:blocked".

## Acceptance

- [ ] A published task with no TODO `blocked-by:` marker but an open native (including cross-repo) `blockedBy` edge reconciles to `status:blocked`
- [ ] A native-lookup failure never projects `status:available`
- [ ] Tasks with no blockers still reconcile to `status:available`

title: fix(release): surface GitHub write failures in release lane instead of silent exit 1
body:
## What

`aidevops release patch <PR> incremental` exits `1` with no diagnostic when a GitHub Git Database write fails. The last line printed is `RELEASE_TIMING phase=release-existing-guard state=finish ... result=no-tag`, so the failure looks unexplained and could easily be mistaken for a tooling bug, or prompt blind retries.

Observed 2026-10-07 while releasing PR #33919. An xtrace showed:

```text
release-lane-helper.sh:_release_lane_create_commit:135: gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/git/blobs --method POST --input - --jq '.sha // empty'
release-lane-helper.sh:_release_lane_create_commit:135: blob_sha=
release-lane-helper.sh:_release_lane_create_commit:135: return 1
release-lane-helper.sh:_release_lane_write:158: return 1
release-lane-helper.sh:release_lane_acquire:545: return 1
full-loop-release-helper.sh:_full_loop_release_start_new:786: return 1
```

Direct probe: `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/git/blobs --method POST ... --include` → `HTTP/2.0 500 Internal Server Error`, `Content-Length: 0`. The same call succeeded (`201`) about 90 seconds later, and the release then proceeded. No lane state was written, so this failure was safe. The problem is that it gave no signal.

## Reproducer

```bash
# During a GitHub Git Database 5xx window (confirm with a direct probe):
gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/git/blobs --method POST -f content=probe -f encoding=utf-8 --include
# -> HTTP/2.0 500 Internal Server Error, Content-Length: 0
aidevops release patch <merged-PR> incremental
# -> last line: RELEASE_TIMING phase=release-existing-guard state=finish elapsed_seconds=4 result=no-tag
# -> exit 1, no error message; `aidevops release status <PR>` shows the lane unchanged
```

Deterministic reproduction without an outage: put a stub `gh` on `PATH` that returns HTTP 500 with an empty body for `git/blobs` POST.

## Why

Every `gh api` call in `_release_lane_create_commit`, `_release_lane_write` and `release_lane_read` uses `2>/dev/null` and returns a bare `1`. A transient GitHub 5xx is therefore indistinguishable from a permission, validation or logic failure. The workflow allows one recovery attempt for a terminal failure, so without a diagnostic, operators cannot tell a retryable outage from a real defect.

## How

1. In `.agents/scripts/release-lane-helper.sh`, `_release_lane_create_commit`: on each failed Git Database call (commit read, blobs, trees, commits POST), print one stderr line naming the step and HTTP status, e.g. `RELEASE_LANE_WRITE step=blob status=500 retryable=true`. Never print request payloads; they contain the lane `operation_token`. Obtain the status the way `_release_lane_remote_head` already does (`gh api --include --silent`), or capture `gh`'s stderr into a local variable instead of discarding it.
2. Have `release_lane_acquire` / `_full_loop_release_start_new` map a retryable 5xx before any lane write to the existing deferred/retry exit (`75`) rather than `1`, so callers see "retry later" instead of a terminal failure. Keep `1` for 4xx and validation errors.
3. Optionally add one bounded retry (short backoff) for 5xx on the blob/tree/commit creation steps. Before the ref update these create only unreferenced objects, so a retry is side-effect free.

## Verification

- `shellcheck -x .agents/scripts/release-lane-helper.sh`
- Run the existing release-lane tests (`rg -l release_lane_ .agents/scripts/tests/`) and confirm no regression.
- With a stubbed `gh` returning HTTP 500 for `git/blobs`, `aidevops release` prints the `RELEASE_LANE_WRITE step=blob status=500` line and exits `75`, and no lane ref is updated.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/release-lane-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-helper.sh`

<!-- aidevops:sig -->

title: What next closeout obscures unresolved dependency and authority gates
body:
## Observed failure

An interactive cross-repository status check correctly identified several open implementation/acceptance issues, a source-evidence hold, unresolved native dependencies, and missing separate operational authority. It then ended with `Needed from you: None` and `Ready to close; the handed-off session retains the cross-repository completion plan` without identifying which exact prerequisites the receiving executor owned versus which authority or inaccessible inputs the operator still needed to supply.

The operator corrected this as misleading and asked what was actually needed to start the first held issue and unblock its two downstream phases. The follow-up had to reconstruct the actionable sequence and human-only gates from the leaf briefs. Evidence is this observed interaction, anonymized here; no private repository names, source evidence, local paths, or customer information are included.

The completed status inspection was not completion of the underlying objective. The handoff also did not prove that the recipient had all required operational authority or private-source inputs. This is an observed closeout-policy adherence/harness guidance gap, not proof of a specific plugin implementation defect.

## Deduplication and existing pattern

Searches for `What next` / `Needed from you` found existing closed issues #33088 (avoid asking humans for agent-doable work), #33130 (uncommitted work capture), and #33094 (fixed labels). Those fixes should be retained. This finding concerns unresolved dependency/authority classification and ambiguous completion ownership, not uncommitted changes or label formatting.

## Target files

- `.agents/reference/session.md`: What Next Block, Capture Check and completion/ownership rules.
- `.agents/AGENTS.md`: only the narrow universal pointer if necessary; preserve the existing size ratchet.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-session-completion-summary-policy.sh`: existing focused verification pattern if a deterministic prompt invariant is added.
- No plugin change is established as necessary; discover an actual enforcement seam before expanding scope.

## Recommended bounded change

Clarify that a blocked/held multi-phase objective needs an evidence-backed next actor and resume condition before a closeout can imply that the handoff is sufficient. Distinguish completed inspection from the unresolved objective. When human-only authority or inaccessible input is actually missing, list the exact scoped decision under Needed from you. When an authorized agent or live receiving session can safely resolve it, name its ownership and next action instead of manufacturing another approval request.

`Needed from you: None` remains valid when no human input is required; open issues alone must not force an ask. Safe source implementation, prerequisite discovery, coordination and tracking remain agent-owned. Preserve native dependencies, other sessions' worktrees, explicit private-evidence holds, and separate deployment/customer-write/activation authority. Handoff prose, merged source and auto-dispatch labels cannot manufacture operational authority or acceptance evidence.

## Acceptance and verification

- A report-only completion states that the inspection is done without implying the broader objective is complete.
- A handed-off unresolved chain identifies a verified executor/next action or an exact missing owner/authority/input; a plan alone is not proof of ownership or execution authority.
- A genuine human-only gate appears as a bounded ask with scope, exclusions and object evidence; agent-doable discovery or coordination is not exported to the user.
- Do not ask for redundant permission, weaken safety holds, invent an assignee, or declare a complete census from a merged observation adapter.
- Reuse the existing session completion policy check when changing its prompt invariants; Markdownlint affected guidance and run `git diff --check`. No new runner, broad repository gate or private reproduction fixture is needed.

## Maintainer triage boundary

The reporter has READ permission on the upstream repository. This is an external framework finding, not authority to change shared instructions or dispatch upstream workers. Maintainer triage may narrow the diagnosis or authorize the bounded implementation after confirming the premise.

## Dispatch Hold

External reporter has READ permission; maintainer triage is required before upstream framework implementation or worker dispatch

title: playwright subagent screenshots land in the canonical checkout when the parent gives an absolute path
body:
## Observed

An interactive Build+ session delegated browser screenshots to the `playwright` subagent and asked it to save PNGs to an absolute path under `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp/<dir>/`. The Playwright MCP screenshot tool rejected the absolute destination, so the child saved the files with bare file names. They landed in the child's working directory, which was the **canonical checkout** of the project repo, not the linked worktree the parent was working in.

Two results:

1. Untracked files appeared in a canonical checkout, which interactive sessions must never write to.
2. The canonical mirror-sync routine then preserved and removed them (into `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp/dirty-main-backups/<repo>-main-canonical-sync-.../untracked/`). The parent had to search the filesystem to find its evidence. The child's report linked `./editor-desktop.png`-style relative paths and said it could not confirm the requested paths.

## Expected

Screenshots requested by a parent end up at a predictable, allowed location outside any canonical checkout, and the child reports their absolute paths.

## Suggested fix (worker-ready)

- `tools/browser/` docs and/or the `playwright` agent definition: say where the Playwright MCP screenshot tool can write (its output dir or a relative path under its cwd), and tell parents to give a relative file name plus an allowed output dir instead of an arbitrary absolute path.
- Launch delegated browser children with the parent's worktree (or `${AIDEVOPS_TEMP_DIR}`) as cwd, never the canonical checkout. Or configure the Playwright MCP `--output-dir` to `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/tmp/playwright-output/` so relative names land there.
- Have the child report the absolute path of each saved artifact (`realpath`), or say plainly that it is unknown.

Files that likely need changes: the `playwright` subagent definition under `.agents/` and the MCP registry entry for `playwright` (output-dir arg). Exact paths not verified.

## Verification

Delegate "screenshot X to <dir>/a.png" to the `playwright` child from a session whose parent works in a linked worktree. Check that the PNG exists at the reported absolute path and that `git status --untracked-files=all` in the canonical checkout stays clean.

title: transcription-helper.sh install has no discoverable venv; fails on PEP 668 Python and causes duplicate installs
body:
## Problem

`transcription-helper.sh` has no canonical, discoverable install location for its
recommended local backend (faster-whisper). On a modern Linux host the `install`
command cannot succeed, and `status`/auto-selection cannot find working installs
made elsewhere. Agents then create ad-hoc virtual environments per task, which
duplicates ~400 MB installs and makes auto-selection fall through to paid cloud
backends.

## Evidence

- `find_python` (`.agents/scripts/transcription-helper.sh` lines 95-108) checks only
  `VENV_DIR=~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/work/speech-to-speech/.venv` (owned by the
  speech-to-speech helper, absent unless that feature was set up), then falls back
  to system `python3`.
- `cmd_install` (lines 964-969) runs `"$python_bin" -m pip install faster-whisper`
  against that interpreter. On Ubuntu 24.04 (Python 3.12.3) the stdlib
  `EXTERNALLY-MANAGED` marker is present, so per PEP 668 pip refuses system
  installs. Line 955 (`pip3 install -U yt-dlp`) has the same problem. No venv is
  created.
- Observed result: `status` reported faster-whisper as not installed while a
  working faster-whisper venv existed elsewhere under `.agent-workspace/work/`;
  auto-selection (lines 551-570, local-first by design) then chose `openai`, and a
  second duplicate venv was created to transcribe locally.
- Related: an unpinned fresh install resolved PyAV 19 with faster-whisper 1.2.1;
  transcribing an `.m4a` raised `TypeError: open() got an unexpected keyword

title: transcription-helper.sh install --help runs a real install including sudo package-manager calls
body:
## Problem

`transcription-helper.sh install --help` runs a real installation instead of
printing help. The installation can call `sudo apt-get update`, `apt-get install`,
`pacman -S` or `brew install`, so a user or agent asking for help triggers
privileged system changes.

## Evidence

- `main()` (`.agents/scripts/transcription-helper.sh` lines 1109-1111) calls
  `cmd_install` without passing arguments, so `--help` is silently ignored.
- `cmd_install` (lines 935-974) has no argument handling and starts system package
  installation immediately (lines 944-962).
- The same pattern applies to `status` and `models`, which also discard arguments.

## Expected

`install --help` (and `-h`) prints usage for the subcommand and exits 0 without
running any installer. Unknown subcommand arguments are rejected with a non-zero
exit.

## Suggested fix

- Pass `"$@"` to `cmd_install`, `cmd_status` and `cmd_models`.
- In each, handle `-h|--help` by printing usage and returning 0; reject unknown
  options with an error and `return 1`.
- Reference pattern: the existing top-level `help | -h | --help` branch in `main()`
  (line 1115).

## Verification

1. `transcription-helper.sh install --help` prints help, exits 0, and makes no
   package-manager or pip calls.
2. `transcription-helper.sh install --bogus` exits non-zero with an error.
3. `transcription-helper.sh install` still installs as before.
4. ShellCheck reports zero violations for the helper.

title: fix(release): postflight queue fails on installation rate limit because SYNC_PAT cannot dispatch workflows
body:
## What

Release publication of `v3.38.26` reached GitHub, npm and Homebrew, but `Publish Release` still failed. The failing step was `Queue exact-tag postflight`. As a result `aidevops release reconcile 33933` cannot write a terminal receipt.

The step has two routes and both failed:

1. `SYNC_PAT` returns `HTTP 403: Resource not accessible by personal access token` on `actions/workflows/<id>/dispatches`. This is not new: the `v3.38.25` run (37657223445) logged the same warning and was saved only by the job-token fallback.
2. The `GITHUB_TOKEN` fallback then hit `HTTP 403: API rate limit exceeded for installation`. This happened on the push run 37665132232 and again on the reconcile-dispatched run 37665825815.

#29172 made `SYNC_PAT` the quota-exhaustion route for this step. Because the PAT cannot dispatch workflows, that protection never takes effect. Every release now depends on the shared installation quota.

## Reproducer

1. Release with an exhausted `GITHUB_TOKEN` installation quota and the current `SYNC_PAT`. This happens naturally under heavy pulse activity: `aidevops release patch 33933 incremental` → tag `v3.38.26`.
2. Observed in `Queue exact-tag postflight`:
   - `could not create workflow dispatch event: HTTP 403: Resource not accessible by personal access token`
   - then `HTTP 403: API rate limit exceeded for installation` → exit 1
3. `aidevops release reconcile 33933` re-dispatches the publish job, which fails the same way. `aidevops release status 33933` reports `terminal_receipt: null`.

## Why

Without a terminal receipt the release stays open as "published; deployment deferred" even though every public channel converged. Recovery currently means waiting an unknown time for the quota to reset and then re-running the whole publish job.

## How

Files to modify:

- `.github/workflows/publish-packages.yml` (`Queue exact-tag postflight`, about lines 413-432). When the job-token dispatch fails with an installation rate limit, defer instead of failing. Reuse the existing `steps.github-release.outputs.deferred` pattern (about lines 185-194 and 442-443): emit `postflight_deferred=true`, write a step-summary line, and finish successfully only when every earlier verify step succeeded. All other 403 or 5xx errors must still fail.
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-reconcile.sh`: when the exact-tag run reports postflight deferred, dispatch `postflight.yml` with `--ref main -f tag=<tag>` using the operator's token. Treat the run as publication-complete only after that postflight run is terminal-success. Keep the `#aidevops:trust-boundary` guarantees: the main-ref dispatch is limited to the verified tag only.
- `.agents/workflows/release.md` "Post-Release" > Postflight: document the deferral and the required `SYNC_PAT` permission (fine-grained `Actions: Read and write` on the repository). The current docs describe `SYNC_PAT` only for issue-sync.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-release-publication-workflows.sh` (about lines 177-189 and 245): update the pinned dispatch literals to the new step shape.

Reference pattern: the GitHub-release deferral path in the same workflow, and the stale-publication verification in `full-loop-release-reconcile.sh` (`_full_loop_release_stale_publication_jobs_valid`, about line 692), which already checks a "only the postflight queue step failed" job shape.

### Files Scope

- `.github/workflows/postflight.yml`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-reconcile.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-reconcile-channels.sh`
- `.github/workflows/publish-packages.yml`
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-reconcile.sh`
- `.agents/workflows/release.md`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-release-publication-workflows.sh`

Integration scope recovery: postflight currently has no exact-tag run identity in the runs API. Add a tag-bound run-name so reconciliation can select only the verified tag, and extend the existing reconcile fixture and its sourced channel API stub to cover deferred, pending and terminal postflight evidence. Collision discovery found no open related PR. Verify with the existing three scoped test commands and ShellCheck.

## Acceptance

- A run where only the postflight dispatch hits the installation rate limit ends with `postflight_deferred=true`, not `failure`.
- `aidevops release reconcile <PR>` then queues exact-tag postflight and records the terminal receipt without re-running publication.
- A `SYNC_PAT` permission 403 is reported as a distinct, actionable annotation that names the missing permission.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-release-publication-workflows.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-reconcile.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-reconcile-channels.sh`
- `shellcheck` on the changed scripts, and actionlint (if configured) on `publish-packages.yml`

Evidence: https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/actions/runs/37665132232 and https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/actions/runs/37665825815 (failed at the postflight queue step after successful npm and Homebrew verification); https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/actions/runs/37657223445 (same `SYNC_PAT` 403, rescued by the job token).

title: Terminal-blocker consolidation supersedes permission_required issues on a single worker checkpoint comment
body:
## What happened

In a managed private repo, a headless worker implemented an auto-dispatch child issue and posted an "Implementation checkpoint: ..." comment (~1000 chars, `aidevops:origin:worker`). It then stopped with `TERMINAL_BLOCKER_REASON=permission_required`, because the source-access guard denied reading `.env.example`. Within about 35 minutes the pulse:

1. routed the terminal breaker to consolidation (`_route_terminal_breaker_to_consolidation`), labelled the issue `needs-consolidation`, and
2. filed a `consolidation-task` child that would create a superseding issue and close the original.

The maintainer meanwhile signed a development approval against the original issue body. Completing the consolidation would have:

- dropped the issue's native sub-issue link to its parent and its `blockedBy` edges, and
- left the signed approval pointing at a closed issue.

The interactive maintainer session had to close the consolidation child by hand and reword a maintainer comment to fall under the `Brief repaired:` exclusion.

## Root cause

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-triage.sh` `_route_terminal_breaker_to_consolidation` (about lines 85-118) needs only **one** substantive comment and does not consider the breaker reason. A human-owned `permission_required` boundary cannot be resolved by merging comments into a new spec; per `reference/worker-discipline.md` step 5 the correct state is "wait for the human decision, then `terminal-blocker-circuit:retry`".
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-triage-evaluation.sh` `_consolidation_filter_substantive_comments` (about lines 918-958) counts worker progress comments (`Implementation checkpoint:` from `aidevops:origin:worker`) as scope comments. They are progress evidence, not scope changes.

## Proposed fix

- In `_route_terminal_breaker_to_consolidation`, skip consolidation when the breaker reason is a permission, secret, spend or trust boundary (`permission_required`, `needs_maintainer_permissions`, and similar), and log the skip.
- In `_consolidation_filter_substantive_comments`, treat `^Implementation checkpoint:` (and other worker checkpoint shapes) as operational. Keep classification and child composition on one predicate, as the comment at `pulse-triage.sh` lines 195-203 requires.
- Optional: never consolidate an issue that carries a live `aidevops-signed-approval` whose body digest matches the current body.

## Files

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-triage.sh` (`_route_terminal_breaker_to_consolidation`)
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-triage-evaluation.sh` (`_consolidation_filter_substantive_comments`)
- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-consolidation-dispatch.sh` (regression cases)

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-consolidation-dispatch.sh`
- New cases:
  - a `permission_required` breaker with one worker checkpoint comment does not dispatch consolidation;
  - an issue with one maintainer scope comment plus one worker checkpoint stays below the threshold of 2;
  - a non-permission breaker with a real scope comment still consolidates (no regression).
- `shellcheck` on both scripts.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Permission-boundary terminal breakers never create `consolidation-task` children or `needs-consolidation` labels
- [ ] Worker checkpoint comments do not count toward the substantive threshold, and existing consolidation behaviour for genuine scope comments is unchanged

```bash
  --label "consolidated,origin:worker,auto-dispatch,status:available,<copy relevant labels from parent, excluding all status:* labels, needs-consolidation, consolidation-task, and origin:interactive>" \
  --body-file "<file containing the merged body from step 2>"
```

**Note (GH#18670):** `origin:worker` is mandatory on this label list — consolidated issues are pulse-generated artifacts, not interactive maintainer work. Use the signed wrapper above rather than the raw GitHub CLI so the successor retains the managed signature and origin metadata.

**Dispatch handoff:** `auto-dispatch` and `status:available` are also mandatory. Keep exactly one `status:*` label on the successor: `status:available`, never the parent's lifecycle status. The consolidated successor marker and this explicit handoff must both be present before `_has_consolidated_label` permits implementation dispatch; the fill-floor enumerator also needs the available status.

   Capture the new issue number as $NEW_NUM.

4. **Close the parent #33938:**

```bash
gh issue comment 33938 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Superseded by #$NEW_NUM. The merged spec is inlined on the new issue — continue discussion there."
gh issue edit 33938 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --add-label "consolidated" --remove-label "needs-consolidation"
gh issue close 33938 --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "not planned"
```

5. **Close this consolidation-task issue** with a summary comment:

```bash
gh issue comment $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" \
  --body "Consolidation complete. Parent: #33938 → New: #$NEW_NUM. Contributors @-mentioned: @alex-solovyev @marcusquinn."
gh issue close $THIS_ISSUE --repo "marcusquinn/aidevops" --reason "completed"
```

- **Do NOT read #33938** — it is inlined below. Reading it wastes the token budget.
- **Preserve all substantive content.** Merging is not summarising. If a comment adds a constraint, that constraint must appear in the merged body.
- **Preserve author attribution** for specific contributions: "per @user1: …".
- **No PR is required.** This is an operational task. The completion signal is the new issue number + parent closure + self-close.

title: fix(pulse): bound dependency normalization before product refill
body:
## Problem

A fresh Linux Pulse cycle on merged commit `ae46946a61e78a7cbe42c1ef8958ee8ce4a37792` successfully launched an initial tooling worker, but synchronous dependency normalization delayed the product refill until most of its dispatch budget was gone. This is a separate issue from the fixed PATH precedence regression in #33934.

## Observed evidence

- The first worker launch completed at 18:37:18 UTC on 2026-10-07.
- Label maintenance completed in 76 seconds at 18:39:07 UTC; it was not the long-running stage.
- `preflight_post_label_refill` completed at 18:54:50 UTC with duration **936 seconds**.
- During that refill, logs showed sequential native dependency checks across a large product backlog before candidate attempts began.
- The product pass processed only **5 of 118** ranked candidates, launched **0** product workers, and stopped with `cycle wall-clock budget below per-candidate floor (remaining=582s floor=600s)`.
- The initial worker exited at 18:50:09 UTC. Its event refill recorded `lock_busy` twice while the main cycle retained ownership.
- Cycle telemetry still reported `preflight`, and its heartbeat became older than the 900-second observation window during this scan.

This does not establish that every available award-enrichment issue would pass live admission. The observed defect is candidate discovery consuming the refill budget before those candidates can be evaluated.

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-repo-meta.sh`

title: consolidated: defer installation-quota-limited release postflight and reconcile exact tags
body:
_Supersedes #33938 — this issue is the consolidated spec._

## What

Make release publication resilient to installation-quota exhaustion when queuing exact-tag postflight. Defer only the postflight queue, then let `aidevops release reconcile <PR>` queue and verify that tag's postflight without republishing. Provide an actionable `SYNC_PAT` permission annotation and document its required repository permission.

Historical incident: `v3.38.26` reached GitHub, npm and Homebrew, but `Publish Release` failed at `Queue exact-tag postflight`, leaving `aidevops release reconcile 33933` unable to write a terminal receipt. Per @marcusquinn, the maintainer subsequently granted `SYNC_PAT` `Actions: Read and write`; publish run 37668162601 successfully started postflight through that PAT, and the release receipt is now `published`. Do not reopen or republish that release merely to reproduce this task.

## Why

#29172 introduced `SYNC_PAT` as the installation-quota-exhaustion route, but its missing workflow-dispatch permission made publication depend on the shared installation quota. Before the permission fix, PAT dispatch returned `HTTP 403: Resource not accessible by personal access token`; the `GITHUB_TOKEN` fallback then returned `HTTP 403: API rate limit exceeded for installation` on push run 37665132232 and reconcile-dispatched run 37665825815. The same PAT warning occurred for `v3.38.25` in run 37657223445, rescued only by the job token.

Without a terminal receipt a release remains "published; deployment deferred" despite converged public channels. Waiting an unknown time for quota reset and rerunning the entire publish job is unnecessary. The durable quota recovery and permission diagnostics remain needed even though the specific release incident is resolved.

## How

1. **Recover the existing implementation first.** Per @alex-solovyev, commits `bcb9ba9f7` and `b7a19655b` preserve the implementation, exact head `b7a19655b7baccad7ed26a03e04cca35ede051aa`. No push succeeded and no PR existed at that checkpoint. Locate and reuse salvageable commits rather than restarting; inspect against the current default branch and any existing PR/issue branch before editing. Resume workflow publication only after an explicitly authorized workflow-capable credential is available. The worker OAuth credential lacked `workflow` scope; recovery belongs to the repository administrator. Do not use alternate credentials or bypass security controls.
2. `.github/workflows/publish-packages.yml`, `Queue exact-tag postflight` (source references about lines 413-432): retain PAT-first and job-token fallback. When both routes fail and the job-token error is an installation rate limit, emit `postflight_deferred=true`, write a step-summary line, and finish successfully only if every earlier verification succeeded. Reuse `steps.github-release.outputs.deferred` (source references about lines 185-194 and 442-443). All other 403 and 5xx errors must remain fatal. A PAT permission 403 needs a distinct actionable annotation naming fine-grained repository `Actions: Read and write`, not a generic warning.
3. `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-reconcile.sh`: recognize exact-tag postflight deferral and dispatch `postflight.yml` using the operator token with `--ref main -f tag=<tag>`, without rerunning publication. Select only verified-tag postflight evidence and require terminal-success before recording a publication-complete receipt. Pending or failed postflight must not become success. Preserve read-only `release status` behavior and all `#aidevops:trust-boundary` guarantees limiting main-ref dispatch to the verified tag. Reference `_full_loop_release_stale_publication_jobs_valid` at line 692, which already validates the "only the postflight queue step failed" shape.
4. `.github/workflows/postflight.yml`: add a tag-bound run-name, because runs API evidence previously had no exact-tag run identity. This adjacent integration was already included in the parent's corrected canonical scope after collision discovery found no related open PR.
5. `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-reconcile.sh` and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-reconcile-channels.sh`: extend the existing reconcile fixture and its sourced channel API stub for deferred, pending and terminal postflight evidence.
6. `.agents/scripts/tests/test-release-publication-workflows.sh` (source references about lines 177-189 and 245): update pinned dispatch literals to the new step shape and retain focused executable scenarios for PAT success, job-token success, quota deferral, actionable PAT warning, fatal permission errors and 5xx errors.
7. `.agents/workflows/release.md`, Post-Release > Postflight (current line 343): document deferral and reconciliation plus fine-grained `SYNC_PAT` repository `Actions: Read and write`. Previously this PAT was documented only for issue-sync.

All seven scope files exist on default branch `main` at verified revision `ae46946a61e78a7cbe42c1ef8958ee8ce4a37792`; use EDIT, not NEW. Line references supplied by the original brief are locators, not a substitute for reading the current code.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: .github/workflows/postflight.yml
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-reconcile.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-reconcile-channels.sh
- EDIT: .github/workflows/publish-packages.yml
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/full-loop-release-reconcile.sh
- EDIT: .agents/workflows/release.md
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/tests/test-release-publication-workflows.sh

## Runner prerequisites

Consolidation itself does not require workflow publishing credentials. Implementation delivery remains permission-blocked until an explicitly authorized workflow-capable credential is available; the repository administrator owns that recovery. This is separate from the release-job `SYNC_PAT` Actions permission already granted by the maintainer. No secret values are required in the brief or logs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A run where only postflight dispatch encounters installation rate-limit exhaustion succeeds with `postflight_deferred=true`, with a step summary, only after earlier verification succeeds.
- [ ] Other 403 and 5xx dispatch failures remain failures; earlier publication/verification failures cannot be masked.
- [ ] `aidevops release reconcile <PR>` queues postflight for the verified exact tag without rerunning publication and records a terminal receipt only after that postflight run is terminal-success.
- [ ] Deferred, pending and terminal postflight evidence is covered; exact-tag selection and read-only status preserve the trust boundary.
- [ ] A `SYNC_PAT` permission 403 yields a distinct actionable annotation naming the missing repository `Actions: Read and write` permission.
- [ ] Release documentation explains the permission, deferral and recovery.
- [ ] Reuse existing implementation commits where salvageable, rerun scoped verification, and report unrelated pre-existing failures separately without repairing them in this task.
- [ ] After authorized credential recovery, successfully push, create a draft PR early, complete exact-head readiness and MERGE_SUMMARY, make the PR non-draft and attempt guarded merge once; hand pending asynchronous gates to pulse without polling or bypassing controls.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-release-publication-workflows.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-reconcile.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-release-reconcile-channels.sh`
- ShellCheck on `.agents/scripts/full-loop-release-reconcile.sh` and the three scoped shell tests.
- actionlint, if configured/available, on the changed workflows; do not claim a result if not installed.

## Reproducer

Historical reproducer before the permission fix: exhaust the job-token installation quota under heavy pulse activity, then `aidevops release patch 33933 incremental` for tag `v3.38.26`; observe the PAT permission 403 followed by installation-quota 403 at `Queue exact-tag postflight`. `aidevops release reconcile 33933` redispatches publication and fails similarly; `aidevops release status 33933` reports `terminal_receipt: null`. Prefer existing executable queue-step scenarios instead of republishing the now-completed release.

## Context & Decisions

- Per @marcusquinn (2026-10-07 18:42 UTC), granting `SYNC_PAT` `Actions: Read and write` resolved the immediate credential issue; run 37668162601 started postflight and `v3.38.26` now has a `published` receipt. Remaining scope is quota-only deferral, reconcile without republishing, permission documentation and a distinct annotation. This supersedes the original claim that the current release remains unresolved.
- Per @alex-solovyev (2026-10-07 18:49 UTC), the preserved implementation includes installation-quota-only deferral, actionable PAT annotation, exact-tag postflight run identity, operator-token reconciliation without republishing, terminal-success gating, read-only status, documentation and focused coverage. The clean checkpoint had two implementation commits ahead of base, but push was rejected for missing OAuth `workflow` scope. No alternate credential or bypass was attempted. Remaining delivery is successful push, PR, exact-head remote verification, merge summary and guarded merge/handoff; the checkpoint is not completed full-loop delivery.
- Checkpoint verification reported by @alex-solovyev: ShellCheck passed on all four changed shell files; both reconcile tests passed; executable queue-step PAT/job-token success, deferral, annotation and fatal permission/5xx scenarios passed; pre-push repository typecheck passed. actionlint was not installed, so no result is claimed.
- The full publication-workflow test stopped at an unrelated pre-existing npm propagation schedule assertion: base `ae46946a6` pins 14 attempts while the unchanged workflow uses 18. Do not repair that drift inside this task; retain evidence and distinguish it from failures caused by current changes.
- Parent scope recovery already added the postflight workflow and both reconcile fixtures before edits; carry all seven paths forward. No additional superseded issue bodies, wildcard entries or `requires-secrets:` source lines were supplied.

title: full-loop commit-and-pr accepts PR titles that merge later rejects as invalid squash subjects
body:
## Problem

`full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr --title` accepts a PR title that `full-loop-helper.sh merge` later refuses. The failure only appears after CI has finished, so a ready PR blocks at the last step and needs a manual retitle.

## Evidence

- PR #33948 was created with `--title "GH#33937 GH#33936: transcription-helper ..."` (two task IDs, so the PR could close both issues). `commit-and-pr` created the PR with that title.
- After all required checks passed, `merge` stopped with: `PR #33948 title is not a valid squash subject; refusing merge`.
- The validator is `_merge_resolve_squash_subject` in `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`. Its `task_ere` is `^(t[0-9]+|GH#[0-9]+):[[:space:]]+...` and `conventional_ere` is the conventional-commit pattern. A title with two leading IDs matches neither.
- `commit-and-pr` parses `--title` in `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh` (the `--title)` case, around line 97) and does not run that check.

## Fix

- Extract the squash-subject check (the `task_ere`/`conventional_ere` match plus the WIP/newline rejections) from `_merge_resolve_squash_subject` into a shared predicate, e.g. `_full_loop_valid_squash_subject TITLE`.
- Have `commit-and-pr` call it for the explicit `--title` value, or for the default title derived from `--message`, **before** pushing or creating the PR. On failure, exit 1 with the accepted shapes (`GH#N: ...`, `tNNN: ...`, conventional `type(scope): ...`) and a hint that extra issues belong in the body as `Resolves #N`.
- Keep `merge` using the same predicate so the producer and consumer can't drift apart.

## Verification

1. `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr --issue N --message "fix: x" --title "GH#1 GH#2: x"` fails before any push. Check this in a scratch worktree, or with the existing `tests/test-full-loop-merge-authority-guard.sh` harness pattern if a test is needed.
2. `--title "GH#1: fix: x"` and the default title from `--message "fix: x"` still succeed.
3. `merge` still refuses an invalid title edited in on GitHub after creation.
4. ShellCheck is clean on both files.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-subject.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-merge-authority-guard.sh`

The orchestration entrypoint owns title derivation; the sibling subject library shares the predicate between creation and merge. Existing merge harness coverage will load that shared library.

title: Postflight docs: same-session PATH resolves helpers to the start-time runtime bundle, not the deployed release
body:
## Problem

After a release deploys inside an interactive OpenCode session, helpers resolved through `PATH` still run the **session-pinned runtime bundle** from session start, not the newly deployed `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/`. Postflight guidance says "verify the deployed agent version", but doesn't warn that `PATH` lookups in the same session hit stale code.

## Evidence (v3.38.27, PR #33948)

- After `release:published tag=v3.38.27`, `~/.aidevops/agents/VERSION` was `3.38.27` and the deployed `transcription-helper.sh` contained the fix.
- In the same session, `which -a transcription-helper.sh` returned only `~/.aidevops/runtime-bundles/3.38.26-<id>/agents/scripts/transcription-helper.sh`.
- Running `transcription-helper.sh install --help` to verify the fix therefore ran the **old** code. That code ignores `--help`, so it ran a real install (`brew install ffmpeg yt-dlp`, plus pip in an existing venv). The verification step reproduced the very side effect the release had fixed.

## Fix

Documentation only. Add one sentence to the postflight verification step in `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md` ("4.9 Conditional Postflight + Deploy") and to the matching postflight text in `.agents/workflows/release.md`:

> Verify deployed helpers by absolute path (`~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/<helper>.sh`); the current session's `PATH` stays pinned to its start-time runtime bundle until a new session starts. Never verify a side-effect fix through `PATH`.

Check for duplicates first with `rg -n "runtime.bundle" .agents/workflows .agents/reference`.

## Verification

- `rg -n "pinned to its start-time runtime bundle" .agents/workflows/full-loop.md .agents/workflows/release.md` returns both lines.
- markdownlint is clean on both files.
- No net growth to `.agents/AGENTS.md` (ratchet unchanged).

- `.agents/workflows/release.md`

title: Pulse TODO-handoff PRs (Ref #NNN, origin:worker) never auto-merge and give no maintainer signal
body:
## Problem

PRs created by the pulse's own TODO publication step (`pulse-todo-publication.sh`, body marker `<!-- aidevops:pulse-todo-handoff ... -->`, title `GH#NNN: sync verified TODO refs`) are never merged by the pulse and give the maintainer no signal that they need attention.

Observed on a managed private repo (v3.38.26): one such PR stayed open with all checks green while `pulse-diagnose-helper.sh pr <N>` logged `pm-wb-no-issue` ("Worker-briefed auto-merge skipped — no linked issue found") more than 20 times, then `pw-merge-skip-mergeable` once the branch fell behind the default branch. It needed a manual update-branch and `full-loop-helper.sh merge`.

By contrast, `issue-sync` PRs titled `chore: sync GitHub issue state to TODO.md [skip ci]` on the same repo auto-merged normally.

## Cause (from code at v3.38.26)

1. `pulse-todo-publication.sh:73` writes `- Ref #NNN` in the body (deliberately non-closing; the referenced issue can be a parent tracker that must stay open) and the PR carries `origin:worker`.
2. `origin:worker` routes it to `_attempt_worker_briefed_auto_merge` (`pulse-merge-process.sh:1266-1270`), which requires a linked issue.
3. `_extract_linked_issue` (`pulse-merge.sh:1911-1947`) only accepts closing keywords (`close/fix/resolve`), so `Ref #NNN` yields empty → permanent skip.
4. `_pulse_is_trusted_issue_sync_pr` (`pulse-merge-gates.sh:62`, via `review-bot-gate-helper.sh is-trusted-issue-sync-pr`) recognises the `issue-sync` PR shape but not the pulse-todo-handoff shape.

## Open question for maintainers

The handoff PR body says the changes are "pending review" and "maintainer gates still apply", so manual merge may be intended. Either way the current state is a silent dead end. Pick one:

- **A (auto-merge):** extend the trusted generated-PR predicate to the pulse-todo-handoff marker (bound to exact head SHA, allowlisted `TODO.md`-only diff, trusted author), and let the pulse update-branch when BEHIND.
- **B (manual by design):** surface these PRs to the maintainer (e.g. `needs-maintainer-review` label or a status/notification) instead of re-skipping every cycle, and stop logging repeated `pm-wb-no-issue`.

## Files to modify

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-todo-publication.sh` (PR shape/labels)
- `.agents/scripts/review-bot-gate-helper.sh` (`is-trusted-issue-sync-pr`) and/or `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-gates.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh` (worker-briefed path skip for this PR class)
- Reference pattern: existing issue-sync trusted path (`tests/test-pulse-merge-issue-sync-authority.sh`)

## Verification

- A pulse-todo-handoff PR with green checks either merges on the next pulse cycle (A) or carries a visible maintainer-attention signal within one cycle (B).
- `pulse-diagnose-helper.sh pr <N>` no longer shows repeated `pm-wb-no-issue` for this PR class.
- Existing trust-boundary tests still pass; untrusted or non-TODO diffs remain fail-closed (#aidevops:trust-boundary).

title: Issue Sync enrich re-blocks dependants after Pulse unblocks them; stale_blocked_reconcile always times out
body:
## Observed

A blocker issue closed, and Pulse moved its 13 dependants from `status:blocked` to `status:available` (dependency close event). About 40 seconds later the repository's Issue Sync workflow (`push` run from the blocker's merged PR) ran `issue-sync-helper.sh enrich` over every task and put `status:blocked` back on 11 of the 13. The two that had already been queued by Pulse kept their active status (enrich skips active claims). The other 11 then stayed blocked although their only native `blockedBy` edge was closed.

The safety net did not recover them: the Pulse stage `stale_blocked_reconcile` hits its 60 s timeout on every cycle (killed at about 19:27, 19:52, 20:03, 20:30, 20:48 and 21:11 UTC on the same day), so `reconcile_stale_blocked_issues` never completes.

Result: a fan-out of parallel worker tasks ran one or two at a time until a maintainer ran `reconcile_dependants_after_verified_closure <repo> <closed-issue>` from `dependency-event-reconciler.sh` by hand, which made all 11 available at once.

## Likely causes

1. Enrich derives the status label from the pushed TODO.md snapshot. In that snapshot the blocker's TODO line was still open (the "mark complete" sync commit lands later), so `blocked-by:tNNN` looked unresolved and enrich re-applied `status:blocked`, overriding a newer, verified unblock.
2. `stale_blocked_reconcile` cannot finish within 60 s for a repo with many open issues, so missed or reverted unblocks are never repaired.

## Suggested fix

- Enrich should not add `status:blocked` when every native `blockedBy` edge is closed (native relationship is the primary gate per `reference/task-lifecycle.md`), or should leave status labels to the dependency reconciler entirely.
- Bound `stale_blocked_reconcile` work per cycle (resume cursor or smaller batch) so it completes inside its timeout.

## Verification

- Close a blocker whose dependants have `blocked-by:` in TODO.md; confirm dependants stay `status:available` after the push-triggered Issue Sync run.
- `pulse.log` shows `Stage complete: stale_blocked_reconcile` rather than `Stage timeout`.

Paths: `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh` (enrich), `.agents/scripts/dependency-event-reconciler.sh`, `.agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph.sh`, the Pulse stage runner for `stale_blocked_reconcile` (exact file not confirmed).

title: fix(secret-helper): list omits tenant credentials and causes false worker holds
body:
## Problem

`aidevops secret list` omits tenant-backed credential names and can cause false worker holds.

## Verified evidence

On 2026-10-07 a worker invoked `secret list` through the aidevops tool and received only `AIDEVOPS_ACTIVE_TENANT`. It reported five required credentials absent and stopped. Independent status-only checks for all five succeeded without emitting values. This establishes incomplete listing, not worker-sandbox authentication or authorization. A separate network-policy denial must remain intact.

## Reproducer

Observed: `aidevops secret list` returns only the tenant-selector name while `aidevops secret check NAME` succeeds silently for five tenant-backed names. In the existing isolated fake-HOME harness, create a supported tenant loader and a tenant file exporting placeholder `TEST_SECRET` with a dummy value. List currently omits `TEST_SECRET`, although check succeeds. Do not use real credentials or print values.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/secret-helper.sh`

title: full-loop status should direct to complete while merge-receipt finalization is pending
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

# full-loop status should direct to `complete` while merge-receipt finalization is pending

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-07
- **Session:** OpenCode interactive (follow-up from GH#33955 / PR #33956 / release v3.38.28)
- **Created by:** AI DevOps (ai-interactive)
- **Parent task:** none
- **Blocked by:** none
- **Related (closed):** #31633 (made `complete` finalize merge-created receipts), #29105

## What

1. `full-loop-helper.sh status --json` reports `next_action: "complete"` when a matching cleanup receipt exists with `executor_completion_state == FINALIZATION_PENDING`. Today it reports the stale value saved at `start` (`complete-task-development`).
2. `workflows/full-loop.md` names `full-loop-helper.sh complete` as the executor finalization command for stateful loops, after terminal release or no-release evidence. Today the workflow names only `finalize-receipt`, for flows *without* local lifecycle state.

## Why

Observed after PR #33956 merged and v3.38.28 reached a terminal `published` receipt: `status --json` returned

```json
{"phase":"pr-review","phase_status":"waiting","executor_status":"initialized-only","executor_completion_state":"FINALIZATION_PENDING","resource_cleanup_state":"CLEANUP_DEFERRED","next_action":"complete-task-development"}
```

The interactive executor reported completion without running `complete`, because neither status nor the workflow pointed to it. Running `full-loop-helper.sh complete` immediately produced `executor_completion_state: COMPLETE`, `next_action: await-resource-cleanup`, `phase_is_historical: true`. The finalization step works; it is just not discoverable, so loops end with executor finalization pending.

## Tier

`tier:standard`: small lifecycle-status semantics change plus a doc pointer. Existing behaviour and tests define the surrounding contract.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-state-lifecycle-commands.sh`, in `cmd_status()` (starts at line 450 after PR #33971). In the receipt-projection block (lines 497-507 after PR #33971), after the `executor_completion_state == $_FULL_LOOP_EXECUTOR_COMPLETE` branch, add an `elif` for `"$_FULL_LOOP_EXECUTOR_FINALIZATION_PENDING"` (defined in `.agents/scripts/full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh:25`) that sets `status_next_action="complete"`. Leave `observed_status` and `phase_is_historical` unchanged in that branch: the executor is not complete yet.
- EDIT: `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md`
  - Step table row 9 (about line 78): mention `full-loop-helper.sh complete`.
  - Paragraph at about lines 308-310 (`Direct merge-wrapper flows without local lifecycle state use finalize-receipt ...`): add one preceding sentence stating that loops *with* local lifecycle state finalize with `full-loop-helper.sh complete` after the release receipt is terminal (`published`, `superseded`, or recorded `not-requested`), and that `status --json` reports `next_action: complete` until then.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-completion-evidence.sh`. Next to the existing receipt-projection status assertions (about lines 984-1060, which check `await-resource-cleanup`), add one case: a valid receipt with `FINALIZATION_PENDING` yields `.next_action == "complete"` and `.phase_is_historical == false`.

### Reference pattern

Copy the existing `COMPLETE` branch in the same block (`status_next_action="await-resource-cleanup"` / `"none"`).

### Complexity Impact

`cmd_status` is about 80 lines and grows by about 3-4 lines, staying under the 100-line gate. No new functions.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- Malformed or identity-mismatched receipts must still project `in-progress`/`none`. The existing assertions at about lines 1045-1060 must keep passing, so add the new branch only inside the successful projection path.
- Do not make `status` call `complete` or mutate state. `status` stays read-only.
- `complete` already enforces release gating (`Cleanup blocked: release:... is not terminal-success`), so pointing `next_action` to it is safe before the release is terminal.

### Scope Boundaries

- Out of scope: advancing `phase` from `pr-review` during the merge/release wrapper path (`phase_is_historical` already covers it once complete), and auto-running `complete` from `merge` or `aidevops release reconcile`. If wanted, file these separately.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-state-lifecycle-commands.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-completion-evidence.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

1. With a valid matching receipt in `FINALIZATION_PENDING`, `full-loop-helper.sh status --json` reports `next_action == "complete"`, with `executor_completion_state == "FINALIZATION_PENDING"` and `phase_is_historical == false`.
2. After `full-loop-helper.sh complete`, status reports `executor_completion_state == "COMPLETE"` and `next_action == "await-resource-cleanup"`, as today.
3. Malformed or mismatched receipts still yield `executor_completion_state == "in-progress"`, `resource_cleanup_state == "none"`.
4. `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md` names `full-loop-helper.sh complete` in step 9 and in the finalization paragraph.
5. `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-completion-evidence.sh` passes, and ShellCheck is clean on the edited scripts.

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-state-lifecycle-commands.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-completion-evidence.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-completion-evidence.sh
rg -n "full-loop-helper.sh complete" .agents/workflows/full-loop.md
```

## Context & Decisions

- Chose a status pointer plus a documentation fix over auto-completion. It keeps `status` read-only and the executor's explicit ownership transfer intact (`workflows/full-loop.md` 4.10).
