title: Move direct-API helpers (ai-research, verify-operation) to Claude Haiku 5.5 with thinking-safe parsing
body:
## What

Move the direct Anthropic Messages API helpers from Claude Haiku 4.5 to Claude Haiku 5.5 (`claude-haiku-5-5`) safely. Today `ai-research-helper.sh` resolves its `simple` model (and its unknown-name default) to `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`, and `verify-operation-helper.sh` labels its Anthropic verifier and same-provider fallback as `claude-haiku-4-5`.

## Why

GH#33278 moved the `simple` tier and OpenCode paths to Haiku 5.5 (10x cheaper base rate: $0.10 in / $0.50 out per 1M tokens for prompts up to 100K). These two helpers call `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages` directly, so a plain ID swap would break them. Anthropic's Haiku 5.5 migration guide (platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/haiku-5-5/migration-guide) says:

- Adaptive thinking is on by default, so a response can start with a `thinking` block. `extract_anthropic_text` reads `.content[0].text` and would return empty.
- Thinking tokens count toward `max_tokens`. The helper default is 150, so a reply can stop with `stop_reason: "max_tokens"` before any text.
- `temperature`/`top_p`/`top_k` other than defaults return 400. Assistant prefill returns 400. (The current payload sends neither; keep it that way.)

## How

1. `.agents/scripts/ai-research-helper.sh`:
   - `extract_anthropic_text` (about line 211): select the first block with `type == "text"` (jq: `[.content[]? | select(.type == "text") | .text] | first // empty`; mirror it in the python fallback).
   - `json_payload` (about line 196): when the model starts with `claude-haiku-5-5`, add `"output_config": {"effort": "low"}` so short classifications skip most thinking. Pick a `max_tokens` floor for that model (for example `max(max_tokens, 1024)`) so thinking cannot consume the whole budget. Note: GH#33278 routes background work at `medium`; this helper is a short classifier, so `low` is the intended exception. Document that choice in a comment.
   - `resolve_model_id` (about line 30): `simple` and `*` → `claude-haiku-5-5`.
2. `.agents/scripts/verify-operation-helper.sh`: replace the `claude-haiku-4-5` labels (about lines 62, 63, 72, 154, 548) with `claude-haiku-5-5`. The verifier call goes through `ai-research-helper.sh --model simple`, so step 1 decides the real model.
3. `.agents/tools/context/model-routing.md`: in the "Haiku 5.5 update (2026-10-07, GH#33278)" bullet, remove the sentence saying these helpers stay on Haiku 4.5.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `ai-research-helper.sh --provider anthropic --model simple --prompt "Reply with only the number: 17+40"` prints `57` using `claude-haiku-5-5` (needs Anthropic API key or OAuth pool credentials).
- [ ] A response whose first content block is `thinking` still yields the text block.
- [ ] `shellcheck` is clean on both scripts; existing tests that cover them still pass (`rg -l "ai-research-helper|verify-operation-helper" .agents/scripts/tests`).

### Files Scope

- EDIT: .agents/scripts/ai-research-helper.sh
- EDIT: .agents/scripts/verify-operation-helper.sh
- EDIT: .agents/tools/context/model-routing.md

## Context

Found while implementing GH#33278 (Haiku 5.5 adoption). Pricing and behaviour sources: Anthropic pricing page and Haiku 5.5 overview/migration guide, fetched 2026-10-07.

title: Worker loopback policy: Bash denies 127.0.0.1 but bounded operations allow it; worker abandoned required Lighthouse run
body:
## Observed

Two headless workers in the same project repo ran the same brief, which requires Lighthouse against a local static server on a task-specific port (`npx --yes lighthouse@12 http://127.0.0.1:<port>/...`). The repo is not registered with localdev.

- Worker A ran the server and Lighthouse through `aidevops_bounded_operation`. Lighthouse completed and its PR merged with the numbers.
- Worker B started the server through `aidevops_bounded_operation`, then probed it with `curl http://127.0.0.1:<port>/` in Bash. The command policy denied it:
  `[NET-TIER] BLOCKED: 127.0.0.1 (Tier 5: DENY) Loopback HTTP is allowed only for this repository's registered local-hosting site and port (services/hosting/local-hosting.md)`.
  Worker B concluded local servers were unavailable, skipped the required Lighthouse run, opened a draft PR, released its claim with `worker_draft_checkpoint` and labelled the issue `status:blocked`. The task then needed human intervention.

## Problem

The loopback rule applies to Bash commands but not to processes started via `aidevops_bounded_operation` (Lighthouse/Chrome there reach 127.0.0.1 freely). Workers therefore get inconsistent signals: the same action is denied on one path and allowed on another, and a denial on the probe path can end a run that could have completed.

The sanctioned route (register the repo with `localdev-helper.sh add`) is also unavailable when the localdev port pool is exhausted (see the related stale-registration issue).

## Suggested fix

Pick one consistent rule and make the denial actionable:

- Either allow loopback to a port served by a process the same worker started (owned bounded operation), on both paths; or apply the same denial to bounded operations.
- Make the `[NET-TIER]` denial message say which path is allowed (e.g. "run the server and the client inside one `aidevops_bounded_operation`" or "register with `localdev-helper.sh add`"), so workers do not treat it as terminal.
- Worker guidance: a blocked loopback probe is not a reason to release with `status:blocked` when the brief names a supported alternative.

## Verification

- A worker that starts a static server and runs Lighthouse against it completes the same way whichever tool path it uses, or gets a denial that names the working path.
- Policy tests (`tests/test-sandbox-command-policy.sh`, `tests/test-command-policy-helper.sh`) cover the owned-server loopback case.

Paths: `.agents/scripts/network-tier-helper.sh`, `.agents/scripts/sandbox-exec-helper.sh`, the bounded-operation tool in the OpenCode plugin (exact file not confirmed), `services/hosting/local-hosting.md`.

title: localdev: Pulse worktree cleanup leaves branch registrations; 3100-3999 port pool exhausts
body:
## Observed

On one runner, the localdev registry (`ports.json` in `$LOCALDEV_DIR`) held 920 branch registrations for a single localdev app (`<app-a>`), but only 6 matching worktrees still existed in the worktree base directory. 570 matching Traefik route files remained in `$LOCALDEV_DIR/conf.d`.

Effects:

1. **Port pool exhausted.** `PORT_RANGE_START=3100`/`PORT_RANGE_END=3999` (`localdev-helper-ports.sh:97-98`) gives 900 ports. The newest registration (2026-05-20) holds port 3999; no branch registrations happened after that, and `localdev-helper.sh add <new-app>` cannot get a port. Several ports also appear twice in the registry (e.g. two branches on 3616), so assignment already collided near exhaustion.
2. **`localdev-helper.sh list` is slow and noisy.** It health-checks every registered branch, so it walks hundreds of dead `[--]` entries.
3. **Headless workers lose the sanctioned loopback path.** The worker network policy allows loopback HTTP only for the repo's registered localdev site/port, and new repos cannot register while the pool is full (see the related loopback issue).

## Cause (verified in code)

`worktree-helper-cmds.sh:340` and `worktree-clean-lib.sh:1592` call `localdev_auto_branch_rm` when a worktree is removed. The Pulse cleanup path does not: `pulse-cleanup-worktree-removal.sh:226` runs `git worktree remove --force` without deregistering the localdev branch. Worker worktrees are mostly removed by Pulse, so their registrations accumulate.

## Suggested fix

- Call `localdev_auto_branch_rm` (or `localdev-helper.sh branch rm <app> <branch>`) after a successful removal in `pulse-cleanup-worktree-removal.sh`.
- Add a prune routine (e.g. `localdev-helper.sh branch prune [app]`) that removes branch entries and route files whose worktree path no longer exists, and run it from the existing worktree cleanup routine.
- Make `assign_port` fail clearly with a prune hint when the range is full, and never hand out a port already in the registry.

## Verification

- Remove a worker worktree via Pulse cleanup; confirm its branch is gone from `ports.json` and its `conf.d/<app>--<branch>.yml` is deleted.
- `localdev-helper.sh branch prune <app>` on a registry with dead entries leaves only live worktrees.
- `localdev-helper.sh add <new-app>` succeeds after pruning.

Manual workaround used here: back up `ports.json` and `conf.d`, then `localdev-helper.sh branch rm <app> <branch>` for every branch without a live worktree.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup-worktree-removal.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/localdev-helper-branch.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/localdev-helper-ports.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/localdev-helper.sh`

title: Opus concurrency cap double-counts workers (sandbox wrapper + opencode both match pgrep)
body:
## Observed

With 3 Opus headless workers running, Pulse deferred every further thinking-tier candidate:

```
Dispatch_max: #NNN (<repo>) deferred — opus_concurrency_cap: inflight=6 cap=4 model=anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 (retry next cycle)
```

`pgrep -af 'opencode.*-m anthropic/claude-opus'` returned 6 PIDs for 3 workers: one `sandbox-exec-helper.sh run ...` wrapper and one `opencode run ...` process per worker. Both command lines contain `opencode` and `-m anthropic/claude-opus-...`.

## Cause

`_dispatch_check_model_concurrency_cap` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh` (around line 904) counts every process whose full command line matches `opencode.*-m anthropic/claude-opus`. The sandbox wrapper's arguments include the inner opencode command, so each worker is counted twice. With the default `OPUS_CONCURRENCY_CAP=4` (`.agents/configs/dispatch-model-caps.conf`), only 2 real Opus workers can run, regardless of `orchestration.max_workers_cap`.

## Suggested fix

Count workers, not processes. For example, match only the `opencode` binary (`pgrep -f '/opencode run .*-m anthropic/claude-opus'`, or `pgrep -x`-style matching on the executable plus an argument check), or count distinct worker session keys from the headless-runtime state instead of `pgrep -f`.

## Verification

- With N Opus workers running, the deferral log line reports `inflight=N`.
- With cap 4 and 3 running workers, a 4th thinking-tier candidate dispatches.
- Extend the existing dispatch tests for `_dispatch_check_model_concurrency_cap` with a wrapper+child process pair.

Workaround applied locally: `AIDEVOPS_OPUS_CONCURRENCY_CAP=10` (= 5 real workers).

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh`

import fcntl, os, pty, re, select, signal, struct, sys, termios, time
env = dict(os.environ)

body:
## Observed

`.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-worker-detection.sh` fails 6 of 40 cases on current `main` (`113316fac2`). Found while working on #33976; the failures are identical with and without that change.

## Reproducer

From a clean checkout of `main`, run:

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-worker-detection.sh
```

Result: `Ran 40 tests, 6 failed.`, with this output:

```
pulse-dispatch-core.sh: line 1141: <tmp>/runner-capability-helper.sh: No such file or directory
pulse-dispatch-core.sh: line 1142: runner_capability_check_fresh: command not found
FAIL dispatch_with_dedup proceeds when no duplicate detected (GH#12436)
FAIL dispatch_with_dedup detaches stdin and captures worker output to issue log (GH#14483)
FAIL dispatch_with_dedup forwards explicit model override to worker launch
FAIL tier mutation re-resolves candidate default before worker launch
FAIL tier mutation preserves explicit model pin
FAIL unchanged simple tier retains candidate model
```

## Cause

`dispatch_with_dedup` sources `"${SCRIPT_DIR}/runner-capability-helper.sh"` and calls `runner_capability_check_fresh` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh:1141-1142`, added in #33404 / GH#33341). The dispatch_with_dedup cases in the test set `SCRIPT_DIR="$TEST_ROOT"` (temp dir, e.g. `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-worker-detection.sh:722`, `:742`, `:776`, `:820`, `:867`, `:920`) and stub the other dispatch helpers, but nothing provides `runner-capability-helper.sh` there, so the gate returns 1 before launch.

## Fix

Make these test cases provide the capability gate in the same way they stub the other pre-launch gates:

- **File to edit:** `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-worker-detection.sh`.
- **Option A:** Write a stub `runner-capability-helper.sh` into `$TEST_ROOT` that defines `runner_capability_check_fresh() { return 0; }`. Reuse the existing test setup that populates `$TEST_ROOT`.
- **Option B:** Copy or symlink the real helper into `$TEST_ROOT`, if its fresh check passes with no declared requirements.
- **Do not change** `pulse-dispatch-core.sh`. The production gate is correct.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-worker-detection.sh` reports `Ran 40 tests, 0 failed.`
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-worker-detection.sh` is clean.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-wrapper-worker-detection.sh`

- Run 37671140471 (`Code Quality Analysis`, PR #33945): job `Model replay verifier boundary (ubuntu-22.04)` started 18:49Z/19:00Z and stayed `in_progress` in step `Install Bubblewrap` (`apt-get update`/`install`) for ~4.5 h.

- Run 37669642160 (`Code Review Monitoring`, PR #33941): job `Monitor & Auto-Fix Code Quality` stuck `in_progress` for ~4.7 h.
- A normal `gh run cancel` did not take effect. Only `POST .../force-cancel` worked. After a rerun, both replay jobs passed in minutes.

Neither job sets `timeout-minutes` (`rg -n 'timeout-minutes' .github/workflows/code-quality.yml .github/workflows/code-review-monitoring.yml` returns nothing).

## Tier

## Context & Decisions

The timeout values are deliberately generous. The goal is to bound hangs, not to tighten normal runtime.
Do not move these jobs to self-hosted runners. That is out of scope.

title: Pulse systemd unit timeout kills workers started by supervisor manual dispatch (shared control group)
body:
## What happened

Workers that the supervisor pulse AI step starts through the manual dispatch path are killed when the pulse systemd service hits its start timeout. All in-flight work is lost to checkpoint recovery.

Observed 2026-10-07 on Linux (systemd user units, aidevops 3.38.29):

- `aidevops-supervisor-pulse.service` is `Type=oneshot`, `KillMode=control-group`, `TimeoutStartSec=3660`, running `pulse-wrapper.sh`.
- The supervisor AI step started 5 workers at 23:18–23:22 UTC via manual dispatch (`session-key manual-cli-<N>-<epoch>`, logs `/tmp/worker-manual-cli-<N>-<epoch>.log`, "Detaching worker").
- At about 23:46–23:47 UTC the journal shows `aidevops-supervisor-pulse.service: State 'stop-sigterm' timed out. Killing.` then `Failed with result 'timeout'`.
- All 5 workers died within the same 3 minutes (23:43–23:46). One log ends mid tool-call with no error, which is consistent with SIGTERM from the cgroup kill. The metrics record `result=local_error`. Some logs also show `Cannot connect to API: The socket connection was closed unexpectedly` just before exit.
- Pulse then filed draft "checkpoint: recover dirty worker worktree" PRs for the killed workers.

"Detaching" the worker does not leave the service's control group, so systemd's `KillMode=control-group` takes the workers down with the pulse cycle.

## Expected

A worker outlives the pulse cycle that dispatched it, whatever the dispatch path (normal `Dispatch_max` or supervisor manual dispatch).

## Suggested fix

Launch every worker in its own transient scope or unit (for example `systemd-run --user --scope` or `--unit`) when running under systemd, or set `KillMode=process` on the pulse unit with explicit cleanup. Then add a check that a worker's cgroup differs from the pulse unit's.

## Files

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` and the systemd unit template that generates `aidevops-supervisor-pulse.service`
- The manual dispatch path that writes `manual-dispatch-<N>-<ts>.log` ("Detaching worker")
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh` (worker launch)

## Verification

Start a worker through manual dispatch from inside the pulse unit, let the unit time out or stop, then confirm the worker PID is still alive and `/proc/<pid>/cgroup` is not under `aidevops-supervisor-pulse.service`.

title: Pulse never continues a worker draft checkpoint when the killed worker's issue stays assigned
body:
## Description

When a worker is killed without writing `CLAIM_RELEASED`, its issue stays assigned with `status:queued`, and a worker draft checkpoint PR exists for it. Pulse then never continues that draft. Each cycle, two paths hand the case to each other and neither acts:

- `dispatch-dedup-stale.sh:338-343` (`_stale_recovery_preserve_draft_checkpoint`): "stale recovery must not unassign its issue owner … The pulse caller consumes this signal and launches a bounded direct-PR continuation worker."
- `pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh:778-781`: if the issue has any assignee, it prints `STALLED_CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_SKIPPED: issue #N is assigned`, with the comment "Assigned drafts belong to stale-assignment recovery (Layer 6)."

The pulse log never shows `STALE_PR_CONTINUATION` or any other stale-recovery line for these issues, so in practice neither path runs. The issues stay stuck until someone manually unassigns them.

This is the inverse of #33654 (fixed by #33663). That fix covers a killed worker whose release *unassigned* the issue. Here the issue is still assigned, because the kill skipped the release entirely; see #33993 for how that kill happens.

## Expected Behavior

An assigned issue with a stale claim (no live worker, claim past `max_age_s`, no activity for `STALE_ASSIGNMENT_THRESHOLD_SECONDS`) and a worker draft checkpoint PR gets an exact-head continuation worker within a cycle or two.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command** (pulse log, 4 consecutive cycles from 23:56Z to 00:10Z+):

```
rg -n "#589" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log
```

**Actual output** (repeats every cycle, identical for #593 and #594):

```
Dedup: WORKER_DRAFT_CHECKPOINT: draft PR #647 is a durable checkpoint for issue #589; ordinary redispatch is blocked
STALLED_CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_SKIPPED: issue #589 in <repo> is assigned
Dedup: #589 in <repo> already assigned — DISPATCH_BLOCK_REASON reason=dedup_active_claim_unverified signal=ASSIGNED: issue #589 in <repo> is assigned to <runner>
Dispatch_max: #589 (<repo>) pre-launch failure stage=dispatch_with_dedup rc=3 reason=dedup_active_claim_unverified
```

The issue timeline has only `DISPATCH_CLAIM ... phase=prelaunch max_age_s=1800` at 23:18:01Z, then nothing. There is no `CLAIM_RELEASED`, and no stale-recovery or `STALE_PR_CONTINUATION` comment or log line.

**Expected output**: `STALE_PR_CONTINUATION: issue #589 … PR #647 preserved for exact-head continuation`, followed by a continuation worker launch.

**Causal status**: confirmed symptom; unconfirmed investigation for the exact reason stale-assignment recovery never evaluates these issues.

**Owning-path proof**:

- **Production entry point**: `pulse-wrapper.sh` Dispatch_max → `dispatch_with_dedup` → `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` claim layer
- **Call chain**: dedup open-PR layer (`WORKER_DRAFT_CHECKPOINT`) → `pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` stalled path (skips because assigned) → claim layer `_classify_claim_dispatch_blocker_reason` (`dispatch-dedup-helper.sh:1326`, broad `*assigned*` → `dedup_active_claim_unverified`, a benign deferral) → no stale-assignment evaluation
- **Integrated verification**: live pulse cycles on aidevops 3.38.29 and 3.38.30

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Launch a worker through manual dispatch (`dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`) so it is assigned with `status:queued` and has a `DISPATCH_CLAIM`.
2. Let it commit work, then kill it without the release path running (for example, through the systemd cgroup kill in #33993).
3. Let pulse write the "checkpoint: recover dirty worker worktree for #N" draft PR.
4. Watch subsequent cycles: the issue is never continued and stays assigned.

## Workarounds Applied

- Manually removed the stale assignee and `status:queued` from the three issues so the existing unassigned-draft continuation (#33663) can pick them up.

See-also: #33993, #33654

## Environment

- aidevops 3.38.29, then 3.38.30 (auto-updated mid-incident; the behaviour is unchanged)
- OpenCode 1.18.34 / 1.18.35, Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS (VirtualBox VM), systemd user units, bash 5.2.21, gh 2.100.0

title: Parallel dispatch defers non-overlapping candidates a full cycle on footprint reservation lock_busy
body:
## Description

With parallel dispatch (`Dispatch_max mode=parallel(N)`), candidates in the same repo compete for the per-repo footprint reservation lock (`dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh:402-427`, 50 attempts × 0.1s). Losers do not wait or retry within the cycle. They emit `FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP (reservation_lock_busy; retry next cycle)` (`:946-949`) and are deferred for the whole cycle. In practice, at most one candidate per repo gets past the footprint check per cycle, so `max_parallel` is ineffective. The candidates' file scopes do not overlap: each owns its own template folder.

## Expected Behavior

Candidates whose footprints do not overlap launch in the same cycle, up to `max_parallel` or the worker cap. Lock contention between them should wait briefly or retry within the cycle, not cost a full cycle.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```
rg -n "footprint-reservation\] event=" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | rg -o "event=[a-z_]+" | sort | uniq -c
```

**Actual output** (single repo, about 2 hours, 2026-10-07):

```
     22 event=lock_busy
     28 event=reserved
      2 event=retired
      9 event=superseded
```

Per-cycle pattern (timestamps are epoch seconds):

```
event=lock_busy issue=#592 ts=1791417557
event=lock_busy issue=#596 ts=1791417560
event=lock_busy issue=#599 ts=1791417569
...next cycle...
event=lock_busy issue=#596 ts=1791417929
event=lock_busy issue=#592 ts=1791417930
event=lock_busy issue=#599 ts=1791417931
...next cycle...
event=reserved issue=#591 ts=1791418056
event=lock_busy issue=#596 ts=1791418425
event=lock_busy issue=#599 ts=1791418431
event=reserved issue=#592 ts=1791418514
```

The cycle summaries read `Dispatch path=max complete: implementation_dispatched=0 ... simultaneous_worker_slots_targeted=4` while 3–4 non-overlapping candidates were deferred and free worker slots existed (`workers=1/5`).

**Expected output**: the non-overlapping candidates each reach `event=reserved` in the same cycle.

**Causal status**: unconfirmed investigation. The symptom (one reservation per cycle, losers deferred a full cycle) is confirmed from the logs. Why the holder keeps the lock longer than the ~5s retry window is not confirmed. The critical section is `_footprint_reservation_entries`, `_footprint_repo_low_info_basenames` and `_footprint_find_overlap` (`:951-976`). The host was CPU-saturated (load about 7 on 7 vCPUs), and these functions spawn subprocesses per path.

**Owning-path proof**:

- **Production entry point**: `pulse-wrapper.sh` Dispatch_max parallel candidate launch → `dispatch_with_dedup`
- **Call chain**: `_dispatch_dedup_check_layers` → `_footprint_check_overlap` (`dispatch-dedup-footprint.sh:926`) → `_footprint_reservation_lock` (`:402`) → lock_busy → `FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP (reservation_lock_busy; retry next cycle)` → `Dispatch_max: ... blocked:footprint_overlap benign dispatch block`
- **Integrated verification**: live pulse cycles on aidevops 3.38.29 and 3.38.30; needs critical-section timing telemetry (lock hold duration per issue)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Queue 4+ auto-dispatch issues in one repo, each with a distinct, non-overlapping Files Scope.
2. Run pulse with parallel dispatch on a busy host.
3. Count `event=reserved` versus `event=lock_busy` per cycle.

## Suggested direction

Log the lock hold duration. Either keep only the minimal write inside the lock, or have losers re-check within the cycle (bounded) instead of deferring a full cycle.

## Workarounds Applied

None. Deferred candidates eventually start one per cycle.

See-also: #33993

## Environment

- aidevops 3.38.29 / 3.38.30, OpenCode 1.18.35, Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS (VirtualBox VM, 7 vCPU, 15 GiB), bash 5.2.21, gh 2.100.0

**Task ID:** `t18618` | **Status:** open
**Tags:** `auto-dispatch` `enhancement`

## Outcome

feat(pulse-merge): auto-merge green worker PRs linked via For #N to open non-parent issues

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## Task


Let the worker-briefed auto-merge path accept a PR whose only issue reference is a non-closing
`For #NNN`/`Ref #NNN`. All three conditions must hold:
- the referenced issue is open,
- it is not labelled `parent-task`,
- it has the same trust and NMR properties already checked for closing-keyword links.

The merge must not close the issue: the squash commit must contain no closing keyword. Parent-task
references (`For #parent`) must stay ineligible.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## Origin

Found on 2026-10-07 during an interactive check of PRs that looked stuck in a managed private repo.
There were 13 green, CLEAN, non-draft `origin:worker` multi-phase enrichment PRs. Each linked its issue
with `For #NNN` because the enrichment issue stays open for later phases. Pulse skipped every one with
`worker-briefed auto-merge: skipping PR #N — no linked issue (t2449)`, about 16 to 17 times each. In the end
they all had to be merged by hand.

## What

Let the worker-briefed auto-merge path accept a PR whose only issue reference is a non-closing
`For #NNN`/`Ref #NNN`. All three conditions must hold:
- the referenced issue is open,
- it is not labelled `parent-task`,
- it has the same trust and NMR properties already checked for closing-keyword links.

The merge must not close the issue: the squash commit must contain no closing keyword. Parent-task
references (`For #parent`) must stay ineligible.

## Why

- Multi-phase work, such as data enrichment with core, people, and logo phases, deliberately keeps the issue open. Today every phase PR then needs a manual merge, even though the same gates (trust, NMR, required checks, review-bot) would pass. On 2026-10-07, 13 PRs piled up in one day.
- `_attempt_worker_briefed_auto_merge` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh`, gate at around line 1266) only receives `linked_issue` from closing keywords.

## Tier

tier:standard. The change sits on a trust boundary in the merge path. Preserve GH#17671 defence-in-depth and mark any new check with `#aidevops:trust-boundary`.

## How (Approach)

1. Find where `linked_issue` is derived for the merge pass: search callers of `_attempt_worker_briefed_auto_merge` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh` and the shared parsing helpers.
2. Add a fallback: if no closing-keyword issue is found, parse a single `For #N`/`Ref #N` reference. Accept it only when the issue is open and not labelled `parent-task`. Then reuse the existing author-association, NMR, and crypto-approval checks unchanged.
3. Make sure the merge path never writes a closing keyword into the squash body for this case.
4. Log a distinct reason, for example `linked via non-closing reference`, so throughput reports can tell the two cases apart.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A green worker PR referencing an open, non-parent issue via `For #N` is auto-merged by pulse, and issue #N stays open.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "non-closing reference"
  ```

- [ ] Regression guard: a PR whose only reference is `For #N`, where #N is labelled `parent-task`, is still skipped. Closing-keyword PRs behave exactly as before. External or untrusted authors still hit the NMR/crypto gates. Existing pulse-merge tests pass.

## Context & Decisions

The repo-side alternative, changing enrichment workers to `Resolves`, was rejected because it would close issues that still have pending phases.
